D027622.name: Crocus
D027622.definition: A plant genus, in the IRIDACEAE family, known as a source of Saffron.

D027623.name: Yucca
D027623.definition: A genus (and common name) in the AGAVACEAE family. It is known for SAPONINS in the root that are used in SOAPS.

D027641.name: Laughter Therapy
D027641.definition: Therapeutic use of humor and laughter to improve emotional well being and health.

D027681.name: Eclecticism, Historical
D027681.definition: A system of medicine, most popular in the 19th century, that advocates the use of indigenous plants in the treatment of specific signs and symptoms.

D027682.name: Cation Transport Proteins
D027682.definition: Membrane proteins whose primary function is to facilitate the transport of positively charged molecules (cations) across a biological membrane.

D027701.name: Organic Cation Transport Proteins
D027701.definition: A family of proteins involved in the transport of organic cations. They play an important role in the elimination of a variety of endogenous substances, xenobiotics, and their metabolites from the body.

D027702.name: Organic Cation Transporter 1
D027702.definition: An organic cation transporter found in kidney. It is localized to the basal lateral membrane and is likely to be involved in the renal secretion of organic cations.

D027703.name: Amaranthaceae
D027703.definition: A family of flowering plants in the order Caryophyllales, with about 60 genera and more than 800 species of plants, with a few shrubs, trees, and vines. The leaves usually have nonindented edges.

D027721.name: Amaranthus
D027721.definition: A plant genus, in the family AMARANTHACEAE, best known as a source of high-protein grain crops and of Red Dye No. 2 (AMARANTH DYE). Tumbleweed sometimes refers to Amaranthus but more often refers to SALSOLA.

D027722.name: Convolvulaceae
D027722.definition: The morning glory family of flowering plants, of the order Solanales, which includes about 50 genera and at least 1,400 species. Leaves are alternate and flowers are funnel-shaped. Most are twining and erect herbs, with a few woody vines, trees, and shrubs.

D027723.name: Ipomoea batatas
D027723.definition: A plant species of the genus IPOMOEA, family CONVOLVULACEAE. Some cultivars are sweet and edible whereas bitter varieties are a source of SAPONINS. This sweet potato is sometimes referred to as a yam (DIOSCOREA).

D027724.name: Reproductive Techniques, Assisted
D027724.definition: Clinical and laboratory techniques used to enhance fertility in humans and animals.

D027741.name: Ipomoea
D027741.definition: A plant genus in the family CONVOLVULACEAE best known for morning glories (a common name also used with CONVOLVULUS) and sweet potato.

D027742.name: Dioscorea
D027742.definition: A plant genus best known for edible underground tubers. Yam may also refer to a moist variety of sweet potato, IPOMOEA BATATAS.

D027743.name: Dioscoreaceae
D027743.definition: The yam plant family, of the order Liliales, has thick roots or tubers and net-veined, heart-shaped leaves that sometimes are lobed.

D027744.name: Tamus
D027744.definition: A plant genus of the DIOSCOREACEAE plant family.

D027761.name: Asparagus Plant
D027761.definition: A plant genus in the family LILIACEAE (sometimes placed in Asparagaceae) that contains ECDYSTEROIDS and is an ingredient of Siotone. The shoots are used as a vegetable and the roots are used in FOLK MEDICINE.

D027762.name: Lilium
D027762.definition: A plant genus in the family LILIACEAE generally growing in temperate areas. The word lily is also used in the common names of many plants of other genera that resemble true lilies. True lilies are erect perennial plants with leafy stems, scaly bulbs, usually narrow leaves, and solitary or clustered flowers.

D027781.name: Shallots
D027781.definition: Mildly aromatic herb in the Allium genus used in SPICES.

D027782.name: Chive
D027782.definition: A plant in the genus ALLIUM, similar to ONIONS.

D027801.name: Galanthus
D027801.definition: A plant genus in the family LILIACEAE (sometimes classified as Amaryllidaceae). Galanthus nivalis L. is the source of GALANTHAMINE.

D027802.name: Hypoxis
D027802.definition: Hypoxis is a plant genus in the family LILIACEAE (sometimes classified as Hypoxidaceae).

D027805.name: Phaseolus
D027805.definition: A plant genus in the family FABACEAE which is the source of edible beans and the lectin PHYTOHEMAGGLUTININS.

D027806.name: Lens Plant
D027806.definition: A plant genus of the FABACEAE family known for the seeds used as food.

D027807.name: Lathyrus
D027807.definition: A plant genus in the family FABACEAE known for LATHYRISM poisoning.

D027821.name: Rutaceae
D027821.definition: A plant family in the order Sapindales that grows in warmer regions and has conspicuous flowers.

D027822.name: Myrtaceae
D027822.definition: The myrtle plant family of the order Myrtales. It includes several aromatic medicinal plants such as EUCALYPTUS.

D027823.name: Rhamnaceae
D027823.definition: The buckthorn plant family, of the order Rhamnales, includes some species with edible fruits and some that are medicinal.

D027824.name: Rosaceae
D027824.definition: The rose plant family in the order ROSALES and class Magnoliopsida. They are generally woody plants. A number of the species of this family contain cyanogenic compounds.

D027825.name: Crataegus
D027825.definition: A genus in the family ROSACEAE of shrubs and small trees native to the North Temperate Zone. It is best known for a traditional medication for the heart.

D027826.name: Rosa
D027826.definition: A plant genus in the family ROSACEAE and order Rosales. This should not be confused with the genus RHODIOLA which is sometimes called roseroot.

D027841.name: Pimenta
D027841.definition: A plant genus in the family MYRTACEAE, order Myrtales, subclass Rosidae. It is best known for allspice from the dried berry of Pimenta diocia.

D027842.name: Syzygium
D027842.definition: A plant genus in the family Myrtaceae. It is known for cloves, which is the flower bud of Syzygium aromaticum and is the source of an oil rich in EUGENOL.

D027843.name: Vitis
D027843.definition: A plant genus in the family VITACEAE, order Rhamnales, subclass Rosidae. It is a woody vine cultivated worldwide. It is best known for grapes, the edible fruit and used to make WINE and raisins.

D027844.name: Vitaceae
D027844.definition: A plant family of the order Rhamnales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida, best known for the VITIS genus, the source of grapes.

D027845.name: Malus
D027845.definition: A plant genus in the family ROSACEAE, order Rosales, subclass Rosidae. It is best known as a source of the edible fruit (apple) and is cultivated in temperate climates worldwide.

D027861.name: Prunus
D027861.definition: A plant genus in the family ROSACEAE, order Rosales, subclass Rosidae. It is best known as a source of edible fruits such as apricot, plum, peach, cherry, and almond.

D027881.name: Agavaceae
D027881.definition: A plant family of the order Liliales, subclass Liliidae, class Liliopsida. Members of the family have narrow, lance-shaped, sometimes fleshy or toothed leaves that are clustered at the base of each plant. Most species have large flower clusters containing many flowers. The fruit is a capsule or berry.

D027882.name: Agave
D027882.definition: A genus known for fibers obtained from their leaves: sisal from A. sisalana, henequen from A. fourcroyoides and A. cantala, or Manila-Maguey fiber from A. cantala. Some species provide a sap that is fermented to an intoxicating drink, called pulque in Mexico. Some contain agavesides.

D027883.name: Astragalus Plant
D027883.definition: A plant genus in the family FABACEAE, subfamily Papilionaceae, order Fabales, subclass Rosidae. Many of the species are associated with poisoning of grazing animals. Some of the species are used medicinally.

D027884.name: Astragalus gummifer
D027884.definition: Astragalus gummifer Labill. is the source of gum TRAGACANTH.

D027885.name: Astragalus membranaceus
D027885.definition: A plant species of the Astragalus genus which is source of Huang qi preparation used in TRADITIONAL CHINESE MEDICINE.

D027901.name: Acanthaceae
D027901.definition: A plant family of the order Lamiales. It is characterized by simple leaves in opposite pairs, cystoliths (enlarged cells containing crystals of calcium carbonate), and bilaterally symmetrical and bisexual flowers that are usually crowded together. The common name for Ruellia of wild petunia is easily confused with PETUNIA.

D027902.name: Justicia
D027902.definition: A plant genus in the family ACANTHACEAE. Adhatoda vasica Nees is a source of vasicine.

D027922.name: Caprifoliaceae
D027922.definition: A plant family of the order Dipsacales, subclass Asteridae, class Magnoliopsida.

D027923.name: Sambucus
D027923.definition: A plant genus in the family CAPRIFOLIACEAE known for elderberries.

D027924.name: Sambucus nigra
D027924.definition: A plant species in the genus SAMBUCUS, known for the elderberry fruit. The plant is also a source of Sambucus nigra lectins and ribosome-inactivating protein.

D027925.name: Viburnum
D027925.definition: A plant genus in the family CAPRIFOLIACEAE. The common name derives from its traditional use for menstrual cramps. It is a source of viburnine, valerianic acid, vibsanin, and ursolic acid. Note that true cranberry is VACCINIUM MACROCARPON.

D027926.name: Anacardiaceae
D027926.definition: The sumac plant family in the order Sapindales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. They are tropical and subtropical trees, shrubs, and woody vines that have resin ducts in the bark. The sap of many of the species is irritating to the skin.

D027927.name: Pistacia
D027927.definition: A plant genus in the ANACARDIACEAE family known for the Pistachio nuts and for gum Mastic.

D027961.name: Potassium-Hydrogen Antiporters
D027961.definition: Membrane proteins that allow the exchange of hydrogen ions for potassium ions across the cellular membrane. The action of these antiporters influences intracellular pH and potassium ion homeostasis.

D027963.name: Chloride-Bicarbonate Antiporters
D027963.definition: Electroneutral chloride bicarbonate exchangers that allow the exchange of BICARBONATE IONS exchange for CHLORIDE IONS across the cellular membrane. The action of specific antiporters in this class serve important functions such as allowing the efficient exchange of bicarbonate across red blood cell membranes as they passage through capillaries and the reabsorption of bicarbonate ions by the kidney.

D027981.name: Symporters
D027981.definition: Membrane transporters that co-transport two or more dissimilar molecules in the same direction across a membrane. Usually the transport of one ion or molecule is against its electrochemical gradient and is "powered" by the movement of another ion or molecule with its electrochemical gradient.

D027982.name: Sodium-Bicarbonate Symporters
D027982.definition: Proteins that cotransport sodium ions and bicarbonate ions across cellular membranes.

D027983.name: Aralia
D027983.definition: A plant genus in the family ARALIACEAE, order Apiales, subclass Rosidae. It includes Aralia californica S. Watson, Aralia nudicaulis L., and Aralia racemosa L.

D028001.name: Eleutherococcus
D028001.definition: A plant genus in the family ARALIACEAE, order Apiales, subclass Rosidae. It is best known as an adaptogen and a substitute for PANAX GINSENG.

D028002.name: Oplopanax
D028002.definition: A plant genus in the family ARALIACEAE, order Apiales, subclass Rosidae. It is the source of cirensenosides (triterpenoid saponins).

D028021.name: Sodium-Potassium-Chloride Symporters
D028021.definition: A subclass of symporters that specifically transport SODIUM CHLORIDE and/or POTASSIUM CHLORIDE across cellular membranes in a tightly coupled process.

D028022.name: Low-Level Light Therapy
D028022.definition: Treatment using irradiation with light of low power intensity so that the effects are a response to the light and not due to heat. A variety of light sources, especially low-power lasers are used.

D028023.name: Arecaceae
D028023.definition: The palm family of order Arecales, subclass Arecidae, class Liliopsida.

D028024.name: Serenoa
D028024.definition: A plant genus in the family ARECACEAE, order Arecales, subclass Arecidae. The fruit or the extract (Permixon) is used for PROSTATIC HYPERPLASIA.

D028041.name: Centella
D028041.definition: A plant of the family APIACEAE which is the source of asiatic acid and asiaticoside. Centella asiatica (L.) Urb. = Hydrocotyle asiatica L. is known for effect on peripheral circulation.

D028042.name: Pimpinella
D028042.definition: A plant genus in the family APIACEAE (Umbelliferae) that is used in SPICES and is a source of anethole.

D028044.name: Phosphate-Binding Proteins
D028044.definition: Proteins that bind to and are involved in the metabolism of phosphate ions.

D028061.name: Phosphate Transport Proteins
D028061.definition: Membrane proteins that are involved in the active transport of phosphate.

D028081.name: Proton-Phosphate Symporters
D028081.definition: Proteins that cotransport hydrogen ions and phosphate ions across cellular membranes.

D028082.name: Boraginaceae
D028082.definition: The Borage plant family is in the class Magnoliopsida, subclass Asteridae, order Lamiales. It is characterized by hairy foliage, usually alternate and simple; flowers are funnel-shaped or tubular. Some of the species contain PYRROLIZIDINE ALKALOIDS.

D028083.name: Scrophulariaceae
D028083.definition: The figwort plant family of the order Lamiales. The family is characterized by bisexual flowers with tubular corollas (fused petals) that are bilaterally symmetrical (two-lips) and have four stamens in most, two of which are usually shorter.

D028084.name: Clusiaceae
D028084.definition: The mangosteen plant family (sometimes classified as Guttiferae; also known as Hypericaceae) of the order THEALES, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida. It includes trees and shrubs with resinous, sticky sap, usually with broad-ended, oblong, leathery leaves with a strong, central vein, flowers with many stamens.

D028101.name: Papaveraceae
D028101.definition: The poppy plant family of the order Papaverales, subclass Magnoliidae, class Magnoliopsida. These have bisexual, regular, cup-shaped flowers with one superior pistil and many stamens; 2 or 3 conspicuous, separate sepals and a number of separate petals. The fruit is a capsule. Leaves are usually deeply cut or divided into leaflets.

D028121.name: Canarypox virus
D028121.definition: A species of AVIPOXVIRUS, subfamily CHORDOPOXVIRINAE. Canarypox virus vectors are used in vaccine and immunotherapy research.

D028141.name: Berberidaceae
D028141.definition: The Barberry plant family of the order Ranunculales, subclass Magnoliidae, class Magnoliopsida. The shrubs have spiny leaves.

D028142.name: Berberis
D028142.definition: A plant genus in the family BERBERIDACEAE. The common names of Barberry or Oregon Grape are also used for MAHONIA. The similar-named Bayberry is the unrelated MYRICA. Oregon Grape was classified by Pursh as a Berberis but Nuttall claimed it is different enough to call it a new genus, MAHONIA. Botanists insist on this name while horticulturists stay with Mahonia. They are shrubs with yellow wood and usually three-branched spines at the base of leafstalks. Flowers are yellow, six-petaled and fruit is a berry with one to several seeds. Members contain BERBERINE.

D028143.name: Mahonia
D028143.definition: A plant genus in the family BERBERIDACEAE. Oregon Grape was discovered in North America and classified by Pursh as a BERBERIS but Nuttall claimed it is different enough to call it a new genus, MAHONIA. Now botanists insist on Berberis while horticulturists stay with this genus. It is a source of BERBERINE.

D028144.name: Podophyllum peltatum
D028144.definition: A plant of the genus PODOPHYLLUM, family BERBERIDACEAE (sometimes classified as Podophyllaceae) which is the source of PODOPHYLLIN and of PODOPHYLLOTOXIN that inhibits DNA TOPOISOMERASES, TYPE II. It is different from the European mandrake, MANDRAGORA.

D028145.name: Caulophyllum
D028145.definition: A plant genus of the family BERBERIDACEAE (sometimes classified as Leonticaceae), most notably Caulophyllum thalictroides (L.) Michx.

D028161.name: Valerianaceae
D028161.definition: The Valerian plant family of the order Dipsacales, subclass Asteridae, class Magnoliopsida that is characterized by 3-5-lobed tubular flowers, often spurred at the base and clustered in tight heads.

D028162.name: Heliotropium
D028162.definition: A plant genus in the family Boraginaceae, order Lamiales, subclass Asteridae. This is the True Heliotrope that should not be confused with an unrelated plant sometimes called Garden Heliotrope (VALERIAN).

D028163.name: Viscaceae
D028163.definition: The Christmas Mistletoe plant family of the order Santalales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. They are parasitic primarily on coniferous trees forming a drooping evergreen bush of leathery leaves on tree branches. The berries are sticky and toxic.

D028181.name: Viscum
D028181.definition: A plant genus in the family VISCACEAE, order Santalales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. Species of this genus contain cytotoxic LECTINS. The common name of MISTLETOE is used for many species of this and the LORANTHACEAE families.

D028182.name: Viscum album
D028182.definition: A plant species of the family VISCACEAE, order Santalales, subclass Rosidae. This is the traditional mistletoe of literature and Christmas. Members contain viscotoxin (5 kDa basic polypeptides related to thionins), beta-galactoside- and N-acetyl-D-galactosamine-specific lectin II (60 kDa), and polysaccharides. Mistletoe lectin I is a type 2 ribosome-inactivating protein. Commercial extracts include Plenosol, Eurixor, Helixor Isorel, Iscador, and NSC 635089 (ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS, PHYTOGENIC).

D028183.name: Loranthaceae
D028183.definition: The showy mistletoe plant family of the order Santalales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. This includes parasitic tropical plants with haustoria connecting to the hosts. The leaves are opposite and thick. The flowers (4-7) have both calyx and corolla. The fruit is a berry with one seed.

D028184.name: Phoradendron
D028184.definition: A plant genus in the family VISCACEAE, order Santalales, subclass Rosidae. Members contain phoratoxin and oleanane TRITERPENES.

D028201.name: Pinaceae
D028201.definition: A plant family of the order Pinales, class Pinopsida, division Coniferophyta, known for the various conifers.

D028202.name: Abies
D028202.definition: A plant genus in the family PINACEAE, order Pinales, class Pinopsida, division Coniferophyta. Balm of Gilead is a common name more often referring to POPULUS and sometimes to COMMIPHORA.

D028203.name: Cedrus
D028203.definition: A plant genus in the family PINACEAE, order Pinales, class Pinopsida, division Coniferophyta. It is the source of cedarwood oil. Cedar ordinarily refers to this but also forms part of the name of plants in other genera.

D028221.name: Larix
D028221.definition: A plant genus in the family PINACEAE, order Pinales, class Pinopsida, division Coniferophyta.

D028222.name: Picea
D028222.definition: A plant genus in the family PINACEAE, order Pinales, class Pinopsida, division Coniferophyta. They are evergreen, pyramidal trees with whorled branches and thin, scaly bark. Each of the linear, spirally arranged leaves is jointed near the stem on a separate woody base.

D028223.name: Pinus
D028223.definition: A plant genus in the family PINACEAE, order Pinales, class Pinopsida, division Coniferophyta. They are evergreen trees mainly in temperate climates.

D028224.name: Pseudotsuga
D028224.definition: A plant genus in the family PINACEAE, order Pinales, class Pinopsida, division Coniferophyta. They are coniferous evergreen trees with long, flat, spirally arranged needles that grow directly from the branch.

D028225.name: Tsuga
D028225.definition: A plant genus in the family PINACEAE, order Pinales, class Pinopsida, division Coniferophyta. They are coniferous evergreen trees and should not be confused with hemlock plants (CICUTA and CONIUM).

D028226.name: Amyloidosis, Familial
D028226.definition: Diseases in which there is a familial pattern of AMYLOIDOSIS.

D028227.name: Amyloid Neuropathies, Familial
D028227.definition: Inherited disorders of the peripheral nervous system associated with the deposition of AMYLOID in nerve tissue. The different clinical types based on symptoms correspond to the presence of a variety of mutations in several different proteins including transthyretin (PREALBUMIN); APOLIPOPROTEIN A-I; and GELSOLIN.

D028241.name: Camellia sinensis
D028241.definition: Camellia sinensis L. (formerly Thea sinensis) is an evergreen Asiatic shrub of the THEACEAE family. The infusion of leaves of this plant is used as Oriental TEA which contains CAFFEINE; THEOPHYLLINE; and epigallocatechin gallate.

D028242.name: Theaceae
D028242.definition: A plant family of the order THEALES, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida, best known for CAMELLIA SINENSIS, which is the source of Oriental TEA.

D028243.name: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy, Familial
D028243.definition: A familial disorder marked by AMYLOID deposits in the walls of small and medium sized blood vessels of CEREBRAL CORTEX and MENINGES.

D028244.name: Camellia
D028244.definition: A plant genus in the family THEACEAE, order THEALES best known for CAMELLIA SINENSIS which is the source of Oriental TEA.

D028281.name: Chelidonium
D028281.definition: A plant genus in the family PAPAVERACEAE, order Papaverales, subclass Magnoliidae.

D028301.name: Feline Panleukopenia Virus
D028301.definition: A species of PARVOVIRUS infecting cats with a highly contagious enteric disease. Host range variants include mink enteritis virus, canine parvovirus (PARVOVIRUS, CANINE), and raccoon parvovirus. After infecting their new hosts, many of these viruses have further evolved and are now considered distinct species.

D028322.name: Inhibin-beta Subunits
D028322.definition: They are glycopeptides and subunits in INHIBINS and ACTIVINS. Inhibins and activins belong to the transforming growth factor beta superfamily.

D028323.name: Parvovirus, Porcine
D028323.definition: A species of PARVOVIRUS causing reproductive failure in pigs.

D028341.name: Activins
D028341.definition: Activins are produced in the pituitary, gonads, and other tissues. By acting locally, they stimulate pituitary FSH secretion and have diverse effects on cell differentiation and embryonic development. Activins are glycoproteins that are hetero- or homodimers of INHIBIN-BETA SUBUNITS.

D028361.name: Mitochondrial Diseases
D028361.definition: Diseases caused by abnormal function of the MITOCHONDRIA. They may be caused by mutations, acquired or inherited, in mitochondrial DNA or in nuclear genes that code for mitochondrial components. They may also be the result of acquired mitochondria dysfunction due to adverse effects of drugs, infections, or other environmental causes.

D028381.name: Nidovirales
D028381.definition: An order comprising three families of eukaryotic viruses possessing linear, nonsegmented, positive sense RNA genomes. The families are CORONAVIRIDAE; ARTERIVIRIDAE; and RONIVIRIDAE.

D028382.name: Arteriviridae
D028382.definition: A family of viruses, of the order NIDOVIRALES, containing spherical virions. In contrast to CORONAVIRIDAE, no protruding spikes are obvious on the surface.

D028421.name: Isoprostanes
D028421.definition: A series of prostaglandin-like compounds that are produced by the attack of free-radical species on unsaturated fatty acids, especially ARACHIDONIC ACID, of cellular MEMBRANES. Once cleaved from the lipid membrane by the action of phospholipases they can circulate into various bodily fluids and eventually be excreted. Although these compounds resemble enzymatically synthesized prostaglandins their stereoisometric arrangement is usually different than the "naturally occurring" compounds.

D028441.name: F2-Isoprostanes
D028441.definition: Isoprostanes derived from the free radical oxidation of ARACHIDONIC ACID. Although similar in structure to enzymatically synthesized prostaglandin F2alpha (DINOPROST), they occur through non-enzymatic oxidation of cell membrane lipids.

D028461.name: Zygophyllaceae
D028461.definition: A plant family of the order Sapindales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida which is a small family of small trees and shrubs growing in arid and warm regions.

D028462.name: Cucumis
D028462.definition: A plant genus of the family CUCURBITACEAE, order Violales, subclass Dilleniidae best known for cucumber (CUCUMIS SATIVUS) and cantaloupe (CUCUMIS MELO). Watermelon is a different genus, CITRULLUS. Bitter melon may refer to MOMORDICA or this genus.

D028463.name: Cucumis melo
D028463.definition: A plant species of the family CUCURBITACEAE, order Violales, subclass Dilleniidae known for the melon fruits with reticulated (net) surface including cantaloupes, honeydew, casaba, and Persian melons.

D028464.name: Cucurbita
D028464.definition: A plant genus of the family CUCURBITACEAE, order Violales, subclass Dilleniidae, which includes pumpkin, gourd and squash.

D028481.name: Euphorbia
D028481.definition: A large plant genus of the family EUPHORBIACEAE, order Euphorbiales, subclass Rosidae. They have a milky sap and a female flower consisting of a single pistil, surrounded by numerous male flowers of one stamen each. Euphorbia hirta is rarely called milkweed but that name is normally used for ASCLEPIAS.

D028482.name: Hevea
D028482.definition: A plant genus of the family EUPHORBIACEAE, order Euphorbiales, subclass Rosidae. Commercial natural RUBBER is mainly obtained from Hevea brasiliensis but also from some other plants.

D028483.name: Abelmoschus
D028483.definition: A plant genus of the family MALVACEAE, order Malvales, subclass Dilleniidae best known for okra.

D028501.name: Malva
D028501.definition: A plant genus of the family MALVACEAE, order Malvales, subclass Dilleniida. The common name of 'Mallow' may sometimes get confused with other plants.

D028502.name: Polygonum
D028502.definition: A plant genus of the family POLYGONACEAE that is an ingredient of Shou-Wu-Pian, a Chinese herbal preparation (DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL). The common name of black bindweed also refers to TAMUS or Fallopia (use POLYGONACEAE).

D028503.name: Cephaelis
D028503.definition: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE, order Rubiales, subclass Asteridae. Cephaelis ipecacuanha is the source of IPECAC.

D028521.name: Musa
D028521.definition: A plant genus of the family Musaceae, order Zingiberales, subclass Zingiberidae, class Liliopsida.

D028522.name: Musaceae
D028522.definition: A plant family of the order ZINGIBERALES, subclass Zingiberidae, class Liliopsida best known for banana (MUSA). The slender false trunk, formed by leaf sheaths of the spirally arranged leaves, may rise to 15 meters (50 feet). There is a crown of large leaves at the top.

D028523.name: Elettaria
D028523.definition: A plant genus of the family ZINGIBERACEAE, order Zingiberales, subclass Zingiberidae. Elettaria cardamomum (L.) Maton is the source of Cardamom used in SPICES.

D028524.name: Anethum graveolens
D028524.definition: Anethum graveolens L. is a plant species of the family APIACEAE. The leaves are considered as a spice (SPICES).

D028525.name: Apium graveolens
D028525.definition: A plant species of the family APIACEAE. The stalks are a food source.

D028526.name: Coriandrum
D028526.definition: A plant genus of the family APIACEAE. The leaves are the source of cilantro and the seeds are the source of coriander, both of which are used in SPICES.

D028527.name: Cuminum
D028527.definition: A plant genus of the family APIACEAE. The seed is used in SPICES.

D028528.name: Petroselinum
D028528.definition: A plant genus of the family APIACEAE used for flavoring food.

D028529.name: Pastinaca
D028529.definition: A plant genus of the family APIACEAE. The roots are used as food.

D028561.name: Transition Elements
D028561.definition: Elements with partially filled d orbitals. They constitute groups 3-12 of the periodic table of elements.

D028581.name: Lanthanoid Series Elements
D028581.definition: Elements of the lanthanoid series including atomic number 57 (LANTHANUM) through atomic number 71 (LUTETIUM).

D028601.name: Euthanasia, Active
D028601.definition: The act or practice of killing for reasons of mercy, i.e., in order to release a person or animal from incurable disease, intolerable suffering, or undignified death. (from Beauchamp and Walters, Contemporary Issues in Bioethics, 5th ed)

D028642.name: Mentally Ill Persons
D028642.definition: Persons with psychiatric illnesses or diseases, particularly psychotic and severe mood disorders.

D028661.name: Complicity
D028661.definition: Association with or participation in an act that is, or is perceived to be, criminal or immoral. One is complicitous when one promotes or unduly benefits from practices or institutions that are morally or legally suspect.

D028662.name: Principle-Based Ethics
D028662.definition: An approach to ethics that focuses on theories of the importance of general principles such as respect for autonomy, beneficence/nonmaleficence, and justice.

D028663.name: Ethical Theory
D028663.definition: A philosophically coherent set of propositions (for example, utilitarianism) which attempts to provide general norms for the guidance and evaluation of moral conduct. (from Beauchamp and Childress, Principles of Biomedical Ethics, 4th ed)

D028681.name: Moral Obligations
D028681.definition: Duties that are based in ETHICS, rather than in law.

D028683.name: National Socialism
D028683.definition: The doctrines and policies of the Nazis or the National Social German Workers party, which ruled Germany under Adolf Hitler from 1933-1945. These doctrines and policies included racist nationalism, expansionism, and state control of the economy. (from Columbia Encyclopedia, 6th ed. and American Heritage College Dictionary, 3d ed.)

D028701.name: Patient Rights
D028701.definition: Fundamental claims of patients, as expressed in statutes, declarations, or generally accepted moral principles. (Bioethics Thesaurus) The term is used for discussions of patient rights as a group of many rights, as in a hospital's posting of a list of patient rights.

D028722.name: Virtues
D028722.definition: Character traits that are considered to be morally praiseworthy. (Bioethics Thesaurus)

D028723.name: Personhood
D028723.definition: The state or condition of being a human individual accorded moral and/or legal rights. Criteria to be used to determine this status are subject to debate, and range from the requirement of simply being a human organism to such requirements as that the individual be self-aware and capable of rational thought and moral agency.

D028725.name: Theology
D028725.definition: The study of religion and religious belief, or a particular system or school of religious beliefs and teachings (from online Cambridge Dictionary of American English, 2000 and WordNet: An Electronic Lexical Database, 1997)

D028741.name: Ethics Committees, Clinical
D028741.definition: Hospital or other institutional ethics committees established to consider the ethical dimensions of patient care. Distinguish from ETHICS COMMITTEES, RESEARCH, which are established to monitor the welfare of patients or healthy volunteers participating in research studies.

D028743.name: Professional Misconduct
D028743.definition: Violation of laws, regulations, or professional standards.

D028744.name: Ethics Committees, Research
D028744.definition: Hospital or other institutional committees established to protect the welfare of research subjects. Federal regulations (the "Common Rule" (45 CFR 46)) mandate the use of these committees to monitor federally-funded biomedical and behavioral research involving human subjects.

D028761.name: Withholding Treatment
D028761.definition: Withholding or withdrawal of a particular treatment or treatments, often (but not necessarily) life-prolonging treatment, from a patient or from a research subject as part of a research protocol. The concept is differentiated from REFUSAL TO TREAT, where the emphasis is on the health professional's or health facility's refusal to treat a patient or group of patients when the patient or the patient's representative requests treatment. Withholding of life-prolonging treatment is usually indexed only with EUTHANASIA, PASSIVE, unless the distinction between withholding and withdrawing treatment, or the issue of withholding palliative rather than curative treatment, is discussed.

D028781.name: Ethical Relativism
D028781.definition: The philosophical view that conceptions of truth and moral values are not absolute but are relative to the persons or groups holding them. (from American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language, 4th ed)

D028861.name: Nuclear Pore Complex Proteins
D028861.definition: Proteins that form the structure of the NUCLEAR PORE. They are involved in active, facilitated and passive transport of molecules in and out of the CELL NUCLEUS.

D028884.name: Karyopherins
D028884.definition: A family of proteins involved in NUCLEOCYTOPLASMIC TRANSPORT. Karyopherins are heteromeric molecules composed two major types of components, ALPHA KARYOPHERINS and BETA KARYOPHERINS, that function together to transport molecules through the NUCLEAR PORE COMPLEX. Several other proteins such as RAN GTP BINDING PROTEIN and CELLULAR APOPTOSIS SUSCEPTIBILITY PROTEIN bind to karyopherins and participate in the transport process.

D028901.name: alpha Karyopherins
D028901.definition: Nucleocytoplasmic transport molecules that bind to the NUCLEAR LOCALIZATION SIGNALS of cytoplasmic molecules destined to be imported into the CELL NUCLEUS. Once attached to their cargo they bind to BETA KARYOPHERINS and are transported through the NUCLEAR PORE COMPLEX. Inside the CELL NUCLEUS alpha karyopherins dissociate from beta karypherins and their cargo. They then form a complex with CELLULAR APOPTOSIS SUSCEPTIBILITY PROTEIN and RAN GTP-BINDING PROTEIN which is exported to the CYTOPLASM.

D028921.name: Biotinidase Deficiency
D028921.definition: The late onset form of MULTIPLE CARBOXYLASE DEFICIENCY (deficiency of the activities of biotin-dependent enzymes propionyl-CoA carboxylase, methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase, and PYRUVATE CARBOXYLASE) due to a defect or deficiency in biotinidase which is essential for recycling BIOTIN.

D028922.name: Holocarboxylase Synthetase Deficiency
D028922.definition: The neonatal form of MULTIPLE CARBOXYLASE DEFICIENCY that is caused by a defect or deficiency in holocarboxylase synthetase. HLCS is the enzyme that covalently links biotin to the biotin dependent carboxylases (propionyl-CoA-carboxylase, pyruvate carboxylase, and beta-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase).

D028941.name: Coronavirus 229E, Human
D028941.definition: A species in the genus CORONAVIRUS causing the common cold and possibly nervous system infections in humans. It lacks hemagglutinin-esterase.

D028961.name: beta Karyopherins
D028961.definition: Nucleocytoplasmic transport molecules that bind to ALPHA KARYOPHERINS in the CYTOSOL and are involved in transport of molecules through the NUCLEAR PORE COMPLEX. Once inside the CELL NUCLEUS beta karyopherins interact with RAN GTP-BINDING PROTEIN and dissociate from alpha karyopherins. Beta karyopherins bound to RAN GTP-BINDING PROTEIN are then re-transported to the cytoplasm where hydrolysis of the GTP of RAN GTP-BINDING PROTEIN causes release of karyopherin beta.

D028962.name: Coronavirus OC43, Human
D028962.definition: A species in the genus CORONAVIRUS causing the common cold and possibly nervous system infections in humans. It contains hemagglutinin-esterase.

D028981.name: Bornaviridae
D028981.definition: A family in the order MONONEGAVIRALES comprising one genus Bornavirus. This family has a unique form of mRNA processing: replication and transcription takes place in the nucleus.

D029001.name: Herbal Medicine
D029001.definition: The study of medicines derived from botanical sources.

D029002.name: Steam Bath
D029002.definition: Therapy of sitting in a hot steamy room followed by a cool bath or shower.

D029021.name: Peste-des-Petits-Ruminants
D029021.definition: A highly fatal contagious disease of goats and sheep caused by PESTE-DES-PETITS-RUMINANTS VIRUS. The disease may be acute or subacute and is characterized by stomatitis, conjunctivitis, diarrhea, and pneumonia.

D029022.name: Acoraceae
D029022.definition: A plant family of the order Arales, subclass Arecidae, class Liliopsida (monocot).

D029023.name: Acorus
D029023.definition: A plant genus of the family ACORACEAE, order Arales, subclass Arecidae most notable for Acorus calamus L. root which contains asarone and has been used in TRADITIONAL MEDICINE.

D029024.name: Marburgvirus
D029024.definition: A genus in the family FILOVIRIDAE consisting of one species (Lake Victoria marburgvirus) with several strains. The genus shows no antigenic cross-reactivity with EBOLAVIRUS.

D029041.name: Actinidiaceae
D029041.definition: A plant family of the order Theales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida. It is best known for Kiwi fruit (ACTINIDIA).

D029042.name: Actinidia
D029042.definition: A plant species of the family ACTINIDIACEAE, order Theales.

D029043.name: Ebolavirus
D029043.definition: A genus in the family FILOVIRIDAE consisting of several distinct species of Ebolavirus, each containing separate strains. These viruses cause outbreaks of a contagious, hemorrhagic disease (HEMORRHAGIC FEVER, EBOLA) in humans, usually with high mortality.

D029044.name: Achyranthes
D029044.definition: A plant genus of the family AMARANTHACEAE, order Caryophyllales, which has been used in traditional medicine (MEDICINE, CHINESE TRADITIONAL).

D029045.name: Rhus
D029045.definition: A plant genus of the family Anacardiaceae, order Sapindales, subclass Rosidae. It is a source of gallotannin (TANNIC ACID) and of somewhat edible fruit. Do not confuse with TOXICODENDRON which used to be part of this genus.

D029061.name: Annonaceae
D029061.definition: The custard-apple plant family of the order Magnoliales, subclass Magnoliidae, class Magnoliopsida. Some members provide large pulpy fruits and commercial timber. Leaves and wood are often fragrant. Leaves are simple, with smooth margins, and alternately arranged in two rows along the stems.

D029062.name: Apocynaceae
D029062.definition: The dogbane family of the order Gentianales.  Members of the family have milky, often poisonous juice, smooth-margined leaves, and flowers in clusters. Asclepiadacea (formerly the milkweed family) has been included since 1999 and before 1810.

D029063.name: Aquifoliaceae
D029063.definition: The holly plant family of the order Celastrales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029064.name: Araceae
D029064.definition: A plant family of the order Arales, subclass Arecidae, class Liliopsida (monocot). Many members contain OXALIC ACID and calcium oxalate (OXALATES).

D029065.name: Aristolochiaceae
D029065.definition: A plant family of the order Aristolochiales subclass Magnoliidae class Magnoliopsida. They are mostly tropical woody vines and a few temperate-zone species. The flowers are 3-parted; some species lack petals while others are large and foul smelling.

D029068.name: Balsaminaceae
D029068.definition: A plant family of the order Geraniales (or Ericales in APG system), subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029069.name: Impatiens
D029069.definition: A plant genus of subsucculent annual or perennial plants in the family BALSAMINACEAE, order Geraniales.

D029082.name: Sendai virus
D029082.definition: The type species of RESPIROVIRUS in the subfamily PARAMYXOVIRINAE. It is the murine version of HUMAN PARAINFLUENZA VIRUS 1, distinguished by host range.

D029101.name: Parainfluenza Virus 3, Bovine
D029101.definition: A species of RESPIROVIRUS, subfamily PARAMYXOVIRINAE, most often seen in conjunction with a secondary infection of MANNHEIMIA HAEMOLYTICA resulting in pneumonic pasteurellosis (PASTEURELLOSIS, PNEUMONIC).

D029121.name: Metapneumovirus
D029121.definition: A genus of the subfamily PNEUMOVIRINAE, containing two members: Turkey rhinotracheitis virus and a human Metapneumovirus. Virions lack HEMAGGLUTININ and NEURAMINIDASE.

D029122.name: Murine pneumonia virus
D029122.definition: A species of the genus PNEUMOVIRUS causing pneumonia in mice.

D029141.name: Novirhabdovirus
D029141.definition: A genus in the family RHABDOVIRIDAE, infecting numerous species of fish with broad geographic distribution. The type species is INFECTIOUS HEMATOPOIETIC NECROSIS VIRUS.

D029142.name: Infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus
D029142.definition: The type species of NOVIRHABDOVIRUS, in the family RHABDOVIRIDAE. It is a major pathogen of TROUT and SALMON.

D029161.name: Oleavirus
D029161.definition: A genus in the family BROMOVIRIDAE containing one species: Olive latent virus 2.

D029181.name: Spirituality
D029181.definition: Sensitivity or attachment to religious values, or to things of the spirit as opposed to material or worldly interests. (from Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 10th ed, and Oxford English Dictionary, 2nd ed)

D029201.name: Hamamelidaceae
D029201.definition: A plant family of the order Hamamelidales, subclass Hamamelidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029221.name: Faith Healing
D029221.definition: The use of faith and spirit to cure disease.

D029222.name: Piper nigrum
D029222.definition: A plant species in the PIPERACEAE plant family. It is a common spice on foods and is used medicinally to increase gastrointestinal assimilation of other supplements and drugs. Piperine is a key component. Black pepper is picked unripe and heaped for a few days to ferment. White Pepper is the ripe fruit dehulled by maceration in water.

D029223.name: Ascoviridae
D029223.definition: A family of insect viruses causing disease in lepidopterous larvae, most commonly from species of the owlet moth family Noctuidae. There is one genus: Ascovirus.

D029241.name: Optic Atrophy, Autosomal Dominant
D029241.definition: Dominant optic atrophy is a hereditary optic neuropathy causing decreased visual acuity, color vision deficits, a centrocecal scotoma, and optic nerve pallor (Hum. Genet. 1998; 102: 79-86). Mutations leading to this condition have been mapped to the OPA1 gene at chromosome 3q28-q29. OPA1 codes for a dynamin-related GTPase that localizes to mitochondria.

D029242.name: Optic Atrophy, Hereditary, Leber
D029242.definition: A maternally linked genetic disorder that presents in mid-life as acute or subacute central vision loss leading to central scotoma and blindness. The disease has been associated with missense mutations in the mtDNA, in genes for Complex I, III, and IV polypeptides, that can act autonomously or in association with each other to cause the disease. (from Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man, http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Omim/, MIM#535000 (April 17, 2001))

D029261.name: Sin Nombre virus
D029261.definition: A species of HANTAVIRUS which emerged in the Four Corners area of the United States in 1993. It causes a serious, often fatal pulmonary illness (HANTAVIRUS PULMONARY SYNDROME) in humans. Transmission is by inhaling aerosolized rodent secretions that contain virus particles, carried especially by deer mice (PEROMYSCUS maniculatus) and pinyon mice (P. truei).

D029262.name: Puumala virus
D029262.definition: A species of HANTAVIRUS causing nephropathia epidemica, a mild form of HEMORRHAGIC FEVER WITH RENAL SYNDROME. It is found in most of Europe and especially in Finland, along with its carrier rodent, the bank vole (Clethrionomys glareolus).

D029263.name: Seoul virus
D029263.definition: A species of HANTAVIRUS causing a less severe form of HEMORRHAGIC FEVER WITH RENAL SYNDROME in Asia (primarily Korea and Japan). It is transmitted by rats, especially Rattus rattus and R. norvegicus.

D029281.name: Nairobi sheep disease virus
D029281.definition: A species of NAIROVIRUS, transmitted by the ixodid ticks and producing a lethal gastroenteritis in sheep and goats. Though a major veterinary pathogen, its effect on humans has not been firmly established.

D029282.name: Patient Education Handout
D029282.definition: Works consisting of a handout or self-contained informative material used to explain a procedure or a condition or the contents of a specific article in a biomedical journal and written in non-technical language for the patient or consumer.

D029301.name: Sandfly fever Naples virus
D029301.definition: A species in the genus PHLEBOVIRUS causing PHLEBOTOMUS FEVER, an influenza-like illness. Related serotypes include Toscana virus and Tehran virus.

D029321.name: Lagovirus
D029321.definition: A genus of the family CALICIVIRIDAE, associated with infections in rabbits and hares, responsible for epidemics with high mortality. RABBIT HEMORRHAGIC DISEASE VIRUS is the type species.

D029322.name: Norovirus
D029322.definition: A genus in the family CALICIVIRIDAE, associated with epidemic GASTROENTERITIS in humans. The type species, NORWALK VIRUS, contains multiple strains.

D029341.name: Sapovirus
D029341.definition: A genus of the family CALICIVIRIDAE associated with worldwide sporadic outbreaks of GASTROENTERITIS in humans. The first recorded outbreak was in human infants in Sapporo, Japan in 1977. The genus is comprised of a single species, Sapporo virus, containing multiple strains.

D029342.name: Vesivirus
D029342.definition: A genus of the family CALICIVIRIDAE comprised of species infecting a wide range of organisms. Most members of this genus can be readily propagated in cell culture (as opposed to other genera of Caliciviridae). The type species is VESICULAR EXANTHEMA OF SWINE VIRUS.

D029362.name: Organic Anion Transporters, Sodium-Independent
D029362.definition: A subclass of ORGANIC ANION TRANSPORTERS that do not rely directly or indirectly upon sodium ion gradients for the transport of organic ions.

D029363.name: Organic Anion Transporters, Sodium-Dependent
D029363.definition: A subclass of ORGANIC ANION TRANSPORTERS whose transport of organic anions is driven either directly or indirectly by a gradient of sodium ions.

D029364.name: Tenuivirus
D029364.definition: A genus of RNA plant viruses as yet unassigned to any family. Plant hosts are all in the family Poaceae. Each species is transmitted by a particular species of planthopper. The type species is Rice stripe virus.

D029365.name: Organic Anion Transporters, ATP-Dependent
D029365.definition: A subclass of ORGANIC ANION TRANSPORTERS whose transport of organic anions is linked directly to the hydrolysis of ATP. The subclass includes those ATP-BINDING CASSETTE TRANSPORTERS that transport organic ions.

D029381.name: Closteroviridae
D029381.definition: A family of plant viruses containing the largest single-stranded RNA genomes. Infections typically involve yellowing and necrosis, particularly affecting the phloem.

D029382.name: Dicarboxylic Acid Transporters
D029382.definition: A family of organic anion transporters that specifically transport DICARBOXYLIC ACIDS such as alpha-ketoglutaric acid across cellular membranes.

D029383.name: Crinivirus
D029383.definition: A genus of plant viruses in the family CLOSTEROVIRIDAE. Transmission is by whiteflies. Lettuce infectious yellows virus is the type species.

D029401.name: Betulaceae
D029401.definition: A plant family of the order Fagales, subclass Hamamelidae, class Magnoliopsida. They have simple, serrate, alternate leaves. Male flowers are borne in long, pendulous catkins; the female in shorter, pendulous or erect catkins. The fruit is usually a small nut or a short-winged samara.

D029402.name: Bignoniaceae
D029402.definition: A plant family of the order Lamiales. The family is characterized by oppositely paired, usually compound leaves and bell- or funnel-shaped, bisexual flowers having a five-lobed calyx and corolla.

D029403.name: Burseraceae
D029403.definition: A plant family of the order Sapindales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. They are resinous trees and shrubs with alternate leaves composed of many leaflets.

D029404.name: Activin Receptors
D029404.definition: Receptors for ACTIVINS are membrane protein kinases belonging to the family of PROTEIN-SERINE-THREONINE KINASES, thus also named activin receptor-like kinases (ALK's). Activin receptors also bind TRANSFORMING GROWTH FACTOR BETA. As those transmembrane receptors of the TGF-beta superfamily (RECEPTORS, TRANSFORMING GROWTH FACTOR BETA), ALK's consist of two different but related protein kinases, Type I and Type II. Activins initiate cellular signal transduction by first binding to the type II receptors (ACTIVIN RECEPTORS, TYPE II ) which then recruit and phosphorylate the type I receptors (ACTIVIN RECEPTORS, TYPE I ) with subsequent activation of the type I kinase activity.

D029405.name: GB virus A
D029405.definition: A species of virus (unassigned to a genus) in the family FLAVIVIRIDAE, that have been identified in at least six species of New World monkeys. They do not cause HEPATITIS in the host or other susceptible species.

D029406.name: GB virus B
D029406.definition: A species of virus (tentatively placed in the genus HEPACIVIRUS) in the family FLAVIVIRIDAE, that was recovered from a tamarin monkey, but may have been of human origin. It causes HEPATITIS in several species of New World monkeys.

D029407.name: GB virus C
D029407.definition: A species of virus (unassigned to a genus) in the family FLAVIVIRIDAE. It is genetically heterogeneous, of human origin, and transmitted by blood or blood products. Despite its alternate name (Hepatitis G virus), its pathogenicity remains controversial.

D029421.name: Cactaceae
D029421.definition: The cactus plant family of the order Caryophyllales, subclass Caryophyllidae, class Magnoliopsida. Cacti are succulent perennial plants well adapted to dry regions.

D029422.name: Campanulaceae
D029422.definition: A plant family of the order Campanulales, subclass Asteridae, class Magnoliopsida

D029424.name: Pulmonary Disease, Chronic Obstructive
D029424.definition: A disease of chronic diffuse irreversible airflow obstruction. Subcategories of COPD include CHRONIC BRONCHITIS and PULMONARY EMPHYSEMA.

D029441.name: Carica
D029441.definition: A plant genus of the family Caricaceae, order Violales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida. It is the source of edible fruit and PAPAIN.

D029461.name: Sialic Acid Storage Disease
D029461.definition: Autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorders caused by lysosomal membrane transport defects that result in accumulation of free sialic acid (N-ACETYLNEURAMINIC ACID) within the lysosomes. The two main clinical phenotypes, which are allelic variants of the SLC17A5 gene, are ISSD, a severe infantile form, or Salla disease, a slowly progressive adult form, named for the geographic area in Finland where the kindred first studied resided.

D029481.name: Bronchitis, Chronic
D029481.definition: A subcategory of CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE. The disease is characterized by hypersecretion of mucus accompanied by a chronic (more than 3 months in 2 consecutive years) productive cough. Infectious agents are a major cause of chronic bronchitis.

D029482.name: Parainfluenza Virus 4, Human
D029482.definition: A species of RUBULAVIRUS causing endemic upper respiratory infections in children. It produces only a mild clinical disease and often goes undetected.

D029501.name: Hamamelis
D029501.definition: A plant genus of the family Hamamelidaceae, order Hamamelidales. It is known for the astringent (ASTRINGENTS) extract of leaves and bark used in over the counter preparations. This should not be confused with the similar named Hamelia genus (RUBIACEAE).

D029502.name: Anemia, Hypoplastic, Congenital
D029502.definition: An inborn condition characterized by deficiencies of red cell precursors that sometimes also includes LEUKOPENIA and THROMBOCYTOPENIA.

D029503.name: Anemia, Diamond-Blackfan
D029503.definition: A rare congenital hypoplastic anemia that usually presents early in infancy. The disease is characterized by a moderate to severe macrocytic anemia, occasional neutropenia or thrombocytosis, a normocellular bone marrow with erythroid hypoplasia, and an increased risk of developing leukemia. (Curr Opin Hematol 2000 Mar;7(2):85-94)

D029521.name: Influenzavirus A
D029521.definition: A genus in the family ORTHOMYXOVIRIDAE causing influenza and other diseases in humans and animals. It contains many strains as well as antigenic subtypes of the integral membrane proteins hemagglutinin (HEMAGGLUTININS) and NEURAMINIDASE. The type species is INFLUENZA A VIRUS.

D029522.name: Hydrophyllaceae
D029522.definition: The waterleaf plant family of the order Solanales, subclass Asteridae, class Magnoliopsida. They have alternate leaves, regular flowers with five-lobed corollas (united petals), and a one- or two-celled ovary.

D029523.name: Illicium
D029523.definition: A plant genus of the family Illiciaceae, order Illiciales, subclass Magnoliidae, class Magnoliopsida. They have evergreen, aromatic leaves and bisexual flowers. The female portion of the flower consists of 7 to 15 carpels.

D029524.name: Influenzavirus B
D029524.definition: A genus of the family ORTHOMYXOVIRUS causing HUMAN INFLUENZA and other diseases primarily in humans. In contrast to INFLUENZAVIRUS A, no distinct antigenic subtypes of hemagglutinin (HEMAGGLUTININS) and NEURAMINIDASE are recognized.

D029525.name: Juglandaceae
D029525.definition: The walnut plant family of the order Juglandales, subclass Hamamelidae, class Magnoliopsida. They are mainly temperate zone trees.

D029541.name: Loganiaceae
D029541.definition: A plant family of the order Gentianales, subclass Asteridae, class Magnoliopsida. They have leaflike appendages at the base of the leafstalks, have terminal flower clusters. Petals have four or five overlapping lobes and the fruit is a capsule containing winged or wingless seeds.

D029542.name: Lycopodiaceae
D029542.definition: The club-moss plant family of the order Lycopodiales, class Lycopodiopsida, division Lycopodiophyta, subkingdom Tracheobionta. The common name of clubmoss applies to several genera of this family. Despite the name this is not one of the true mosses (BRYOPSIDA ).

D029543.name: Nucleocytoplasmic Transport Proteins
D029543.definition: Proteins involved in the process of transporting molecules in and out the cell nucleus. Included here are: NUCLEOPORINS, which are membrane proteins that form the NUCLEAR PORE COMPLEX; KARYOPHERINS, which carry molecules through the nuclear pore complex; and proteins that play a direct role in the transport of karyopherin complexes through the nuclear pore complex.

D029544.name: Foot-and-Mouth Disease Virus
D029544.definition: The type species of APHTHOVIRUS, causing FOOT-AND-MOUTH DISEASE in cloven-hoofed animals. Several different serotypes exist.

D029561.name: Lythraceae
D029561.definition: The loosestrife plant family of the order Myrtales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. Members are mainly herbs and many of them contain ALKALOIDS.

D029562.name: Magnoliaceae
D029562.definition: A plant family of the order Magnoliales, subclass Magnoliidae, class Magnoliopsida. They are trees and shrubs having an elongated conelike floral axis with fragrant flowers that have six tepals (sepals and petals that are not distinctly different) and many spirally arranged stamens.

D029563.name: Cellular Apoptosis Susceptibility Protein
D029563.definition: A nucleocytoplasmic transport protein that binds to ALPHA KARYOPHERINS and RAN GTP BINDING PROTEIN inside the CELL NUCLEUS and participates in their export into CYTOPLASM. It is also associated with the regulation of APOPTOSIS and microtubule assembly.

D029581.name: Malpighiaceae
D029581.definition: A plant family of the order Polygalales, subclass Rosidae class, Magnoliopsida that are mostly shrubs and small trees. Many of the members contain indole alkaloids.

D029582.name: Meliaceae
D029582.definition: The mahogany plant family of the order Sapindales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029583.name: Menispermaceae
D029583.definition: A plant family of the order Ranunculales, subclass Magnoliidae, class Magnoliopsida. Members are mostly vines and shrubs and they contain isoquinoline alkaloids, some of which have been used as arrow poisons.

D029584.name: Prostatic Secretory Proteins
D029584.definition: Proteins secreted by the prostate gland. The major secretory proteins from the human prostate gland include PROSTATE-SPECIFIC ANTIGEN, prostate-specific acid phosphatase, prostate-specific membrane antigen, and prostate-specific protein-94.

D029585.name: Monimiaceae
D029585.definition: A plant family of the order Laurales, subclass Magnoliidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029586.name: Moraceae
D029586.definition: The mulberry plant family of the order Urticales, subclass Hamamelidae, class Magnoliopsida. They have milky latex and small, petalless male or female flowers.

D029587.name: Moringa
D029587.definition: A plant genus of the family Moringaceae, order Capparales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029588.name: Moringa oleifera
D029588.definition: A plant species of the family Moringaceae, order Capparales, subclass Dilleniidae. It is a source of niaziminin and hypotensive thiocarbamate glycosides.

D029589.name: Seminal Plasma Proteins
D029589.definition: Proteins found in SEMEN. Major seminal plasma proteins are secretory proteins from the male sex accessory glands, such as the SEMINAL VESICLES and the PROSTATE. They include the seminal vesicle-specific antigen, an ejaculate clotting protein; and the PROSTATE-SPECIFIC ANTIGEN, a protease and an esterase.

D029590.name: Myricaceae
D029590.definition: A plant family of the order Myricales, subclass Hamamelidae, class Magnoliopsida. They are trees and shrubs having aromatic leaves that often have yellow glandular dots on the surface. Single-seeded fruits are often covered with waxy granules, bumps, or layers. The flowers are small, greenish, and inconspicuous.

D029591.name: Myrsinaceae
D029591.definition: A plant family of the order Primulales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029592.name: Oleaceae
D029592.definition: A plant family of the order Lamiales. The leaves are usually opposite and the flowers usually have four sepals, four petals, two stamens, and two fused carpels that form a single superior ovary.

D029593.name: Jervell-Lange Nielsen Syndrome
D029593.definition: A form of long QT syndrome that is associated with congenital deafness. It is characterized by abnormal cardioelectrophysiology involving the VOLTAGE-GATED POTASSIUM CHANNEL. It results from mutation of KCNQ1 gene (Subtype 1 or JLN1) or the KCNE1 gene (Subtype 2 or JLN2).

D029594.name: Onagraceae
D029594.definition: The evening primrose plant family of the order Myrtales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. Flower parts are mostly in fours and the ovary is inferior.

D029595.name: Orchidaceae
D029595.definition: A plant family of the order Orchidales, subclass Liliidae, class Liliopsida (monocotyledons). All orchids have the same bilaterally symmetrical flower structure, with three sepals, but the flowers vary greatly in color and shape.

D029596.name: Paeonia
D029596.definition: A plant genus of the family Paeoniaceae, order Dilleniales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida. These perennial herbs are up to 2 m (6') tall. Leaves are alternate and are divided into three lobes, each lobe being further divided into three smaller lobes. The large flowers are symmetrical, bisexual, have 5 sepals, 5 petals (sometimes 10), and many stamens.

D029597.name: Romano-Ward Syndrome
D029597.definition: A form of long QT syndrome that is without congenital deafness. It is caused by mutation of the KCNQ1 gene which encodes a protein in the VOLTAGE-GATED POTASSIUM CHANNEL.

D029598.name: Passiflora
D029598.definition: A plant genus of the family Passifloraceae, order Violales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida. They are vines with ornamental flowers and edible fruit.

D029601.name: Pedaliaceae
D029601.definition: The sesame family of the order Lamiales that are mainly herbs and shrubs growing in warm regions.

D029602.name: Phytolaccaceae
D029602.definition: The pokeweed plant family of the order Caryophyllales, subclass Caryophyllidae, class Magnoliopsida. The leaves are alternate, simple and smooth-edged and the flowers are in spikes or panicles and are usually bisexual.

D029603.name: Phytolacca
D029603.definition: A plant genus of the family PHYTOLACCACEAE, order Caryophyllales.

D029604.name: Phytolacca americana
D029604.definition: A plant species of the family PHYTOLACCACEAE. The root has been used in traditional medicine and contains POKEWEED MITOGENS, triterpene glycosides, and antiviral protein.

D029605.name: Phytolacca dodecandra
D029605.definition: A plant species of the family PHYTOLACCACEAE. The root has been used in traditional medicine and contains SAPONINS used to poison SNAILS.

D029606.name: Plumbaginaceae
D029606.definition: A plant family of the order Plumbaginales, subclass Caryophyllidae, class Magnoliopsida of shrubs and herbs. Some members contain ANTHOCYANINS and naphthaquinones.

D029607.name: Seminal Vesicle Secretory Proteins
D029607.definition: The secretory proteins of the seminal vesicles are proteins and enzymes that are important in the rapid clotting of the ejaculate. The major clotting protein is seminal vesicle-specific antigen. Many of these seminal vesicle proteins are under androgen regulation, and are substrates for the prostatic enzymes, such as the PROSTATE-SPECIFIC ANTIGEN, a protease and an esterase.

D029608.name: Polygalaceae
D029608.definition: A plant family of the order Polygalales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029621.name: Polypodiaceae
D029621.definition: The fern plant family of the order Polypodiales, class Filicopsida, division Pteridophyta, subkingdom Tracheobionta.

D029622.name: Portulacaceae
D029622.definition: A plant family of the order Caryophyllales, subclass Caryophyllidae, class Magnoliopsida. There are no true petals; each flower has two to six sepals. They produce betacyanin and betaxanthin pigments and lack anthocyanins.

D029623.name: Primulaceae
D029623.definition: A plant family of the order Primulales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida. The flowers have both stamens and pistil, and the fruits are capsules.

D029624.name: Ferns
D029624.definition: Seedless nonflowering plants of the class Filicinae. They reproduce by spores that appear as dots on the underside of feathery fronds. In earlier classifications the Pteridophyta included the club mosses, horsetails, ferns, and various fossil groups. In more recent classifications, pteridophytes and spermatophytes (seed-bearing plants) are classified in the Subkingdom Tracheobionta (also known as Tracheophyta).

D029625.name: Pteridaceae
D029625.definition: A plant family of the order Polypodiales, class Filicopsida, division Pteridophyta (FERNS).

D029626.name: Ranunculaceae
D029626.definition: The buttercup plant family of the order Ranunculales, subclass Magnoliidae, class Magnoliopsida. The leaves are usually alternate and stalkless. The flowers usually have two to five free sepals and may be radially symmetrical or irregular.

D029627.name: Crassulaceae
D029627.definition: The stonecrop plant family of the order ROSALES, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida that grow in warm, dry regions. The leaves are thick. The flower clusters are red, yellow, or white.

D029628.name: Hydrangeaceae
D029628.definition: A plant family of the order ROSALES, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029629.name: Salicaceae
D029629.definition: A plant family of the order Salicales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida. The leaves are alternate and simple. Staminate (male) flowers consist of from one to many stamens. Pistillate (female) flowers consist of a one-chambered ovary with several to many ovules (potential silky seeds).

D029630.name: Santalaceae
D029630.definition: A plant family of the order Santalales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. They are parasites that form connections (haustoria) to their hosts to obtain water and nutrients. The one-seeded fruit may be surrounded by a brightly colored nut-like structure.

D029631.name: Sapindaceae
D029631.definition: The soapberry plant family of the order Sapindales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. Some members contain SAPONINS.

D029632.name: Sapotaceae
D029632.definition: A plant family of the order Ebenales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida that are tropical trees which have elongate latex cells. Several members bear sweet edible fruits and produce triterpenoid saponins.

D029633.name: Schisandraceae
D029633.definition: A plant family of the order Illiciales, subclass Magnoliidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029641.name: Simaroubaceae
D029641.definition: A plant family of the order Sapindales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. Leaves are alternate and compound. Most have small flowers, bitter bark, and fleshy fruits that are sometimes winged. Members contain QUASSINS.

D029642.name: Smilacaceae
D029642.definition: A plant family of the order Liliales, subclass Liliidae, class Liliopsida (monocotyledon).

D029643.name: Sterculiaceae
D029643.definition: A plant family of the order Malvales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida. The leaves of Sterculiaceae are alternate and simple or palmately compound. Flowers have three to five sepals and five or no petals.

D029644.name: Styracaceae
D029644.definition: A plant family of the order Ebenales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029645.name: Thymelaeaceae
D029645.definition: A plant family of the order Myrtales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. They are mainly trees and shrubs. Many members contain mucilage and COUMARINS.

D029646.name: Tiliaceae
D029646.definition: A plant family of the order Malvales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029647.name: Turnera
D029647.definition: A plant genus of the family Turneraceae, order Violales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029648.name: Verbenaceae
D029648.definition: A plant family of the order Lamiales, subclass Asteridae, class Magnoliopsida. The leaves are opposite or whorled. The flowers are aggregated in spikes, clusters, or racemes.

D029649.name: Violaceae
D029649.definition: A plant family of the order Violales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029650.name: Enterovirus, Bovine
D029650.definition: A species in the family ENTEROVIRUS infecting cattle.

D029661.name: Alnus
D029661.definition: A plant genus of the family BETULACEAE that is distinguished from birch (BETULA) by its usually stalked winter buds and by cones that remain on the branches after the small, winged nutlets are released.

D029662.name: Betula
D029662.definition: A plant genus of the family BETULACEAE. The tree has smooth, resinous, varicolored or white bark, marked by horizontal pores (lenticels), which usually peels horizontally in thin sheets.

D029663.name: Tabebuia
D029663.definition: A plant genus of the family BIGNONIACEAE that is a source of lapachol.

D029681.name: Arabidopsis Proteins
D029681.definition: Proteins that originate from plants species belonging to the genus ARABIDOPSIS. The most intensely studied species of Arabidopsis, Arabidopsis thaliana, is commonly used in laboratory experiments.

D029682.name: Amsinckia
D029682.definition: A plant genus of the family BORAGINACEAE. Members contain PYRROLIZIDINE ALKALOIDS. The common name of burweed is also used for Triumfetta (TILIACEAE).

D029683.name: Borago
D029683.definition: A plant genus of the family BORAGINACEAE.

D029684.name: Lithospermum
D029684.definition: A plant genus of the family BORAGINACEAE. Members contain lithospermans and lithospermic acid.

D029685.name: Pulmonaria
D029685.definition: A plant genus of the family BORAGINACEAE.

D029686.name: Lepidium
D029686.definition: A plant genus of the family BRASSICACEAE growing in Peru mountains. It is the source of maca root.

D029687.name: Capsella
D029687.definition: A plant genus of the family CRUCIFERAE.

D029688.name: Brassica napus
D029688.definition: A plant species of the family BRASSICACEAE best known for the edible roots.

D029701.name: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Proteins
D029701.definition: Proteins obtained from the species SACCHAROMYCES CEREVISIAE. The function of specific proteins from this organism are the subject of intense scientific interest and have been used to derive basic understanding of the functioning similar proteins in higher eukaryotes.

D029702.name: Schizosaccharomyces pombe Proteins
D029702.definition: Proteins obtained from the species Schizosaccharomyces pombe. The function of specific proteins from this organism are the subject of intense scientific interest and have been used to derive basic understanding of the functioning similar proteins in higher eukaryotes.

D029721.name: Drosophila Proteins
D029721.definition: Proteins that originate from insect species belonging to the genus DROSOPHILA. The proteins from the most intensely studied species of Drosophila, DROSOPHILA MELANOGASTER, are the subject of much interest in the area of MORPHOGENESIS and development.

D029741.name: Brassica rapa
D029741.definition: A plant species cultivated for the seed used as animal feed and as a source of canola cooking oil.

D029742.name: Caenorhabditis elegans Proteins
D029742.definition: Proteins from the nematode species CAENORHABDITIS ELEGANS. The proteins from this species are the subject of scientific interest in the area of multicellular organism MORPHOGENESIS.

D029743.name: Boswellia
D029743.definition: A plant genus of the family BURSERACEAE used medicinally since ancient times. It is a source of salai guggal (the gum resin), boswellic acid (ursane type TRITERPENES), and FRANKINCENSE.

D029744.name: Commiphora
D029744.definition: A plant genus of the family BURSERACEAE which is a source of gugulipid and guggulu extract. Balm of Gilead is a common name more often referring to POPULUS and sometimes to ABIES.

D029745.name: Codonopsis
D029745.definition: A plant genus of the family CAMPANULACEAE. The common name of bellflower may sometimes be confused with other plants in the family that have similar appearance.

D029746.name: Lobelia
D029746.definition: A plant genus of the family CAMPANULACEAE used medicinally and is a source of LOBELINE.

D029747.name: Opuntia
D029747.definition: A plant genus of the family CACTACEAE. Species with cylindrical joints are called Cholla; flat jointed ones are Prickly-pear.

D029748.name: Caryophyllaceae
D029748.definition: A plant family of the order Caryophyllales, subclass Caryophyllidae, class Magnoliopsida. The species are diverse in appearance and habitat; most have swollen leaf and stem joints.

D029749.name: Dianthus
D029749.definition: A plant genus of the family CARYOPHYLLACEAE. Members contain dianthins, which are ribosome inactivating proteins.

D029750.name: Saponaria
D029750.definition: A plant species of the family CARYOPHYLLACEAE. It is a source of SAPONINS. The common name "Soapwort" is also used with VACCARIA. The common name of "Bouncing Bet" is occasionally used with VIOLA.

D029751.name: Silene
D029751.definition: A plant genus of the family CARYOPHYLLACEAE. The common name of campion is also used with LYCHNIS. The common name of 'pink' can be confused with other plants.

D029752.name: Stellaria
D029752.definition: A plant genus of the family CARYOPHYLLACEAE.

D029753.name: Celastraceae
D029753.definition: A plant family of the order Celastrales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D029754.name: Catha
D029754.definition: A plant genus of the family CELASTRACEAE. The leafy stems of khat are chewed by some individuals for stimulating effect. Members contain ((+)-norpseudoephedrine), cathionine, cathedulin, cathinine & cathidine.

D029755.name: Maytenus
D029755.definition: A plant genus of the family CELASTRACEAE.

D029756.name: Euonymus
D029756.definition: A plant genus of the family CELASTRACEAE.

D029757.name: Tripterygium
D029757.definition: A plant genus of the family CELASTRACEAE that is a source of triterpenoids and diterpene epoxides such as triptolide.

D029758.name: Cistus
D029758.definition: A plant genus of the family CISTACEAE. The common name of rock rose is also sometimes used with the closely related Helianthemum genus (CISTACEAE).

D029759.name: Calophyllum
D029759.definition: A plant genus of the family CLUSIACEAE. Members contain costatolide, calanolides and 4-phenylfuranocoumarins (FUROCOUMARINS).

D029760.name: Garcinia
D029760.definition: A plant genus of the family CLUSIACEAE. Members contain XANTHONES.

D029761.name: Garcinia cambogia
D029761.definition: A plant species of the family CLUSIACEAE. It is a source of hydroxycitric acid.

D029762.name: Garcinia mangostana
D029762.definition: A plant genus of the family CLUSIACEAE. It is the source of the mangosteen fruit.

D029763.name: Garcinia kola
D029763.definition: A plant species of the family CLUSIACEAE. The common name of 'Bitter Kola' is sometimes also used to refer to COLA.

D029764.name: Combretaceae
D029764.definition: A plant family of the order Myrtales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. They are mostly trees and shrubs growing in warm areas.

D029765.name: Combretum
D029765.definition: A plant genus of the family COMBRETACEAE. Triterpenes and combretastatin have been identified in members of this genus.

D029766.name: Terminalia
D029766.definition: A plant genus of the family COMBRETACEAE. Members contain arjunin, an ellagitannin (TANNINS).

D029767.name: Cornaceae
D029767.definition: A plant family of the order Cornales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida that is a loose grouping of woody ornamentals: 11 of its 14 genera have been placed in single families by some authorities. Some botanists combine members of NYSSACEAE into this family.

D029768.name: Cornus
D029768.definition: A plant genus of the family CORNACEAE. It is widely cultivated for the attractive flowers.

D029769.name: Camptotheca
D029769.definition: A plant genus of the family NYSSACEAE (sometimes classified in the CORNACEAE family). It is a source of CAMPTOTHECIN.

D029770.name: Costus
D029770.definition: A plant genus of the family Costaceae (sometimes classified in Zingiberaceae), order Zingiberales, subclass Zingiberidae, class Liliopsida (monocotyledons). It is a source of SAPONINS and furostanol glycosides.

D029771.name: Rhodiola
D029771.definition: A plant genus of the family CRASSULACEAE. Members contain rhodioloside. This roseroot is unrelated to the familiar rose (ROSA). Some species in this genus are called stonecrop which is also a common name for SEDUM.

D029772.name: Bryonia
D029772.definition: A plant genus of the family CUCURBITACEAE that is the source of bryodin 1 (a ribosome-inactivating protein).

D029773.name: Citrullus
D029773.definition: A plant genus of the family CUCURBITACEAE known for the edible fruit.

D029774.name: Gynostemma
D029774.definition: A plant genus of the family CUCURBITACEAE. It is a source of gypenosides and triterpenoid SAPONINS.

D029775.name: Momordica
D029775.definition: A plant genus of the family CUCURBITACEAE. It is a source of momordin.

D029776.name: Luffa
D029776.definition: A plant genus of the family CUCURBITACEAE known for the fruit which is the source of the luffa sponge and the seeds which contain luffin.

D029777.name: Momordica charantia
D029777.definition: A plant species of the family CUCURBITACEAE. It is a source of ribosome-inactivating proteins and triterpene glycosides.

D029778.name: Trichosanthes
D029778.definition: A plant species of the family CUCURBITACEAE that is a source of TRICHOSANTHIN (a ribosomal inhibitory protein).

D029779.name: Cupressaceae
D029779.definition: A plant family of the order Pinales, class Pinopsida, division Coniferophyta (conifers). They are mainly resinous, aromatic evergreen trees.

D029780.name: Chamaecyparis
D029780.definition: A plant genus of the family CUPRESSACEAE which should not be confused with other cedar and cypress trees of THUJA or CUPRESSUS genera.

D029781.name: Cupressus
D029781.definition: A plant genus of the family CUPRESSACEAE. Cypress ordinarily refers to this but also forms part of the name of plants in other genera.

D029782.name: Libocedrus
D029782.definition: A plant genus of the family CUPRESSACEAE. The common name of 'Cedar' makes this easily confused with other trees using that name including cedrus, JUNIPERUS; and CHAMAECYPARIS.

D029783.name: Thuja
D029783.definition: A plant genus of the family CUPRESSACEAE.

D029784.name: Cycas
D029784.definition: A plant genus of the family Cycadaceae, order Cycadales, class Cycadopsida, division CYCADOPHYTA of palm-like trees. It is a source of CYCASIN, the beta-D-glucoside of methylazoxymethanol.

D029785.name: Cyperaceae
D029785.definition: The sedge plant family of the order Cyperales, subclass Commelinidae, class Liliopsida (monocotyledons)

D029786.name: Cyperus
D029786.definition: A plant genus of the family CYPERACEAE. SESQUITERPENES are found in some of the species.

D029787.name: Drosera
D029787.definition: A plant genus of the family Droseraceae, order Nepenthales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida, that contains naphthoquinone glucosides. The name sundew is rarely used for PYROLA.

D029788.name: Diospyros
D029788.definition: A plant genus of the family EBENACEAE, order Ebenales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida best known for the edible fruit and the antibacterial activity and compounds of the wood.

D029789.name: Ephedra
D029789.definition: A plant genus of the family Ephedraceae, order Ephedrales, class Gnetopsida, division Gnetophyta.

D029790.name: Ephedra sinica
D029790.definition: A plant species of the family Ephedraceae, order Ephedrales, class Gnetopsida, division Gnetophyta. It is a source of EPHEDRINE and other alkaloids.

D029791.name: Ericaceae
D029791.definition: The heath plant family of the order Ericales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida that are generally shrubs or small trees. Leaves are alternate, simple, and leathery; flowers are symmetrical with a 4- or 5-parted corolla of partly fused petals.

D029792.name: Arctostaphylos
D029792.definition: A plant genus of the family ERICACEAE.

D029793.name: Rhododendron
D029793.definition: A plant genus of the family ERICACEAE.

D029794.name: Ledum
D029794.definition: A plant genus of the family ERICACEAE.

D029795.name: Calluna
D029795.definition: A plant genus of the family ERICACEAE.

D029796.name: Vaccinium
D029796.definition: A plant genus of the family ERICACEAE known for species with edible fruits.

D029797.name: Huckleberry Plant
D029797.definition: Several plant species of the genus VACCINIUM known for the edible huckleberry fruit.

D029798.name: Blueberry Plant
D029798.definition: Several plant species of the genus VACCINIUM known for the edible blueberry fruit.

D029799.name: Vaccinium macrocarpon
D029799.definition: A plant species of the family VACCINIUM known for the sour fruit which is sometimes used for urinary tract infections.

D029800.name: Vaccinium myrtillus
D029800.definition: A plant species of the family VACCINIUM.

D029801.name: Vaccinium vitis-idaea
D029801.definition: A plant species of the genus VACCINIUM.

D029802.name: Croton
