D031742.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The seed is used in folk medicine (DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL).

D031743.name: Cymbopogon
D031743.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE which is a source of citronella oil and lemongrass oil.

D031744.name: Cynodon
D031744.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that is considered a lawn grass by some and a weed by others. It contains allergen Cyn d 7.

D031745.name: Dactylis
D031745.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that contains allergen Dac g I.

D031746.name: Digitaria
D031746.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that many people consider to be a weed.

D031747.name: Echinochloa
D031747.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that is grown mainly as a hay crop.

D031748.name: Eleusine
D031748.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. Finger millet or raggee (E. coracana) is an important food grain in southern Asia and parts of Africa.

D031749.name: Elymus
D031749.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The common name of wild rye is used with some other grasses.

D031750.name: Eragrostis
D031750.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE.

D031751.name: Festuca
D031751.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The common name of fescue is also used with some other grasses.

D031752.name: Holcus
D031752.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that contains Hol l 1 and Hol l 5 allergens.

D031781.name: Paspalum
D031781.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that is used for forage.

D031782.name: Pennisetum
D031782.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The seed is one of the millets used in EDIBLE GRAIN. It contains vitexin. The common name of buffelgrass is also used for CENCHRUS.

D031783.name: Phalaris
D031783.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE.

D031784.name: Phleum
D031784.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that contains the Phl p 4 allergen.

D031785.name: Poa
D031785.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that contains the Poa p Ia allergen and allergen C KBGP.

D031786.name: Saccharum
D031786.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE widely cultivated in the tropics for the sweet cane that is processed into sugar.

D031787.name: Sasa
D031787.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. Folin is the water-soluble extract from Sasa albomarginata. Sasa kurinensis is an ingredient of Sho-ju-sen, a Japanese herbal medicine.

D031801.name: Polygala
D031801.definition: A plant genus of the family POLYGALACEAE that contains onjisaponins, xanthones, pyrones, and benzophenones. The name is similar to other snakeroots such as ASARUM; SANICULA; ARISTOLOCHIA; AGERATINA; and others.

D031802.name: Securidaca
D031802.definition: A plant genus of the family POLYGALACEAE that contains securiosides and indole alkaloids.

D031803.name: Eriogonum
D031803.definition: A plant genus of the family POLYGONACEAE.

D031804.name: Rumex
D031804.definition: A plant genus of the family POLYGONACEAE that contains patientosides and other naphthalene glycosides.

D031805.name: Pontederiaceae
D031805.definition: A plant family of the order Liliales, subclass Liliidae, class Liliopsida (monocotyledons). Most species are perennials, native primarily to tropical America. They have creeping rootstocks, fibrous roots, and leaves in clusters at the base of the plant or borne on branched stems. The fruit is a capsule containing many seeds, or a one-seeded winged structure.

D031806.name: Eichhornia
D031806.definition: A plant genus of the family PONTEDERIACEAE that is used as a biological filter for treating wastewater.

D031821.name: Potamogetonaceae
D031821.definition: A plant family of the order Najadales, subclass Alismatidae, class Liliopsida (monocotyledons).

D031822.name: Portulaca
D031822.definition: A plant genus of the family PORTULACACEAE.

D031823.name: Anagallis
D031823.definition: A plant genus of the family PRIMULACEAE that contains anagallosides, which are molluscacidal triterpenoid saponins.

D031824.name: Cyclamen
D031824.definition: A plant genus of the family PRIMULACEAE that contains triterpenoid saponins.

D031825.name: Primula
D031825.definition: A plant genus of the family PRIMULACEAE. It can cause CONTACT DERMATITIS. SAPONINS have been identified in the root.

D031826.name: Punicaceae
D031826.definition: A plant family of the order Myrtales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida that is a small family with a single genus.

D031827.name: Pyrolaceae
D031827.definition: A plant family of the order Ericales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D031828.name: Pyrola
D031828.definition: A plant genus of the family PYROLACEAE. The common name of wintergreen is more often used for GAULTHERIA.

D031841.name: Aconitum
D031841.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Members contain a number of diterpenoid alkaloids including: aconitans, hypaconitine, ACONITINE, jesaconitine, ignavine, napelline, and mesaconitine. The common name of Wolfbane is similar to the common name for ARNICA.

D031842.name: Actaea
D031842.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Cycloartanes have been found in the rhizomes.

D031843.name: Adonis
D031843.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Members contain cardenolide oligoglycosides such as adoniside, adonisidum and alepposide.

D031844.name: Nigella
D031844.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE.

D031845.name: Hajdu-Cheney Syndrome
D031845.definition: Rare, autosomal dominant syndrome characterized by ACRO-OSTEOLYSIS, generalized OSTEOPOROSIS, and skull deformations.

D031861.name: Nigella damascena
D031861.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. The name is similar to giant fennel (FERULA), true fennel (FOENICULUM), and dog fennel (ANTHEMIS).

D031881.name: Nigella sativa
D031881.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE that contains alpha-hederin, a triterpene saponin in the seeds, and is the source of black seed oil.

D031882.name: Delphinium
D031882.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Members contain ACONITINE and other diterpenoid alkaloids.

D031883.name: Anemone
D031883.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE that contains triterpene saponins. The root of Anemone raddeana is the source of a Chinese folk medicine, zhu jie xian fu. The common name of liverwort is also used with other plants. This genus is unrelated to SEA ANEMONES.

D031884.name: Aquilegia
D031884.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE that contains aquiledine, isoaquiledine and cycloartane-type glycosides.

D031885.name: Cimicifuga
D031885.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE that contains triterpenoid saponins. Remifemin from C. racemosa is used to suppress LUTEINIZING HORMONE. It is reclassified by some to ACTAEA. The common name of black snakeroot is also used with ASARUM and SANICULA.

D031901.name: Gestational Trophoblastic Disease
D031901.definition: A group of diseases arising from pregnancy that are commonly associated with hyperplasia of trophoblasts (TROPHOBLAST) and markedly elevated human CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN. They include HYDATIDIFORM MOLE, invasive mole (HYDATIDIFORM MOLE, INVASIVE), placental-site trophoblastic tumor (TROPHOBLASTIC TUMOR, PLACENTAL SITE), and CHORIOCARCINOMA. These neoplasms have varying propensities for invasion and spread.

D031941.name: Hemorrhagic Septicemia, Viral
D031941.definition: A systemic infection of various salmonid and a few nonsalmonid fishes caused by Viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (see NOVIRHABDOVIRUS),

D031942.name: Cynara
D031942.definition: A plant genus of the family ASTERACEAE.

D031943.name: Cynara scolymus
D031943.definition: A plant species of the genus CYNARA, family ASTERACEAE. The flower bud is the familiar artichoke eaten as a vegetable.

D031944.name: Dahlia
D031944.definition: A plant genus of the family ASTERACEAE that contains antifungal plant defensin.

D031945.name: Coreopsis
D031945.definition: A plant genus of the family ASTERACEAE that contains phenyl propanoids.

D031946.name: Pulsatilla
D031946.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Members contain cernuosides and other oleanane and hederagenin saponins.

D031947.name: Ranunculus
D031947.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE that contains protoanemonin, anemonin, and ranunculin.

D031948.name: Semiaquilegia
D031948.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE that contains griffonilide, lithospermoside, and magnoflorine.

D031949.name: Thalictrum
D031949.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Members contain isoquinoline alkaloids and triterpene glycosides.

D031950.name: Xanthorhiza
D031950.definition: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Members contain isoquinoline alkaloids.

D031951.name: Resedaceae
D031951.definition: A plant family of the order Capparales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida. It is a small family of herbs and shrubs. Some produce GLUCOSINOLATES.

D031952.name: Ceanothus
D031952.definition: A plant genus of the family RHAMNACEAE. Root nodules host the Frankia (ACTINOMYCETES) nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

D031953.name: Colubrina
D031953.definition: A plant genus of the family RHAMNACEAE. Members contain antifungal jujubogenin saponins.

D031954.name: Choriocarcinoma, Non-gestational
D031954.definition: A highly malignant CHORIOCARCINOMA derived from the non-placental origin such as the totipotent cells in the TESTIS, the OVARY, and the PINEAL GLAND. It produces high levels of CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN and can metastasize widely through the bloodstream to the lungs, brain, liver, bone, and other viscera by the time of diagnosis.

D031955.name: Frangula
D031955.definition: A plant genus of the family RHAMNACEAE. This genus is often called buckthorn but should not be confused with other plants called that such as HIPPOPHAE or KARWINSKIA. Some RHAMNUS species have been reclassified into this genus. F. purshiana bark is cascara sagrada (CASCARA). Members contain emodine, frangulanin, frangulin, and anthraquinones such as EMODIN.

D031956.name: Karwinskia
D031956.definition: A plant genus of the family RHAMNACEAE that contains tullidinol (toxin T-544) and peroxisomicine (toxin T-514). It is sometimes called buckthorn but should not be confused with other plants called that.

D031957.name: Ziziphus
D031957.definition: A plant genus of the family RHAMNACEAE. Members contain nummularogenin (a spirostane) and is the source of an edible fruit.

D031961.name: Connaraceae
D031961.definition: A plant family of the order ROSALES, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida that are tropical plants. The flowers are usually bisexual and have 5 sepals and petals; 5 or 10 stamens; and 1, 4, or usually 5 separate, one-chambered, female ovule-bearing structures (carpels).

D031962.name: Kalanchoe
D031962.definition: A plant genus of the family CRASSULACEAE. Members contain bryophyllins (also called bryotoxins) which are bufadienolides (BUFANOLIDES) that have insecticidal activity.

D031963.name: Sedum
D031963.definition: A plant genus of the family CRASSULACEAE. Some species in this genus are called stonecrop which is also a common name for RHODIOLA.

D031964.name: Grossulariaceae
D031964.definition: A plant family of the order ROSALES, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. They are deciduous woody shrubs with alternate leaves. The flowers are in terminal racemes with 5 petals and 5 stamens.

D031965.name: Ribes
D031965.definition: A plant genus of the family GROSSULARIACEAE. GAMMA-LINOLENIC ACID is obtained from the black currant oil of the seeds.

D031966.name: Hydrangea
D031966.definition: A plant genus of the family HYDRANGEACEAE. Members contain hydrangenol, thunberginols, hydramacrosides A and B, and secoiridoid glucosides.

D031981.name: Agrimonia
D031981.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE that has been used in folk treatment of diabetes. Members contain agrimoniin (TANNINS).

D031982.name: Alchemilla
D031982.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE. Members contain esculetin and QUERCETIN.

D031983.name: Eriobotrya
D031983.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE that is the source of an edible fruit. Members contain TRITERPENES.

D031984.name: Filipendula
D031984.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE. Members contain TANNINS.

D031985.name: Fragaria
D031985.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE known for the edible fruit.

D031986.name: Geum
D031986.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE. Members contain TRITERPENES.

D031987.name: Potentilla
D031987.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE. Members contain procyanidins and TANNINS.

D031989.name: Pyrus
D031989.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE known for the edible fruit.

D031990.name: Quillaja
D031990.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE whose members produce SAPONINS.

D031991.name: Pyracantha
D031991.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE widely cultivated as a prickly hedge with bright red berries. Members contain pyracrenic acid (a lupane triterpenoid).

D031992.name: Spiraea
D031992.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE. Members contain prunioside, spiramine and other diterpene alkaloids.

D031993.name: Sanguisorba
D031993.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE. Members contain sanguiin.

D031994.name: Sorbus
D031994.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE.

D031995.name: Saxifragaceae
D031995.definition: The saxifrage plant family of the order ROSALES, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. The leaves are alternate and sometimes deeply lobed or form rosettes. The flowers have both male and female parts and 4 or 5 sepals and petals; they are usually in branched clusters. The fruit is a capsule with many seeds.

D031996.name: Heuchera
D031996.definition: A plant genus of the family SAXIFRAGACEAE with dark green round or heart-shaped leaves and tiny flowers.

D032022.name: Delegation, Professional
D032022.definition: The process of assigning duties to a subordinate with lesser qualifications.

D032023.name: Integrons
D032023.definition: DNA elements that include the component genes and insertion site for a site-specific recombination system that enables them to capture mobile gene cassettes.

D032024.name: Personnel Delegation
D032024.definition: To entrust to the care or management of another, to transfer or to assign tasks within an organizational or administrative unit or structure

D032041.name: Nested Genes
D032041.definition: Genes whose entire sequences are contained within other genes.

D032061.name: Galium
D032061.definition: A genus of herbaceous annual and perennial plants in the family RUBIACEAE.

D032062.name: Gardenia
D032062.definition: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members contain genepin, from which geniposide is obtained for use as a crosslinking agent in ADHESIVES, and 3-caffeoyl-4-sinapoylquinic acid.

D032063.name: Hamelia
D032063.definition: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE that has a name very similar to another plant genus, HAMAMELIS.

D032064.name: Hedyotis
D032064.definition: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members contain anthraquinones and iridoids. H. diffusa is used in DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL.

D032065.name: Mitragyna
D032065.definition: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members contain antimalarial (ANTIMALARIALS) and analgesic (ANALGESICS) indole alkaloids.

D032066.name: Morinda
D032066.definition: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members contain iridoid glycosides and ANTHRAQUINONES.

D032067.name: Oldenlandia
D032067.definition: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Some species are used as an ingredient in Chinese and African traditional medicines. Members contain kalata B1, a macrocyclic peptide.

D032068.name: Pausinystalia
D032068.definition: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members produce YOHIMBINE.

D032069.name: Psychotria
D032069.definition: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members contain psychotridine and brachycerine (indole alkaloids).

D032070.name: Uncaria
D032070.definition: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members contain uncarine and other cytotoxic and hypotensive oxindole alkaloids.

D032081.name: Casimiroa
D032081.definition: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE. The fruit is edible and the seed has cardiovascular activity.

D032082.name: Citrus aurantiifolia
D032082.definition: A plant species of the genus CITRUS, family RUTACEAE that provides the familiar lime fruit. Its common name of lime is similar to the limetree (TILIA).

D032083.name: Citrus paradisi
D032083.definition: A plant species of the genus CITRUS, family RUTACEAE that produces the familiar grapefruit. There is evidence that grapefruit inhibits CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP3A4, resulting in delayed metabolism and higher blood levels of a variety of drugs.

D032084.name: Citrus sinensis
D032084.definition: A plant species of the genus CITRUS, family RUTACEAE that provides the familiar orange fruit which is also a source of orange oil.

D032085.name: Isochores
D032085.definition: Large regions of the GENOME that contain local similarities in BASE COMPOSITION.

D032086.name: Evodia
D032086.definition: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE which is used in Chinese medicine (DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL). Evodiamine and other quinazoline alkaloids (QUINAZOLINES) are obtained from the fruit of E. ruticarpa.

D032101.name: Murraya
D032101.definition: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE. Members contain murrayanine, koenine, isomahanine, kwangsine, siamenol, murrayafoline A, murrayaquinone A and other cytotoxic carbazolequinones.

D032102.name: Phellodendron
D032102.definition: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE. Members contain BERBERINE, indolopyridoquinazoline and other ALKALOIDS and limonoids.

D032103.name: Pilocarpus
D032103.definition: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE that is the natural source of PILOCARPINE.

D032104.name: Poncirus
D032104.definition: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE. Members contain ponfolin, a coumarin (COUMARINS).

D032105.name: Ruta
D032105.definition: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE. Members contain quinoline alkaloids.

D032106.name: Zanthoxylum
D032106.definition: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE. Some members of Zanthoxylum are reclassified from ELEUTHEROCOCCUS, Melicope, and EVODIA. The twigs are used as dental brushing sticks (TOOTHBRUSHING).  Most plants that are called Fagara have been reclassified as Zanthoxylum, however some Fagara were reclassified  to MELICOPE (also in the Rutacea family) or to GLEDITSIA (a genus in the FABACEAE family).

D032107.name: Populus
D032107.definition: A plant genus of the family SALICACEAE. Balm of Gilead is a common name used for P. candicans, or P. gileadensis, or P. jackii, and sometimes also used for ABIES BALSAMEA or for COMMIPHORA.

D032108.name: Salix
D032108.definition: A plant genus of the family SALICACEAE. Members contain salicin, which yields SALICYLIC ACID.

D032121.name: Salvadoraceae
D032121.definition: A plant family of the order Celastrales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida, a small family growing in the tropics. Members contain piperidine alkaloids and GLUCOSINOLATES.

D032122.name: Pyrularia
D032122.definition: A plant genus of the family SANTALACEAE. Members contain thionin toxin, which shouldn't be confused with thionine.

D032123.name: Santalum
D032123.definition: A plant genus of the family SANTALACEAE which is the source of sandalwood oil.

D032124.name: Blighia
D032124.definition: A plant genus of the family SAPINDACEAE. Members contain hypoglycins and ackee oil.

D032125.name: Litchi
D032125.definition: A plant genus of the family SAPINDACEAE that bears sweet fruits. Unusual fatty acids such as cyclopropanoic fatty acids have been identified in the seeds.

D032126.name: Paullinia
D032126.definition: A plant genus of the family SAPINDACEAE. The seed of P. cupana is the source of guarana powder which contains 4% CAFFEINE.

D032127.name: Sapindus
D032127.definition: A plant genus of the family SAPINDACEAE that contain SAPONINS.

D032128.name: Madhuca
D032128.definition: A plant genus of the family SAPOTACEAE that is the source of mahua oil. Members contain oleanene triterpenoid saponins.

D032129.name: Manilkara
D032129.definition: A plant genus of the family SAPOTACEAE that bears sweet fruit.

D032130.name: Mimusops
D032130.definition: A plant genus of the family SAPOTACEAE. Members contain triterpenoid saponins. Latex from bark incisions is processed into gutta balata.

D032131.name: Palaquium
D032131.definition: A plant genus of the family SAPOTACEAE. Latex from bark incisions is processed into GUTTA-PERCHA.

D032132.name: Pouteria
D032132.definition: A plant genus of the family SAPOTACEAE. Members contain triterpenes. Some species in this genus are called mamey which is also a common name for MAMMEA.

D032133.name: Synsepalum
D032133.definition: A plant genus of the family SAPOTACEAE. Members contain miraculin (also spelled mieraculin), a sweet protein.

D032134.name: Saururaceae
D032134.definition: A plant family of the order Piperales, subclass Magnoliidae class Magnoliopsida. Members contain sauristolactam, and aristololactam BII.

D032135.name: Kadsura
D032135.definition: A plant genus of the family SCHISANDRACEAE that is used in folk medicine much like SCHISANDRA. Members contain kadsurenone and kadsurin.

D032141.name: Schisandra
D032141.definition: A plant genus of the family SCHISANDRACEAE. Members contain schisandrins (Russian) which are also called gomisins (Japanese) or wuweizins (Chinese). The compounds in this genus are very similar to those in the related KADSURA and medicinal usage is very similar. It is sometimes adulterated with KADSURA.

D032161.name: Antirrhinum
D032161.definition: A plant genus of the family Plantaginaceae. Members contain DEFICIENS PROTEIN.

D032181.name: Craterostigma
D032181.definition: A plant genus of the order Lamiales, family Linderniaceae.

D032201.name: Euphrasia
D032201.definition: A plant genus of the family Orobanchaceae used in FOLK REMEDIES for the eyes.

D032221.name: Linaria
D032221.definition: A plant genus of the family Plantaginaceae. Members contain linarin (also called acaciin).

D032241.name: Mimulus
D032241.definition: A plant genus of the family Phrymaceae. Members contain 6-geranylflavanones and mimulone.

D032261.name: Picrorhiza
D032261.definition: A plant genus of the family Plantaginaceae. Members contain scrosides (CINNAMATES) and phenylethanoid glycoside. P. kurrooa is the source of picroliv (a purified iridoid glycoside fraction from the roots having hepatoprotective, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties).

D032262.name: Pedicularis
D032262.definition: A plant genus of the family Orobanchaceae. Members contain phenylpropanoid glycosides and iridoids.

D032263.name: Penstemon
D032263.definition: A plant genus of the family Plantaginaceae. Members contain phenylpropanoid and iridoid glycosides.

D032264.name: Veronica
D032264.definition: A plant genus of the family Plantaginaceae. Members contain bis-sesquiterpene and iridoid glucosides.

D032265.name: Verbascum
D032265.definition: A plant genus of the family SCROPHULARIACEAE.

D032266.name: Scrophularia
D032266.definition: A plant genus of the family SCROPHULARIACEAE. Members contain iridoids.

D032267.name: Rehmannia
D032267.definition: A plant genus of the family Rehmanniaceae. Members contain catapol, rehmannin and ALKALOIDS.

D032268.name: Ailanthus
D032268.definition: A plant genus of the family SIMAROUBACEAE. Members contain ailantinols and other quassinoids.

D032269.name: Brucea
D032269.definition: A plant genus of the family SIMAROUBACEAE. Members contain bruceosides and bruceanols (quassinoids). The astringent seeds have been used to treat dysentery in southeastern Asia.

D032270.name: Picrasma
D032270.definition: A plant genus of the family SIMAROUBACEAE. Members contain javanicins, picrasinoside and other quassinoids.

D032271.name: Quassia
D032271.definition: A plant genus of the family SIMAROUBACEAE. Members contain quassinoids. Quassia simarouba has been reclassified as SIMAROUBA.

D032272.name: Simarouba
D032272.definition: A plant genus of the family SIMAROUBACEAE. Members produce quassinoids.

D032281.name: Smilax
D032281.definition: A plant genus of the family SMILACACEAE. Members contain smiglasides (phenylpropanoid glycosides) and steroidal saponins. Commercially it is sometimes adulterated with HEMIDESMUS, which would affect experimental results.

D032282.name: Atropa
D032282.definition: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE which contain SOLANACEOUS ALKALOIDS including ATROPINE which is named after this genus.

D032301.name: Cestrum
D032301.definition: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain steroidal saponins and cause CALCINOSIS in grazing livestock due to high levels of 1 ALPHA,25-DIHYDROXYVITAMIN D3.

D032302.name: Datura
D032302.definition: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain TROPANES. The common name of trumpet flower is also sometimes used for GELSEMIUM.

D032303.name: Duboisia
D032303.definition: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE that is a source of SCOPOLAMINE HYDROBROMIDE and other TROPANES.

D032304.name: Hyoscyamus
D032304.definition: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE which contains TROPANES.

D032305.name: Lycium
D032305.definition: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain CEREBROSIDES and SCOPOLETIN.

D032306.name: Petunia
D032306.definition: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain steroidal glycosides.

D032321.name: Physalis
D032321.definition: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain physalin and withangulatin.

D032322.name: Solanum
D032322.definition: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain SOLANACEOUS ALKALOIDS. Some species in this genus are called deadly nightshade which is also a common name for ATROPA BELLADONNA.

D032323.name: Solanum melongena
D032323.definition: A plant species of the genus SOLANUM, family SOLANACEAE. The fruit is a large, egg-shaped berry, varying in color from dark purple to red, yellowish, or white. The leaves are large and ovate. The flowers are pendant, violet, and two inches across.

D032324.name: Solanum nigrum
D032324.definition: A plant species of the genus SOLANUM, family SOLANACEAE that contains steroidal glycosides.

D032341.name: Withania
D032341.definition: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain withanolides. Withania somnifera is the source of ashwagandha and aswal.

D032342.name: Muscle Cells
D032342.definition: Mature contractile cells, commonly known as myocytes, that form one of three kinds of muscle. The three types of muscle cells are skeletal (MUSCLE FIBERS, SKELETAL), cardiac (MYOCYTES, CARDIAC), and smooth (MYOCYTES, SMOOTH MUSCLE). They are derived from embryonic (precursor) muscle cells called MYOBLASTS.

D032361.name: Sterculia
D032361.definition: A plant genus of the family STERCULIACEAE. S. urens is the source of KARAYA GUM which is sometimes called Indian tragacanth, which is different from the true TRAGACANTH which comes from ASTRAGALUS GUMMIFER.

D032362.name: Styrax
D032362.definition: A plant genus of the family STYRACACEAE. Sap of these Asian trees are a source of a balsam (BALSAMS). This styrax balsam is 3/4 coniferyl benzoate, 1/8 free BENZOIC ACID, along with benzyl cinnamate, vanillin, and TRITERPENES.

D032363.name: Tamaricaceae
D032363.definition: A plant family of the order Violales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D032364.name: Daphne
D032364.definition: A plant genus of the family THYMELAEACEAE. They are evergreen shrubs much cultivated in garden borders and rock gardens in mild climates. Members contain mezerein, flavonoids, and COUMARINS such as daphnetin and daphnin.

D032365.name: Wikstroemia
D032365.definition: A plant genus of the family THYMELAEACEAE. Members contain daphnoretin and wikstroelides and daphnane-type DITERPENES.

D032381.name: Corchorus
D032381.definition: A plant genus of the family TILIACEAE. Members contain cycloartane saponins and CARDENOLIDES.

D032382.name: Grewia
D032382.definition: A plant genus of the family TILIACEAE. Members contain lupeol and betulin TRITERPENES.

D032383.name: Myocytes, Cardiac
D032383.definition: Striated muscle cells found in the heart. They are derived from cardiac myoblasts (MYOBLASTS, CARDIAC).

D032384.name: Tilia
D032384.definition: A plant genus of the family TILIACEAE. Some species in this genus are called Limetree which is nearly the same as the common name for lime (CITRUS AURANTIIFOLIA). Some people are allergic to the POLLEN.

D032385.name: Triumfetta
D032385.definition: A plant genus of the family TILIACEAE. The common name of burweed is also used for AMSINCKIA. Triumfetta semitriloba is considered a noxious weed.

D032386.name: Myoblasts, Cardiac
D032386.definition: Precursor cells destined to differentiate into cardiac myocytes (MYOCYTES, CARDIAC).

D032387.name: Tropaeolaceae
D032387.definition: A plant family of the order Geraniales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida.

D032388.name: Tropaeolum
D032388.definition: A plant genus of the family TROPAEOLACEAE. The common nasturtium is a plant that grows 2.4-3.6 m (8-12 feet) tall and has funnel-shaped flowers that are commonly yellow-orange with red spots or stripes and have a long spur that contains sweet nectar. Some species in this genus are called watercress which is also a common name for RORIPPA and NASTURTIUM.

D032389.name: Myocytes, Smooth Muscle
D032389.definition: Non-striated, elongated, spindle-shaped cells found lining the digestive tract, uterus, and blood vessels. They are derived from specialized myoblasts (MYOBLASTS, SMOOTH MUSCLE).

D032390.name: Myoblasts, Smooth Muscle
D032390.definition: Precursor cells destined to differentiate into smooth muscle myocytes (MYOCYTES, SMOOTH MUSCLE).

D032401.name: Typhaceae
D032401.definition: A plant family of the order Typhales, subclass Commelinidae, class Liliopsida (monocotyledons) that contains a single genus, Typha, that grows worldwide.

D032402.name: Boehmeria
D032402.definition: A plant genus of the family URTICACEAE. Members contain cryptopleurine, beta-sitosterol, daucosterol and 19 alpha-hydroxyursolic acid.

D032403.name: Parietaria
D032403.definition: A plant genus of the family URTICACEAE which is the most common cause of pollinosis in Mediterranean countries. It is the source of 'allergen Par o I' and of Pollinex used for DESENSITIZATION, IMMUNOLOGIC.

D032404.name: Nardostachys
D032404.definition: A plant genus of the family VALERIANACEAE. Nardostachysin, nardostachin, nardosinone, valeranone, and patchoulene have been found in this genus. Nardostachys jatamansi is classified by some as Valeriana jatamansi.

D032405.name: Patrinia
D032405.definition: A plant genus of the family VALERIANACEAE. Members contain ursolic acid and oleanolic acid glycosides, sulfapatrinosides (triterpenoid glycosides), and patriscabrol (iridolactone).

D032406.name: Valerianella
D032406.definition: A plant genus of the family VALERIANACEAE. It is sometimes called goosefoot cornsalad but should not be confused with true goosefoot (CHENOPODIUM).

D032407.name: Avicennia
D032407.definition: A plant genus of the family Acanthaceae. Members contain NAPHTHOQUINONES. Black mangroves (common name for the genus) are distinguished from other mangroves by their spike-like aerial roots called pneumatophores that project from the soil or water surrounding the plants.

D032408.name: Callicarpa
D032408.definition: A plant genus of the family Lamiaceae. Members contain clerodane DITERPENES and callicarpone.

D032409.name: Clerodendrum
D032409.definition: A plant genus of the family Lamiaceae. Inerminosides (iridoid glycosides); colebroside A; STEROIDS; STEROLS; terpenoid glucosides; and abietane DITERPENES have been found in this genus.

D032410.name: Lantana
D032410.definition: A plant genus of the family VERBENACEAE. Members contain lantadene and other TRITERPENES.

D032411.name: Lippia
D032411.definition: A plant genus of the family VERBENACEAE. Lippsidoquinone; TRITERPENES; SESQUITERPENES; and THYMOL have been found in this genus. Plant extracts have cytotoxic activity. It is sometimes called Mexican oregano but that confuses it with real oregano (ORIGANUM).

D032412.name: Verbena
D032412.definition: A plant genus of the family VERBENACEAE. Members contain verbenachalcone (dimeric dihydrochalcone), iridoids, and phenylethanoids.

D032413.name: Viola
D032413.definition: A plant genus of the family VIOLACEAE. Some species in this genus are called bouncing bet which is a common name more often used with SAPONARIA OFFICINALIS. Members contain macrocyclic peptides.

D032421.name: Ampelopsis
D032421.definition: A plant genus of the family VITACEAE. Members contain momordin and SITOSTEROLS.

D032422.name: Cissus
D032422.definition: A plant genus of the family VITACEAE. Cissus rufescence gum is considered comparable to TRAGACANTH.

D032423.name: Winteraceae
D032423.definition: A plant family of the order Magnoliales, subclass Magnoliidae, class Magnoliopsida. The wood lacks water-conducting cells but has acrid sap. The leaves are gland-dotted, leathery, and smooth-margined. The flowers are small, in clusters, with two to six sepals, petals in two or more series, several stamens, and one to several carpels.

D032424.name: Drimys
D032424.definition: A plant genus of the family WINTERACEAE. They have leathery, elliptic-shaped leaves; red-tinged shoots; and jasmine-scented, cream-colored, 8- to 12-petaled, 2.5-centimeter (1-inch) flowers in clusters.

D032425.name: Pseudowintera
D032425.definition: A plant genus of the family WINTERACEAE. Members contain polygodial.

D032426.name: Marantaceae
D032426.definition: A plant family of the order ZINGIBERALES, subclass Zingiberidae, class Liliopsida.

D032427.name: Heliconiaceae
D032427.definition: A plant family of the order ZINGIBERALES, subclass Zingiberidae, class Liliopsida.

D032428.name: Strelitziaceae
D032428.definition: A plant family of the order ZINGIBERALES, subclass Zingiberidae, class Liliopsida. Some species in this genus are called bird-of-paradise which is also a common name for CAESALPINIA and Heliconia (HELICONIACEAE).

D032429.name: Alpinia
D032429.definition: A plant genus of the family ZINGIBERACEAE. Members contain galangin, yakuchinone-A, and diarylheptanoids.

D032430.name: Balanites
D032430.definition: A plant genus of the family ZYGOPHYLLACEAE. Feruloyltyramine, balanitoside (a furostanol glycoside), and cytostatic steroidal saponins have been found in this genus. B. aegyptiaca fruit water extract is traditionally used as an anthelmintic in the Sudan.

D032441.name: Guaiacum
D032441.definition: A plant genus of the family ZYGOPHYLLACEAE. GUAIAC is obtained from G. officinale or G. sanctum. Some species in this genus are called lignum vitae which is also a common name for other trees.

D032442.name: Larrea
D032442.definition: A plant genus of the family ZYGOPHYLLACEAE. It is sometimes called chaparral but that is a generic word which is used with a number of other plants. Members contain NORDIHYDROGUAIARETIC ACID.

D032443.name: Peganum
D032443.definition: A plant genus of the family ZYGOPHYLLACEAE. Harmala and other ALKALOIDS, phenylpropanoids, and TRITERPENES have been found in plants of this genus.

D032444.name: Tribulus
D032444.definition: A plant genus of the family ZYGOPHYLLACEAE. Members contain steroidal saponins. Ingestion by grazing animals causes PHOTOSENSITIVITY DISORDERS called geeldikkop (yellow thick head) in South Africa.

D032445.name: Zygophyllum
D032445.definition: A plant genus of the family ZYGOPHYLLACEAE. Members contain SAPONINS.

D032446.name: Myoblasts
D032446.definition: Embryonic (precursor) cells of the myogenic lineage that develop from the MESODERM. They undergo proliferation, migrate to their various sites, and then differentiate into the appropriate form of myocytes (MYOCYTES, SKELETAL; MYOCYTES, CARDIAC; MYOCYTES, SMOOTH MUSCLE).

D032447.name: Wisteria
D032447.definition: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE. Members contain wistarin, wisteria lectin and wistariasaponin.

D032448.name: Myoblasts, Skeletal
D032448.definition: Precursor cells destined to differentiate into skeletal myocytes (MYOCYTES, SKELETAL).

D032449.name: Canavalia
D032449.definition: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE. Canavalia ensiformis is the source of CONCANAVALIN A.

D032461.name: Chromosomes, Plant
D032461.definition: Complex nucleoprotein structures which contain the genomic DNA and are part of the CELL NUCLEUS of PLANTS.

D032462.name: Cycadophyta
D032462.definition: A division of GYMNOSPERMS which look like palm trees (ARECACEAE) but are more closely related to PINUS. They have large cones and large pinnate leaves and are sometimes called cycads, a term which may also refer more narrowly to cycadales or CYCAS.

D032481.name: Zamiaceae
D032481.definition: A plant family of the order Cycadales, class Cycadopsida, division CYCADOPHYTA.

D032482.name: Coniferophyta
D032482.definition: A plant division of GYMNOSPERMS consisting of cone-bearing trees and shrubs.

D032483.name: Cephalotaxus
D032483.definition: A plant genus of the family Cephalotaxaceae, order Pinales, class Pinopsida, division CONIFEROPHYTA. Members contain homoharringtonine.

D032484.name: Taxodiaceae
D032484.definition: The redwood plant family of the order Pinales, class Pinopsida, division CONIFEROPHYTA (Conifers).

D032485.name: Cryptomeria
D032485.definition: A plant genus of the family TAXODIACEAE. Its POLLEN is one of the major ALLERGENS.

D032486.name: Cunninghamia
D032486.definition: A plant genus of the family TAXODIACEAE. Members contain DITERPENES.

D032487.name: Sequoia
D032487.definition: A plant genus of the family TAXODIACEAE known for including some of the tallest trees.

D032488.name: Sequoiadendron
D032488.definition: A plant genus of the family TAXODIACEAE known for tall trees like the SEQUOIA redwoods.

D032489.name: Taxodium
D032489.definition: A plant genus of the family TAXODIACEAE. Members contain taxodione and taxodone, which are diterpenoid quinone methide tumor inhibitors.

D032490.name: Taxaceae
D032490.definition: A plant family of the order Taxales, class Pinopsida, division CONIFEROPHYTA.

D032491.name: Dryopteridaceae
D032491.definition: The wood fern plant family of the order Polypodiales, class Filicopsida, division Pteridophyta.

D032492.name: Dryopteris
D032492.definition: A plant genus of the family DRYOPTERIDACEAE. Members contain aspidin and filicic acid.

D032493.name: Polystichum
D032493.definition: A plant genus of the family DRYOPTERIDACEAE.

D032494.name: Polypodium
D032494.definition: A plant genus of the family POLYPODIACEAE. Members contain polypodoside.

D032495.name: Pteris
D032495.definition: A plant genus of the family PTERIDACEAE. Members contain entkaurane DITERPENES. The name is similar to bracken fern (PTERIDIUM).

D032496.name: Satellite Cells, Skeletal Muscle
D032496.definition: Elongated, spindle-shaped, quiescent myoblasts lying in close contact with adult skeletal muscle. They are thought to play a role in muscle repair and regeneration.

D032497.name: Dennstaedtiaceae
D032497.definition: The bracken fern plant family of the order Polypodiales, class Filicopsida, division Pteridophyta.

D032498.name: Pteridium
D032498.definition: A plant genus of the family DENNSTAEDTIACEAE. Members contain ptaquiloside, braxin A1, and braxin B. The name is similar to brake fern (PTERIS).

D032501.name: Huperzia
D032501.definition: A plant genus of the family LYCOPODIACEAE. Members contain huperzine, one of the CHOLINESTERASE INHIBITORS.

D032502.name: Lycopodium
D032502.definition: A plant genus of the family LYCOPODIACEAE. Members contain ALKALOIDS. Lycopodium oil is obtained from L. clavatum.

D032503.name: Selaginellaceae
D032503.definition: A plant family of the order Selaginellales, class Lycopodiopsida, division Lycopodiophyta, subkingdom Tracheobionta. Members contain bilobetin. The rarely used common name of resurrection plant is mainly used with CRATEROSTIGMA.

D032521.name: Immunity, Herd
D032521.definition: The non-susceptibility to infection of a large group of individuals in a population. A variety of factors can be responsible for herd immunity and this gives rise to the different definitions used in the literature. Most commonly, herd immunity refers to the case when, if most of the population is immune, infection of a single individual will not cause an epidemic. Also, in such immunized populations, susceptible individuals are not likely to become infected. Herd immunity can also refer to the case when unprotected individuals fail to contract a disease because the infecting organism has been banished from the population.

D032541.name: Mass Vaccination
D032541.definition: Administration of a vaccine to large populations in order to elicit IMMUNITY.

D032561.name: Cotton Fiber
D032561.definition: A TEXTILE fiber obtained from the pappus (outside the SEEDS) of cotton plant (GOSSYPIUM). Inhalation of cotton fiber dust over a prolonged period can result in BYSSINOSIS.

D032581.name: Tuberculosis Vaccines
D032581.definition: Vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent or treat TUBERCULOSIS.

D032601.name: Erysimum
D032601.definition: A plant genus of the family BRASSICACEAE. Some members contain CARDIAC GLYCOSIDES.

D032602.name: Caragana
D032602.definition: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE. Members contain STILBENES.

D032603.name: Scopolia
D032603.definition: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE after which the compound SCOPOLAMINE HYDROBROMIDE got its name.

D032604.name: Alangiaceae
D032604.definition: A plant family of the order Cornales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida, consisting of slow-growing evergreen trees common in tropical forests of south India and Burma. Members contain tetrahydroisoquinoline-monoterpene and iridoid glycosides.

D032621.name: DNA Shuffling
D032621.definition: The use of DNA recombination (RECOMBINATION, GENETIC) to prepare a large gene library of novel, chimeric genes from a population of randomly fragmented DNA from related gene sequences.

D032641.name: Eurotiales
D032641.definition: An order of fungi in the phylum ASCOMYCOTA characterized by the presence of well defined peridia and cleistothecial asci. Notable anamorphs (mitosporic forms) of Eurotiales include PENICILLIUM and ASPERGILLUS.

D032661.name: Cordyceps
D032661.definition: A genus of ascomycetous fungi (ASCOMYCOTA), family Clavicipitaceae, order HYPOCREALES, that grows by infecting insect larvae or mature insects with spores that germinate often before the cocoon is formed.

D032681.name: Spectral Karyotyping
D032681.definition: The simultaneous identification of all chromosomes from a cell by fluorescence in situ hybridization (IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION, FLUORESCENCE) with chromosome-specific florescent probes that are discerned by their different emission spectra.

D032701.name: Biomimetics
D032701.definition: An interdisciplinary field in materials science, ENGINEERING, and BIOLOGY, studying the use of biological principles for synthesis or fabrication of BIOMIMETIC MATERIALS.

D032721.name: Adult Children
D032721.definition: Children who have reached maturity or the legal age of majority.

D032722.name: Advance Care Planning
D032722.definition: Discussions with patients and/or their representatives about the goals and desired direction of the patient's care, particularly end-of-life care, in the event that the patient is or becomes incompetent to make decisions.

D032741.name: Monascus
D032741.definition: A genus in the family Monascaceae, order EUROTIALES. One species, Monascus purpureus, has multiple uses in traditional Chinese medicine (MEDICINE, CHINESE TRADITIONAL).

D032761.name: Animal Experimentation
D032761.definition: The use of animals as investigational subjects.

D032762.name: Autoexperimentation
D032762.definition: Intentionally using oneself as a research subject.

D032763.name: Behavior Control
D032763.definition: Manipulation of the behavior of persons or animals by biomedical, physical, psychological, or social means, including for nontherapeutic reasons.

D032764.name: Casuistry
D032764.definition: A method of ETHICAL ANALYSIS that emphasizes practical problem solving through examining individual cases that are considered to be representative; sometimes used to denote specious argument or rationalization. Differentiate from casuistics, which is the recording and study of cases and disease.

D032781.name: Codes of Ethics
D032781.definition: Systematic statements of principles or rules of appropriate professional conduct, usually established by professional societies.

D032801.name: Iridectomy
D032801.definition: Surgical removal of a section of the iris.

D032802.name: Committee Membership
D032802.definition: The composition of a committee; the state or status of being a member of a committee.

D032821.name: Commodification
D032821.definition: The social process by which something or someone comes to be regarded and treated as an article of trade or commerce.

D032841.name: Sinomenium
D032841.definition: A plant genus of the family MENISPERMACEAE. Members contain sinomenine, caffeine, 1,7-dimethylxanthine, and other ALKALOIDS.

D032842.name: Emericella
D032842.definition: A genus in the family Trichocomaceae, order EUROTIALES. The anamorph is ASPERGILLUS.

D032861.name: Buddleja
D032861.definition: A plant genus of the family SCROPHULARIACEAE. Members contain mimengoside B, verbascoside, and phenylethanoids.

D032862.name: Litsea
D032862.definition: A plant genus of the family LAURACEAE. Members contain laurotetanine and other APORPHINES.

D032882.name: Comprehension
D032882.definition: The act or fact of grasping the meaning, nature, or importance of; understanding. (American Heritage Dictionary, 4th ed) Includes understanding by a patient or research subject of information disclosed orally or in writing.

D032901.name: Talaromyces
D032901.definition: A fungal genus in the family Trichocomaceae, order EUROTIALES, characterized by loose hyphal fruiting bodies containing spherical asci. Anamorphs include PENICILLIUM and PAECILOMYCES.

D032902.name: Ganoderma
D032902.definition: A genus of fungi in the family Ganodermataceae, order POLYPORALES, containing a dimitic hyphal system. It causes a white rot, and is a wood decomposer. Ganoderma lucidum (REISHI) is used in traditional Chinese medicine (MEDICINE, CHINESE TRADITIONAL).

D032903.name: Confucianism
D032903.definition: A school of thought and set of moral, ethical, and political teachings usually considered to be founded by Confucius in 6th-5th century B.C. China. (from Cambridge Dictionary of Philosophy, 1995)

D032904.name: Cinnamomum aromaticum
D032904.definition: A plant species of the genus CINNAMOMUM that contains CINNAMATES and has been used in traditional Chinese medicine (DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL).

D032921.name: Consensus
D032921.definition: General agreement or collective opinion; the judgment arrived at by most of those concerned.

D032961.name: Sperm Midpiece
D032961.definition: The middle piece of the spermatozoon is a highly organized segment consisting of MITOCHONDRIA, the outer dense fibers and the core microtubular structure.

D032962.name: Consent Forms
D032962.definition: Documents describing a medical treatment or research project, including proposed procedures, risks, and alternatives, that are to be signed by an individual, or the individual's proxy, to indicate his/her understanding of the document and a willingness to undergo the treatment or to participate in the research.

D032981.name: Dehumanization
D032981.definition: The process by which a person or group of persons comes to be regarded or treated as lacking in human qualities.

D032982.name: Contracts
D032982.definition: Agreements between two or more parties, especially those that are written and enforceable by law (American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language, 4th ed). It is sometimes used to characterize the nature of the professional-patient relationship.

D032983.name: Setaria Plant
D032983.definition: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The small pointed seeds are grown for hay in North America and western Europe and important as food in China and other Asian countries.

D032984.name: Ethics, Research
D032984.definition: The moral obligations governing the conduct of research. Used for discussions of research ethics as a general topic.

D033001.name: Directed Tissue Donation
D033001.definition: Tissue, organ, or gamete donation intended for a designated recipient.

D033002.name: Duty to Recontact
D033002.definition: The ethical and/or legal obligation of a health provider or researcher to communicate with a former patient or research subject about advances in research relevant to a treatment or to a genetic or other diagnostic test provided earlier, or about proposed new uses of blood or tissue samples taken in the past for another purpose.

D033003.name: Eastern Orthodoxy
D033003.definition: The name given to the religion of the body of modern churches, including among others the Greek and Russian Orthodox, that is derived from the church of the Byzantine Empire, adheres to the Byzantine rite, and acknowledges the honorary primacy of the patriarch of Constantinople. (from American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language, 4th ed)

D033021.name: Oxytropis
D033021.definition: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE. Members contain SWAINSONINE.

D033022.name: Vicia sativa
D033022.definition: A plant species of the genus VICIA, family FABACEAE. The seed is used for food and contains THIOCYANATES such as prunasin, cyanoalanine, cyanogen, and vicine.

D033023.name: Foot Joints
D033023.definition: The articulations extending from the ANKLE distally to the TOES. These include the ANKLE JOINT; TARSAL JOINTS; METATARSOPHALANGEAL JOINT; and TOE JOINT.

D033041.name: Embryo Research
D033041.definition: Experimentation on, or using the organs or tissues from, a human or other mammalian conceptus during the prenatal stage of development that is characterized by rapid morphological changes and the differentiation of basic structures. In humans, this includes the period from the time of fertilization to the end of the eighth week after fertilization.

D033042.name: Fetal Research
D033042.definition: Experimentation on, or using the organs or tissues from, a human or other mammalian conceptus in the postembryonic period, after the major structures have been outlined. In humans, this corresponds to the period from the third month after fertilization until birth.

D033061.name: Ethics Consultation
D033061.definition: Services provided by an individual ethicist (ETHICISTS) or an ethics team or committee (ETHICS COMMITTEES, CLINICAL) to address the ethical issues involved in a specific clinical case. The central purpose is to improve the process and outcomes of patients' care by helping to identify, analyze, and resolve ethical problems.

D033062.name: Friends
D033062.definition: Persons whom one knows, likes, and trusts.

D033081.name: Shear Strength
D033081.definition: The internal resistance of a material to moving some parts of it parallel to a fixed plane, in contrast to stretching (TENSILE STRENGTH) or compression (COMPRESSIVE STRENGTH). Ionic crystals are brittle because, when subjected to shear, ions of the same charge are brought next to each other, which causes repulsion.

D033101.name: Euthanasia, Active, Voluntary
D033101.definition: Active euthanasia of a patient at the patient's request and/or with the patient's consent.

D033141.name: Genetic Determinism
D033141.definition: The theory that human CHARACTER and BEHAVIOR are shaped by the GENES that comprise the individual's GENOTYPE rather than by CULTURE; ENVIRONMENT; and individual choice.

D033142.name: Genetic Services
D033142.definition: Organized services to provide diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of genetic disorders.

D033161.name: Government Regulation
D033161.definition: Exercise of governmental authority to control conduct.

D033162.name: Incidental Findings
D033162.definition: Unanticipated information discovered in the course of testing or medical care. Used in discussions of information that may have social or psychological consequences, such as when it is learned that a child's biological father is someone other than the putative father, or that a person tested for one disease or disorder has, or is at risk for, something else.

D033181.name: Information Dissemination
D033181.definition: The circulation or wide dispersal of information.

D033182.name: Intention
D033182.definition: What a person has in mind to do or bring about.

D033183.name: Interdisciplinary Communication
D033183.definition: Communication, in the sense of cross-fertilization of ideas, involving two or more academic disciplines (such as the disciplines that comprise the cross-disciplinary field of bioethics, including the health and biological sciences, the humanities, and the social sciences and law). Also includes problems in communication stemming from differences in patterns of language usage in different academic or medical disciplines.

D033201.name: Euphausiacea
D033201.definition: An order of pelagic, shrimplike CRUSTACEA. Many consume ZOOPLANKTON and a few are predacious. Many antarctic species, such as Euphausia superba, constitute the chief food of other animals.

D033202.name: Anostraca
D033202.definition: An order of CRUSTACEA comprised of shrimp-like organisms containing body trunks with at least 20 segments. The are commonly used as aquarium food.

D033221.name: Jehovah's Witnesses
D033221.definition: Members of a religious denomination founded in the United States during the late 19th century in which active evangelism is practiced, the imminent approach of the millennium is preached, and war and organized government authority in matters of conscience are strongly opposed (from American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language, 4th ed). Jehovah's Witnesses generally refuse blood transfusions and other blood-based treatments based on religious belief.

D033222.name: Judicial Role
D033222.definition: The kind of action or activity proper to the judiciary, particularly its responsibility for decision making.

D033241.name: Lawyers
D033241.definition: Persons whose profession is to give legal advice and assistance to clients and represent them in legal matters. (American Heritage Dictionary, 3d ed)

D033242.name: Minors
D033242.definition: A person who has not attained the age at which full civil rights are accorded.

D033261.name: Maternal-Fetal Relations
D033261.definition: The bond or lack thereof between a pregnant woman and her FETUS.

D033262.name: Narration
D033262.definition: The act, process, or an instance of narrating, i.e., telling a story. In the context of MEDICINE or ETHICS, narration includes relating the particular and the personal in the life story of an individual.

D033281.name: Nontherapeutic Human Experimentation
D033281.definition: Human experimentation that is not intended to benefit the subjects on whom it is performed. Phase I drug studies (CLINICAL TRIALS, PHASE I AS TOPIC) and research involving healthy volunteers are examples of nontherapeutic human experimentation.

D033282.name: Parental Consent
D033282.definition: Informed consent given by a parent on behalf of a minor or otherwise incompetent child.

D033283.name: Patient Access to Records
D033283.definition: The freedom of patients to review their own medical, genetic, or other health-related records.

D033301.name: Deciduoma
D033301.definition: An intrauterine mass containing decidual cells (DECIDUA) or with structures resembling the PLACENTA. Deciduomas usually are induced experimentally.

D033302.name: Postmodernism
D033302.definition: A late 20th-century philosophical approach or style of cultural analysis that seeks to reveal the cultural or social construction of concepts conventionally assumed to be natural or universal. (from E.R. DuBose, The Illusion of Trust: Toward a Medical Theological Ethics in the Postmodern Age, Kluwer, 1995)

D033303.name: Protestantism
D033303.definition: The name given to all Christian denominations, sects, or groups rising out of the Reformation. Protestant churches generally agree that the principle of authority should be the Scriptures rather than the institutional church or the pope. (from W.L. Reese, Dictionary of Philosophy and Religion, 1999)

D033304.name: Amphipoda
D033304.definition: An order of mostly marine CRUSTACEA containing more than 5500 species in over 100 families. Like ISOPODA, the other large order in the superorder Peracarida, members are shrimp-like in appearance, have sessile compound eyes, and no carapace. But unlike Isopoda, they possess thoracic gills and their bodies are laterally compressed.

D033321.name: Isopoda
D033321.definition: One of the largest orders of mostly marine CRUSTACEA, containing over 10,000 species. Like AMPHIPODA, the other large order in the superorder Peracarida, members are shrimp-like in appearance, have sessile compound eyes, and no carapace. But unlike Amphipoda, they possess abdominal pleopods (modified as gills) and their bodies are dorsoventrally flattened.

D033341.name: Arguloida
D033341.definition: An order of CRUSTACEA that are parasitic on freshwater fish.

D033342.name: Copepoda
D033342.definition: A huge subclass of mostly marine CRUSTACEA, containing over 14,000 species. The 10 orders comprise both planktonic and benthic organisms, and include both free-living and parasitic forms. Planktonic copepods form the principle link between PHYTOPLANKTON and the higher trophic levels of the marine food chains.

D033361.name: Cladocera
D033361.definition: A suborder of CRUSTACEA, order Diplostraca, comprising the water fleas. They are benthic filter feeders that consume PHYTOPLANKTON. The body is laterally compressed and enclosed in a bivalved carapace, from which the head extends.

D033362.name: Powder Diffraction
D033362.definition: Method of using a polycrystalline powder and Rietveld refinement (LEAST SQUARES ANALYSIS) of X-RAY DIFFRACTION or NEUTRON DIFFRACTION. It circumvents the difficulties of producing single large crystals.

D033363.name: Neutron Diffraction
D033363.definition: The scattering of NEUTRONS by matter, especially crystals, with accompanying variation in intensity due to interference effects. It is useful in CRYSTALLOGRAPHY and POWDER DIFFRACTION.

D033364.name: Decapoda (Crustacea)
D033364.definition: The largest order of CRUSTACEA, comprising over 10,000 species. They are characterized by three pairs of thoracic appendages modified as maxillipeds, and five pairs of thoracic legs. The order includes the familiar shrimps, crayfish (ASTACOIDEA), true crabs (BRACHYURA), and lobsters (NEPHROPIDAE and PALINURIDAE), among others.

D033381.name: Anomura
D033381.definition: An infraorder of CRUSTACEA, in the order DECAPODA comprising the hermit crabs and characterized by a small fifth pair of legs.

D033401.name: Microscopy, Acoustic
D033401.definition: A scientific tool based on ULTRASONOGRAPHY and used not only for the observation of microstructure in metalwork but also in living tissue. In biomedical application, the acoustic propagation speed in normal and abnormal tissues can be quantified to distinguish their tissue elasticity and other properties.

D033421.name: Beginning of Human Life
D033421.definition: The point at which religious ensoulment or PERSONHOOD is considered to begin.

D033441.name: Andrology
D033441.definition: A scientific or medical discipline concerning the study of male reproductive biology, diseases of the male genital organs, and male infertility. Major areas of interest include ENDOCRINOLOGY; SPERMATOGENESIS; semen analysis; FERTILIZATION; CONTRACEPTION; and CRYOPRESERVATION.

D033461.name: Hyperuricemia
D033461.definition: Excessive URIC ACID or urate in blood as defined by its solubility in plasma at 37 degrees C; greater than 0.42mmol per liter (7.0mg/dL) in men or 0.36mmol per liter (6.0mg/dL) in women. This condition is caused by overproduction of uric acid or impaired renal clearance. Hyperuricemia can be acquired, drug-induced or genetically determined (LESCH-NYHAN SYNDROME). It is associated with HYPERTENSION and GOUT.

D033481.name: Chromosomes, Mammalian
D033481.definition: Complex nucleoprotein structures which contain the genomic DNA and are part of the CELL NUCLEUS of MAMMALS.

D033501.name: Crangonidae
D033501.definition: A family of shrimp in the class CRUSTACEA, order DECAPODA, containing a single genus, Crangon, with multiple species.

D033521.name: Palinuridae
D033521.definition: A family of marine CRUSTACEA, in the order DECAPODA, comprising the clawless lobsters. They are found in tropical and subtropical waters and characterized by short spines along the length of the tail and body.

D033541.name: Palaemonidae
D033541.definition: A family of CRUSTACEA, order DECAPODA, comprising the palaemonid shrimp. Genera include Macrobrachium, Palaemon, and Palaemonetes. Palaemonidae osmoregulate by means of gills.

D033542.name: Pandalidae
D033542.definition: A family of CRUSTACEA, order DECAPODA, comprising the pandalid shrimp. They are protandric hermaphrodites and can breed in both male and female stages. Many species are commercially harvested in the Pacific Northwest.

D033561.name: Penaeidae
D033561.definition: A family of CRUSTACEA, order DECAPODA, comprising the penaeid shrimp. Species of the genus Penaeus are the most important commercial shrimp throughout the world.

D033581.name: Stem Cell Transplantation
D033581.definition: The transfer of STEM CELLS from one individual to another within the same species (TRANSPLANTATION, HOMOLOGOUS) or between species (XENOTRANSPLANTATION), or transfer within the same individual (TRANSPLANTATION, AUTOLOGOUS). The source and location of the stem cells determines their potency or pluripotency to differentiate into various cell types.

D033601.name: Gordonia Bacterium
D033601.definition: A genus of gram-positive BACTERIA in the family Gordoniaceae, isolated from soil and from sputa of patients with chest disorders. It is also used for biotransformation of natural products.

D033621.name: Tephritidae
D033621.definition: A large family of fruit flies in the order DIPTERA, comprising over 4,500 species in about 100 genera. They have patterned wings and brightly colored bodies and are found predominantly in the tropical latitudes.

D033622.name: Ceratitis capitata
D033622.definition: A species of fruit fly originating in sub-Saharan Africa but widely distributed worldwide. One of the most destructive fruit pests, its larvae feed and develop on many different fruits and some vegetables.

D033641.name: Millettia
D033641.definition: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE. Members contain ISOFLAVONES, some of which show molluscicidal and schistosomicidal activity. Some species of Pongamia have been reclassified to this genus and some to DERRIS.

D033661.name: Oocysts
D033661.definition: Zygote-containing cysts of sporozoan protozoa. Further development in an oocyst produces small individual infective organisms called SPOROZOITES. Then, depending on the genus, the entire oocyst is called a sporocyst or the oocyst contains multiple sporocysts encapsulating the sporozoites.

D033681.name: Mitochondrial Membrane Transport Proteins
D033681.definition: Proteins involved in the transport of specific substances across the membranes of the MITOCHONDRIA.

D033701.name: Nucleobase, Nucleoside, Nucleotide, and Nucleic Acid Transport Proteins
D033701.definition: A broad class of proteins involved in the transport of nucleobases, NUCLEOSIDES; NUCLEOTIDES; and NUCLEIC ACIDS; across membranes.

D033702.name: Nucleobase Transport Proteins
D033702.definition: Proteins involved in the transport of nucleobases such as PYRIMIDINES and PURINES across membranes.

D033703.name: Nucleoside Transport Proteins
D033703.definition: Proteins involved in the transport of NUCLEOSIDES across cellular membranes.

D033704.name: Nucleotide Transport Proteins
D033704.definition: Proteins involved in the transport of NUCLEOTIDES across cellular membranes.

D033705.name: Equilibrative Nucleoside Transport Proteins
D033705.definition: A class of sodium-independent nucleoside transporters that mediate the facilitative transport of NUCLEOSIDES.

D033721.name: Equilibrative Nucleoside Transporter 1
D033721.definition: A subtype of equilibrative nucleoside transporter proteins that is sensitive to inhibition by 4-nitrobenzylthioinosine.

D033722.name: Equilibrative-Nucleoside Transporter 2
D033722.definition: A subtype of equilibrative nucleoside transporter proteins that is insensitive to inhibition by 4-nitrobenzylthioinosine.

D033741.name: Adenine Nucleotide Translocator 1
D033741.definition: A subtype of mitochondrial ADP, ATP translocase found primarily in heart muscle (MYOCARDIUM) and skeletal muscle (MUSCLE, SKELETAL).

D033742.name: Adenine Nucleotide Translocator 2
D033742.definition: A subtype of mitochondrial ADP, ATP translocase found primarily in FIBROBLASTS.

D033761.name: Spores, Protozoan
D033761.definition: A vegetative stage in the life cycle of sporozoan protozoa. It is characteristic of members of the phyla APICOMPLEXA and MICROSPORIDIA.

D033781.name: Adenine Nucleotide Translocator 3
D033781.definition: A subtype of mitochondrial ADP, ATP translocase found primarily in the LIVER.

D033862.name: Iron-Binding Proteins
D033862.definition: Proteins that specifically bind to IRON.

D033863.name: Transferrin-Binding Proteins
D033863.definition: A class of carrier proteins that bind to TRANSFERRIN. Many strains of pathogenic bacteria utilize transferrin-binding proteins to acquire their supply of iron from serum.

D033881.name: Transferrin-Binding Protein A
D033881.definition: A subtype of bacterial transferrin-binding protein found in bacteria. It forms a cell surface receptor complex with TRANSFERRIN-BINDING PROTEIN B.

D033882.name: Transferrin-Binding Protein B
D033882.definition: A subtype of bacterial transferrin-binding protein found in bacteria. It forms a cell surface receptor complex with TRANSFERRIN-BINDING PROTEIN A.

D033901.name: Bacterial Transferrin Receptor Complex
D033901.definition: A complex of proteins that forms a receptor for TRANSFERRIN in BACTERIA. Many pathogenic bacteria utilize the transferrin-binding complex to acquire their supply of iron from serum.

D033902.name: Periplasmic Binding Proteins
D033902.definition: Periplasmic proteins that scavenge or sense diverse nutrients. In the bacterial environment they usually couple to transporters or chemotaxis receptors on the inner bacterial membrane.

D033903.name: Periplasmic Proteins
D033903.definition: Proteins found in the PERIPLASM of organisms with cell walls.

D033921.name: Vesicular Transport Proteins
D033921.definition: A broad category of proteins involved in the formation, transport and dissolution of TRANSPORT VESICLES. They play a role in the intracellular transport of molecules contained within membrane vesicles. Vesicular transport proteins are distinguished from MEMBRANE TRANSPORT PROTEINS, which move molecules across membranes, by the mode in which the molecules are transported.

D033922.name: Clathrin Heavy Chains
D033922.definition: The heavy chain subunits of clathrin.

D033941.name: Clathrin Light Chains
D033941.definition: The light chain subunits of clathrin.

D033942.name: Adaptor Proteins, Vesicular Transport
D033942.definition: A class of proteins involved in the transport of molecules via TRANSPORT VESICLES. They perform functions such as binding to the cell membrane, capturing cargo molecules and promoting the assembly of CLATHRIN. The majority of adaptor proteins exist as multi-subunit complexes, however monomeric varieties have also been found.

D033961.name: Adaptor Protein Complex 1
D033961.definition: A clathrin adaptor protein complex primarily involved in clathrin-related transport at the TRANS-GOLGI NETWORK.

D033962.name: Adaptor Protein Complex 2
D033962.definition: An adaptor protein complex primarily involved in the formation of clathrin-related endocytotic vesicles (ENDOSOMES) at the CELL MEMBRANE.

D033963.name: Adaptor Protein Complex 3
D033963.definition: An adaptor protein complex found primarily on perinuclear compartments.

D033964.name: Adaptor Protein Complex 4
D033964.definition: An adaptor protein complex involved in transport of molecules between the TRANS-GOLGI NETWORK and the endosomal-lysosomal system.

D033965.name: Adaptor Protein Complex alpha Subunits
D033965.definition: A family of large adaptin protein subunits of approximately 100 kDa in size. They have been primarily found as components of ADAPTOR PROTEIN COMPLEX 2.

D033966.name: Adaptor Protein Complex beta Subunits
D033966.definition: A family of large adaptin protein complex subunits of approximately 90-130 kDa in size.

D033981.name: Adaptor Protein Complex delta Subunits
D033981.definition: A family of large adaptin protein subunits of approximately 130-kDa in size. They have been primarily found as components of ADAPTOR PROTEIN COMPLEX 3.

D033982.name: Adaptor Protein Complex gamma Subunits
D033982.definition: A family of large adaptin protein subunits of approximately 90 KDa in size. They have been primarily found as components of ADAPTOR PROTEIN COMPLEX 1.

D033983.name: Adaptor Protein Complex mu Subunits
D033983.definition: A family of medium adaptin protein subunits of approximately 45 KDa in size. They have been primarily found as components of ADAPTOR PROTEIN COMPLEX 3 and ADAPTOR PROTEIN COMPLEX 4.

D034001.name: Adaptor Protein Complex Subunits
D034001.definition: The subunits that make up the large, medium and small chains of adaptor proteins.

D034002.name: Adaptor Protein Complex sigma Subunits
D034002.definition: A family of small adaptin protein complex subunits of approximately 19 KDa in size.

D034021.name: Auxilins
D034021.definition: A family of proteins that play a role as cofactors in the process of CLATHRIN recycling in cells.

D034041.name: Monomeric Clathrin Assembly Proteins
D034041.definition: A subclass of clathrin assembly proteins that occur as monomers.

D034061.name: Thrombopoiesis
D034061.definition: The process of generating thrombocytes (BLOOD PLATELETS) from the pluripotent HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS in the BONE MARROW via the MEGAKARYOCYTES. The humoral factor with thrombopoiesis-stimulating activity is designated THROMBOPOIETIN.

D034062.name: Insomnia, Fatal Familial
D034062.definition: An autosomal dominant disorder characterized by degeneration of the THALAMUS and progressive insomnia. It is caused by a mutation in the prion protein (PRIONS).

D034081.name: Wasting Disease, Chronic
D034081.definition: A transmissible spongiform encephalopathy (prion disease) of DEER and elk characterized by chronic weight loss leading to death. It is thought to spread by direct contact between animals or through environmental contamination with the prion protein (PRIONS).

D034101.name: Sporozoites
D034101.definition: The product of meiotic division of zygotes in parasitic protozoa comprising haploid cells. These infective cells invade the host and undergo asexual reproduction producing MEROZOITES (or other forms) and ultimately gametocytes.

D034121.name: Reproductive Health Services
D034121.definition: Health care services related to human REPRODUCTION and diseases of the reproductive system. Services are provided to both sexes and usually by physicians in the medical or the surgical specialties such as REPRODUCTIVE MEDICINE; ANDROLOGY; GYNECOLOGY; OBSTETRICS; and PERINATOLOGY.

D034141.name: Hypoalbuminemia
D034141.definition: A condition in which albumin level in blood (SERUM ALBUMIN) is below the normal range. Hypoalbuminemia may be due to decreased hepatic albumin synthesis, increased albumin catabolism, altered albumin distribution, or albumin loss through the urine (ALBUMINURIA).

D034161.name: Pelvic Infection
D034161.definition: Infection involving the tissues or organs in the PELVIS.

D034181.name: Epimedium
D034181.definition: A plant genus of the family BERBERIDACEAE which is used in DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL. Members contain flavonol glycosides including epimedins, icariin and noricariin.

D034182.name: Cuscuta
D034182.definition: A plant genus of the family Cuscutaceae. It is a threadlike climbing parasitic plant that is used in DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL.

D034201.name: Computers, Handheld
D034201.definition: A type of MICROCOMPUTER, sometimes called a personal digital assistant, that is very small and portable and fitting in a hand. They are convenient to use in clinical and other field situations for quick data management. They usually require docking with MICROCOMPUTERS for updates.

D034221.name: Moritella
D034221.definition: A genus of gram-negative, curved or straight rod-shaped bacteria, in the family ALTEROMONADACEAE. They are chemo-organotrophic, halophilic, and associated with cold marine habitats.

D034241.name: Alteromonadaceae
D034241.definition: A family of marine, gram-negative PROTEOBACTERIA including the genera ALTEROMONAS; Colwellia; Idiomarina; MARINOBACTER; MORITELLA; PSEUDOALTEROMONAS; and SHEWANELLA.

D034242.name: Cyclooctanes
D034242.definition: A group of compounds with an 8-carbon ring. They may be saturated or unsaturated.

D034261.name: Epothilones
D034261.definition: A group of 16-member MACROLIDES which stabilize MICROTUBULES in a manner similar to PACLITAXEL. They were originally found in the myxobacterium Sorangium cellulosum, now renamed to Polyangium (MYXOCOCCALES).

D034281.name: Dynamins
D034281.definition: A family of high molecular weight GTP phosphohydrolases that play a direct role in vesicle transport. They associate with microtubule bundles (MICROTUBULES) and are believed to produce mechanical force via a process linked to GTP hydrolysis. This enzyme was formerly listed as EC 3.6.1.50.

D034284.name: Dynamin I
D034284.definition: A subtype of dynamin found primarily in the NEURONS of the brain.

D034285.name: Dynamin II
D034285.definition: A subtype of dynamin found ubiquitously expressed in a variety of tissues.

D034286.name: Dynamin III
D034286.definition: A subtype of dynamin found expressed exclusively in the testis, lung and brain.

D034301.name: Deinococcus
D034301.definition: A genus of gram-positive aerobic cocci found in the soil, that is highly resistant to radiation, especially ionizing radiation (RADIATION, IONIZING). Deinococcus radiodurans is the type species.

D034321.name: Hyperamylasemia
D034321.definition: A condition with abnormally elevated level of AMYLASES in the serum. Hyperamylasemia due to PANCREATITIS or other causes may be differentiated by identifying the amylase isoenzymes.

D034341.name: Aristolochic Acids
D034341.definition: Nitro-phenanthrenes occurring in ARISTOLOCHIACEAE and other plants. They derive from stephanine (APORPHINES) by oxidative ring cleavage. The nitro group is a reactive alkylator (ALKYLATING AGENTS) that binds to biological macromolecules. Ingestion by humans is associated with nephropathy (NEPHRITIS). There is no relationship to the similar named aristolochene (SESQUITERPENES).

D034361.name: Streptococcus mitis
D034361.definition: A species of gram-positive, coccoid bacteria commensal in the respiratory tract.

D034362.name: Striga
D034362.definition: A plant genus of the family Orobanchaceae that is parasitic on the roots of other plants. Members contain the flavones, APIGENIN and LUTEOLIN.

D034363.name: Viridans Streptococci
D034363.definition: A large heterogeneous group of mostly alpha-hemolytic streptococci. They colonize the respiratory tract at birth and generally have a low degree of pathogenicity. This group of species includes STREPTOCOCCUS MITIS; STREPTOCOCCUS MUTANS; STREPTOCOCCUS ORALIS; STREPTOCOCCUS SANGUIS; STREPTOCOCCUS SOBRINUS; and the STREPTOCOCCUS MILLERI GROUP. The latter are often beta-hemolytic and commonly produce invasive pyogenic infections including brain and abdominal abscesses.

D034364.name: Streptococcus milleri Group
D034364.definition: A subset of VIRIDANS STREPTOCOCCI, but the species in this group differ in their hemolytic pattern and diseases caused. These species are often beta-hemolytic and produce pyogenic infections.

D034365.name: Streptococcus constellatus
D034365.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the STREPTOCOCCUS MILLERI GROUP. It is commonly found in the oropharnyx flora and has a proclivity for abscess formation in the upper body and respiratory tract.

D034366.name: Streptococcus anginosus
D034366.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the STREPTOCOCCUS MILLERI GROUP. It is the most frequently seen isolate of that group, has a proclivity for abscess formation, and is most often isolated from the blood, gastrointestinal, and urogenital tract.

D034367.name: Streptococcus intermedius
D034367.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the STREPTOCOCCUS MILLERI GROUP. It is commonly found in the oropharynx flora and has a proclivity for abscess formation, most characteristically in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM and LIVER.

D034381.name: Hearing Loss
D034381.definition: A general term for the complete or partial loss of the ability to hear from one or both ears.

D034401.name: Ulmaceae
D034401.definition: A plant family of the order Urticales, subclass Hamamelidae, class Magnoliopsida. Members are trees and shrubs of temperate regions that have watery sap and alternate leaves which are lopsided at the base. The flowers lack petals.

D034402.name: Trema
D034402.definition: A plant genus of the family ULMACEAE. Members contain PHENANTHRENES and COUMARINS.

D034403.name: Ulmus
D034403.definition: A plant genus of the family ULMACEAE that is susceptible to Dutch elm disease which is caused by the ASCOMYCOTA fungus, Ophiostoma.

D034421.name: Sus scrofa
D034421.definition: A species of SWINE, in the family Suidae, comprising a number of subspecies including the domestic pig Sus scrofa domestica.

D034441.name: Heterogeneous-Nuclear Ribonucleoproteins
D034441.definition: A family of ribonucleoproteins that were originally found as proteins bound to nascent RNA transcripts in the form of ribonucleoprotein particles. Although considered ribonucleoproteins they are primarily classified by their protein component. They are involved in a variety of processes such as packaging of RNA and RNA TRANSPORT within the nucleus. A subset of heterogeneous-nuclear ribonucleoproteins are involved in additional functions such as nucleocytoplasmic transport (ACTIVE TRANSPORT, CELL NUCLEUS) of RNA and mRNA stability in the CYTOPLASM.

D034442.name: N-substituted Glycines
D034442.definition: AMINO ACIDS composed of GLYCINE substituted at the nitrogen rather than the usual carbon position, resulting in the loss of HYDROGEN BONDING donors. Polymers of these compounds are called PEPTOIDS.

D034443.name: RNA Transport
D034443.definition: The process of moving specific RNA molecules from one cellular compartment or region to another by various sorting and transport mechanisms.

D034444.name: Peptoids
D034444.definition: Polymers of N-SUBSTITUTED GLYCINES containing chiral centers at the a-position of their side chains. These oligomers lack HYDROGEN BONDING donors, preventing formation of the usual intrachain hydrogen bonds but can form helices driven by the steric influence of chiral side chains.

D034445.name: Ovulation Inhibition
