D046409.definition: A genus in the family PSITTACIDAE containing three species of PARAKEETS: the Derbyan, the Alexandrine, and the rose-ringed.

D046410.name: Cockatoos
D046410.definition: Large crested BIRDS in the family Cacatuidae, found in Australia, New Guinea, and islands adjacent to the Philippines. The cockatiel (species Nymphicus hollandicus) is much smaller.

D046428.name: Hawks
D046428.definition: Common name for many members of the FALCONIFORMES order, family Accipitridae, generally smaller than EAGLES, and containing short, rounded wings and a long tail.

D046429.name: Spheniscidae
D046429.definition: The sole family in the order Sphenisciformes, comprised of 17 species of penguins in six genera. They are flightless seabirds of the Southern Hemisphere, highly adapted for marine life.

D046448.name: Ice Cover
D046448.definition: A thick mass of ICE formed over large regions of land; RIVERS; LAKES; ponds; or SEAWATER.

D046449.name: Hernia, Abdominal
D046449.definition: A protrusion of abdominal structures through the retaining ABDOMINAL WALL. It involves two parts: an opening in the abdominal wall, and a hernia sac consisting of PERITONEUM and abdominal contents. Abdominal hernias include groin hernia (HERNIA, FEMORAL; HERNIA, INGUINAL) and VENTRAL HERNIA.

D046468.name: Sexual Development
D046468.definition: The processes of anatomical and physiological changes related to sexual or reproductive functions during the life span of a human or an animal, from FERTILIZATION to DEATH. These include SEX DETERMINATION PROCESSES; SEX DIFFERENTIATION; SEXUAL MATURATION; and changes during AGING.

D046508.name: Culture Techniques
D046508.definition: Methods of maintaining or growing biological materials in controlled laboratory conditions. These include the cultures of CELLS; TISSUES; organs; or embryo in vitro. Both animal and plant tissues may be cultured by a variety of methods. Cultures may derive from normal or abnormal tissues, and consist of a single cell type or mixed cell types.

D046509.name: Tissue Culture Techniques
D046509.definition: A technique for maintaining or growing TISSUE in vitro, usually by DIFFUSION, perifusion, or PERFUSION. The tissue is cultured directly after removal from the host without being dispersed for cell culture.

D046528.name: Chimerism
D046528.definition: The occurrence in an individual of two or more cell populations of different chromosomal constitutions, derived from different individuals. This contrasts with MOSAICISM in which the different cell populations are derived from a single individual.

D046529.name: Microscopy, Electron, Transmission
D046529.definition: Electron microscopy in which the ELECTRONS or their reaction products that pass down through the specimen are imaged below the plane of the specimen.

D046548.name: Pubic Symphysis Diastasis
D046548.definition: Separation of the PUBIC SYMPHYSIS. It is an uncommon complication of CHILDBIRTH causing postpartum PAIN, but it can also arise from other causes.

D046549.name: Plantibodies
D046549.definition: Recombinant antibodies produced in TRANSGENIC PLANTS. The plants serve as BIOREACTORS to produce the antibodies for medical use or industrial processes.

D046568.name: Neuroepithelial Bodies
D046568.definition: Innervated clusters of NEUROEPITHELIAL CELLS found in the LUNGS. They act as airway OXYGEN sensors, releasing regulatory PEPTIDES and SEROTONIN in response to HYPOXIA.

D046569.name: Neuroepithelial Cells
D046569.definition: Cells of epithelial origin possessing specialized sensory functions. They include cells that are found in the TASTE BUDS; OLFACTORY MUCOSA; COCHLEA; and NEUROEPITHELIAL BODIES.

D046588.name: Nanoarchaeota
D046588.definition: A kingdom of hyperthermophilic ARCHAEA found in diverse environments.

D046589.name: CADASIL
D046589.definition: A familial, cerebral arteriopathy mapped to chromosome 19q12, and characterized by the presence of granular deposits in small CEREBRAL ARTERIES producing ischemic STROKE; PSEUDOBULBAR PALSY; and multiple subcortical infarcts (CEREBRAL INFARCTION). CADASIL is an acronym for Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy. CADASIL differs from BINSWANGER DISEASE by the presence of MIGRAINE WITH AURA and usually by the lack of history of arterial HYPERTENSION. (From Bradley et al, Neurology in Clinical Practice, 2000, p1146)

D046590.name: Spectroscopy, Electron Energy-Loss
D046590.definition: A technique for analysis of the chemical composition of molecules. A substance is bombarded with monochromatic ELECTRONS. Some of the electrons passing through the specimen will lose energy when they ionize inner shell electrons of the atoms in the specimen. The energy loss is element dependent. Analysis of the energy loss spectrum reveals the elemental composition of a specimen. ENERGY-FILTERED TRANSMISSION ELECTRON MICROSCOPY is a type of electron energy loss spectroscopy carried out in electron microscopes specially outfitted to analyze the spectrum of electron energy loss.

D046608.name: Synkinesis
D046608.definition: An involuntary movement accompanying a volitional movement. It often refers to facial movements that accompany FACIAL PARALYSIS.

D046609.name: Libraries, Digital
D046609.definition: Libraries in which a major proportion of the resources are available in machine-readable format, rather than on paper or MICROFORM.

D046628.name: Sphincter of Oddi Dysfunction
D046628.definition: Organic or functional motility disorder involving the SPHINCTER OF ODDI and associated with biliary COLIC. Pathological changes are most often seen in the COMMON BILE DUCT sphincter, and less commonly the PANCREATIC DUCT sphincter.

D046648.name: Hematoma, Subdural, Intracranial
D046648.definition: Accumulation of blood in the SUBDURAL SPACE over the CEREBRAL HEMISPHERE.

D046649.name: Hematoma, Subdural, Spinal
D046649.definition: Subdural hematoma of the SPINAL CANAL.

D046650.name: Medical Subject Headings
D046650.definition: Controlled vocabulary thesaurus produced by the NATIONAL LIBRARY OF MEDICINE. It consists of sets of terms naming descriptors in a hierarchical structure that permits searching at various levels of specificity.

D046688.name: Child Mortality
D046688.definition: Number of deaths of children between one year of age to 12 years of age in a given population.

D046689.name: Fetal Mortality
D046689.definition: Number of fetal deaths with stated or presumed gestation of 20 weeks or more in a given population. Late fetal mortality is death after of 28 weeks or more.

D046690.name: Deep Brain Stimulation
D046690.definition: Therapy for MOVEMENT DISORDERS, especially PARKINSON DISEASE, that applies electricity via stereotactic implantation of ELECTRODES in specific areas of the BRAIN such as the THALAMUS. The electrodes are attached to a neurostimulator placed subcutaneously.

D046708.name: Amazona
D046708.definition: One of the largest genera of PARROTS, ranging from South American to Northern Mexico. Many species are commonly kept as house pets.

D046709.name: Pattern Recognition, Physiological
D046709.definition: The analysis of a critical number of sensory stimuli or facts (the pattern) by physiological processes such as vision (PATTERN RECOGNITION, VISUAL), touch, or hearing.

D046710.name: Agapornis
D046710.definition: A genus comprised of nine species of small PARROTS from Africa. They are noted for showing affection for their mates.

D046728.name: Colitis, Microscopic
D046728.definition: A condition characterized by chronic watery DIARRHEA of unknown origin, a normal COLONOSCOPY but abnormal histopathology on BIOPSY. This syndrome was first described in 1980 by Read and associates. Subtypes include COLLAGENOUS COLITIS and LYMPHOCYTIC COLITIS. Both have similar clinical symptoms and are distinguishable only by histology.

D046729.name: Colitis, Collagenous
D046729.definition: A subtype of MICROSCOPIC COLITIS, characterized by chronic watery DIARRHEA of unknown origin, a normal COLONOSCOPY but abnormal histopathology on BIOPSY. Microscopic examination of biopsy samples taken from the COLON show larger-than-normal band of subepithelial COLLAGEN.

D046730.name: Colitis, Lymphocytic
D046730.definition: A subtype of MICROSCOPIC COLITIS, characterized by chronic watery DIARRHEA of unknown origin, a normal COLONOSCOPY but abnormal histopathology on BIOPSY. Microscopic examination of biopsy samples taken from the COLON show infiltration of LYMPHOCYTES in the superficial EPITHELIUM and the underlying connective tissue (lamina propria).

D046748.name: Hematoma, Epidural, Spinal
D046748.definition: A rare epidural hematoma in the spinal epidural space, usually due to a vascular malformation (CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM VASCULAR MALFORMATIONS) or TRAUMA. Spontaneous spinal epidural hematoma is a neurologic emergency due to a rapidly evolving compressive MYELOPATHY.

D046749.name: Starlings
D046749.definition: The family Sturnidae, in the order PASSERIFORMES. The starling family also includes mynahs and oxpeckers.

D046768.name: Nesidioblastosis
D046768.definition: An inherited autosomal recessive syndrome characterized by the disorganized formation of new islets in the PANCREAS and CONGENITAL HYPERINSULINISM. It is due to focal hyperplasia of pancreatic ISLET CELLS budding off from the ductal structures and forming new islets of Langerhans. Mutations in the islet cells involve the potassium channel gene KCNJ11 or the ATP-binding cassette transporter gene ABCC8, both on CHROMOSOME 11.

D046788.name: Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome
D046788.definition: A syndrome characterized by retropatellar or peripatellar PAIN resulting from physical and biochemical changes in the patellofemoral joint. The pain is most prominent when ascending or descending stairs, squatting, or sitting with flexed knees. There is a lack of consensus on the etiology and treatment. The syndrome is often confused with (or accompanied by) CHONDROMALACIA PATELLAE, the latter describing a pathological condition of the CARTILAGE and not a syndrome.

D046789.name: Chondromalacia Patellae
D046789.definition: A degeneration of the ARTICULAR CARTILAGE of the PATELLA, caused by a decrease in sulfated MUCOPOLYSACCHARIDES in the ground substance. When accompanied by pain, it is sometimes considered part of or confused with PATELLOFEMORAL PAIN SYNDROME.

D046790.name: Pancreas, Exocrine
D046790.definition: The major component (about 80%) of the PANCREAS composed of acinar functional units of tubular and spherical cells. The acinar cells synthesize and secrete several digestive enzymes such as TRYPSINOGEN; LIPASE; AMYLASE; and RIBONUCLEASE. Secretion from the exocrine pancreas drains into the pancreatic ductal system and empties into the DUODENUM.

D046808.name: Atadenovirus
D046808.definition: A genus of ADENOVIRIDAE that comprises viruses of several species of MAMMALS and BIRDS. The type species is Ovine adenovirus D.

D046809.name: Siadenovirus
D046809.definition: A genus of ADENOVIRIDAE comprising species including viruses of frogs (FROGS AND TOADS) and TURKEYS. The type species is Frog adenovirus.

D046810.name: Gyrovirus
D046810.definition: A genus in the family CIRCOVIRIDAE comprising the single species CHICKEN ANEMIA VIRUS.

D046828.name: Roniviridae
D046828.definition: A family of rod-shaped viruses, in the order NIDOVIRALES. It includes one genus: Okavirus.

D046829.name: Isavirus
D046829.definition: A genus in the family ORTHOMYXOVIRIDAE containing one species: Infectious salmon anemia virus.

D046830.name: Tymoviridae
D046830.definition: A family of icosahedral, non-enveloped, RNA plant viruses comprised of three genera: TYMOVIRUS, Marafivirus and Maculavirus.

D046848.name: White spot syndrome virus 1
D046848.definition: A species of DNA virus, in the genus WHISPOVIRUS, infecting PENAEID SHRIMP.

D046849.name: Nimaviridae
D046849.definition: A family of DNA invertebrate viruses with one genus: Whispovirus.

D046868.name: Anabaena cylindrica
D046868.definition: A species in the genus ANABAENA whose trichomes are composed of cylindrical cells.

D046869.name: Anabaena flos-aquae
D046869.definition: A species in the genus ANABAENA containing gas vacuoles that gives buoyancy to the organism. It can form extensive blooms in FRESH WATER and is responsible for acute poisonings of various animals.

D046870.name: Anabaena variabilis
D046870.definition: A species of ANABAENA that can form SPORES called akinetes.

D046888.name: Tissue Array Analysis
D046888.definition: The simultaneous analysis of multiple samples of TISSUES or CELLS from BIOPSY or in vitro culture that have been arranged in an array format on slides or microchips.

D046889.name: Cyanothece
D046889.definition: A form-genus of unicellular coccoid to rod-shaped CYANOBACTERIA, in the order Chroococcales. Three different clusters of strains from diverse habitats are included.

D046890.name: Aphanizomenon
D046890.definition: A form-genus of planktonic CYANOBACTERIA in the order Nostocales.

D046891.name: Cylindrospermopsis
D046891.definition: A form-genus of CYANOBACTERIA in the order Nostocales, characterized by thin trichomes, cylindrical akinetes, and terminal heterocysts.

D046908.name: Peptide Biosynthesis, Nucleic Acid-Independent
D046908.definition: The enzymatic synthesis of PEPTIDES without an RNA template by processes that do not use the ribosomal apparatus (RIBOSOMES).

D046910.name: Fertile Period
D046910.definition: The period in the MENSTRUAL CYCLE that is optimal for FERTILIZATION of the OVUM and yielding PREGNANCY. The duration of fertile period depends on the life span of male GAMETES within the female reproductive tract and the time of OVULATION. It usually begins a few days before ovulation and ends on the day of ovulation.

D046911.name: Macromolecular Substances
D046911.definition: Compounds and molecular complexes that consist of very large numbers of atoms and are generally over 500 kDa in size. In biological systems macromolecular substances usually can be visualized using ELECTRON MICROSCOPY and are distinguished from ORGANELLES by the lack of a membrane structure.

D046912.name: Multiprotein Complexes
D046912.definition: Macromolecular complexes formed from the association of defined protein subunits.

D046913.name: Medicago truncatula
D046913.definition: A plant species of the family FABACEAE used to study GENETICS because it is DIPLOID, self fertile, has a small genome, and short generation time.

D046914.name: Dipteryx
D046914.definition: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE. Members contain COUMARINS.

D046915.name: Penicillin-Binding Proteins
D046915.definition: Bacterial proteins that share the property of binding irreversibly to PENICILLINS and other ANTIBACTERIAL AGENTS derived from LACTAMS. The penicillin-binding proteins are primarily enzymes involved in CELL WALL biosynthesis including MURAMOYLPENTAPEPTIDE CARBOXYPEPTIDASE; PEPTIDE SYNTHASES; TRANSPEPTIDASES; and HEXOSYLTRANSFERASES.

D046928.name: Peptidoglycan Glycosyltransferase
D046928.definition: A hexosyltransferase involved in the transfer of disaccharide molecules to the peptidoglycan structure of the CELL WALL SKELETON. It plays an important role in the genesis of the bacterial CELL WALL.

D046929.name: Serine-Type D-Ala-D-Ala Carboxypeptidase
D046929.definition: A carboxypeptidase that is specific for proteins that contain two ALANINE residues on their C-terminal. Enzymes in this class play an important role in bacterial CELL WALL biosynthesis.

D046930.name: Thymus Plant
D046930.definition: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE best known for the thyme spice added to foods.

D046931.name: Microcystis
D046931.definition: A form-genus of CYANOBACTERIA in the order Chroococcales. Many species are planktonic and possess gas vacuoles.

D046932.name: Nodularia
D046932.definition: A form-genus of filamentous CYANOBACTERIA in the order Nostocales. Its members can be planktonic or benthic and the trichomes are composed of disc-shaped vegetative cells.

D046934.name: Ginkgolides
D046934.definition: DITERPENES with three LACTONES and a unique tert-butyl group, which are found in GINKGO plants along with BILOBALIDES.

D046935.name: Bilobalides
D046935.definition: A degraded form of GINKGOLIDES that have three LACTONES and a unique tert-butyl group which are found in GINKGO plants.

D046936.name: Photinia
D046936.definition: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE. The common names of chokeberry or chokecherry are also used for some species of PRUNUS.

D046937.name: Nostoc
D046937.definition: A form-genus of CYANOBACTERIA in the order Nostocales. Trichomes composed of spherical or ovoid vegetative cells along with heterocysts and akinetes. The species form symbiotic associations with a wide range of eukaryotes.

D046938.name: Plectonema
D046938.definition: A form-genus of CYANOBACTERIA in the order Oscillatoriales. They are non-heterocystous but may carry out NITROGEN FIXATION under microaerobic conditions. Some smaller members have undergone transfer to the form-genus Leptolyngbya.

D046939.name: Synechocystis
D046939.definition: A form-genus of unicellular CYANOBACTERIA in the order Chroococcales. None of the strains fix NITROGEN, there are no gas vacuoles, and sheath layers are never produced.

D046940.name: Synechococcus
D046940.definition: A form-genus of spherical to rod-shaped CYANOBACTERIA in the order Chroococcales. They contain THYLAKOIDS and are found in a wide range of habitats.

D046948.name: Secologanin Tryptamine Alkaloids
D046948.definition: Compounds formed by condensation of secologanin with tryptamine resulting in a tetrahydro-beta-carboline which is processed further to a number of bioactive compounds. These are especially found in plants of the APOCYNACEAE; LOGANIACEAE; and RUBIACEAE families.

D046949.name: Thermotoga neapolitana
D046949.definition: A species of extremophilic bacteria in the family Thermotogaceae. Generally anaerobic but in the presence of OXYGEN, it can produce hydrogen gas as a byproduct of metabolism.

D046950.name: Thermoanaerobacterium
D046950.definition: A genus of gram-positive, anaerobic bacteria in the family Thermoanaerobacteriaceae. They are thermophilic and saccharolytic.

D046968.name: Thermoanaerobacter
D046968.definition: A genus of gram-positive, anaerobic bacteria in the family Thermoanaerobacteriaceae. Cultures consist of rods interspersed with coccoid cells.

D046969.name: Clostridium acetobutylicum
D046969.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae, used for the industrial production of SOLVENTS.

D046970.name: Clostridium beijerinckii
D046970.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae, capable of solventogenesis, and isolated from SOIL, infected WOUNDS, fermenting OLIVES, and spoiled CANDY.

D046971.name: Clostridium bifermentans
D046971.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae that ferments both CARBOHYDRATES and AMINO ACIDS.

D046972.name: Clostridium butyricum
D046972.definition: Type species of the genus CLOSTRIDIUM, a gram-positive bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae. It is used as a source of PROBIOTICS.

D046973.name: Clostridium cellulolyticum
D046973.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae. It is a cellulolytic, mesophilic species isolated from decayed GRASS.

D046974.name: Clostridium cellulovorans
D046974.definition: A species of gram-positive, cellulolytic bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae. It produces CELLULOSOMES which are involved in plant CELL WALL degradation.

D046975.name: Clostridium chauvoei
D046975.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae isolated from infected CATTLE; SHEEP; and other animals. It causes blackleg in cattle and sheep and is transmitted through soil-borne spores.

D046988.name: Proteasome Endopeptidase Complex
D046988.definition: A large multisubunit complex that plays an important role in the degradation of most of the cytosolic and nuclear proteins in eukaryotic cells. It contains a 700-kDa catalytic sub-complex and two 700-kDa regulatory sub-complexes. The complex digests ubiquitinated proteins and protein activated via ornithine decarboxylase antizyme.

D047008.name: Marchantia
D047008.definition: A liverwort plant genus of the family Marchantiaceae, order Marchantiales, subclass MARCHANTIAE. Members contain brassinosteroids and DITERPENES.

D047009.name: Clostridium histolyticum
D047009.definition: A species of gram-positive, strongly proteolytic bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae. It contains several forms of COLLAGENASE whose action can lead to GAS GANGRENE in humans and HORSES.

D047010.name: Clostridium kluyveri
D047010.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae. It is distinctive for its ability to ferment ETHANOL to caproic acid.

D047011.name: Silk
D047011.definition: A continuous protein fiber consisting primarily of FIBROINS. It is synthesized by a variety of INSECTS and ARACHNIDS.

D047013.name: Clostridium botulinum type A
D047013.definition: Subtype of CLOSTRIDIUM BOTULINUM that produces BOTULINUM TOXINS, TYPE A which is neurotoxic to humans and animals.

D047014.name: Clostridium botulinum type B
D047014.definition: Subtype of CLOSTRIDIUM BOTULINUM that produces botulinum toxin type B which is neurotoxic to humans and animals.

D047028.name: Macrocyclic Compounds
D047028.definition: Cyclic compounds with a ring size of approximately 1-4 dozen atoms.

D047029.name: Lactams, Macrocyclic
D047029.definition: LACTAMS forming compounds with a ring size of approximately 1-3 dozen atoms.

D047030.name: Sericins
D047030.definition: A serine-rich sticky protein secreted by MOTHS. Generally, the term refers to silkworm silk gum protein secreted in the middle section of silk gland cells of SILKWORMS, Bombyx mori. Sericin acts as a cement and coating for the two fibroin filaments in a silk strand and is readily soluble in mild alkaline solution.

D047048.name: Vitellins
D047048.definition: Major egg yolk proteins from egg-laying animals such as non-mammalian VERTEBRATES; ARTHROPODS; and others. They are high-density lipoglycoproteins derived from circulating precursors, VITELLOGENINS. Vitellins serve as nutrients for the growing non-mammalian embryos (EMBRYO, NONMAMMALIAN).

D047068.name: Arylalkylamine N-Acetyltransferase
D047068.definition: An acetyltransferase with specificity towards the amine group of aromatic alkylamines (arylalkylamines) such as SEROTONIN. This enzyme is also referred to as serotonin acetylase despite the fact that serotonin acetylation can also occur through the action of broad specificity acetyltransferases such as ARYLAMINE N-ACETYLTRANSFERASE.

D047069.name: Pyrazolones
D047069.definition: Compounds with a five-membered heterocyclic ring with two nitrogens and a keto OXYGEN. Some are inhibitors of TNF-ALPHA production.

D047070.name: Bandages, Hydrocolloid
D047070.definition: Dressings comprised of a self-adhesive matrix to which hydrophilic absorbent particles are embedded. The particles consist of CELLULOSE derivatives; calcium ALGINATES; PECTINS; or GELS. The utility is based on providing a moist environment for WOUND HEALING.

D047071.name: beta-Glucans
D047071.definition: Glucose polymers consisting of a backbone of beta(1->3)-linked beta-D-glucopyranosyl units with beta(1->6) linked side chains of various lengths. They are a major component of the CELL WALL of organisms and of soluble DIETARY FIBER.

D047072.name: Aromatase Inhibitors
D047072.definition: Compounds that inhibit AROMATASE in order to reduce production of estrogenic steroid hormones.

D047088.name: Dysidea
D047088.definition: A genus of SPONGES in the family Dysideidae, in which all skeletal fibers are filled with detritus.

D047089.name: Axinella
D047089.definition: A genus of SPONGES in the family Axinellidae, comprised of a choanosomal skeleton differentiated in the axial and extra-axial region. The type species is Axinella polypoides.

D047090.name: beta-Lactams
D047090.definition: Four-membered cyclic AMIDES, best known for the PENICILLINS based on a bicyclo-thiazolidine, as well as the CEPHALOSPORINS based on a bicyclo-thiazine, and including monocyclic MONOBACTAMS. The BETA-LACTAMASES hydrolyze the beta lactam ring, accounting for BETA-LACTAM RESISTANCE of infective bacteria.

D047091.name: Eosinophil Granule Proteins
D047091.definition: Proteins found in EOSINOPHIL granules. They are primarily basic proteins that play a role in host defense and the proinflammatory actions of activated eosinophils.

D047093.name: Eosinophil Major Basic Protein
D047093.definition: One of several basic proteins released from EOSINOPHIL cytoplasmic granules. Eosinophil major basic protein is a 14-kDa cytotoxic peptide with a pI of 10.9. In addition to its direct cytotoxic effects, it stimulates the release of variety of INFLAMMATION MEDIATORS.

D047108.name: Embryonic Development
D047108.definition: Morphological and physiological development of EMBRYOS.

D047109.name: Fetal Development
D047109.definition: Morphological and physiological development of FETUSES.

D047128.name: Callyspongia
D047128.definition: A genus of SPONGES in the family Callyspongiidae comprised of a regular ectosomal reticulate skeleton.

D047129.name: Haliclona
D047129.definition: A genus of SPONGES in the family Chalinidae characterized by unispicular secondary lines in the choanosomal skeleton.

D047130.name: Petrosia
D047130.definition: A genus of SPONGES in the family Petrosiidae, characterized by an ectosomal triangular or polygonal reticulation of spicule tracts or single spicules.

D047131.name: Xestospongia
D047131.definition: A genus of SPONGES in the family Petrosiidae, characterized by an ectosomal skeleton consisting only of an isotropic reticulation of single spicules or spicule tracts.

D047132.name: Crambe Sponge
D047132.definition: A genus of SPONGES in the family Crambeidae characterized by desmoid spicules. The type species is Crambe crambe.

D047150.name: Eosinophil Cationic Protein
D047150.definition: One of several basic proteins released from EOSINOPHIL cytoplasmic granules. Eosinophil cationic protein is a 21-kDa cytotoxic peptide with a pI of 10.9. Although eosinophil cationic protein is considered a member of the RNAse A superfamily of proteins, it has only limited RNAse activity.

D047151.name: Amaryllidaceae Alkaloids
D047151.definition: Alkaloids derived from TYRAMINE combined with 3,4-dihydroxybenzaldehyde via a norbelladine pathway, including GALANTAMINE, lycorine and crinine. They are found in the Amaryllidaceae (LILIACEAE) plant family.

D047168.name: Cystine Knot Motifs
D047168.definition: Amino acid sequence in which two disulfide bonds (DISULFIDES) and their connecting backbone form a ring that is penetrated by a third disulfide bond. Members include CYCLOTIDES and agouti-related protein.

D047169.name: Cyclotides
D047169.definition: A continuous circle of peptide bonds, typically of 2-3 dozen AMINO ACIDS, so there is no free N- or C-terminus. They are further characterized by six conserved CYSTEINE residues that form CYSTINE KNOT MOTIFS.

D047188.name: Chalcones
D047188.definition: Compounds based on CHALCONE. They are important intermediates in the formation of FLAVONOIDS.

D047208.name: Eosinophil-Derived Neurotoxin
D047208.definition: A 19-kDa cationic peptide found in EOSINOPHIL granules. Eosinophil-derived neurotoxin is a RIBONUCLEASE and may play a role as an endogenous antiviral agent.

D047209.name: Eosinophil Peroxidase
D047209.definition: A 66-kDa peroxidase found in EOSINOPHIL granules. Eosinophil peroxidase is a cationic protein with a pI of 10.8 and is comprised of a heavy chain subunit and a light chain subunit. It possesses cytotoxic activity towards BACTERIA and other organisms, which is attributed to its peroxidase activity.

D047228.name: Angiotensin II Type 1 Receptor Blockers
D047228.definition: Agents that antagonize ANGIOTENSIN II TYPE 1 RECEPTOR. Included are ANGIOTENSIN II analogs such as SARALASIN and biphenylimidazoles such as LOSARTAN. Some are used as ANTIHYPERTENSIVE AGENTS.

D047229.name: Plakortis
D047229.definition: A genus of SPONGES in the family Plakinidae, with the skeleton formed by small diactine (and some triactine) needle-like terminations.

D047230.name: Agelas
D047230.definition: A genus of large, brightly colored SPONGES in the family Agelasidae, possessing a skeleton of spongin fibers with a core of large spicules (megascleres).

D047231.name: Geodia
D047231.definition: A genus of massive or globular SPONGES in the family Geodiidae, with large spicules at or near the surface.

D047232.name: Theonella
D047232.definition: A genus of shallow-cupped SPONGES with a broad base in the family Theonellidae. They are characterized by ectosomal spicules dominated by phyllotriaenes.

D047233.name: Suberites
D047233.definition: A genus of velvety smooth SPONGES in the family Suberitidae, characterized by the ectosomal and choanosomal skeletons dominated by tylostyles (pin-like spicules with a pinched bulbous end).

D047248.name: Crown Compounds
D047248.definition: Macrocyclic compounds analogous to CROWN ETHERS but which lack any OXYGEN atoms.

D047250.name: Calixarenes
D047250.definition: Phenolic metacyclophanes derived from condensation of PHENOLS and ALDEHYDES. The name derives from the vase-like molecular structures. A bracketed [n] indicates the number of aromatic rings.

D047268.name: Lingual Goiter
D047268.definition: Pathological enlargement of the LINGUAL THYROID, ectopic thyroid tissue at the base of the TONGUE. It may cause upper AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION; DYSPHAGIA; or HYPOTHYROIDISM symptoms.

D047269.name: Strongylocentrotus
D047269.definition: A genus of SEA URCHINS in the family Strongylocentrotidae. They possess more than three pore pairs per ambulacral plate. The species STRONGYLOCENTROTUS PURPURATUS is commonly used for research.

D047270.name: Strongylocentrotus purpuratus
D047270.definition: A species of SEA URCHINS in the family Strongylocentrotidae found on the Pacific coastline from Alaska to Mexico. This species serves as a major research model for molecular developmental biology and other fields.

D047271.name: Asterias
D047271.definition: A genus of STARFISH in the family Asteriidae. One species, Asterias rubens, is the most common in the north-east Atlantic region.

D047288.name: Asterina
D047288.definition: A genus of STARFISH in the family Asterinidae. They externally hold developing embryos (EMBRYO, NON-MAMMALIAN) among the spines below the oral surface.

D047308.name: Arbacia
D047308.definition: A genus of SEA URCHINS in the family Arbaciidae. They have only one spheridium (stalked body) per ambulacral area (contains tube feet); most sea urchins have several spheridia per area.

D047328.name: Paracentrotus
D047328.definition: A genus of SEA URCHINS in the family Echinidae found primarily on the western coasts of Ireland.

D047329.name: Anthocidaris
D047329.definition: A genus of SEA URCHINS in the family Echinometridae. They are closely related to and some say indistinguishable from the genus Heliocidaris.

D047330.name: Hemicentrotus
D047330.definition: A genus of SEA URCHINS in the family Strongylocentrotidae with a hemicyclic apical disk and short spines.

D047331.name: Lytechinus
D047331.definition: A genus of SEA URCHINS in the family Toxopneustidae possessing trigeminate ambulacral plating.

D047332.name: Holothuria
D047332.definition: A genus of large SEA CUCUMBERS in the family Holothuriidae possessing thick body walls, a warty body surface, and microscopic ossicles.

D047348.name: Hydrolyzable Tannins
D047348.definition: Polymeric derivatives of GALLIC ACID that are esters of a sugar.

D047368.name: Tumor Burden
D047368.definition: The total amount (cell number, weight, size or volume) of tumor cells or tissue in the body.

D047369.name: Chromatin Immunoprecipitation
D047369.definition: A technique for identifying specific DNA sequences that are bound, in vivo, to proteins of interest. It involves formaldehyde fixation of CHROMATIN to crosslink the DNA-BINDING PROTEINS to the DNA. After shearing the DNA into small fragments, specific DNA-protein complexes are isolated by immunoprecipitation with protein-specific ANTIBODIES. Then, the DNA isolated from the complex can be identified by PCR amplification and sequencing.

D047388.name: Casein Kinases
D047388.definition: A group of protein-serine-threonine kinases that was originally identified as being responsible for the PHOSPHORYLATION of CASEINS. They are ubiquitous enzymes that have a preference for acidic proteins. Casein kinases play a role in SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION by phosphorylating a variety of regulatory cytoplasmic and regulatory nuclear proteins.

D047389.name: Casein Kinase I
D047389.definition: A casein kinase that was originally described as a monomeric enzyme with a molecular weight of 30-40 kDa. Several ISOENZYMES of casein kinase I have been found which are encoded by separate genes. Many of the casein kinase I isoenzymes have been shown to play distinctive roles in intracellular SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION.

D047390.name: Casein Kinase II
D047390.definition: A ubiquitous casein kinase that is comprised of two distinct catalytic subunits and dimeric regulatory subunit. Casein kinase II has been shown to phosphorylate a large number of substrates, many of which are proteins involved in the regulation of gene expression.

D047391.name: alpha-Cyclodextrins
D047391.definition: Cyclic GLUCANS consisting of six (6) glucopyranose units linked by 1,4-glycosidic bonds.

D047392.name: beta-Cyclodextrins
D047392.definition: Cyclic GLUCANS consisting of seven (7) glucopyranose units linked by 1,4-glycosidic bonds.

D047408.name: gamma-Cyclodextrins
D047408.definition: Cyclic GLUCANS consisting of eight (8) glucopyranose units linked by 1,4-glycosidic bonds.

D047468.name: Immunoprecipitation
D047468.definition: The aggregation of soluble ANTIGENS with ANTIBODIES, alone or with antibody binding factors such as ANTI-ANTIBODIES or STAPHYLOCOCCAL PROTEIN A, into complexes large enough to fall out of solution.

D047488.name: Retinoid X Receptors
D047488.definition: A subtype of RETINOIC ACID RECEPTORS that are specific for 9-cis-retinoic acid which function as nuclear TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS that regulate multiple signaling pathways.

D047489.name: Preconception Injuries
D047489.definition: Damages to reproductive health prior to conception (FERTILIZATION), a legal term for torts liability concerning environmental safety issues. Preconception injuries may involve either the male or the female, such as chromosomal mutations in the OVA or the SPERMATOZOA.

D047490.name: Retinoid X Receptor alpha
D047490.definition: A nuclear transcription factor. Heterodimerization with PPAR GAMMA is important in regulation of GLUCOSE metabolism and CELL GROWTH PROCESSES.

D047491.name: Retinoid X Receptor gamma
D047491.definition: A nuclear transcription factor. Heterodimerization with PPAR ALPHA is important to metabolism of LIPIDS.

D047492.name: Peroxisome Proliferator-Activated Receptors
D047492.definition: TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS that are activated by ligands and heterodimerize with RETINOID X RECEPTORS and bind to peroxisome proliferator response elements in the promoter regions of target genes.

D047493.name: PPAR alpha
D047493.definition: A nuclear transcription factor. Heterodimerization with RETINOID X RECEPTOR GAMMA is important to metabolism of LIPIDS. It is the target of FIBRATES to control HYPERLIPIDEMIAS.

D047494.name: PPAR delta
D047494.definition: A nuclear transcription factor. It is activated by PROSTACYCLIN.

D047495.name: PPAR gamma
D047495.definition: A nuclear transcription factor. Heterodimerization with RETINOID X RECEPTOR ALPHA is important in regulation of GLUCOSE metabolism and CELL GROWTH PROCESSES. It is a target of THIAZOLIDINEDIONES for control of DIABETES MELLITUS.

D047508.name: Massive Hepatic Necrosis
D047508.definition: Extensive and rapid death of parenchymal cells in the LIVER, often due to exposure to toxic materials. It is characterized by a soft, flabby, yellow-brown wrinkled, and shrunken liver. It was called "acute yellow atrophy".

D047528.name: Stichopus
D047528.definition: A genus of very large, epibenthic SEA CUCUMBERS in the family Stichopodidae, commercially harvested in Southeast Asia for food.

D047548.name: Defibrillators
D047548.definition: Cardiac electrical stimulators that apply brief high-voltage electroshocks to the HEART. These stimulators are used to restore normal rhythm and contractile function in hearts of patients who are experiencing VENTRICULAR FIBRILLATION or ventricular tachycardia (TACHYCARDIA, VENTRICULAR) that is not accompanied by a palpable PULSE. Some defibrillators may also be used to correct certain noncritical dysrhythmias (called synchronized defibrillation or CARDIOVERSION), using relatively low-level discharges synchronized to the patient's ECG waveform. (UMDNS, 2003)

D047549.name: Coronary Artery Bypass, Off-Pump
D047549.definition: Coronary artery bypass surgery on a beating HEART without a CARDIOPULMONARY BYPASS (diverting the flow of blood from the heart and lungs through an oxygenator).

D047568.name: Unsafe Sex
D047568.definition: Sexual behaviors which are high-risk for contracting SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASES or for producing PREGNANCY.

D047569.name: Laser Scanning Cytometry
D047569.definition: A scanning microscope-based, cytofluorimetry technique for making fluorescence measurements and topographic analysis on individual cells. Lasers are used to excite fluorochromes in labeled cellular specimens. Fluorescence is detected in multiple discrete wavelengths and the locational data is processed to quantitatively assess APOPTOSIS; PLOIDIES; cell proliferation; GENE EXPRESSION; PROTEIN TRANSPORT; and other cellular processes.

D047589.name: Leukocyte Reduction Procedures
D047589.definition: The removal of LEUKOCYTES from BLOOD to reduce BLOOD TRANSFUSION reactions and lower the chance of transmitting VIRUSES. This may be performed by FILTRATION or by CYTAPHERESIS.

D047608.name: Pyrroloiminoquinones
D047608.definition: Derivatives of QUINOLINES with fused PYRROLES and a keto group or INDOLEQUINONES with fused PIPERIDINES.

D047628.name: Estrogen Receptor alpha
D047628.definition: One of the ESTROGEN RECEPTORS that has marked affinity for ESTRADIOL. Its expression and function differs from, and in some ways opposes, ESTROGEN RECEPTOR BETA.

D047629.name: Estrogen Receptor beta
D047629.definition: One of the ESTROGEN RECEPTORS that has greater affinity for ISOFLAVONES than ESTROGEN RECEPTOR ALPHA does. There is great sequence homology with ER alpha in the DNA-binding domain but not in the ligand binding and hinge domains.

D047630.name: Depsipeptides
D047630.definition: Compounds consisting of chains of AMINO ACIDS alternating with CARBOXYLIC ACIDS via ester and amide linkages. They are commonly cyclized.

D047648.name: Perimenopause
D047648.definition: The transitional period before and after MENOPAUSE. Perimenopausal symptoms are associated with irregular MENSTRUAL CYCLE and widely fluctuated hormone levels. They may appear 6 years before menopause and subside 2 to 5 years after menopause.

D047649.name: Andropause
D047649.definition: An endocrine state in men, characterized by a significant decline in the production of TESTOSTERONE; DEHYDROEPIANDROSTERONE; and other hormones such as HUMAN GROWTH HORMONE. Andropause symptoms are related to the lack of androgens including DEPRESSION, sexual dysfunction, and OSTEOPOROSIS. Andropause may also result from hormonal ablation therapy for malignant diseases.

D047668.name: Inteins
D047668.definition: The internal fragments of precursor proteins (INternal proTEINS) that are autocatalytically removed by PROTEIN SPLICING. The flanking fragments (EXTEINS) are ligated forming mature proteins. The nucleic acid sequences coding for inteins are considered to be MOBILE GENETIC ELEMENTS. Inteins are composed of self-splicing domains and an endonuclease domain which plays a role in the spread of the intein's genomic sequence. Mini-inteins are composed of the self-splicing domains only.

D047669.name: Exteins
D047669.definition: The (EXternal proTEIN) sequences flanking INTEINS, which are internal fragments of precursor proteins removed by PROTEIN SPLICING. Concomitantly, as the inteins are excised, the exteins are ligated to form mature proteins.

D047688.name: Breast Cyst
D047688.definition: A fluid-filled closed cavity or sac that is lined by an EPITHELIUM and found in the BREAST. It may appear as a single large cyst in one breast, multifocal, or bilateral in FIBROCYSTIC BREAST DISEASE.

D047708.name: Myofibroma
D047708.definition: A benign tumor that consists chiefly of fibrous CONNECTIVE TISSUE, with variable numbers of MUSCLE CELLS forming portions of the neoplasm (From Stedman's, 27th ed).

D047709.name: Hirudo medicinalis
D047709.definition: A species of European freshwater LEECHES used for BLOODLETTING in ancient times and also for LEECHING in modern times.

D047728.name: Myopia, Degenerative
D047728.definition: Excessive axial myopia associated with complications (especially posterior staphyloma and CHOROIDAL NEOVASCULARIZATION) that can lead to BLINDNESS.

D047748.name: Pituitary ACTH Hypersecretion
D047748.definition: A disease of the PITUITARY GLAND characterized by the excess amount of ADRENOCORTICOTROPIC HORMONE secreted. This leads to hypersecretion of cortisol (HYDROCORTISONE) by the ADRENAL GLANDS resulting in CUSHING SYNDROME.

D047768.name: Glycerophosphoinositol Inositolphosphodiesterase
D047768.definition: A phosphoric diester hydrolase with specificity for the cleavage of GLYCEROL from 1-(sn-glycero-3-phospho)-1D-myo-inositol. It also has specificity for hydrolysis of the cyclic phosphate bond in inositol 1,2-cyclic phosphate

D047788.name: American Revolution
D047788.definition: Armed conflict that resulted in separation of American colonies from Britain and established the United States of America.

D047789.name: World War II
D047789.definition: Global conflict involving countries of Europe, Africa, Asia, and North America that occurred between 1939 and 1945.

D047808.name: Adrenogenital Syndrome
D047808.definition: Abnormal SEX DIFFERENTIATION or congenital DISORDERS OF SEX DEVELOPMENT caused by abnormal levels of steroid hormones expressed by the GONADS or the ADRENAL GLANDS, such as in CONGENITAL ADRENAL HYPERPLASIA and ADRENAL CORTEX NEOPLASMS. Due to abnormal steroid biosynthesis, clinical features include VIRILISM in females; FEMINIZATION in males; or precocious sexual development in children.

D047828.name: World War I
D047828.definition: Global conflict primarily fought on European continent, that occurred between 1914 and 1918.

D047829.name: Vietnam Conflict
D047829.definition: A conflict occurring from 1954 through 1975 within the Republic of Vietnam. It involved neighboring nations and the United States and other members of the Southeast Asia Treaty Organization.

D047830.name: Gulf War
D047830.definition: United Nations' action to intervene in conflict between the nation of Kuwait and occupying Iraqi forces, occurring from 1990 through 1991.

D047831.name: American Civil War
D047831.definition: 1861-1865 conflict between the Union (Northern states) and the 11 Southern states that seceded and were organized as the Confederate States of America.

D047832.name: Spanish-American War, 1898
D047832.definition: Conflict between Spain and the United States, arising out of Spanish policies in Cuba.

D047848.name: Russian-Japanese War
D047848.definition: Conflict from 1904 through 1905 between Russia and Japan regarding Manchuria and Korea.

D047849.name: Crimean War
D047849.definition: Conflict between RUSSIA (Pre-1917); the OTTOMAN EMPIRE; ENGLAND; FRANCE; and Sardinia.

D047850.name: French Revolution
D047850.definition: Conflict during which traditional monarchy was ended and modern government functions were instituted.

D047851.name: September 11 Terrorist Attacks
D047851.definition: Terrorism on September 11, 2001 against targets in New York, the Pentagon in Virginia, and an aborted attack that ended in Pennsylvania.

D047852.name: Chernobyl Nuclear Accident
D047852.definition: April 25th -26th, 1986 nuclear power accident that occurred at Chernobyl in the former USSR (Ukraine) located 80 miles north of Kiev.

D047868.name: Pulmonary Sclerosing Hemangioma
D047868.definition: A benign neoplasm of pneumocytes, cells of the PULMONARY ALVEOLI. Originally considered to be vascular in origin, it is now classified as an epithelial tumor with several elements, including solid cellular areas, papillary structure, sclerotic regions, and dilated blood-filled spaces resembling HEMANGIOMA.

D047869.name: Korean War
D047869.definition: An armed conflict between Communist and non-Communist forces in Korea from June 25, 1950, to July 27, 1953. The parties included United Nations forces from 15 member nations under United States command against military from North Korea and the Peoples Republic of China.

D047888.name: Receptors, Tumor Necrosis Factor, Type I
D047888.definition: A tumor necrosis factor receptor subtype that has specificity for TUMOR NECROSIS FACTOR ALPHA and LYMPHOTOXIN ALPHA. It is constitutively expressed in most tissues and is a key mediator of tumor necrosis factor signaling in the vast majority of cells. The activated receptor signals via a conserved death domain that associates with specific TNF RECEPTOR-ASSOCIATED FACTORS in the CYTOPLASM.

D047889.name: Receptors, Tumor Necrosis Factor, Type II
D047889.definition: A tumor necrosis factor receptor subtype that is expressed primarily in IMMUNE SYSTEM cells. It has specificity for membrane-bound form of TUMOR NECROSIS FACTORS and mediates intracellular-signaling through TNF RECEPTOR ASSOCIATED FACTORS.

D047908.name: Intracellular Signaling Peptides and Proteins
D047908.definition: Proteins and peptides that are involved in SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION within the cell. Included here are peptides and proteins that regulate the activity of TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS and cellular processes in response to signals from CELL SURFACE RECEPTORS. Intracellular signaling peptide and proteins may be part of an enzymatic signaling cascade or act through binding to and modifying the action of other signaling factors.

D047928.name: Premature Birth
D047928.definition: CHILDBIRTH before 37 weeks of PREGNANCY (259 days from the first day of the mother's last menstrual period, or 245 days after FERTILIZATION).

D047929.name: Term Birth
D047929.definition: CHILDBIRTH at the end of a normal duration of PREGNANCY, between 37 to 40 weeks of gestation or about 280 days from the first day of the mother's last menstrual period.

D047968.name: Clostridium botulinum type C
D047968.definition: Subtype of CLOSTRIDIUM BOTULINUM that produces botulinum toxin type C which is neurotoxic to ANIMALS, especially CATTLE, but not humans. It causes dissociation of ACTIN FILAMENTS.

D047969.name: Clostridium botulinum type D
D047969.definition: Subtype of CLOSTRIDIUM BOTULINUM that produces botulinum toxin type D which is neurotoxic to ANIMALS, especially CATTLE, but not humans.

D047970.name: Clostridium botulinum type E
D047970.definition: Subtype of CLOSTRIDIUM BOTULINUM that produces botulinum toxin type E which is neurotoxic to humans and animals.

D047971.name: Clostridium botulinum type F
D047971.definition: Subtype of CLOSTRIDIUM BOTULINUM that produces botulinum toxin type F which is neurotoxic to humans and animals.

D047988.name: Tumor Necrosis Factor Receptor-Associated Peptides and Proteins
D047988.definition: Intracellular signaling peptides and proteins that bind directly or indirectly to the cytoplasmic portion of TUMOR NECROSIS FACTOR RECEPTORS.

D047989.name: Clostridium sordellii
D047989.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae, found in INTESTINES and SOIL.

D047990.name: TNF Receptor-Associated Factor 1
D047990.definition: A signal transducing tumor necrosis factor receptor associated factor that is involved in TNF RECEPTOR feedback regulation. It is similar in structure and appears to work in conjunction with TNF RECEPTOR-ASSOCIATED FACTOR 2 to inhibit APOPTOSIS.

D047991.name: Clostridium sticklandii
D047991.definition: A species of gram-positive, anaerobic bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae frequently used for the study of ENZYMES.

D047992.name: TNF Receptor-Associated Factor 2
D047992.definition: A signal transducing tumor necrosis factor receptor associated factor that is involved in TNF RECEPTOR feedback regulation. It is similar in structure and appears to work in conjunction with TNF RECEPTOR-ASSOCIATED FACTOR 1 to inhibit APOPTOSIS.

D048008.name: TNF Receptor-Associated Factor 3
D048008.definition: A signal transducing tumor necrosis factor receptor associated factor that is involved in regulation of NF-KAPPA B signaling and activation of MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASES.

D048009.name: Clostridium symbiosum
D048009.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae. Its GLUTAMATE DEHYDROGENASE is commonly used in research.

D048010.name: Clostridium tertium
D048010.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae, causing BACTEREMIA in humans and ANIMALS.

D048012.name: Clostridium tetanomorphum
D048012.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae. Its glutamate mutase is commonly used in research.

D048013.name: Clostridium thermocellum
D048013.definition: A species of gram-positive, thermophilic, cellulolytic bacteria in the family Clostridaceae. It degrades and ferments CELLOBIOSE and CELLULOSE to ETHANOL in the CELLULOSOME.

D048014.name: Clostridium tyrobutyricum
D048014.definition: A species of gram-positive bacteria in the family Clostridiaceae responsible for spoilage of some CHEESE via FERMENTATION of BUTYRIC ACID.

D048015.name: TNF Receptor-Associated Factor 5
D048015.definition: A signal transducing tumor necrosis factor receptor associated factor that mediates signaling from CD27 ANTIGENS; CD40 ANTIGENS; and the LYMPHOTOXIN BETA RECEPTOR. It is involved in regulation of NF-KAPPA B signaling.

D048016.name: Cucumaria
D048016.definition: A genus of large SEA CUCUMBERS possessing the primitive radial configuration of podia in all five ambulacral areas.

D048028.name: DNA, Algal
D048028.definition: Deoxyribonucleic acid that makes up the genetic material of algae.

D048029.name: TNF Receptor-Associated Factor 6
D048029.definition: A signal transducing tumor necrosis factor receptor associated factor that is involved in regulation of NF-KAPPA B signalling and activation of JNK MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASES.

D048030.name: RNA, Algal
D048030.definition: Ribonucleic acid in algae having regulatory and catalytic roles as well as involvement in protein synthesis.

D048031.name: JNK Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinases
D048031.definition: A subgroup of mitogen-activated protein kinases that activate TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR AP-1 via the phosphorylation of C-JUN PROTEINS. They are components of intracellular signaling pathways that regulate CELL PROLIFERATION; APOPTOSIS; and CELL DIFFERENTIATION.

D048048.name: Dental Informatics
D048048.definition: The application of computer and information sciences to improve dental practice, research, education and management.

D048049.name: Extracellular Signal-Regulated MAP Kinases
D048049.definition: A mitogen-activated protein kinase subfamily that is widely expressed and plays a role in regulation of MEIOSIS; MITOSIS; and post mitotic functions in differentiated cells. The extracellular signal regulated MAP kinases are regulated by a broad variety of CELL SURFACE RECEPTORS and can be activated by certain CARCINOGENS.

D048051.name: p38 Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinases
D048051.definition: A mitogen-activated protein kinase subfamily that regulates a variety of cellular processes including CELL GROWTH PROCESSES; CELL DIFFERENTIATION; APOPTOSIS; and cellular responses to INFLAMMATION. The P38 MAP kinases are regulated by CYTOKINE RECEPTORS and can be activated in response to bacterial pathogens.

D048052.name: Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase 3
D048052.definition: A 44-kDa extracellular signal-regulated MAP kinase that may play a role the initiation and regulation of MEIOSIS; MITOSIS; and postmitotic functions in differentiated cells. It phosphorylates a number of TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS; and MICROTUBULE-ASSOCIATED PROTEINS.

D048053.name: Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase 6
D048053.definition: A 97-kDa extracellular signal-regulated MAP kinase. Mitogen-activated protein kinase 6 levels increase during cellular differentiation, while in proliferating cells the enzyme is degraded rapidly via the PROTEASOME ENDOPEPTIDASE COMPLEX.

D048054.name: Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase 7
D048054.definition: A 110-kDa extracellular signal-regulated MAP kinase that is activated in response to cellular stress and by GROWTH FACTOR RECEPTORS-mediated pathways.

D048055.name: Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase 8
D048055.definition: A c-jun amino-terminal kinase that is activated by environmental stress and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Several isoforms of the protein with molecular sizes of 43 and 48 KD exist due to multiple ALTERNATIVE SPLICING.

D048056.name: Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase 9
D048056.definition: A c-jun amino-terminal kinase that is activated by environmental stress and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Several isoforms of the protein with molecular sizes of 48 and 54 KD exist due to multiple ALTERNATIVE SPLICING.

D048057.name: Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase 10
D048057.definition: A c-jun amino-terminal kinase that is found predominantly within NEURONS of the BRAIN, suggesting a role in stress-induced neuronal APOPTOSIS. Several isoforms of the protein with molecular sizes of 47 kDa and 52 kDa exist due to multiple ALTERNATIVE SPLICING.

D048068.name: PPAR-beta
D048068.definition: One of the PPAR nuclear transcription factors.

D048069.name: Tumor Necrosis Factors
D048069.definition: A family of proteins that were originally identified by their ability to cause NECROSIS of NEOPLASMS. Their necrotic effect on cells is mediated through TUMOR NECROSIS FACTOR RECEPTORS which induce APOPTOSIS.

D048070.name: Fetal Nutrition Disorders
D048070.definition: Disorders caused by nutritional imbalance, either overnutrition or undernutrition, in the FETUS in utero.

D048088.name: Informatics
D048088.definition: The field of information science concerned with the analysis and dissemination of data through the application of computers.

D048089.name: Pneumonia of Calves, Enzootic
D048089.definition: Chronic endemic respiratory disease of dairy calves and an important component of bovine respiratory disease complex. It primarily affects calves up to six months of age and the etiology is multifactorial. Stress plus a primary viral infection is followed by a secondary bacterial infection. The latter is most commonly associated with PASTEURELLA MULTOCIDA producing a purulent BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. Sometimes present are MANNHEIMIA HAEMOLYTICA; HAEMOPHILUS SOMNUS and mycoplasma species.

D048090.name: Bovine Respiratory Disease Complex
D048090.definition: A multifactorial disease of CATTLE resulting from complex interactions between environmental factors, host factors, and pathogens. The environmental factors act as stressors adversely affecting the IMMUNE SYSTEM and other host defenses and enhancing transmission of infecting agents.

D048091.name: Guided Tissue Regeneration
D048091.definition: Procedures for enhancing and directing tissue repair and renewal processes, such as BONE REGENERATION; NERVE REGENERATION; etc. They involve surgically implanting growth conducive tracks or conduits (TISSUE SCAFFOLDING) at the damaged site to stimulate and control the location of cell repopulation. The tracks or conduits are made from synthetic and/or natural materials and may include support cells and induction factors for CELL GROWTH PROCESSES; or CELL MIGRATION.

D048108.name: Nursing Informatics
D048108.definition: The field of information science concerned with the analysis and dissemination of data through the application of computers applied to the field of nursing.

D048128.name: Casein Kinase Ialpha
D048128.definition: A casein kinase I isoenzyme that plays a role in intracellular signaling pathways including the WNT SIGNALING PATHWAY, the CELL CYCLE, membrane trafficking, and RNA processing. Multiple isoforms of casein kinase I alpha exist and are due to ALTERNATIVE SPLICING.

D048148.name: Casein Kinase Idelta
D048148.definition: A casein kinase I isoenzyme that plays a regulatory role in a variety of cellular functions including vesicular transport, CHROMOSOME SEGREGATION; CYTOKINESIS, developmental processes, and the CIRCADIAN RHYTHM.

D048149.name: Casein Kinase Iepsilon
D048149.definition: A casein kinase I isoenzyme with specificity for proteins involved the regulation of the CIRCADIAN RHYTHM.

D048168.name: Escherichia coli K12
D048168.definition: A species of gram-negative, rod-shaped bacteria belonging to the K serogroup of ESCHERICHIA COLI. It lives as a harmless inhabitant of the human LARGE INTESTINE and is widely used in medical and GENETIC RESEARCH.

D048169.name: Anopheles gambiae
D048169.definition: A species of mosquito in the genus Anopheles and the principle vector of MALARIA in Africa.

D048170.name: Streptomyces lividans
D048170.definition: An actinomycete used for production of commercial ANTIBIOTICS and as a host for gene cloning.

D048188.name: Locusta migratoria
D048188.definition: A species of migratory Old World locusts, in the family ACRIDIDAE, that are important pests in Africa and Asia.

D048189.name: Hymenolepis nana
D048189.definition: The smallest species of TAPEWORMS. It is the only cestode that parasitizes humans without requiring an intermediate host.

D048190.name: Hymenolepis diminuta
D048190.definition: A species of tapeworm (TAPEWORMS) infecting RATS and MICE but rarely causing disease in humans. Its life cycle involves RODENTS as the definitive host and BEETLES as the intermediate host.

D048191.name: Lactobacillus plantarum
D048191.definition: A species of rod-shaped, LACTIC ACID bacteria used in PROBIOTICS and SILAGE production.

D048208.name: Nuchal Translucency Measurement
D048208.definition: A prenatal ultrasonography measurement of the soft tissue behind the fetal neck. Either the translucent area below the skin in the back of the fetal neck (nuchal translucency) or the distance between occipital bone to the outer skin line (nuchal fold) is measured.

D048209.name: Echinococcus granulosus
D048209.definition: A species of hydatid tapeworm (class CESTODA) in the family Taeniidae, whose adult form infects the DIGESTIVE TRACT of DOGS, other canines, and CATS. The larval form infects SHEEP; PIGS; HORSES; and may infect humans, where it migrates to various organs and forms permanent HYDATID CYSTS.

D048210.name: Echinococcus multilocularis
D048210.definition: A north temperate species of tapeworm (CESTODA) whose adult form infects FOXES and wild RODENTS. The larval form can infect humans producing HEPATIC HYDATID CYSTS.

D048228.name: Intermittent Pneumatic Compression Devices
D048228.definition: Instruments that generate intermittent forces, uniformed or graduated, to facilitate the emptying of VEINS. These devices are used to reduce limb EDEMA and prevent venous THROMBOEMBOLISM, such as deep vein thrombosis in the legs.

D048229.name: Sulfolobus solfataricus
D048229.definition: A species of thermoacidophilic ARCHAEA in the family Sulfolobaceae, found in volcanic areas where the temperature is about 80 degrees C and SULFUR is present.

D048230.name: Corynebacterium glutamicum
D048230.definition: A species of gram-positive, asporogenous, non-pathogenic, soil bacteria that produces GLUTAMIC ACID.

D048248.name: Acanthamoeba castellanii
D048248.definition: A species of free-living soil amoebae in the family Acanthamoebidae. It can cause ENCEPHALITIS and KERATITIS in humans.

D048249.name: Streptococcus thermophilus
D048249.definition: A species of thermophilic, gram-positive bacteria found in MILK and milk products.

D048250.name: Squalus
D048250.definition: A genus of SHARKS in the family SQUALIDAE, comprised of many different species. They travel in large groups and are bottom dwellers that feed mostly on bony fishes.

D048251.name: Squalus acanthias
D048251.definition: A species of shark in the family SQUALIDAE, used for its oil (SQUALENE) and as fish meal. It also figures heavily in biological research, especially with reference to its RECTAL GLAND in studies of WATER-ELECTROLYTE BALANCE.

D048271.name: Chitosan
D048271.definition: Deacetylated CHITIN, a linear polysaccharide of deacetylated beta-1,4-D-glucosamine. It is used in HYDROGEL and to treat WOUNDS.

D048288.name: Imidazolines
D048288.definition: Compounds based on reduced IMIDAZOLES containing a single double bond.

D048289.name: Imidazolidines
D048289.definition: Compounds based on reduced IMIDAZOLINES which contain no double bonds in the ring.

D048290.name: Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase 11
D048290.definition: A 38-kDa mitogen-activated protein kinase that is expressed in a broad variety of cell types. It may play a role in regulating cell proliferation and TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR AP-1 dependent transcription.

D048291.name: Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase 12
D048291.definition: A 38-kDa mitogen-activated protein kinase found primarily in SKELETAL MUSCLE.

D048292.name: Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase 13
D048292.definition: A 38-kDa mitogen-activated protein kinase found expressed at high levels in LUNG; KIDNEY; TESTIS; PANCREAS; and SMALL INTESTINE. It may play a role in regulating functions such as CELL DIFFERENTIATION and APOPTOSIS of EPITHELIAL CELLS.

D048293.name: Didelphis
D048293.definition: A genus of large OPOSSUMS in the family Didelphidae, found in the Americas. The species Didelphis virginiana is prominent in North America.

D048308.name: Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase 14
D048308.definition: A 38-kDa mitogen-activated protein kinase that is abundantly expressed in a broad variety of cell types. It is involved in the regulation of cellular stress responses as well as the control of proliferation and survival of many cell types. The kinase activity of the enzyme is inhibited by the pyridinyl-imidazole compound SB 203580.

D048309.name: Monodelphis
D048309.definition: A genus of short-tailed OPOSSUMS in the family Didelphidae found in South American, chiefly Brazil. They are opossums least well-adapted to arboreal life.

D048328.name: Potoroidae
D048328.definition: A family of rat kangaroos found in and around Australia. Genera include Potorous and Bettongia.

D048329.name: Phalangeridae
D048329.definition: A family of possums and cuscuses found in Australia, Tasmania, New Guinea and other islands.

D048330.name: Trichosurus
D048330.definition: A genus of brush-tailed possums found chiefly in Australia and New Zealand. Secretions from their ANAL GLAND function both in defense and demarcating territory.

D048348.name: Reverse Transcription
D048348.definition: The biosynthesis of DNA carried out on a template of RNA.

D048368.name: Phascolarctidae
D048368.definition: A family of marsupials in the order Diprotodontia, native to Australia and possessing vestigial tails. There is a single living genus and species: Phascolarctos cinereus, the koala.

D048369.name: MAP Kinase Kinase 1
D048369.definition: An abundant 43-kDa mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase subtype with specificity for MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASE 1 and MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASE 3.

D048370.name: MAP Kinase Kinase 2
D048370.definition: A 44 kDa mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase with specificity for MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASE 1 and MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASE 3.

D048371.name: MAP Kinase Kinase 3
D048371.definition: A mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase with specificity for a subset of P38 MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASES that includes MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASE 12; MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASE 13; and MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASE 14.

D048372.name: Streptomyces coelicolor
D048372.definition: A soil-dwelling actinomycete with a complex lifecycle involving mycelial growth and spore formation. It is involved in the production of a number of medically important ANTIBIOTICS.

D048373.name: Treponema denticola
D048373.definition: A species of bacteria in the family SPIROCHAETACEAE, frequently isolated from periodontal pockets (PERIODONTAL POCKET).

D048388.name: Gadiformes
D048388.definition: An order of fish including the families Gadidae (cods), Macrouridae (grenadiers), and hakes. The large Gadidae family includes cod, haddock, whiting, and pollock.

D048389.name: Gadus morhua
D048389.definition: A species of fish in the cod family GADIDAE, known as the Atlantic cod. It is one of the most important commercial FISHES.

D048408.name: Chlorella vulgaris
D048408.definition: A species of green microalgae in the family Chlorellaceae. It is used as a model organism for PHOTOSYNTHESIS, and as a food supplement (DIETARY SUPPLEMENTS).

D048409.name: Aeromonas salmonicida
D048409.definition: A species of gram-negative bacteria, in the family Aeromonadaceae. It is strictly parasitic and often pathogenic causing FURUNCULOSIS in SALMONIDS and ulcer disease in GOLDFISH.

D048428.name: Petromyzon
D048428.definition: A genus of primitive fish in the family Petromyzontidae. The sole species is Petromyzon marinus, known as the sea lamprey. The adult form feeds parasitically on other fish species.

D048429.name: Cell Size
D048429.definition: The quantity of volume or surface area of CELLS.

D048430.name: Cell Shape
D048430.definition: The quality of surface form or outline of CELLS.

D048448.name: Phenylcarbamates
D048448.definition: Phenyl esters of carbamic acid or of N-substituted carbamic acids. Structures are similar to PHENYLUREA COMPOUNDS with a carbamate in place of the urea.

D048468.name: Podospora
D048468.definition: A genus of ascomycete FUNGI in the order SORDARIALES, which is found on SOIL and herbivore dung (FECES).

D048488.name: Paramecium caudatum
D048488.definition: The most widely distributed species of PARAMECIUM. It is elongated and possesses a bluntly pointed posterior.

D048489.name: Paramecium aurelia
D048489.definition: A species of ciliated PARAMECIUM possessing two micronuclei.

D048490.name: raf Kinases
D048490.definition: A family of closely-related serine-threonine kinases that were originally identified as the cellular homologs of the retrovirus-derived V-RAF KINASES. They are MAP kinase kinase kinases that play important roles in SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION.

D048491.name: Proto-Oncogene Proteins A-raf
D048491.definition: A raf kinase subclass expressed primarily in non-neuronal tissues such as SKELETAL MUSCLE. The A-raf kinases are MAP kinase kinase kinases that have specificity for MAP KINASE KINASE 1.

D048492.name: Paragonimus westermani
D048492.definition: A species of lung fluke infecting humans and other animals, and found chiefly in Asia and the Far East.

D048493.name: Proto-Oncogene Proteins B-raf
D048493.definition: A raf kinase subclass found at high levels in neuronal tissue. The B-raf Kinases are MAP kinase kinase kinases that have specificity for MAP KINASE KINASE 1 and MAP KINASE KINASE 2.

D048494.name: Rhipicephalus
D048494.definition: A genus of TICKS, in the family IXODIDAE, widespread in Africa. Members of the genus include many important vectors of animal and human pathogens.

D048508.name: Rhipicephalus sanguineus
D048508.definition: A species of tick (TICKS) in the family IXODIDAE, distributed throughout the world but abundant in southern Europe. It will feed on a wide variety of MAMMALS, but DOGS are its preferred host. It transmits a large number of diseases including BABESIOSIS; THEILERIASIS; EHRLICHIOSIS; and MEDITERRANEAN SPOTTED FEVER.

D048528.name: Mandrillus
D048528.definition: A genus of the subfamily CERCOPITHECINAE, family CERCOPITHECIDAE, comprising two species: the drill (M. leucophaeus) and the mandrill (M. sphinx). They are usually found in thick rainforest and have a gentle disposition despite their ferocious reputation. Some authors consider Mandrillus a subgenus of PAPIO.

D048529.name: Papio hamadryas
D048529.definition: A species of baboon in the family CERCOPITHECIDAE, which has a well-studied trilevel social structure consisting of troops, bands, and clans.

D048530.name: Papio anubis
D048530.definition: A species of baboon in the family CERCOPITHECIDAE with a somewhat different social structure than PAPIO HAMADRYAS. They inhabit several areas in Africa south of the Sahara.

D048531.name: Papio papio
D048531.definition: A species of baboon in the family CERCOPITHECIDAE, often used as an animal model for cognitive studies.

D048548.name: Papio cynocephalus
D048548.definition: A species of baboon in the family CERCOPITHECIDAE found in southern equatorial and east Africa. They are smaller than PAPIO ANUBIS and have a thinner mane.

D048549.name: Papio ursinus
D048549.definition: A species of baboon in the family CERCOPITHECIDAE found in southern Africa. They are dark colored and have a variable social structure.

D048550.name: Hepatic Insufficiency
D048550.definition: Conditions in which the LIVER functions fall below the normal ranges. Severe hepatic insufficiency may cause LIVER FAILURE or DEATH. Treatment may include LIVER TRANSPLANTATION.

D048568.name: Clostridium botulinum type G
D048568.definition: Subtype of CLOSTRIDIUM BOTULINUM that produces botulinum toxin type G. Though it has been isolated from soil, no outbreaks involving this type have been recognized.

D048588.name: Benzoxazines
D048588.definition: OXAZINES with a fused BENZENE ring.

D048608.name: Rupicapra
D048608.definition: A genus of ruminants in the family Bovidae. The common name chamois usually refers to the species Rupicapra rupicapra. Rupicapra pyrenaica, found in the Pyrenees, is more properly referred to as the Pyrenean chamois.

D048628.name: Ketolides
D048628.definition: Compounds based on ERYTHROMYCIN with the 3-cladinose replaced by a ketone. They bind the 23S part of 70S bacterial RIBOSOMES.

D048629.name: Micronuclei, Chromosome-Defective
D048629.definition: Defective nuclei produced during the TELOPHASE of MITOSIS or MEIOSIS by lagging CHROMOSOMES or chromosome fragments derived from spontaneous or experimentally induced chromosomal structural changes.

D048630.name: Polyketide Synthases
D048630.definition: Large enzyme complexes composed of a number of component enzymes that are found in STREPTOMYCES which biosynthesize MACROLIDES and other polyketides.

D048631.name: Micronucleus, Germline
D048631.definition: The smaller, reproductive, transcriptionally inert nucleus in the cells of ciliate protozoans, as distinguished from the larger, vegetative, transcriptionally active MACRONUCLEUS. Micronuclei participate in MEIOSIS and autogamy during GENETIC CONJUGATION.

D048648.name: Macronucleus
D048648.definition: The larger of two types of nuclei in ciliate protozoans. It is the transcriptionally active nucleus of the vegetative cells as distinguished from the smaller transcriptionally inert GERMLINE MICRONUCLEUS.

D048668.name: Lactobacillus delbrueckii
D048668.definition: A species of gram-positive, rod-shaped, facultatively anaerobic bacteria. capable of producing LACTIC ACID. It is important in the manufacture of fermented dairy products.

D048669.name: MAP Kinase Kinase 6
D048669.definition: A mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase with specificity for P38 MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASES.

D048670.name: MAP Kinase Kinase 4
D048670.definition: A mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase with specificity for JNK MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASES; P38 MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASES and the RETINOID X RECEPTORS. It takes part in a SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION pathway that is activated in response to cellular stress.

D048671.name: MAP Kinase Kinase 5
D048671.definition: A mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase with specificity for MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASE 7.

D048688.name: MAP Kinase Kinase 7
D048688.definition: A mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase with specificity for JNK MITOGEN-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASES. It takes part in a SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION pathway that is activated in response to CYTOKINES.

D048690.name: Fruiting Bodies, Fungal
D048690.definition: The fruiting 'heads' or 'caps' of FUNGI, which as a food item are familiarly known as MUSHROOMS, that contain the FUNGAL SPORES.

D048691.name: Grifola
D048691.definition: A member of the AGARICALES known for edible MUSHROOMS.

D048708.name: Cell Growth Processes
D048708.definition: Processes required for CELL ENLARGEMENT and CELL PROLIFERATION.

D048728.name: MAP Kinase Kinase Kinase 1
D048728.definition: A 195-kDa MAP kinase kinase kinase with broad specificity for MAP KINASE KINASES. It is found localized in the CYTOSKELETON and can activate a variety of MAP kinase-dependent pathways.

D048729.name: Anacardic Acids
D048729.definition: A group of 6-alkyl SALICYLIC ACIDS that are found in ANACARDIUM and known for causing CONTACT DERMATITIS.

D048730.name: MAP Kinase Kinase Kinase 2
D048730.definition: A 70-kDa MAP kinase kinase kinase with specificity for MAP KINASE KINASE 5. It is activated during the cellular response to GROWTH FACTORS, oxidative stress, and hyperosmotic conditions.

D048748.name: MAP Kinase Kinase Kinase 3
D048748.definition: A 70-kDa MAPK kinase kinase with specificity for MAP KINASE KINASE 5.

D048749.name: Cytokinesis
D048749.definition: The process by which the CYTOPLASM of a cell is divided.

D048750.name: Cell Nucleus Division
D048750.definition: The process by which the CELL NUCLEUS is divided.

D048768.name: MAP Kinase Kinase Kinase 4
D048768.definition: A 180-kDa MAP kinase kinase kinase with specificity for MAP KINASE KINASE 4 and MAP KINASE KINASE 6.

D048788.name: Growth and Development
D048788.definition: The series of changes to the shape, size, components, and functions of an individual organism that occur over time as the organism progresses from its initial form to full size and maturity.

D048789.name: Phytoestrogens
D048789.definition: PLANT EXTRACTS and compounds, primarily ISOFLAVONES, that mimic or modulate endogenous estrogens, usually by binding to ESTROGEN RECEPTORS.

D048790.name: Renilla
D048790.definition: A genus of bioluminescent marine invertebrates in the family Renillidae, order Pennatulacea, class ANTHOZOA. It contains Renilla LUCIFERASE which oxidizes coelenterazine resulting in LUMINESCENCE.

D048809.name: alpha-N-Acetylgalactosaminidase
D048809.definition: A hexosaminidase with specificity for terminal non-reducing N-acetyl-D-galactosamine residues in N-acetyl-alpha-D-galactosaminides.

D048828.name: beta-N-Acetyl-Galactosaminidase
D048828.definition: A hexosiminidase that specifically hydrolyzes terminal non-reducing N-acetyl-D-galactosamine residues in N-acetyl-beta-D-galactosaminides.

D048848.name: MAP Kinase Kinase Kinase 5
D048848.definition: A 150-kDa MAP kinase kinase kinase that may play a role in the induction of APOPTOSIS. It has specificity for MAP KINASE KINASE 3; MAP KINASE KINASE 4; and MAP KINASE KINASE 6.

D048868.name: Adaptor Proteins, Signal Transducing
D048868.definition: A broad category of carrier proteins that play a role in SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION. They generally contain several modular domains, each of which having its own binding activity, and act by forming complexes with other intracellular-signaling molecules. Signal-transducing adaptor proteins lack enzyme activity, however their activity can be modulated by other signal-transducing enzymes

D048888.name: Fireflies
D048888.definition: The family Lampyidae, which are bioluminescent BEETLES. They contain FIREFLY LUCIFERIN and LUCIFERASES. Oxidation of firefly luciferin results in luminescence.

D048889.name: Weevils
D048889.definition: BEETLES in the family Curculionidae and the largest family in the order COLEOPTERA. They have a markedly convex shape and many are considered pests.

D048908.name: Aliivibrio fischeri
D048908.definition: A species of gram-negative bacteria in the genus ALIIVIBRIO, which exhibits LUMINESCENCE. A. fischeri is found in a symbiotic relationship with the SQUID Euprymna scolopes.

D048909.name: Diabetes Complications
D048909.definition: Conditions or pathological processes associated with the disease of diabetes mellitus. Due to the impaired control of BLOOD GLUCOSE level in diabetic patients, pathological processes develop in numerous tissues and organs including the EYE, the KIDNEY, the BLOOD VESSELS, and the NERVE TISSUE.

D048928.name: Prochlorophytes
D048928.definition: An order of GRAM-NEGATIVE OXYGENIC PHOTOSYNTHETIC BACTERIA containing CHLOROPHYLL, a and b, but lacking PHYCOBILISOMES (light-harvesting antennae). There are three genera: PROCHLORON; PROCHLOROCOCCUS; and PROCHLOROTHRIX. This order was thought to be the missing link between CYANOBACTERIA and plant CHLOROPLASTS, hence the name.

D048929.name: Prochlorococcus
D048929.definition: A genus of marine planktonic CYANOBACTERIA in the order PROCHLOROPHYTES. They lack PHYCOBILISOMES and contain divinyl CHLOROPHYLL, a and b.

D048948.name: 14-3-3 Proteins
D048948.definition: A large family of signal-transducing adaptor proteins present in wide variety of eukaryotes. They are PHOSPHOSERINE and PHOSPHOTHREONINE binding proteins involved in important cellular processes including SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION; CELL CYCLE control; APOPTOSIS; and cellular stress responses. 14-3-3 proteins function by interacting with other signal-transducing proteins and effecting changes in their enzymatic activity and subcellular localization. The name 14-3-3 derives from numerical designations used in the original fractionation patterns of the proteins.

D048949.name: Labor Pain
D048949.definition: Pain associated with OBSTETRIC LABOR in CHILDBIRTH. It is caused primarily by UTERINE CONTRACTION as well as pressure on the CERVIX; BLADDER; and the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT. Labor pain mostly occurs in the ABDOMEN; the GROIN; and the BACK.

D048968.name: Morning Sickness
D048968.definition: Symptoms of NAUSEA and VOMITING in pregnant women that usually occur in the morning during the first 2 to 3 months of PREGNANCY. Severe persistent vomiting during pregnancy is called HYPEREMESIS GRAVIDARUM.

D048988.name: Corneal Surgery, Laser
D048988.definition: Surgical techniques on the CORNEA employing LASERS, especially for reshaping the CORNEA to correct REFRACTIVE ERRORS.

D049008.name: Keratectomy, Subepithelial, Laser-Assisted
D049008.definition: A surgical technique to correct REFRACTIVE ERRORS of the EYE, such as MYOPIA and ASTIGMATISM. In this method, a flap of CORNEAL EPITHELIUM is created by exposure of the area to dilute alcohol. The flap is lifted and then replaced after laser ablation of the subepithelial CORNEA.

D049028.name: Dystrophin-Associated Protein Complex
D049028.definition: A macromolecular complex of proteins that includes DYSTROPHIN and DYSTROPHIN-ASSOCIATED PROTEINS. It plays a structural role in the linking the CYTOSKELETON to the EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX.

D049029.name: Dystrophin-Associated Proteins
D049029.definition: A group of proteins that associate with DYSTROPHIN at the CELL MEMBRANE to form the DYSTROPHIN-ASSOCIATED PROTEIN COMPLEX.

D049030.name: Dystroglycans
