D058288.definition: Metastatic lesion of the UMBILICUS associated with intra-abdominal neoplasms especially of the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT or OVARY.

D058305.name: Sorting Nexins
D058305.definition: A large family of phosphatidylinositol phosphate-binding proteins that are involved in mediating intracellular transport and sorting of proteins via a variety of endocytic pathways.

D058306.name: Receptors, Prostaglandin E, EP1 Subtype
D058306.definition: A subtype of prostaglandin E receptors that specifically couples to GTP-BINDING PROTEIN ALPHA SUBUNIT, GQ and the subsequently activates TYPE C PHOSPHOLIPASES. Additional evidence has shown that the receptor can act through a calcium-dependent signaling pathway.

D058307.name: Receptors, Prostaglandin E, EP2 Subtype
D058307.definition: A subtype of prostaglandin E receptors that specifically couples to GS ALPHA GTP-BINDING PROTEIN SUBUNITS and subsequently activates ADENYLYL CYCLASES.

D058308.name: Receptors, Prostaglandin E, EP3 Subtype
D058308.definition: A subtype of prostaglandin E receptors that specifically couples to GTP-BINDING PROTEIN ALPHA SUBUNIT, GI and subsequently inhibits ADENYLYL CYCLASES.

D058309.name: Receptors, Prostaglandin E, EP4 Subtype
D058309.definition: A subtype of prostaglandin E receptors that specifically couples to GS ALPHA GTP-BINDING PROTEIN SUBUNITS and subsequently activates ADENYLYL CYCLASES. The receptor may also signal through the activation of PHOSPHATIDYLINOSITOL 3-KINASE.

D058325.name: Amblycera
D058325.definition: A suborder of chewing lice, in the order PHTHIRAPTERA, that are ectoparasites of poultry and some mammals.

D058326.name: Ischnocera
D058326.definition: A suborder of chewing lice, in the order PHTHIRAPTERA, that are parasites of birds and mammals.

D058327.name: Norwood Procedures
D058327.definition: A set of surgical procedures performed to establish sufficient outflow to the systemic circulation in individuals with univentricular congenital heart malformations, such as HYPOPLASTIC LEFT HEART SYNDROME, and MITRAL VALVE atresia, associated with systemic outflow obstruction. Follow-on surgeries may be performed and consist of a HEMI-FONTAN PROCEDURE as the stage 2 Norwood procedure and a FONTAN PROCEDURE as the stage 3 Norwood procedure.

D058345.name: Asymptomatic Infections
D058345.definition: Infections that do not exhibit symptoms.

D058365.name: Candidiasis, Invasive
D058365.definition: An important nosocomial fungal infection with species of the genus CANDIDA, most frequently CANDIDA ALBICANS. Invasive candidiasis occurs when candidiasis goes beyond a superficial infection and manifests as CANDIDEMIA, deep tissue infection, or disseminated disease with deep organ involvement.

D058366.name: Blalock-Taussig Procedure
D058366.definition: A cardiovascular procedure performed to create a blood supply to the PULMONARY CIRCULATION. It involves making a connection between the subclavian, or carotid branch of the AORTA, or the AORTIC ARCH to the PULMONARY ARTERY.

D058385.name: Cardiac Valve Annuloplasty
D058385.definition: A type of heart valve surgery that involves the repair, replacement, or reconstruction of the annuli of HEART VALVES. It includes shortening the circumference of the annulus to improve valve closing capacity and reinforcing the annulus as a step in more complex valve repairs.

D058386.name: Mitral Valve Annuloplasty
D058386.definition: A type of heart valve surgery that involves the repair, replacement, or reconstruction of the annulus of the MITRAL VALVE. It includes shortening the circumference of the annulus to improve valve closing capacity and reinforcing the annulus as a step in more complex valve repairs.

D058387.name: Candidemia
D058387.definition: A form of invasive candidiasis where species of CANDIDA are present in the blood.

D058405.name: Desmoplastic Small Round Cell Tumor
D058405.definition: A rare, aggressive soft tissue sarcoma that primarily affects adolescents and young adults. It is most commonly found in the abdomen.

D058406.name: Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy
D058406.definition: The restoration of the sequential order of contraction and relaxation of the HEART ATRIA and HEART VENTRICLES by atrio-biventricular pacing.

D058407.name: Electroencephalography Phase Synchronization
D058407.definition: Adjustment of BRAIN WAVES from two or more neuronal groups within or across a brain structure (e.g., cortical and limbic brain structures) to become uniform in EEG oscillation patterns in response to a stimulus. It is interpreted as a brain integration sign during many processes such as learning, memory, and perception and involves reciprocal neural connections.

D058408.name: Th1-Th2 Balance
D058408.definition: Homeostatic control of the immune system by secretion of different cytokines by the Th1 and Th2 cells. The concentration dependent binding of the various cytokines to specific receptors determines the balance (or imbalance leading to disease).

D058409.name: Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Devices
D058409.definition: Types of artificial pacemakers with implantable leads to be placed at multiple intracardial sites. They are used to treat various cardiac conduction disturbances which interfere with the timing of contraction of the ventricles. They may or may not include defibrillating electrodes (IMPLANTABLE DEFIBRILLATORS) as well.

D058425.name: Vaccines, Virus-Like Particle
D058425.definition: Vaccines using supra-molecular structures composed of multiple copies of recombinantly expressed viral structural proteins. They are often antigentically indistinguishable from the virus from which they were derived.

D058426.name: Neointima
D058426.definition: The new and thickened layer of scar tissue that forms on a PROSTHESIS, or as a result of vessel injury especially following ANGIOPLASTY or stent placement.

D058427.name: Hygroscopic Agents
D058427.definition: Materials that readily absorb moisture from their surroundings.

D058428.name: Silica Gel
D058428.definition: A non-crystalline form of silicon oxide that has absorptive properties. It is commonly used as a desiccating agent and as a stationary phase for CHROMATOGRAPHY. The fully hydrated form of silica gel has distinct properties and is referred to as SILICIC ACID.

D058429.name: Gnathostomiasis
D058429.definition: Infections with nematodes of the genus GNATHOSTOMA, superfamily THELAZIOIDEA. Gnathostomiasis is a food-borne zoonosis caused by eating undercooked or raw fish or meat.

D058430.name: Humeral Head
D058430.definition: The portion of the upper rounded extremity fitting into the glenoid cavity of the SCAPULA. (from Stedman, 27th ed)

D058431.name: Brachypodium
D058431.definition: A plant genus in the family POACEAE. Brachypodium distachyon is a model species for functional genomics studies.

D058432.name: Sporangia
D058432.definition: A structure found in plants, fungi, and algae, that produces and contains spores.

D058433.name: Photobioreactors
D058433.definition: Devices for generating biological products that use light as the energy source. They are used for controlled BIOMASS production such as growing cyanobacteria, mosses, or algae.

D058436.name: Knowledge Management
D058436.definition: The leveraging of collective wisdom within an organization as a catalyst to increase responsiveness and innovation.

D058437.name: Hypertensive Retinopathy
D058437.definition: Degenerative changes to the RETINA due to HYPERTENSION.

D058438.name: Water Cycle
D058438.definition: Circulation of water among various ecological systems, in various states, on, above, and below the surface of the earth.

D058439.name: Plant Somatic Embryogenesis Techniques
D058439.definition: The process of embryo initiation in culture from vegetative, non-gametic, sporophytic, or somatic plant cells.

D058440.name: Denitrification
D058440.definition: Nitrate reduction process generally mediated by anaerobic bacteria by which nitrogen available to plants is converted to a gaseous form and lost from the soil or water column. It is a part of the nitrogen cycle.

D058441.name: Rhizosphere
D058441.definition: The immediate physical zone surrounding plant roots that include the plant roots. It is an area of intense and complex biological activity involving plants, microorganisms, other soil organisms, and the soil.

D058442.name: Capsule Opacification
D058442.definition: Clouding or loss of transparency of the posterior lens capsule, usually following CATARACT extraction.

D058443.name: Catastrophization
D058443.definition: Cognitive and emotional processes encompassing magnification of pain-related stimuli, feelings of helplessness, and a generally pessimistic orientation.

D058445.name: Bullying
D058445.definition: Aggressive behavior intended to cause harm or distress. The behavior may be physical or verbal. There is typically an imbalance of power, strength, or status between the target and the aggressor.

D058446.name: Ligand-Gated Ion Channels
D058446.definition: A subclass of ion channels that open or close in response to the binding of specific LIGANDS.

D058447.name: Eye Pain
D058447.definition: A dull or sharp painful sensation associated with the outer or inner structures of the eyeball, having different causes.

D058448.name: Biota
D058448.definition: The spectrum of different living organisms inhabiting a particular region, habitat, or biotope.

D058449.name: Intravitreal Injections
D058449.definition: The administration of substances into the VITREOUS BODY of the eye with a hypodermic syringe.

D058450.name: Endotamponade
D058450.definition: A method of stopping internal bleeding or blood flow, or the closure of a wound or body cavity, achieved by applying pressure or introducing an absorbent liquid, gel, or tampon.

D058451.name: Oxidative Coupling
D058451.definition: The reaction of two molecular entities via oxidation usually catalyzed by a transition metal compound and involving dioxygen as the oxidant.

D058452.name: Axial Length, Eye
D058452.definition: The distance between the anterior and posterior poles of the eye, measured either by ULTRASONOGRAPHY or by partial coherence interferometry.

D058453.name: Emmetropia
D058453.definition: The condition of where images are correctly brought to a focus on the retina.

D058456.name: Retinal Telangiectasis
D058456.definition: A group of rare, idiopathic, congenital retinal vascular anomalies affecting the retinal capillaries. It is characterized by dilation and tortuosity of retinal vessels and formation of multiple aneurysms, with different degrees of leakage and exudates emanating from the blood vessels.

D058457.name: Trichiasis
D058457.definition: A disease of the eye in which the eyelashes abnormally turn inwards toward the eyeball producing constant irritation caused by motion of the lids.

D058458.name: Nitrogen Cycle
D058458.definition: The circulation of nitrogen in nature, consisting of a cycle of biochemical reactions in which atmospheric nitrogen is compounded, dissolved in rain, and deposited in the soil, where it is assimilated and metabolized by bacteria and plants, eventually returning to the atmosphere by bacterial decomposition of organic matter.

D058465.name: Nitrification
D058465.definition: A process facilitated by specialized bacteria involving the oxidation of ammonium to nitrite and nitrate.

D058466.name: Cysteine Loop Ligand-Gated Ion Channel Receptors
D058466.definition: A subfamily of ligand-gated ion channel receptors that share a characteristic loop which is formed by a disulfide bond between two CYSTEINE residues. These receptors typically contain five subunits with the cysteine-loop occurring near an N-terminal extracellular domain.

D058467.name: Tardigrada
D058467.definition: A phylum of microscopic ecdysozoan invertebrates, closely related to ARTHROPODS. Members exhibit anabiosis and cryptobiosis, dormant states where metabolic activity is reduced or absent, thus making them tolerant to extreme environmental conditions. They are distributed worldwide and most are semi-aquatic.

D058468.name: Receptors, Ionotropic Glutamate
D058468.definition: A class of ligand-gated ion channel receptors that have specificity for GLUTAMATE. They are distinct from METABOTROPIC GLUTAMATE RECEPTORS which act through a G-protein-coupled mechanism.

D058469.name: Receptors, Purinergic P2X
D058469.definition: A subclass of purinergic P2 receptors that signal by means of a ligand-gated ion channel. They are comprised of three P2X subunits which can be identical (homotrimeric form) or dissimilar (heterotrimeric form).

D058470.name: Receptors, Purinergic P2Y
D058470.definition: A subclass of purinergic P2 receptors whose signaling is coupled through a G-PROTEIN signaling mechanism.

D058471.name: Subretinal Fluid
D058471.definition: An exudate between the RETINA and CHOROID from various sources including the vitreous cavity, SUBARACHNOID SPACE, or abnormal vessels.

D058472.name: Receptors, Purinergic P2Y1
D058472.definition: A subclass of purinergic P2Y receptors that have a preference for ATP and ADP. The activated P2Y1 receptor signals through the G-PROTEIN-coupled activation of PHOSPHOLIPASE C and mobilization of intracellular CALCIUM.

D058473.name: Receptors, Purinergic P2Y2
D058473.definition: A subclass of purinergic P2Y receptors that have a preference for ATP and UTP. The activated P2Y2 receptor acts through a G-PROTEIN-coupled PHOSPHATIDYLINOSITOL and intracellular CALCIUM SIGNALING pathway.

D058474.name: Receptors, Purinergic P2X1
D058474.definition: A purinergic P2X neurotransmitter receptor found at sympathetically innervated SMOOTH MUSCLE. It may play a functional role regulating the juxtoglomerular apparatus of the KIDNEY.

D058475.name: Tenon Capsule
D058475.definition: Sheath of the eyeball consisting of fascia extending from the OPTIC NERVE to the corneal limbus.

D058476.name: Receptors, Purinergic P2X2
D058476.definition: A purinergic P2X neurotransmitter receptor involved in sensory signaling of TASTE PERCEPTION, chemoreception, visceral distension and NEUROPATHIC PAIN. The receptor comprises three P2X2 subunits. The P2X2 subunits also have been found associated with P2X3 RECEPTOR subunits in a heterotrimeric receptor variant.

D058477.name: Receptors, Purinergic P2X3
D058477.definition: A purinergic P2X neurotransmitter receptor involved in sensory signaling of TASTE PERCEPTION, chemoreception, visceral distension, and NEUROPATHIC PAIN. The receptor comprises three P2X3 subunits. The P2X3 subunits are also associated with P2X2 RECEPTOR subunits in a heterotrimeric receptor variant.

D058485.name: Receptors, Purinergic P2X5
D058485.definition: A purinergic P2X neurotransmitter receptor found at high levels in the BRAIN and IMMUNE SYSTEM.

D058486.name: Receptors, Purinergic P2X7
D058486.definition: A purinergic P2X neurotransmitter receptor that plays a role in pain sensation signaling and regulation of inflammatory processes.

D058487.name: Cercaria
D058487.definition: The free-swimming larval forms of parasites found in an intermediate host.

D058488.name: Metacercariae
D058488.definition: Encysted cercaria which house the intermediate stages of trematode parasites in tissues of an intermediate host.

D058489.name: 46, XX Disorders of Sex Development
D058489.definition: Congenital conditions in individuals with a female karyotype, in which the development of the gonadal or anatomical sex is atypical.

D058490.name: 46, XY Disorders of Sex Development
D058490.definition: Congenital conditions in individuals with a male karyotype, in which the development of the gonadal or anatomical sex is atypical.

D058491.name: Bacterial Load
D058491.definition: Measurable quantity of bacteria in an object, organism, or organism compartment.

D058492.name: Drug Repositioning
D058492.definition: The deliberate and methodical practice of finding new applications for existing drugs.

D058493.name: Sarcophagidae
D058493.definition: Family of flies in the order DIPTERA, commonly known as flesh flies. They lay their eggs in dead or decaying matter or open wounds.

D058494.name: Walker-Warburg Syndrome
D058494.definition: Rare autosomal recessive lissencephaly type 2 associated with congenital MUSCULAR DYSTROPHY and eye anomalies (e.g., RETINAL DETACHMENT; CATARACT; MICROPHTHALMOS). It is often associated with additional brain malformations such as HYDROCEPHALY and cerebellar hypoplasia and is the most severe form of the group of related syndromes (alpha-dystroglycanopathies) with common congenital abnormalities in the brain, eye and muscle development.

D058495.name: Sotos Syndrome
D058495.definition: Congenital or postnatal overgrowth syndrome most often in height and occipitofrontal circumference with variable delayed motor and cognitive development. Other associated features include advanced bone age, seizures, NEONATAL JAUNDICE; HYPOTONIA; and SCOLIOSIS. It is also associated with increased risk of developing neoplasms in adulthood. Mutations in the NSD1 protein and its HAPLOINSUFFICIENCY are associated with the syndrome.

D058496.name: Smith-Magenis Syndrome
D058496.definition: Complex neurobehavioral disorder characterized by distinctive facial features (FACIES), developmental delay and INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY. Behavioral phenotypes include sleep disturbance, maladaptive, self-injurious and attention-seeking behaviors. The sleep disturbance is linked to an abnormal circadian secretion pattern of MELATONIN. The syndrome is associated with de novo deletion or mutation and HAPLOINSUFFICIENCY of the retinoic acid-induced 1 protein on chromosome 17p11.2.

D058497.name: Fraser Syndrome
D058497.definition: Rare autosomal recessive congenital malformation syndrome characterized by cryptophthalmos, SYNDACTYLY and UROGENITAL ABNORMALITIES. Other anomalies of bone, ear, lung, and nose are common. Mutations on FRAS1 and FREM2 are associated with the syndrome.

D058498.name: Kyphoplasty
D058498.definition: Procedures to restore vertebrae to their original shape following vertebral compression fractures by inflating a balloon inserted into the vertebrae, followed by removal of the balloon and injection of BONE CEMENTS to fill the cavity.

D058499.name: Retinal Dystrophies
D058499.definition: A group of disorders involving predominantly the posterior portion of the ocular fundus, due to degeneration in the sensory layer of the RETINA; RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM; BRUCH MEMBRANE; CHOROID; or a combination of these tissues.

D058500.name: Animal Fins
D058500.definition: Membranous appendage of fish and other aquatic organisms used for locomotion or balance.

D058501.name: Enzyme-Linked Immunospot Assay
D058501.definition: A method of detection of the number of cells in a sample secreting a specific molecule. With this method, a population of cells are plated over top of the immunosorbent substrate that captures the secreted molecules.

D058502.name: Pentalogy of Cantrell
D058502.definition: Rare congenital deformity syndrome characterized by a combination of five anomalies as a result of neural tube defect. The five anomalies are a midline supraumbilical abdominal wall defect (e.g., OMPHALOCELE), a lower STERNUM defect, a congenital intracardiac defect, an anterior DIAPHRAGM defect, and a diaphragmatic PERICARDIUM defect (e.g., PERICARDIAL EFFUSION). Variants with incomplete and variable combinations of the defects are known. ECTOPIA CORDIS; CLEFT LIP; and CLEFT PALATE are often associated with the syndrome.

D058503.name: Mesophyll Cells
D058503.definition: Large and highly vacuolated cells possessing many chloroplasts occuring in the interior cross-section of leaves, juxtaposed between the epidermal layers.

D058504.name: Th17 Cells
D058504.definition: Subset of helper-effector T-lymphocytes which synthesize and secrete IL-17, IL-17F, and IL-22. These cytokines are involved in host defenses and tissue inflammation in autoimmune diseases.

D058506.name: Cambium
D058506.definition: A layer of living cells between the bark and hardwood that each year produces additional wood and bark cells, forming concentric growth rings.

D058507.name: Host Specificity
D058507.definition: The properties of a pathogen that makes it capable of infecting one or more specific hosts. The pathogen can include PARASITES as well as VIRUSES; BACTERIA; FUNGI; or PLANTS.

D058525.name: Quartz Crystal Microbalance Techniques
D058525.definition: The use of a quartz crystal microbalance for measuring weights and forces in the micro- to nanogram range. It is used to study the chemical and mechanical properties of thin layers, such as polymer coatings and lipid membranes; and interactions between molecues.

D058526.name: Plant Vascular Bundle
D058526.definition: A strand of primary conductive plant tissue consisting essentially of XYLEM, PHLOEM, and CAMBIUM.

D058527.name: Enteropathy-Associated T-Cell Lymphoma
D058527.definition: A primary peripheral T-cell lymphoma in the gastrointestinal tract, most often in the jejunum, associated with a history of CELIAC DISEASE or other gastrointestinal diseases.

D058529.name: Single Umbilical Artery
D058529.definition: Congenital abnormality where one, instead of the usual two, UMBILICAL ARTERY connects the fetus to the placenta.

D058530.name: Datura metel
D058530.definition: A plant species and perennial herb of the genus DATURA, family SOLANACEAE, containing poisonous tropane ALKALOIDS.

D058531.name: 46, XX Testicular Disorders of Sex Development
D058531.definition: Congenital conditions in individuals in which male GONADS develop in a genetic female (female to male sex reversal).

D058533.name: Sex Chromosome Disorders of Sex Development
D058533.definition: Congenital conditions of atypical sexual development associated with abnormal sex chromosome constitutions including MONOSOMY; TRISOMY; and MOSAICISM.

D058534.name: Class I Phosphatidylinositol 3-Kinases
D058534.definition: A phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase subclass that includes enzymes with a specificity for 1-phosphatidylinositol, 1-phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate, and 1-phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate. Members of this enzyme subclass are activated by cell surface receptors and occur as heterodimers of enzymatic and regulatory subunits.

D058535.name: Echogenic Bowel
D058535.definition: A PRENATAL ULTRASONOGRAPHY finding of excessively dense fetal bowel due to MECONIUM buildup.

D058536.name: Pyelectasis
D058536.definition: Dilation of fetal KIDNEY PELVIS. It is a common PRENATAL ULTRASONOGRAPHY finding with no significant long-term sequelae.

D058537.name: Electronic Supplementary Materials
D058537.definition: Supporting content or information, such as animation, datasets, multimedia files, video, movies, audio files, text files, or software, which is submitted for publication in an online journal or an online edition of a journal. This information may be referenced in the text of the article with a link to the supplementary data provided. CATALOG: do not use

D058538.name: Phosphatidylinositol-4-Phosphate 3-Kinase
D058538.definition: A phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase that catalyzes the conversion of 1-phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate into phosphatidylinositol 3,4-bisphosphate.

D058539.name: Phosphatidylinositol 3-Kinase
D058539.definition: A phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase that catalyzes the conversion of 1-phosphatidylinositol into 1-phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate.

D058540.name: Aicardi Syndrome
D058540.definition: A rare genetic disorder characterized by partial or complete absence of the CORPUS CALLOSUM, resulting in infantile spasms, MENTAL RETARDATION, and lesions of the RETINA or OPTIC NERVE.

D058541.name: Class II Phosphatidylinositol 3-Kinases
D058541.definition: A subclass of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinases that have specificity for 1-phosphatidylinositol and 1-phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate. Members of this subclass consist of a single subunit structure and are regulated by RECEPTOR TYROSINE KINASES; CYTOKINE RECEPTORS; and INTEGRINS.

D058542.name: Implantable Neurostimulators
D058542.definition: Surgically placed electric conductors through which ELECTRIC STIMULATION of nerve tissue is delivered.

D058543.name: Class Ia Phosphatidylinositol 3-Kinase
D058543.definition: A phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase subclass that includes enzymes formed through the heterodimerization of a p110 catalytic and a p85, p55, or p50 regulatory subunit. This subclass of enzymes is a downstream target of TYROSINE KINASE RECEPTORS and G PROTEIN-COUPLED RECEPTORS.

D058544.name: Class Ib Phosphatidylinositol 3-Kinase
D058544.definition: A phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase subclass that includes enzymes formed through the association of a p110gamma catalytic subunit and one of the three regulatory subunits of 84, 87, and 101 kDa in size. This subclass of enzymes is a downstream target of G PROTEIN-COUPLED RECEPTORS.

D058545.name: Inhalant Abuse
D058545.definition: Illicit use of chemicals and products whose vapors can be inhaled to produce a rapid mind-altering effect. Inhalants include aerosols, gases, and volatile solvents that are often inhaled repeatedly to achieve the short-lived intoxicating effect.

D058546.name: Class III Phosphatidylinositol 3-Kinases
D058546.definition: A phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase subclass that includes enzymes whose specificity is limited to 1-phosphatidylinositol. Members of this class play a role in vesicular transport and in the regulation of TOR KINASES.

D058566.name: Sacroiliitis
D058566.definition: Inflammation of the SACROILIAC JOINT. It is characterized by lower back pain, especially upon walking, fever, UVEITIS; PSORIASIS; and decreased range of motion. Many factors are associated with and cause sacroiliitis including infection; injury to spine, lower back, and pelvis; DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS; and pregnancy.

D058567.name: Photoinitiators, Dental
D058567.definition: Chemical compound used to initiate polymerization of dental resins by the use of DENTAL CURING LIGHTS. It absorbs UV light and undergoes decomposition into free radicals that initiate polymerization process of the resins in the mix. Each photoinitiator has optimum emission spectrum and intensity for proper curing of dental materials.

D058568.name: Necrolytic Migratory Erythema
D058568.definition: Recurrent cutaneous manifestation of GLUCAGONOMA characterized by necrolytic polycyclic migratory lesions with scaling borders. It is associated with elevated secretion of GLUCAGON by the tumor. Other conditions with elevated serum glucagon levels such as HEPATIC CIRRHOSIS may also result in similar skin lesions, which are referred to as pseudoglucagonoma syndrome.

D058570.name: TOR Serine-Threonine Kinases
D058570.definition: A serine threonine kinase that controls a wide range of growth-related cellular processes. The protein is referred to as the target of RAPAMYCIN due to the discovery that SIROLIMUS (commonly known as rapamycin) forms an inhibitory complex with TACROLIMUS BINDING PROTEIN 1A that blocks the action of its enzymatic activity.

D058571.name: Vacuolar Sorting Protein VPS15
D058571.definition: A 150 kDa protein serine-threonine kinase that is found as a regulatory subunit of the class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinases. The protein is believed to play an important role in the regulation of vesicular trafficking with the cell.

D058572.name: Carbon Footprint
D058572.definition: A measure of the total greenhouse gas emissions produced by an individual, organization, event, or product. It is measured in units of equivalent kilograms of CARBON DIOXIDE generated in a given time frame.

D058573.name: Performance-Enhancing Substances
D058573.definition: Agents that improve the ability to carry out activities such as athletics, mental endurance, work, and resistance to stress. The substances can include PRESCRIPTION DRUGS; DIETARY SUPPLEMENTS; phytochemicals; and ILLICIT DRUGS.

D058574.name: Integrin-Binding Sialoprotein
D058574.definition: A highly glycosylated and sulfated phosphoprotein that is found almost exclusively in mineralized connective tissues. It is an extracellular matrix protein that binds to hydroxyapatite through polyglutamic acid sequences and mediates cell attachment through an RGD sequence.

D058575.name: Decorin
D058575.definition: A small leucine-rich proteoglycan that interacts with FIBRILLAR COLLAGENS and modifies the EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX structure of CONNECTIVE TISSUE. Decorin has also been shown to play additional roles in the regulation of cellular responses to GROWTH FACTORS. The protein contains a single glycosaminoglycan chain and is similar in structure to BIGLYCAN.

D058578.name: Biglycan
D058578.definition: A small leucine-rich proteoglycan found in a variety of tissues including CAPILLARY ENDOTHELIUM; SKELETAL MUSCLE; CARTILAGE; BONE; and TENDONS. The protein contains two glycosaminoglycan chains and is similar in structure to DECORIN.

D058579.name: Hyalectins
D058579.definition: A group of high molecular weight chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans that form aggregates with HYALURONIC ACID.

D058580.name: Neurocan
D058580.definition: A hyalectin family member that is expressed in neuronal tissue and plays a role in neuronal CELL ADHESION.

D058581.name: Brevican
D058581.definition: A BRAIN-specific hyalectin that may play a role in terminally differentiating NEURONS. It is found highly overexpressed in primary BRAIN TUMORS and in experimental models of GLIOMA.

D058582.name: Double-Balloon Enteroscopy
D058582.definition: Endoscopy of the small intestines accomplished while advancing the endoscope into the intestines from the stomach by alternating the inflation of two balloons, one on an innertube of the endoscope and the other on an overtube.

D058585.name: Vestibular Evoked Myogenic Potentials
D058585.definition: Recorded electrical responses from muscles, especially the neck muscles or muscles around the eyes, following stimulation of the EAR VESTIBULE.

D058605.name: Host-Derived Cellular Factors
D058605.definition: A broad category of endogenous cellular factors that are used by VIRUSES for essential functions such as VIRUS REPLICATION. Many host-derived factors play normal cellular roles in non-infected cells.

D058606.name: Accessory Atrioventricular Bundle
D058606.definition: Extra impulse-conducting tissue in the heart that creates abnormal impulse-conducting connections between HEART ATRIA and HEART VENTRICLES.

D058607.name: Fibric Acids
D058607.definition: Compounds that either share the structure of fibric acid in their molecular arrangement or are considered variants of the fibric acid structure.

D058608.name: Nanopores
D058608.definition: Small holes of nanometer dimensions in a membrane, that can be used as single molecule detectors. The pores can be biological or synthetic.

D058609.name: Visual Field Tests
D058609.definition: Method of measuring and mapping the scope of vision, from central to peripheral of each eye.

D058610.name: Isobutyrates
D058610.definition: Aliphatic acids that contain four carbons in a branched-chain configuration. Included under this heading are a broad variety of acid forms, salts, esters, and amides that contain the 2-carboxypropane structure.

D058611.name: Horticultural Therapy
D058611.definition: A therapeutic approach in which horticultural artefacts are utilized in improving an individual's social, emotional, educational, psychological, and physical well-being.

D058612.name: Nanodiamonds
D058612.definition: Diamond nanoparticles that exhibit unique biological, thermal, mechanical, and optoelectronic properties. They have important NANOMEDICINE applications including DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEMS; DIAGNOSTIC IMAGING; protein separation; and BIOSENSING TECHNIQUES.

D058614.name: Seed Dispersal
D058614.definition: The various physical methods which include wind, insects, animals, tension, and water, by which a plant scatters its seeds away from the parent plant.

D058615.name: Synthetic Biology
D058615.definition: A field of biological research combining engineering in the formulation, design, and building (synthesis) of novel biological structures, functions, and systems.

D058616.name: Synbiotics
D058616.definition: Nutritional supplements combining PROBIOTICS (bacteria) and PREBIOTICS (sugars).

D058617.name: Composite Lymphoma
D058617.definition: Two or more distinct types of malignant lymphoid tumors occurring within a single organ or tissue at the same time. It may contain different types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma cells or both Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma cells.

D058618.name: Sensilla
D058618.definition: Collective name for a group of external MECHANORECEPTORS and chemoreceptors manifesting as sensory structures in ARTHROPODS. They include cuticular projections (setae, hairs, bristles), pores, and slits.

D058619.name: Maltose-Binding Proteins
D058619.definition: Periplasmic proteins that bind MALTOSE and maltodextrin. They take part in the maltose transport system of BACTERIA.

D058620.name: Elder Nutritional Physiological Phenomena
D058620.definition: Nutritional physiology of adults aged 65 years of age and older.

D058621.name: Blood Buffy Coat
D058621.definition: The fraction of a blood sample, following CENTRIFUGATION, that is distinguished as a thin light-colored layer between the RED BLOOD CELLS, underneath it, and the PLASMA, above it. It is composed mostly of WHITE BLOOD CELLS and PLATELETS.

D058625.name: End Stage Liver Disease
D058625.definition: Final stage of a liver disease when the liver failure is irreversible and LIVER TRANSPLANTATION is needed.

D058626.name: Plasma Gases
D058626.definition: Ionized gases, consisting of free electrons and ionized atoms or molecules which collectively behave differently than gas, solid, or liquid. Plasma gases are used in biomedical fields in surface modification; biological decontamination; dentistry (e.g., PLASMA ARC DENTAL CURING LIGHTS); and in other treatments (e.g., ARGON PLASMA COAGULATION).

D058627.name: Megalencephaly
D058627.definition: A congenital abnormality in which the occipitofrontal circumference is greater than two standard deviations above the mean for a given age. It is associated with HYDROCEPHALUS; SUBDURAL EFFUSION; ARACHNOID CYSTS; or is part of a genetic condition (e.g., ALEXANDER DISEASE; SOTOS SYNDROME).

D058628.name: Myofibroblasts
D058628.definition: Spindle-shaped cells with characteristic CONTRACTILE PROTEINS and structures that contribute to the WOUND HEALING process. They occur in GRANULATION TISSUE and also in pathological processes such as FIBROSIS.

D058629.name: Plasma Skin Regeneration
D058629.definition: A cosmetic technique that uses PLASMA GASES in therapeutic treatment to help achieve skin REJUVENATION or REGENERATION and delay SKIN AGING.

D058630.name: Spinal Cord Regeneration
D058630.definition: Repair of the damaged neuron function after SPINAL CORD INJURY or SPINAL CORD DISEASES.

D058631.name: Pycnodysostosis
D058631.definition: Rare autosomal recessive syndrome characterized by delayed closing of CRANIAL SUTURES, short stature, ACRO-OSTEOLYSIS of distal phalanges, dental and MAXILLOFACIAL ABNORMALITIES and an increase in bone density that results in frequent BONE FRACTURES. It is associated with BONE RESORPTION defect due to mutations in the lysosomal cysteine protease CATHEPSIN K.

D058632.name: Neuroprostanes
D058632.definition: Prostaglandin-like compounds produced by free radical-induced peroxidation of DOCOSAHEXAENOIC ACIDS, which are highly enriched in the brain. Formation is analogous to ISOPROSTANES formation from ARACHIDONIC ACID.

D058633.name: Antipyretics
D058633.definition: Drugs that are used to reduce body temperature in fever.

D058634.name: Molecular Farming
D058634.definition: The large scale production of pharmaceutically important and commercially valuable RECOMBINANT PROTEINS.

D058635.name: Lipid-Linked Proteins
D058635.definition: Proteins that are covalently-linked to lipid molecules or hydrophobic molecules such as those that contain prenyl groups. The lipid moieties aid in the association of the proteins with CELL MEMBRANES.

D058636.name: Surgical Drapes
D058636.definition: Sterile fabric or fabric-like material used to isolate the surgical site from the rest of the body and other possible sources of contamination.

D058637.name: Examination Tables
D058637.definition: A raised flat surface on which a patient is placed during a PHYSICAL EXAMINATION.

D058638.name: Operating Tables
D058638.definition: A raised flat surface on which a patient is placed during surgical procedures.

D058639.name: Cold-Shock Response
D058639.definition: A constellation of responses that occur when an organism is exposed to excessive cold. In humans, a fall in skin temperature triggers gasping, hypertension, and hyperventilation.

D058640.name: Brochothrix
D058640.definition: A genus of gram-positive bacteria in the family Listeriaceae. It has 93% homology to LISTERIA and shares with it many phenotypic properties.

D058641.name: Planococcaceae
D058641.definition: A family of gram-positive bacteria in the order BACILLALES. Most are strict aerobic heterotrophs.

D058642.name: Planococcus Bacteria
D058642.definition: A genus of coccoid bacteria in the family PLANOCOCCACEAE. They are widely distributed in various habitats including sea water, freshwater ponds, cyanobacterial mats, and in marine animals.

D058643.name: Planococcus Insect
D058643.definition: A genus of insect in the mealybug family Pseudococcidae.

D058644.name: Sporosarcina
D058644.definition: A genus of endospore-forming bacteria in the family Planococcaceae. The species are strict or facultative anerobes.

D058645.name: Denaturing Gradient Gel Electrophoresis
D058645.definition: Electrophoresis in which various denaturant gradients are used to induce nucleic acids to melt at various stages resulting in separation of molecules based on small sequence differences including SNPs. The denaturants used include heat, formamide, and urea.

D058646.name: Adrenergic alpha-1 Receptor Agonists
D058646.definition: Compounds that bind to and activate ADRENERGIC ALPHA-1 RECEPTORS.

D058647.name: Adrenergic alpha-2 Receptor Agonists
D058647.definition: Compounds that bind to and activate ADRENERGIC ALPHA-2 RECEPTORS.

D058665.name: Adrenergic beta-1 Receptor Agonists
D058665.definition: Compounds that bind to and activate ADRENERGIC BETA-1 RECEPTORS.

D058666.name: Adrenergic beta-2 Receptor Agonists
D058666.definition: Compounds bind to and activate ADRENERGIC BETA-2 RECEPTORS.

D058667.name: Adrenergic beta-3 Receptor Agonists
D058667.definition: Compounds that bind to and activate ADRENERGIC BETA-3 RECEPTORS.

D058668.name: Adrenergic alpha-1 Receptor Antagonists
D058668.definition: Drugs that bind to and block the activation of ADRENERGIC ALPHA-1 RECEPTORS.

D058669.name: Adrenergic alpha-2 Receptor Antagonists
D058669.definition: Drugs that bind to and block the activation of ADRENERGIC ALPHA-2 RECEPTORS.

D058670.name: Tetrasomy
D058670.definition: The possession of four chromosomes of any one type in an otherwise diploid cell.

D058671.name: Adrenergic beta-1 Receptor Antagonists
D058671.definition: Drugs that bind to and block the activation of ADRENERGIC BETA-1 RECEPTORS.

D058672.name: Adrenergic beta-2 Receptor Antagonists
D058672.definition: Drugs that bind to and block the activation of ADRENERGIC BETA-2 RECEPTORS.

D058673.name: Adrenergic beta-3 Receptor Antagonists
D058673.definition: Drugs that bind to and block the activation of ADRENERGIC BETA-3 RECEPTORS.

D058674.name: Chromosome Duplication
D058674.definition: An aberration in which an extra chromosome or a chromosomal segment is made.

D058675.name: Brevibacillus
D058675.definition: A genus of GRAM-POSITIVE ENDOSPORE-FORMING RODS in the family Paenibacillaceae. Most strains have been isolated from the natural environment, particularly soils.

D058676.name: Pasteuria
D058676.definition: A genus of GRAM-POSITIVE ENDOSPORE-FORMING BACTERIA in the family Pasteuriaceae. It is transmitted via soil or waterborne SPORES.

D058677.name: Anoxybacillus
D058677.definition: A genus of GRAM-POSITIVE ENDOSPORE-FORMING BACTERIA in the family Bacillaceae. Most species have been isolated from HOT SPRINGS.

D058678.name: Halobacillus
D058678.definition: A genus of GRAM-POSITIVE ENDOSPORE-FORMING BACTERIA in the family BACILLACEAE. Species are widely distributed in a variety of hypersaline environments.

D058679.name: Virgibacillus
D058679.definition: A genus of GRAM-POSITIVE ENDOSPORE-FORMING RODS in the family BACILLACEAE. They have been isolated from salty environments, food, water, and clinical specimens.

D058685.name: Genetic Pleiotropy
D058685.definition: A phenomenon in which multiple and diverse phenotypic outcomes are influenced by a single gene (or single gene product.)

D058686.name: Coronary-Subclavian Steal Syndrome
D058686.definition: A complication of INTERNAL MAMMARY-CORONARY ARTERY ANASTOMOSIS whereby an occlusion or stenosis of the proximal SUBCLAVIAN ARTERY causes a reversal of the blood flow away from the CORONARY CIRCULATION, through the grafted INTERNAL MAMMARY ARTERY (internal thoracic artery), and back to the distal subclavian distribution.

D058687.name: Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
D058687.definition: Occurrence of heart arrest in an individual when there is no immediate access to medical personnel or equipment.

D058725.name: Peripartum Period
D058725.definition: The period shortly before, during, and immediately after giving birth.

D058726.name: Nanoconjugates
D058726.definition: Tailored macromolecules harboring covalently-bound biologically active modules that target specific tissues and cells. The active modules or functional groups can include drugs, prodrugs, antibodies, and oligonucleotides, which can act synergistically and be multitargeting.

D058727.name: RNA, Small Untranslated
D058727.definition: Short RNA, about 200 base pairs in length or shorter, that does not code for protein.

D058728.name: Weed Control
D058728.definition: The prevention of growth and or spread of unwanted plants.

D058729.name: Peripheral Arterial Disease
D058729.definition: Lack of perfusion in the EXTREMITIES resulting from atherosclerosis. It is characterized by INTERMITTENT CLAUDICATION, and an ANKLE BRACHIAL INDEX of 0.9 or less.

D058731.name: Blood Safety
D058731.definition: The degree to which the blood supply for BLOOD TRANSFUSIONS is free of harmful substances or infectious agents, and properly typed and crossmatched (BLOOD GROUPING AND CROSSMATCHING) to insure serological compatibility between BLOOD DONORS and recipients.

D058732.name: Embryoid Bodies
D058732.definition: Spontaneous aggregations of human embryonic stem cells that occur in vitro after culturing in a medium that lacks LEUKEMIC INHIBITORY FACTOR. The embryoid bodies can further differentiate into cells that represent different lineages.

D058733.name: Hand-Assisted Laparoscopy
D058733.definition: Placement of one of the surgeon's gloved hands into the ABDOMINAL CAVITY to perform manual manipulations that facilitate the laparoscopic procedures.

D058734.name: Exsanguination
D058734.definition: Rapid and extreme blood loss leading to HEMORRHAGIC SHOCK.

D058735.name: Environmental Policy
D058735.definition: A course of action or principle adopted or proposed by a government, party, business, or individual that concerns human interactions with nature and natural resources.

D058736.name: Intrauterine Device Migration
D058736.definition: The shifting in position or location of an INTRAUTERINE DEVICE from its original placement.

D058738.name: Uterine Balloon Tamponade
D058738.definition: Inflation of a balloon CATHETER within the uterine cavity to control UTERINE HEMORRHAGE.

D058739.name: Aberrant Crypt Foci
D058739.definition: Clusters of colonic crypts that appear different from the surrounding mucosa when visualized after staining. They are of interest as putative precursors to colorectal adenomas and potential biomarkers for colorectal carcinoma.

D058745.name: Iliotibial Band Syndrome
D058745.definition: An overuse injury causing lateral knee pain that results from repetitive friction of the iliotibial band over the lateral femoral epicondyle.

D058746.name: Gestational Sac
D058746.definition: Round-shaped structure usually located in the upper fundus of the UTERUS in early pregnancy. It comprises EMBRYO; AMNIOTIC FLUID; and YOLK SAC. It is visible in PRENATAL ULTRASONOGRAPHY by the fifth week of pregnancy. Its size is often used to determine and monitor GESTATIONAL AGE; FETAL GROWTH; and PREGNANCY COMPLICATIONS.

D058747.name: CHARGE Syndrome
D058747.definition: Rare disease characterized by COLOBOMA; CHOANAL ATRESIA; and abnormal SEMICIRCULAR CANALS. Mutations in CHD7 protein resulting in disturbed neural crest development are associated with CHARGE Syndrome.

D058748.name: Pain Perception
D058748.definition: The process by which PAIN is recognized and interpreted by the brain.

D058749.name: Military Facilities
D058749.definition: Areas designated for use by the armed forces personnel.

D058750.name: Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition
D058750.definition: Phenotypic changes of EPITHELIAL CELLS to MESENCHYME type, which increase cell mobility critical in many developmental processes such as NEURAL TUBE development. NEOPLASM METASTASIS and DISEASE PROGRESSION may also induce this transition.

D058751.name: Livestock
D058751.definition: Domesticated farm animals raised for home use or profit but excluding POULTRY. Typically livestock includes CATTLE; SHEEP; HORSES; SWINE; GOATS; and others.

D058752.name: Free Tissue Flaps
D058752.definition: A mass of tissue that has been cut away from its surrounding areas to be used in TISSUE TRANSPLANTATION.

D058753.name: Laryngoplasty
D058753.definition: Restoration, reconstruction, or improvement of a defective or damaged LARYNX.

D058765.name: Neurofeedback
D058765.definition: A technique to self-regulate brain activities provided as a feedback in order to better control or enhance one's own performance, control or function. This is done by trying to bring brain activities into a range associated with a desired brain function or status.

D058766.name: Levoleucovorin
D058766.definition: A folate analog consisting of the pharmacologically active isomer of LEUCOVORIN.

D058767.name: Protein Unfolding
D058767.definition: Conformational transitions of the shape of a protein to various unfolded states.

D058785.name: GABA-A Receptor Agonists
D058785.definition: Endogenous compounds and drugs that bind to and activate GABA-A RECEPTORS.

D058786.name: GABA-B Receptor Agonists
D058786.definition: Endogenous compounds and drugs that bind to and activate GABA-B RECEPTORS.

D058787.name: GABA-A Receptor Antagonists
D058787.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate GABA-A RECEPTORS thereby blocking the actions of endogenous or exogenous GABA-A RECEPTOR AGONISTS.

D058788.name: GABA-B Receptor Antagonists
D058788.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate GABA-B RECEPTORS thereby blocking the actions of endogenous or exogenous GABA-B RECEPTOR AGONISTS.

D058805.name: GABA Uptake Inhibitors
D058805.definition: Compounds that suppress or block the plasma membrane transport of GAMMA-AMINOBUTYRIC ACID by GABA PLASMA MEMBRANE TRANSPORT PROTEINS.

D058825.name: Serotonin 5-HT1 Receptor Agonists
D058825.definition: Endogenous compounds and drugs that specifically stimulate SEROTONIN 5-HT1 RECEPTORS. Included under this heading are agonists for one or more of the specific 5-HT1 receptor subtypes.

D058826.name: Serotonin 5-HT2 Receptor Agonists
D058826.definition: Endogenous compounds and drugs that specifically stimulate SEROTONIN 5-HT2 RECEPTORS. Included under this heading are agonists for one or more of the specific 5-HT2 receptor subtypes.

D058827.name: Serotonin 5-HT3 Receptor Agonists
D058827.definition: Endogenous compounds and drugs that specifically stimulate SEROTONIN 5-HT3 RECEPTORS.

D058828.name: Serotonin 5-HT4 Receptor Agonists
D058828.definition: Endogenous compounds and drugs that specifically stimulate SEROTONIN 5-HT4 RECEPTORS.

D058829.name: Serotonin 5-HT1 Receptor Antagonists
D058829.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate SEROTONIN 5-HT1 RECEPTORS, thereby blocking the actions of SEROTONIN 5-HT1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS. Included under this heading are antagonists for one or more of the specific 5-HT1 receptor subtypes.

D058830.name: Serotonin 5-HT2 Receptor Antagonists
D058830.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate SEROTONIN 5-HT2 RECEPTORS, thereby blocking the actions of SEROTONIN or SEROTONIN 5-HT2 RECEPTOR AGONISTS. Included under this heading are antagonists for one or more specific 5-HT2 receptor subtypes.

D058831.name: Serotonin 5-HT3 Receptor Antagonists
D058831.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate SEROTONIN 5-HT3 RECEPTORS, thereby blocking the actions of SEROTONIN or SEROTONIN 5-HT3 RECEPTOR AGONISTS.

D058832.name: Serotonin 5-HT4 Receptor Antagonists
D058832.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate SEROTONIN 5-HT4 RECEPTORS, thereby blocking the actions of SEROTONIN or SEROTONIN RECEPTOR AGONISTS.

D058833.name: Antithrombin Proteins
D058833.definition: An endogenous family of proteins belonging to the serpin superfamily that neutralizes the action of thrombin. Six naturally occurring antithrombins have been identified and are designated by Roman numerals I to VI. Of these, Antithrombin I (see FIBRIN) and ANTITHROMBIN III appear to be of major importance.

D058834.name: Gemella
D058834.definition: A genus that has been reclassified into BACILLALES incertae sedis because of its ambiguous taxonomy. Previously it was considered part of the Staphylococcaceae family.

D058835.name: Abiotrophia
D058835.definition: A genus of gram-positive, facultatively anaerobic bacteria in the family Aerococcaceae.

D058836.name: Weissella
D058836.definition: A genus of gram-positive, asporogenous, lactic acid bacteria, in the family LEUCONOSTOCACEAE.

D058845.name: Moorella
D058845.definition: A genus of gram positive, acetogenic, thermophilic bacteria in the family Thermoanaerobacteraceae. Known habitats include HOT SPRINGS, horse manure, emu droppings, and sewage SLUDGE.

D058846.name: Antibodies, Monoclonal, Murine-Derived
D058846.definition: Antibodies obtained from a single clone of cells grown in mice or rats.

D058847.name: Inflammasomes
D058847.definition: Multiprotein complexes that mediate the activation of CASPASE-1. Dysregulation of inflammasomes has also been linked to a number of autoinflammatory and autoimmune disorders.

D058848.name: Receptors, Purinergic P2X4
D058848.definition: A widely distributed purinergic P2X receptor subtype that plays a role in pain sensation. P2X4 receptors found on MICROGLIA cells may also play a role in the mediation of allodynia-related NEUROPATHIC PAIN.

D058849.name: Protein Refolding
D058849.definition: Conformational transitions of a protein from unfolded states to a more folded state.

D058850.name: Opiate Substitution Treatment
D058850.definition: Medical treatment for opioid dependence using a substitute opiate such as METHADONE or BUPRENORPHINE.

D058851.name: GPI-Linked Proteins
D058851.definition: A subclass of lipid-linked proteins that contain a GLYCOSYLPHOSPHATIDYLINOSITOL LINKAGE which holds them to the CELL MEMBRANE.

D058865.name: Introduced Species
D058865.definition: Non-native organisms brought into a region, habitat, or ECOSYSTEM by human activity.

D058866.name: Osteoporotic Fractures
D058866.definition: Breaks in bones resulting from low bone mass and microarchitectural deterioration characteristic of OSTEOPOROSIS.

D058867.name: Lipoprotein Lipase Activators
D058867.definition: Compounds that increase the enzymatic activity of LIPOPROTEIN LIPASE. Lipoprotein lipase activators have a potential role in the treatment of OBESITY by increasing LIPID METABOLISM. Note that substances that increase the synthesis of lipoprotein lipase are not included here.

D058868.name: Compressed Air
D058868.definition: Air that is reduced in volume by pressure.

D058869.name: Gynecological Examination
D058869.definition: Inspection and PALPATATION of female breasts, abdomen, and GENITALIA, as well as obtaining a gynecological history. (from Dictionary of Obstetrics and Gynecology)

D058870.name: Food, Organic
D058870.definition: Food that is grown or manufactured in accordance with nationally regulated production standards that include restrictions on the use of pesticides, non-organic fertilizers, genetic engineering, growth hormones, irradiation, antibiotics, and non-organic ingredients.

D058871.name: Organic Agriculture
D058871.definition: Systems of agriculture which adhere to nationally regulated standards that restrict the use of pesticides, non-organic fertilizers, genetic engineering, growth hormones, irradiation, antibiotics, and non-organic ANIMAL FEED.

D058872.name: Epidemics
D058872.definition: Sudden outbreaks of a disease in a country or region not previously recognized in that area, or a rapid increase in the number of new cases of a previous existing endemic disease. Epidemics can also refer to outbreaks of disease in animal or plant populations.

D058873.name: Pandemics
D058873.definition: Epidemics of infectious disease that have spread to many countries, often more than one continent, and usually affecting a large number of people.

D058874.name: Electrowetting
D058874.definition: Reducing the SURFACE TENSION at a liquid/solid interface by the application of an electric current across the interface thereby enhancing the WETTABILITY of the surface.

D058885.name: Multilocus Sequence Typing
D058885.definition: Direct nucleotide sequencing of gene fragments from multiple housekeeping genes for the purpose of phylogenetic analysis, organism identification, and typing of species, strain, serovar, or other distinguishable phylogenetic level.

D058886.name: Sterol 14-Demethylase
D058886.definition: An NADPH-dependent P450 enzyme that plays an essential role in the sterol biosynthetic pathway by catalyzing the demethylation of 14-methyl sterols such as lanosterol. The enzyme acts via the repeated hydroxylation of the 14-methyl group, resulting in its stepwise conversion into an alcohol, an aldehyde and then a carboxylate, which is removed as formic acid. Sterol 14-demethylase is an unusual cytochrome P450 enzyme in that it is found in a broad variety of organisms including ANIMALS; PLANTS; FUNGI; and protozoa.

D058888.name: 14-alpha Demethylase Inhibitors
D058888.definition: Compounds that specifically inhibit STEROL 14-DEMETHYLASE. A variety of azole-derived ANTIFUNGAL AGENTS act through this mechanism.

D058889.name: Molecular Typing
D058889.definition: Using MOLECULAR BIOLOGY techniques, such as DNA SEQUENCE ANALYSIS; PULSED-FIELD GEL ELECTROPHORESIS; and DNA FINGERPRINTING, to identify, classify, and compare organisms and their subtypes.

D058890.name: Granulomatous Mastitis
D058890.definition: A rare, benign, inflammatory breast disease occurring in premenopausal women shortly after a recent pregnancy. The origin is unknown but it is commonly mistaken for malignancy and sometimes associated with BREAST FEEDING and the use of ORAL CONTRACEPTIVES.

D058891.name: 5-alpha Reductase Inhibitors
D058891.definition: Drugs that inhibit 3-OXO-5-ALPHA-STEROID 4-DEHYDROGENASE. They are commonly used to reduce the production of DIHYDROTESTOSTERONE.

D058892.name: Adenosine Deaminase Inhibitors
D058892.definition: Drugs that inhibit ADENOSINE DEAMINASE activity.

D058893.name: DNA Barcoding, Taxonomic
D058893.definition: Techniques for standardizing and expediting taxonomic identification or classification of organisms that are based on deciphering the sequence of one or a few regions of DNA known as the "DNA barcode".

D058894.name: Nematocyst
D058894.definition: A double-walled capsule found in jellyfish and other CNIDARIA whose functions include prey capture, defense, locomotion, and attachment. Nematocysts contain toxic CNIDARIAN VENOMS which are injected into the victim via a barbed tubule.

D058905.name: Purinergic Agents
D058905.definition: Compounds that act on PURINERGIC RECEPTORS or influence the synthesis, storage, uptake, metabolism, or release of purinergic transmitters.

D058906.name: Purinergic P1 Receptor Agonists
D058906.definition: Compounds that bind to and stimulate PURINERGIC P1 RECEPTORS.

D058907.name: Adenosine A1 Receptor Agonists
D058907.definition: Compounds that bind to and stimulate ADENOSINE A1 RECEPTORS.

D058908.name: Adenosine A2 Receptor Agonists
D058908.definition: Compounds that selectively bind to and activate ADENOSINE A2 RECEPTORS.

D058909.name: Adenosine A3 Receptor Agonists
D058909.definition: Drugs that selectively bind to and activate ADENOSINE A3 RECEPTORS.

D058910.name: Purinergic P2 Receptor Agonists
D058910.definition: Compounds that bind to and stimulate PURINERGIC P2 RECEPTORS.

D058911.name: Purinergic P2X Receptor Agonists
D058911.definition: Compounds that bind to and stimulate PURINERGIC P2X RECEPTORS. Included under this heading are agonists for specific P2X receptor subtypes.

D058912.name: Purinergic P2Y Receptor Agonists
D058912.definition: Compounds that bind to and stimulate PURINERGIC P2Y RECEPTORS. Included under this heading are agonists for specific P2Y receptor subtypes.

D058913.name: Purinergic Agonists
D058913.definition: Compounds that bind to and activate PURINERGIC RECEPTORS.

D058914.name: Purinergic Antagonists
D058914.definition: Drugs that bind to and block the activation of PURINERGIC RECEPTORS.

D058915.name: Purinergic P1 Receptor Antagonists
D058915.definition: Compounds that bind to and block the stimulation of PURINERGIC P1 RECEPTORS.

D058916.name: Adenosine A1 Receptor Antagonists
D058916.definition: Compounds that bind to and block the stimulation of ADENOSINE A1 RECEPTORS.

D058917.name: Adenosine A2 Receptor Antagonists
D058917.definition: Compounds that selectively bind to and block the activation of ADENOSINE A2 RECEPTORS.

D058918.name: Adenosine A3 Receptor Antagonists
D058918.definition: Compounds that selectively bind to and block the activation of ADENOSINE A3 RECEPTORS.

D058919.name: Purinergic P2 Receptor Antagonists
D058919.definition: Compounds that bind to and block the stimulation of PURINERGIC P2 RECEPTORS.

D058920.name: Purinergic P2X Receptor Antagonists
D058920.definition: Compounds that bind to and block the stimulation of PURINERGIC P2X RECEPTORS. Included under this heading are antagonists for specific P2X receptor subtypes.

D058921.name: Purinergic P2Y Receptor Antagonists
D058921.definition: Compounds that bind to and block the stimulation of PURINERGIC P2Y RECEPTORS. Included under this heading are antagonists for specific P2Y receptor subtypes.

D058922.name: Inflammatory Breast Neoplasms
D058922.definition: Metastatic breast cancer characterized by EDEMA and ERYTHEMA of the affected breast due to LYMPHATIC METASTASIS and eventual obstruction of LYMPHATIC VESSELS by the cancer cells.

D058923.name: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome
D058923.definition: SKELETAL MUSCLE pain and tenderness along the posteromedial TIBIA resulting from exercise such as running and other physical activity.

D058924.name: Thienopyridines
D058924.definition: Heterocyclic compounds that contain 4H,5H,6H,7H-thieno[2,3-c]pyridine as part of their structure.

D058925.name: Receptors, Purinergic P2Y12
D058925.definition: A subclass of purinergic P2Y receptors that have a preference for ADP binding and are coupled to GTP-BINDING PROTEIN ALPHA SUBUNIT, GI. The P2Y12 purinergic receptors are found in PLATELETS where they play an important role regulating PLATELET ACTIVATION.

D058926.name: Intraoperative Awareness
D058926.definition: Occurence of a patient becoming conscious during a procedure performed under GENERAL ANESTHESIA and subsequently having recall of these events. (From Anesthesiology 2006, 104(4): 847-64.)

D058927.name: 5-Lipoxygenase-Activating Proteins
D058927.definition: Scaffolding proteins that play an important role in the localization and activation of 5-LIPOXYGENASE.

D058928.name: Riboswitch
D058928.definition: Part of a MESSENGER RNA molecule that undergoes a conformation change upon binding a specific metabolite or other small molecule thereby regulating the messenger RNA's transcription, post-transcriptional processing, transport, translation, or stability in response to varying levels of the metabolite or other small molecule.

D058945.name: Lipoxygenases
D058945.definition: Dioxygenases that catalyze the peroxidation of methylene-interrupted UNSATURATED FATTY ACIDS.

D058946.name: 5-Lipoxygenase-Activating Protein Inhibitors
D058946.definition: Compounds that bind to and inhibit the action of 5-LIPOXYGENASE-ACTIVATING PROTEINS.

D058947.name: Bacterial Secretion Systems
D058947.definition: In GRAM NEGATIVE BACTERIA, multiprotein complexes that function to translocate pathogen protein effector molecules across the bacterial cell envelope, often directly into the host. These effectors are involved in producing surface structures for adhesion, bacterial motility, manipulation of host functions, modulation of host defense responses, and other functions involved in facilitating survival of the pathogen. Several of the systems have homologous components functioning similarly in GRAM POSITIVE BACTERIA.

D058948.name: Cell Tracking
D058948.definition: Non-invasive imaging of cells that have been labeled non-destructively, such as with nanoemulsions or reporter genes that can be detected by molecular imaging, to monitor their location, viability, cell lineage expansion, response to drugs, movement, or other behaviors in vivo.

D058949.name: Uromodulin
D058949.definition: A glycosyl-phosphatidyl-inositol (GPI) - anchored membrane protein found on the thick ascending limb of the LOOP OF HENLE. The cleaved form of the protein is found abundantly in URINE.

D058950.name: Melanoma-Specific Antigens
D058950.definition: Cellular antigens that are specific for MELANOMA cells.

D058951.name: gp100 Melanoma Antigen
D058951.definition: A melanosome-associated protein that plays a role in the maturation of the MELANOSOME.

D058952.name: Human papillomavirus 31
D058952.definition: A type of ALPHAPAPILLOMAVIRUS associated with high risk for anogenital neoplasms.

D058953.name: Neural Stem Cells
D058953.definition: Self-renewing cells that generate the main phenotypes of the nervous system in both the embryo and adult. Neural stem cells are precursors to both NEURONS and NEUROGLIA.

D058954.name: Pancreatic Stellate Cells
D058954.definition: Star-shaped, myofibroblast-like cells located in the periacinar, perivascular, and periductal regions of the EXOCRINE PANCREAS. They play a key role in the pathobiology of FIBROSIS; PANCREATITIS; and PANCREATIC CANCER.

D058955.name: Metalloids
D058955.definition: A class of nonmetals such as arsenic that have some of the chemical properties of a metal.

D058956.name: Administration, Mucosal
D058956.definition: Delivery of a drug or other substance into the body through the epithelium lining of MUCOUS MEMBRANE involved with absorption and secretion.

D058957.name: Coronavirus NL63, Human
D058957.definition: A species in the genus CORONAVIRUS causing upper and lower RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTIONS. It shares the receptor used by the SARS VIRUS.

D058958.name: Organs at Risk
D058958.definition: Organs which might be damaged during exposure to a toxin or to some form of therapy. It most frequently refers to healthy organs located in the radiation field during radiation therapy.

D058965.name: MART-1 Antigen
D058965.definition: A melanosome-specific protein that plays a role in the expression, stability, trafficking, and processing of GP100 MELANOMA ANTIGEN, which is critical to the formation of Stage II MELANOSOMES. The protein is used as an antigen marker for MELANOMA cells.

D058966.name: Contactins
D058966.definition: A family of immunoglobulin-related cell adhesion molecules that are involved in NERVOUS SYSTEM patterning.

D058967.name: Contactin 1
D058967.definition: A contactin subtype that is predominantly expressed in the CEREBELLUM; HIPPOCAMPUS; NEOCORTEX; and HYPOTHALAMUS.

D058968.name: Pythiosis
D058968.definition: A granulomatous disease caused by the aquatic organism PYTHIUM insidiosum and occurring primarily in horses, cattle, dogs, cats, fishes, and rarely in humans. It is classified into three forms: ocular, cutaneous, and arterial.

D058969.name: Contactin 2
D058969.definition: A contactin subtype that plays a role in axon outgrowth, axon fasciculation, and neuronal migration.

D058971.name: Tenotomy
D058971.definition: Surgical division of a tendon for relief of a deformity that is caused by congenital or acquired shortening of a muscle (Stedman, 27th ed). Tenotomy is performed in order to lengthen a muscle that has developed improperly, or become shortened and is resistant to stretching.

D058972.name: Folic Acid Transporters
D058972.definition: Proteins involved in the transport of FOLIC ACID and folate derivatives across the CELLULAR MEMBRANE.

D058973.name: Folate Receptors, GPI-Anchored
D058973.definition: Cell surface receptors that bind to and transport FOLIC ACID, 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, and a variety of folic acid derivatives. The receptors are essential for normal NEURAL TUBE development and transport folic acid via receptor-mediated endocytosis.

D058974.name: Phylogeography
D058974.definition: A field of study concerned with the principles and processes governing the geographic distributions of genealogical lineages, especially those within and among closely related species. (Avise, J.C., Phylogeography: The History and Formation of Species. Harvard University Press, 2000)

D058975.name: Folate Receptor 1
D058975.definition: A subtype of GPI-anchored folate receptors that is expressed in tissues of epithelial origin. This protein is also identified as an ovarian-tumor-specific antigen.

D058976.name: Folate Receptor 2
D058976.definition: A subtype of GPI-anchored folate receptors that is expressed in PLACENTA and hematopoietic cells.

D058977.name: Molecular Sequence Annotation
D058977.definition: The addition of descriptive information about the function or structure of a molecular sequence to its MOLECULAR SEQUENCE DATA record.

D058978.name: Reduced Folate Carrier Protein
D058978.definition: A ubiquitously expressed folic acid transporter that functions via an antiporter mechanism which is coupled to the transport of organic phosphates.

D058979.name: Proton-Coupled Folate Transporter
D058979.definition: A symporter protein that couples the transport of FOLIC ACID with HYDROGEN IONS. The transporter functions most effectively under acidic conditions.

D058980.name: Information Literacy
D058980.definition: The ability to recognize when information is needed and to locate, evaluate, and use the needed information effectively.

D058985.name: Side-Population Cells
D058985.definition: A group of cells identified on FLOW CYTOMETRY profiles as distinct from the main group of cells by their ability to extrude the fluorescent dye Hoechst 33342, often a characteristic property of less differentiated progenitor and STEM CELLS.

D058989.name: Vitrification
D058989.definition: The transformation of a liquid to a glassy solid i.e., without the formation of crystals during the cooling process.

D058990.name: Molecular Targeted Therapy
D058990.definition: Treatments with drugs which interact with or block synthesis of specific cellular components characteristic of the individual's disease in order to stop or interrupt the specific biochemical dysfunction involved in progression of the disease.

D058991.name: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
D058991.definition: An Act prohibiting a health plan from establishing lifetime limits or annual limits on the dollar value of benefits for any participant or beneficiary after January 1, 2014. It permits a restricted annual limit for plan years beginning prior to January 1, 2014. It provides that a health plan shall not be prevented from placing annual or lifetime per-beneficiary limits on covered benefits. The Act sets up a competitive health insurance market.

D058992.name: Social Participation
D058992.definition: Involvement in community activities or programs.

D058993.name: Oral Sprays
D058993.definition: Pharmacologic agents in the form of a mist or spray delivered into the body through the mouth.

D058994.name: Salpingectomy
D058994.definition: Excision of one or both of the FALLOPIAN TUBES.

D058995.name: Dry Powder Inhalers
D058995.definition: A device that delivers medication to the lungs in the form of a dry powder.

D058996.name: Quality Improvement
D058996.definition: The attainment or process of attaining a new level of performance or quality.

D058998.name: Remote Sensing Technology
D058998.definition: Observation and acquisition of physical data from a distance by viewing and making measurements from a distance or receiving transmitted data from observations made at distant location.

D058999.name: Drug-Seeking Behavior
D058999.definition: Activities performed to obtain licit or illicit substances.

D059000.name: El Nino-Southern Oscillation
D059000.definition: El Nino-Southern Oscillation or ENSO is a cycle of extreme alternating warm El Niño and cold La Nina events which is the dominant year-to-year climate pattern on Earth. Both terms refer to large-scale changes in sea-surface temperature across the eastern tropical Pacific. ENSO is associated with a heightened risk of certain vector-borne diseases. (From http://www.elnino.noaa.gov/lanina_new_faq.html, accessed 5/12/2020)

D059002.name: Androgen Receptor Antagonists
D059002.definition: Compounds that bind to and inhibit the activation of ANDROGEN RECEPTORS.

D059003.name: Topoisomerase Inhibitors
D059003.definition: Compounds that inhibit the activity of DNA TOPOISOMERASES.

D059004.name: Topoisomerase I Inhibitors
D059004.definition: Compounds that inhibit the activity of DNA TOPOISOMERASE I.

D059005.name: Topoisomerase II Inhibitors
D059005.definition: Compounds that inhibit the activity of DNA TOPOISOMERASE II. Included in this category are a variety of ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS which target the eukaryotic form of topoisomerase II and ANTIBACTERIAL AGENTS which target the prokaryotic form of topoisomerase II.

D059006.name: Chromosomes, Insect
D059006.definition: Structures within the CELL NUCLEUS of insect cells containing DNA.

D059007.name: Polytene Chromosomes
D059007.definition: Extra large CHROMOSOMES, each consisting of many identical copies of a chromosome lying next to each other in parallel.

D059008.name: Time-Lapse Imaging
D059008.definition: Recording serial images of a process at regular intervals spaced out over a longer period of time than the time in which the recordings will be played back.

D059009.name: Confederate States of America
D059009.definition: The area of those states which seceded in 1861 from the union of the United States of America. They include South Carolina, Mississippi, Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana, Texas, Virginia, Arkansas, North Carolina, and Tennessee.

D059010.name: Single-Cell Analysis
D059010.definition: Assaying the products of or monitoring various biochemical processes and reactions in an individual cell.

D059012.name: Lost to Follow-Up
D059012.definition: Study subjects in COHORT STUDIES whose outcomes are unknown e.g., because they could not or did not wish to attend follow-up visits.(from Dictionary of Epidemiology, 5th ed.)

D059013.name: Microbial Consortia
D059013.definition: A group of different species of microorganisms that act together as a community.

D059014.name: High-Throughput Nucleotide Sequencing
D059014.definition: Techniques of nucleotide sequence analysis that increase the range, complexity, sensitivity, and accuracy of results by greatly increasing the scale of operations and thus the number of nucleotides, and the number of copies of each nucleotide sequenced. The sequencing may be done by analysis of the synthesis or ligation products, hybridization to preexisting sequences, etc.

D059015.name: Wireless Technology
D059015.definition: Techniques using energy such as radio frequency, infrared light, laser light, visible light, or acoustic energy to transfer information without the use of wires, over both short and long distances.

D059016.name: Tumor Microenvironment
D059016.definition: The milieu surrounding neoplasms consisting of cells, vessels, soluble factors, and molecules, that can influence and be influenced by, the neoplasm's growth.

D059017.name: Primary Care Nursing
D059017.definition: Techniques or methods of patient care used by nurses as primary careproviders.

D059018.name: DNA Contamination
D059018.definition: The presence of DNA from a source foreign to the sample being analysed.

D059019.name: Clinical Coding
D059019.definition: Process of substituting a symbol or code for a term such as a diagnosis or procedure. (from Slee's Health Care Terms, 3d ed.)

D059020.name: Suicidal Ideation
D059020.definition: A risk factor for suicide attempts and completions, it is the most common of all suicidal behavior, but only a minority of ideators engage in overt self-harm.

D059021.name: Laboratory Proficiency Testing
D059021.definition: Assessments aimed at determining agreement in diagnostic test results among laboratories. Identical survey samples are distributed to participating laboratories, with results stratified according to testing methodologies.

D059022.name: Food Safety
D059022.definition: Activities involved in ensuring the safety of FOOD including avoidance of bacterial and other contamination.

D059027.name: Recycling
D059027.definition: The extraction and recovery of usable or valuable material from scrap or other discarded materials. (from McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed.)

D059028.name: Airports
D059028.definition: Terminal facilities used for aircraft takeoff and landing and including facilities for handling passengers. (from McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed.)

D059029.name: Electronic Waste
D059029.definition: Discarded electronic devices containing valuable and sometimes hazardous materials such as LEAD, NICKEL, CADMIUM, and MERCURY. (from http://www.epa.gov/osw/conserve/materials/ecycling/faq.htm#impact accessed 4/25/2010)

D059030.name: United States Department of Defense
D059030.definition: A cabinet department in the Executive Branch of the United States Government whose mission is to provide the military forces needed to deter WARFARE and to protect the security of our country.

D059031.name: Anticipation, Psychological
D059031.definition: The ability to foresee what is likely to happen on the basis of past experience. It is largely a frontal lobe function.

D059032.name: Learning Curve
D059032.definition: The course of learning of an individual or a group. It is a measure of performance plotted over time.

D059033.name: For-Profit Insurance Plans
D059033.definition: Health insurance plans that are intended to be for profit.

D059034.name: Not-For-Profit Insurance Plans
D059034.definition: Health insurance plans that are not intended to generate profit.

D059035.name: Perioperative Period
D059035.definition: The time periods immediately before, during and following a surgical operation.

D059036.name: Photographs
D059036.definition: Still images produced from radiation-sensitive materials (sensitive to light, electron beams, or nuclear radiation), generally by means of the chemical action of light on a sensitive film, paper, glass, or metal. Photographs may be positive or negative, opaque or transparent.

D059037.name: Doulas
D059037.definition: Trained lay women who provide emotional and/or physical support during obstetric labor and the postpartum period for mothers and their partners.

D059038.name: Black Sea
D059038.definition: An inland sea between Europe and Asia. It is connected with the Aegean Sea by the Bosporus, the Sea of Marmara, and the Dardanelles.

D059039.name: Standard of Care
D059039.definition: The minimum acceptable patient care, based on statutes, court decisions, policies, or professional guidelines.

D059040.name: Video-Audio Media
D059040.definition: Used with articles which include video files or clips, or for articles which are entirely video.

D059041.name: Plagiocephaly
D059041.definition: The condition characterized by uneven or irregular shape of the head often in parallelogram shape with a flat spot on the back or one side of the head. It can either result from the premature CRANIAL SUTURE closure (CRANIOSYNOSTOSIS) or from external forces (NONSYNOSTOTIC PLAGIOCEPHALY).

D059045.name: Chromosomal Puffs
D059045.definition: Regions along polytene chromosomes that are uncondensed and active in DNA REPLICATION or RNA transcription (GENETIC TRANSCRIPTION).

D059065.name: Medication Reconciliation
D059065.definition: The formal process of obtaining a complete and accurate list of each patient's current home medications including name, dosage, frequency, and route of administration, and comparing admission, transfer, and/or discharge medication orders to that list. The reconciliation is done to avoid medication errors.

D059066.name: Gross Domestic Product
D059066.definition: Value of all final goods and services produced in a country in one year.

D059085.name: Nasal Sprays
D059085.definition: Pharmacologic agents delivered into the nostrils in the form of a mist or spray.

D059125.name: Neanderthals
D059125.definition: Common name for an extinct species of the Homo genus. Fossils have been found in Europe and Asia. Genetic evidence suggests that limited interbreeding with modern HUMANS (Homo sapiens) took place.

D059126.name: Cronobacter
D059126.definition: A genus of gram-negative opportunistic foodborne pathogens.

D059127.name: Phyllobacteriaceae
D059127.definition: Family of gram-negative bacteria that occur in leaf nodules and the rhizosphere of higher plants.

D059128.name: Mesorhizobium
D059128.definition: A genus of gram-negative, rod-shaped bacteria in the family PHYLLOBACTERIACEAE. They are able to invade root-hairs of a wide range of plants, inciting the production of PLANT ROOT NODULES.

D059145.name: Total Disc Replacement
D059145.definition: The replacement of intervertebral discs in the spinal column with artificial devices. The procedure is done in the lumbar or cervical spine to relieve severe pain resulting from INTERVERTEBRAL DISC DEGENERATION.

D059146.name: Metastasectomy
D059146.definition: Surgery to remove one or more NEOPLASM METASTASES.

D059147.name: HIV Serosorting
D059147.definition: The practice of making choices about SEXUAL PARTNERS based on their HIV status.

D059165.name: Hormesis
D059165.definition: Biphasic dose responses of cells or organisms (including microorganisms) to an exogenous or intrinsic factor, in which the factor induces stimulatory or beneficial effects at low doses and inhibitory or adverse effects at high doses.

D059166.name: Osteology
D059166.definition: The branch of anatomy that concerns the structure and function of bones.

D059167.name: Mirror Neurons
D059167.definition: Neurons that fire when an animal acts or observes the same action of another thus coding the motor response. They were originally discovered in the premotor and parietal cortex of the monkey and studies have shown that neurons that have a similar mechanism are present in humans. Mirror neurons are theorized to be related to social cognition.

D059168.name: Carotid Intima-Media Thickness
