D059168.definition: A measurement of the thickness of the carotid artery walls. It is measured by B-mode ULTRASONOGRAPHY and is used as a surrogate marker for ATHEROSCLEROSIS.

D059186.name: Chemoradiotherapy, Adjuvant
D059186.definition: Combined chemotherapy and radiotherapy given to augment some other form of treatment such as surgery. It is commonly used in the therapy of cancer.

D059205.name: Renewable Energy
D059205.definition: Forms of energy that are constantly and rapidly renewed by natural processes such as solar, ocean wave, and wind energy. (from McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

D059206.name: Natural Gas
D059206.definition: A combustible, gaseous mixture of low-molecular weight PARAFFIN hydrocarbons, generated below the surface of the earth. It contains mostly METHANE and ETHANE with small amounts of PROPANE; BUTANES; and higher hydrocarbons, and sometimes NITROGEN; CARBON DIOXIDE; HYDROGEN SULFIDE; and HELIUM. (from McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

D059207.name: Geothermal Energy
D059207.definition: Thermal energy contained in the earth. It can be used directly to supply heat or converted to mechanical or electrical energy. (from McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

D059208.name: Parasite Load
D059208.definition: Measure of the number of the PARASITES present in a host organism.

D059225.name: Nociception
D059225.definition: Sensing of noxious mechanical, thermal or chemical stimuli by NOCICEPTORS. It is the sensory component of visceral and tissue pain (NOCICEPTIVE PAIN).

D059226.name: Nociceptive Pain
D059226.definition: Dull or sharp aching pain caused by stimulated NOCICEPTORS due to tissue injury, inflammation or diseases. It can be divided into somatic or tissue pain and VISCERAL PAIN.

D059227.name: Postsynaptic Potential Summation
D059227.definition: Physiological integration of multiple SYNAPTIC POTENTIAL signals to reach the threshold and initiate postsynaptic ACTION POTENTIALS. In spatial summation stimulations from additional synaptic junctions are recruited to generate s response. In temporal summation succeeding stimuli signals are summed up to reach the threshold. The postsynaptic potentials can be either excitatory or inhibitory (EPSP or IPSP).

D059228.name: Renal Nutcracker Syndrome
D059228.definition: Left RENAL VEIN compression between the AORTA, ABDOMINAL and the SUPERIOR MESENTERIC ARTERY. Variable symptoms include HYPERTENSION, RENOVASCULAR; HEMATURIA; and VARICOSE VEINS.

D059229.name: Osteotomy, Sagittal Split Ramus
D059229.definition: Sagittal sectioning and repositioning of the ramus of the MANDIBLE to correct a mandibular retrusion, MALOCCLUSION, ANGLE CLASS III; and PROGNATHISM. The oblique sectioning line consists of multiple cuts horizontal and vertical to the mandibular ramus.

D059230.name: Reflex, Trigeminocardiac
D059230.definition: Sudden occurrence of BRADYCARDIA or HEART ARREST induced by manipulations of the MAXILLARY NERVE AND MANDIBULAR NERVE during a craniomaxillofacial or oral surgery. It is the maxillary and mandibular variants of OCULOCARDIAC REFLEX.

D059232.name: Laboratory Personnel
D059232.definition: Professionals, technicians, and assistants staffing LABORATORIES.

D059245.name: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn
D059245.definition: Abnormal increase in RESPIRATORY RATE in the newborn. It is self-limiting and attributed to the delayed fetal lung fluid clearance often in CAESAREAN SECTION delivery.

D059247.name: Fertility Preservation
D059247.definition: A method of providing future reproductive opportunities before a medical treatment with known risk of loss of fertility. Typically reproductive organs or tissues (e.g., sperm, egg, embryos and ovarian or testicular tissues) are cryopreserved for future use before the medical treatment (e.g., chemotherapy, radiation) begins.

D059248.name: Chemoradiotherapy
D059248.definition: Treatment that combines chemotherapy with radiotherapy.

D059249.name: Otomycosis
D059249.definition: Fungus infection of the external ear, usually by ASPERGILLUS species

D059250.name: Administration, Metronomic
D059250.definition: Administration of low doses of a drug or a drug combination over prolonged periods of time usually at a regular interval.

D059265.name: Visceral Pain
D059265.definition: Pain originating from internal organs (VISCERA) associated with autonomic phenomena (PALLOR; SWEATING; NAUSEA; and VOMITING). It often becomes a REFERRED PAIN.

D059266.name: Bisphosphonate-Associated Osteonecrosis of the Jaw
D059266.definition: Necrotic jaws or other maxillofacial skeleton necrosis associated with bisphosphonate use (see BISPHOSPHONATES). Injury, dental procedures, and trauma can trigger the necrotic process.

D059267.name: Cardiomegaly, Exercise-Induced
D059267.definition: Heart enlargement and other remodeling in cardiac morphology and electrical circutry found in individuals who participate in intense repeated exercises.

D059268.name: Atrophic Vaginitis
D059268.definition: Inflammation of the vagina due to thinning of the vaginal wall and decreased lubrication associated with reduced estrogen levels at MENOPAUSE.

D059269.name: Chilaiditi Syndrome
D059269.definition: Interposition of a portion of the colon (e.g., SIGMOID COLON) between the liver and the diaphragm. It is associated with abdominal pain, vomiting, constipation, anorexia and volvulus. Chilaiditi anomaly refers to asymptomatic interposition.

D059285.name: Pregnancy, Twin
D059285.definition: The condition of carrying TWINS simultaneously.

D059286.name: Pregnancy, Triplet
D059286.definition: The condition of carrying TRIPLETS simultaneously.

D059287.name: Pregnancy, Quadruplet
D059287.definition: The condition of carrying QUADRUPLETS simultaneously.

D059288.name: Pregnancy, Quintuplet
D059288.definition: The condition of carrying QUINTUPLETS simultaneously.

D059289.name: Vascular Stiffness
D059289.definition: Loss of vascular ELASTICITY due to factors such as AGING; and ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. Increased arterial stiffness is one of the RISK FACTORS for many CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES.

D059290.name: Dopaminergic Neurons
D059290.definition: Neurons whose primary neurotransmitter is DOPAMINE.

D059325.name: Intra-Abdominal Hypertension
D059325.definition: Pathological elevation of intra-abdominal pressure (>12 mm Hg). It may develop as a result of SEPSIS; PANCREATITIS; capillary leaks, burns, or surgery. When the pressure is higher than 20 mm Hg, often with end-organ dysfunction, it is referred to as abdominal compartment syndrome.

D059326.name: Serotonergic Neurons
D059326.definition: Neurons whose primary neurotransmitter is SEROTONIN.

D059327.name: Brachydactyly
D059327.definition: Congenital anomaly of abnormally short fingers or toes.

D059328.name: Diffuse Noxious Inhibitory Control
D059328.definition: A physiological process by which the perception of pain at a local area of the body is inhibited by a second painful stimulus administered at a distal body site

D059329.name: Cholinergic Neurons
D059329.definition: Neurons whose primary neurotransmitter is ACETYLCHOLINE.

D059330.name: GABAergic Neurons
D059330.definition: Neurons whose primary neurotransmitter is GAMMA-AMINOBUTYRIC ACID.

D059331.name: Adrenergic Neurons
D059331.definition: Neurons whose primary neurotransmitter is EPINEPHRINE.

D059333.name: Central Nervous System Sensitization
D059333.definition: An increased response to stimulation that is mediated by amplification of signaling in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS).

D059345.name: Cerebral Small Vessel Diseases
D059345.definition: Pathological processes or diseases where cerebral MICROVESSELS show abnormalities. They are often associated with aging, hypertension and risk factors for lacunar infarcts (see LACUNAR INFARCTION); LEUKOARAIOSIS; and CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE.

D059346.name: Magnets
D059346.definition: Objects that produce a magnetic field.

D059347.name: Cardio-Renal Syndrome
D059347.definition: Condition where a primary dysfunction of either heart or kidney results in failure of the other organ (e.g., HEART FAILURE with worsening RENAL INSUFFICIENCY).

D059349.name: Urine Specimen Collection
D059349.definition: Methods or procedures used to obtain samples of URINE.

D059350.name: Chronic Pain
D059350.definition: Aching sensation that persists for more than a few months. It may or may not be associated with trauma or disease, and may persist after the initial injury has healed. Its localization, character, and timing are more vague than with acute pain.

D059351.name: Organ Sparing Treatments
D059351.definition: Techniques, procedures, and therapies carried out on diseased organs in such a way to avoid complete removal of the organ and preserve the remaining organ function.

D059352.name: Musculoskeletal Pain
D059352.definition: Discomfort stemming from muscles, LIGAMENTS, tendons, and bones.

D059365.name: Nonsense Mediated mRNA Decay
D059365.definition: An mRNA metabolic process that distinguishes a normal STOP CODON from a premature stop codon (NONSENSE CODON) and facilitates rapid degradation of aberrant mRNAs containing premature stop codons.

D059366.name: Asthma, Occupational
D059366.definition: Asthma attacks caused, triggered, or exacerbated by OCCUPATIONAL EXPOSURE.

D059367.name: RNA Cleavage
D059367.definition: A reaction that severs one of the sugar-phosphate linkages of the phosphodiester backbone of RNA. It is catalyzed enzymatically, chemically, or by radiation. Cleavage may be exonucleolytic, or endonucleolytic.

D059368.name: RNA Isoforms
D059368.definition: The different gene transcripts generated from a single gene by RNA EDITING or ALTERNATIVE SPLICING of RNA PRECURSORS.

D059369.name: Pott Puffy Tumor
D059369.definition: Infection of the FRONTAL BONE often as a complication of FRONTAL SINUSITIS or trauma to the frontal bone and skull. It is characterized by subperiosteal abscess with OSTEOMYELITIS.

D059370.name: RNA Folding
D059370.definition: The processes of RNA tertiary structure formation.

D059371.name: DNA, B-Form
D059371.definition: The most common form of DNA found in nature. It is a right-handed helix with 10 base pairs per turn, a pitch of 0.338 nm per base pair and a helical diameter of 1.9 nm.

D059372.name: Nucleotide Motifs
D059372.definition: Commonly observed BASE SEQUENCE or nucleotide structural components which can be represented by a CONSENSUS SEQUENCE or a SEQUENCE LOGO.

D059373.name: Mastodynia
D059373.definition: Pain in the breast generally classified as cyclical (associated with menstrual periods), or noncyclical, i.e. originating from the breast or nearby muscles or joints, ranging from minor discomfort to severely incapacitating.

D059385.name: Plyometric Exercise
D059385.definition: Exercises in which muscles are repeatedly and rapidly stretched, followed by shortening, concentric MUSCLE CONTRACTION (e.g. jumping and rebounding). They are designed to exert maximal force in minimal time by increasing STRETCH REFLEX.

D059386.name: Reverse Genetics
D059386.definition: The use of techniques that produce a functional MUTATION or an effect on GENE EXPRESSION of a specific gene of interest in order to identify the role or activity of the gene product of that gene.

D059387.name: Sphenopalatine Ganglion Block
D059387.definition: Method of treating pain associated with the sphenopalatine ganglion located in the PTERYGOPALATINE FOSSA, posterior to the middle nasal turbinate. The transnasal approach involves application of suitable local anesthetic to the mucous membrane overlying the ganglion.

D059388.name: Pelvic Girdle Pain
D059388.definition: Discomfort associated with the bones that make up the pelvic girdle. It occurs frequently during pregnancy.

D059390.name: Breakthrough Pain
D059390.definition: Acute pain that comes on rapidly despite the use of pain medication.

D059392.name: Petroleum Pollution
D059392.definition: Release of oil into the environment usually due to human activity.

D059405.name: Sun Protection Factor
D059405.definition: A measure of relative protection provided by SUNSCREENING AGENTS against burns due to ultraviolet (UV) radiation from a light source.

D059407.name: Pinguecula
D059407.definition: A yellowish thickened lesion on the conjunctiva near the CORNEA representing a benign degenerative change in the CONJUNCTIVA caused by the leakage and deposition of certain blood proteins through the permeable capillaries near the LIMBUS.

D059408.name: Pain Management
D059408.definition: A form of therapy that employs a coordinated and interdisciplinary approach for easing the suffering and improving the quality of life of those experiencing pain.

D059409.name: Stroke, Lacunar
D059409.definition: Stroke caused by lacunar infarction or other small vessel diseases of the brain. It features hemiparesis (see PARESIS), hemisensory, or hemisensory motor loss.

D059411.name: Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms
D059411.definition: Symptoms of disorders of the lower urinary tract including frequency, NOCTURIA; urgency, incomplete voiding, and URINARY INCONTINENCE. They are often associated with OVERACTIVE BLADDER; URINARY INCOMPETENCE; and INTERSTITIAL CYSTITIS. Lower urinary tract symptoms in males were traditionally called PROSTATISM.

D059413.name: Intraabdominal Infections
D059413.definition: Infection within the PERITONEAL CAVITY. A frequent cause is an ANASTOMOTIC LEAK following surgery.

D059425.name: Interferon-gamma Release Tests
D059425.definition: The assay of INTERFERON-GAMMA released from lymphocytes after their exposure to a specific test antigen, to check for IMMUNOLOGIC MEMORY resulting from a previous exposure to the antigen. The amount of interferon-gamma released is usually assayed by an ENZYME-LINKED IMMUNOSORBENT ASSAY.

D059445.name: Anhedonia
D059445.definition: Inability to experience pleasure due to impairment or dysfunction of normal psychological and neurobiological mechanisms. It is a symptom of many PSYCHOTIC DISORDERS (e.g., DEPRESSIVE DISORDER, MAJOR; and SCHIZOPHRENIA).

D059446.name: Heterotaxy Syndrome
D059446.definition: Abnormal thoracoabdominal VISCERA arrangement (visceral heterotaxy) or malformation that involves additional CONGENITAL HEART DEFECTS (e.g., heart isomerism; DEXTROCARDIA) and/or abnormal SPLEEN (e.g., asplenia and polysplenia). Irregularities with the central nervous system, the skeleton and urinary tract are often associated with the syndrome.

D059447.name: Cell Cycle Checkpoints
D059447.definition: Regulatory signaling systems that control the progression through the CELL CYCLE. They ensure that the cell has completed, in the correct order and without mistakes, all the processes required to replicate the GENOME and CYTOPLASM, and divide them equally between two daughter cells. If cells sense they have not completed these processes or that the environment does not have the nutrients and growth hormones in place to proceed, then the cells are restrained (or "arrested") until the processes are completed and growth conditions are suitable.

D059451.name: Biosimilar Pharmaceuticals
D059451.definition: BIOLOGIC PRODUCTS that are imitations but not exact replicas of innovator products.

D059466.name: White Coat Hypertension
D059466.definition: Phenomenon where BLOOD PRESSURE readings are elevated only when taken in clinical settings.

D059467.name: Transcriptome
D059467.definition: The pattern of GENE EXPRESSION at the level of genetic transcription in a specific organism or under specific circumstances in specific cells.

D059468.name: Masked Hypertension
D059468.definition: Phenomenon where increased BLOOD PRESSURE readings taken in non-clinical settings (e.g., HOME BLOOD PRESSURE MONITORING) do not replicate in clinical settings.

D059470.name: Tetraspanins
D059470.definition: A large superfamily of cell surface membrane proteins characterized by their four transmembrane domains. They play a role in a variety of processes such as cellular adhesion and motility. They may be involved in the organization of cell surface MEMBRANE MICRODOMAINS that regulate the activation of LEUKOCYTES.

D059471.name: In Vitro Oocyte Maturation Techniques
D059471.definition: Methods used to induce premature oocytes, that are maintained in tissue culture, to progress through developmental stages including to a stage that is competent to undergo FERTILIZATION.

D059472.name: Exome
D059472.definition: That part of the genome that corresponds to the complete complement of EXONS of an organism or cell.

D059485.name: Gastropexy
D059485.definition: Surgical fixation of the stomach to the abdominal wall.

D059505.name: Telomere Homeostasis
D059505.definition: Maintenance of TELOMERE length. During DNA REPLICATION, chromosome ends loose some of their telomere sequence (TELOMERE SHORTENING.) Various cellular mechanism are involved in repairing, extending, and recapping the telomere ends.

D059506.name: Telomere Shortening
D059506.definition: The loss of some TELOMERE sequence during DNA REPLICATION of the first several base pairs of a linear DNA molecule; or from DNA DAMAGE. Cells have various mechanisms to restore length (TELOMERE HOMEOSTASIS.) Telomere shortening is involved in the progression of CELL AGING.

D059525.name: Supraglottitis
D059525.definition: Inflammation of the EPIGLOTTIS and supraglottic structures including the PHARYNX; UVULA; base of tongue; and aryepiglottic folds. It is usually caused by HAEMOPHILUS INFLUENZAE in children but often by different organisms in adults.

D059526.name: Foraminotomy
D059526.definition: Surgical enlargement of the intervertebral foramina to relieve NERVE ROOT COMPRESSION.

D059545.name: Paraneoplastic Syndromes, Ocular
D059545.definition: Ocular manifestations secondary to various NEOPLASMS in which antibodies to antigens of the primary tumor cross-react with ocular antigens. This autoimmune response often leads to visual loss and other ocular dysfunctions.

D059546.name: Sinus Floor Augmentation
D059546.definition: Guided BONE TRANSPLANTATION of the MAXILLARY SINUS surface with a BONE SUBSTITUTE grafting. It increases the bone volume at the site of the DENTAL IMPLANT and helps stabilize it.

D059547.name: Stereocilia
D059547.definition: Mechanosensing organelles of hair cells which respond to fluid motion or fluid pressure changes. They have various functions in many different animals, but are primarily used in hearing.

D059549.name: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction
D059549.definition: Rebuilding of the ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT to restore functional stability of the knee. AUTOGRAFTING or ALLOGRAFTING of tissues is often used.

D059550.name: Toxicity Tests, Subchronic
D059550.definition: Experiments designed to determine the potential toxic effects of mid-term (a few months) exposure to a chemical or chemicals.

D059551.name: Toxicity Tests, Subacute
D059551.definition: Experiments designed to determine the potential toxic effects of a short-term (a few weeks) exposure to a chemical or chemicals.

D059552.name: Caves
D059552.definition: Geological formations consisting of underground enclosures with access from the surface.

D059565.name: G2 Phase Cell Cycle Checkpoints
D059565.definition: CELL CYCLE regulatory signaling systems that are triggered by DNA DAMAGE or lack of nutrients during G2 PHASE. When triggered they restrain cells transitioning from G2 phase to M PHASE.

D059566.name: M Phase Cell Cycle Checkpoints
D059566.definition: The cellular signaling system that halts the progression of cells through MITOSIS or MEIOSIS if a defect that will affect CHROMOSOME SEGREGATION is detected.

D059585.name: G1 Phase Cell Cycle Checkpoints
D059585.definition: Regulatory signaling systems that control the progression of the CELL CYCLE through the G1 PHASE and allow transition to S PHASE when the cells are ready to undergo DNA REPLICATION. DNA DAMAGE, or the deficiencies in specific cellular components or nutrients may cause the cells to halt before progressing through G1 phase.

D059586.name: Duddingtonia
D059586.definition: A genus of ascomycetous mitosporic fungi in the family Orbiliaceae. It is used for the biological control of nematodes in livestock.

D059587.name: Calcifying Nanoparticles
D059587.definition: Protein-mineral complexes that comprise substrates needed for the normal calcium-carbonate-phosphate homeostasis. Nanobacteria was the prior name for the particles which were originally thought to be microorganisms.

D059605.name: Dental Implant-Abutment Design
D059605.definition: The plan and delineation of DENTAL IMPLANT fitting with DENTAL ABUTMENT.

D059606.name: Polydipsia
D059606.definition: Excessive thirst manifested by excessive fluid intake. It is characteristic of many diseases such as DIABETES MELLITUS; DIABETES INSIPIDUS; and NEPHROGENIC DIABETES INSIPIDUS. The condition may be psychogenic in origin.

D059607.name: Polydipsia, Psychogenic
D059607.definition: A clinical disorder characterized by excessive fluid intake (polydipsia); HYPONATREMIA; and POLYURIA in SCHIZOPHRENIA and other psychiatric disorders. Impaired water metabolism in psychogenic polydipsia can result in WATER INTOXICATION.

D059608.name: Laryngocele
D059608.definition: Congenital anomalous dilitation of the laryngeal saccule that may extend internally into the airway or externally through the thyrohyoid membrane.

D059609.name: Mallory Bodies
D059609.definition: Cytoplasmic hyaline inclusions in HEPATOCYTES. They are associated with ALCOHOLIC STEATOHEPATITIS and non-alcoholic STEATOHEPATITIS, but are also present in benign and malignant hepatocellular neoplasms, and metabolic, toxic, and chronic cholestatic LIVER DISEASES.

D059611.name: Balamuthia mandrillaris
D059611.definition: A species of free-living soil amoeba in the family Balamuthiidae, causing AMEBIASIS and a deadly form of ENCEPHALITIS in humans.

D059625.name: Liquid-Liquid Extraction
D059625.definition: The removal of a soluble component from a liquid mixture by contact with a second liquid, immiscible with the carrier liquid, in which the component is preferentially soluble. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

D059629.name: Signal-To-Noise Ratio
D059629.definition: The comparison of the quantity of meaningful data to the irrelevant or incorrect data.

D059630.name: Mesenchymal Stromal Cells
D059630.definition: Bone-marrow-derived, non-hematopoietic cells that support HEMATOPOETIC STEM CELLS. They have also been isolated from other organs and tissues such as UMBILICAL CORD BLOOD, umbilical vein subendothelium, and WHARTON JELLY. These cells are considered to be a source of multipotent stem cells because they include subpopulations of mesenchymal stem cells.

D059631.name: Wharton Jelly
D059631.definition: Jelly-like connective tissue of the UMBILICAL CORD that contains MESENCHYMAL STROMAL CELLS.

D059645.name: Mutation Rate
D059645.definition: The number of mutations that occur in a specific sequence, GENE, or GENOME over a specified period of time such as years, CELL DIVISIONS, or generations.

D059646.name: Genome Size
D059646.definition: The amount of DNA (or RNA) in one copy of a genome.

D059647.name: Gene-Environment Interaction
D059647.definition: The combined effects of genotypes and environmental factors together on phenotypic characteristics.

D059648.name: Kisspeptins
D059648.definition: Intercellular signaling peptides that were originally characterized by their ability to suppress NEOPLASM METASTASIS. Kisspeptins have since been found to play an important role in the neuroendocrine regulation of REPRODUCTION.

D059665.name: Immunochromatography
D059665.definition: A type of affinity chromatography where ANTIBODIES are used in the affinity capture reaction on the solid support, in the mobile phase, or both.

D059666.name: Lysosomal-Associated Membrane Protein 3
D059666.definition: A lysosomal-associated membrane glycoprotein that is expressed at high levels in mature DENDRITIC CELLS.

D059685.name: Herniorrhaphy
D059685.definition: Surgical procedures undertaken to repair abnormal openings through which tissue or parts of organs can protrude or are already protruding.

D059705.name: Polar Bodies
D059705.definition: Minute cells produced during development of an OOCYTE as it undergoes MEIOSIS. A polar body contains one of the nuclei derived from the first or second meiotic CELL DIVISION. Polar bodies have practically no CYTOPLASM. They are eventually discarded by the oocyte. (from King & Stansfield, A Dictionary of Genetics, 4th ed)

D059706.name: Aliivibrio
D059706.definition: A genus of gram-negative, rod-shaped bacteria in the family VIBRIONACEAE. They are found in the marine environment often associated with animals.

D059707.name: Aliivibrio Infections
D059707.definition: Infections with bacteria of the genus ALIIVIBRIO.

D059708.name: Ultrasonic Surgical Procedures
D059708.definition: The use of HIGH-ENERGY SHOCK WAVES, in the frequency range of 20-60 kHz, to cut through or remove tissue. The tissue fragmentation by ultrasonic surgical instruments is caused by mechanical effects not heat as with HIGH-INTENSITY FOCUSED ULTRASOUND ABLATION.

D059725.name: Interactive Ventilatory Support
D059725.definition: Mechanical ventilation delivered to match the patient's efforts in breathing as detected by the interactive ventilation device.

D059745.name: Piezosurgery
D059745.definition: The use of HIGH-ENERGY SHOCK WAVES, in the frequency range of 20-30 kHz, to cut through mineralized tissue.

D059746.name: Heimlich Maneuver
D059746.definition: An emergency treatment commonly used to clear food and other foreign objects causing AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION.

D059747.name: Nasal Surgical Procedures
D059747.definition: Surgical operations on the nose and nasal cavity.

D059748.name: Proteolysis
D059748.definition: Cleavage of proteins into smaller peptides or amino acids either by PROTEASES or non-enzymatically (e.g., Hydrolysis). It does not include Protein Processing, Post-Translational.

D059765.name: Homologous Recombination
D059765.definition: An exchange of DNA between matching or similar sequences.

D059766.name: DNA End-Joining Repair
D059766.definition: The repair of DOUBLE-STRAND DNA BREAKS by rejoining the broken ends of DNA to each other directly.

D059767.name: Recombinational DNA Repair
D059767.definition: Repair of DNA DAMAGE by exchange of DNA between matching sequences, usually between the allelic DNA (ALLELES) of sister chromatids.

D059785.name: Karyotype
D059785.definition: The full set of CHROMOSOMES presented as a systematized array of METAPHASE chromosomes from a photomicrograph of a single CELL NUCLEUS arranged in pairs in descending order of size and according to the position of the CENTROMERE. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

D059786.name: Abnormal Karyotype
D059786.definition: A variation from the normal set of chromosomes characteristic of a species.

D059787.name: Acute Pain
D059787.definition: Intensely discomforting, distressful, or agonizing sensation associated with trauma or disease, with well-defined location, character, and timing.

D059788.name: Dried Blood Spot Testing
D059788.definition: Techniques for using whole blood samples collected on filter paper for a variety of clinical laboratory tests.

D059805.name: HLA-DR alpha-Chains
D059805.definition: Transmembrane proteins that form the alpha subunits of the HLA-DR antigens. They are also referred to as the HLA-DR heavy chains.

D059806.name: HLA-DR beta-Chains
D059806.definition: Transmembrane proteins that form the beta subunits of the HLA-DR antigens. They are also referred to as the HLA-DR light chains.

D059807.name: S Phase Cell Cycle Checkpoints
D059807.definition: Cell regulatory signaling system that controls progression through S PHASE and stabilizes the replication forks during conditions that could affect the fidelity of DNA REPLICATION, such as DNA DAMAGE or depletion of nucleotide pools.

D059808.name: Polyphenols
D059808.definition: A large class of organic compounds having more than one PHENOL group.

D059810.name: HLA-DR Serological Subtypes
D059810.definition: HLA-DR antigen subtypes that have been classified according to their affinity to specific ANTIBODIES. The DNA sequence analyses of HLA-DR ALPHA-CHAINS and HLA-DR BETA-CHAINS has for the most part revealed the specific alleles that are responsible for each serological subtype.

D059811.name: HLA-DRB1 Chains
D059811.definition: A subtype of HLA-DRB beta chains that includes over one hundred allele variants. The HLA-DRB1 subtype is associated with several of the HLA-DR SEROLOGICAL SUBTYPES.

D059825.name: Physical Therapists
D059825.definition: Persons trained in PHYSICAL THERAPY SPECIALTY to make use of PHYSICAL THERAPY MODALITIES to prevent, correct, and alleviate movement dysfunction.

D059826.name: HLA-DRB3 Chains
D059826.definition: A subtype of HLA-DRB beta chains that includes over 50 allelic variants. The HLA-DRB3 beta-chain subtype is associated with HLA-DR52 serological subtype.

D059827.name: Agricultural Inoculants
D059827.definition: Beneficial microorganisms (bacteria or fungi) encapsulated in carrier material and applied to the environment for remediation and enhancement of agricultural productivity.

D059845.name: HLA-DRB4 Chains
D059845.definition: A subtype of HLA-DRB beta chains that is associated with the HLA-DR53 serological subtype.

D059846.name: Analgesics, Short-Acting
D059846.definition: Pain-alleviating drugs characterized by rapid action time.

D059847.name: HLA-DRB5 Chains
D059847.definition: A subtype of HLA-DRB beta chains that is associated with the HLA-DR51 serological subtype.

D059848.name: HLA-DQ alpha-Chains
D059848.definition: Transmembrane proteins that form the alpha subunits of the HLA-DQ antigens.

D059865.name: Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress
D059865.definition: Various physiological or molecular disturbances that impair ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM function. It triggers many responses, including UNFOLDED PROTEIN RESPONSE, which may lead to APOPTOSIS; and AUTOPHAGY.

D059866.name: HLA-DQ beta-Chains
D059866.definition: Transmembrane proteins that form the beta subunits of the HLA-DQ antigens.

D059867.name: HLA-DP alpha-Chains
D059867.definition: Transmembrane proteins that form the alpha subunits of the HLA-DP antigens.

D059868.name: HLA-DP beta-Chains
D059868.definition: Transmembrane proteins that form the beta subunits of the HLA-DP antigens.

D059869.name: Radiostereometric Analysis
D059869.definition: Methods for performing three-dimensional measurement and motion analysis using stereoscopic radiographs.

D059870.name: HLA-A11 Antigen
D059870.definition: A specific HLA-A surface antigen subtype. Members of this subtype contain alpha chains that are encoded by the HLA-A*11 allele family.

D059871.name: HLA-A24 Antigen
D059871.definition: A specific HLA-A surface antigen subtype. Members of this subtype contain alpha chains that are encoded by the HLA-A*24 allele family.

D059885.name: Kasabach-Merritt Syndrome
D059885.definition: Rapidly growing vascular lesion along the midline axis of the neck, upper trunk, and extremities that is characterized by CONSUMPTION COAGULOPATHY; THROMBOCYTOPENIA; and HEMOLYTIC ANEMIA. It is often associated with infantile Kaposiform HEMANGIOENDOTHELIOMA and other vascular tumors such as tufted ANGIOMA.

D059905.name: Endocarditis, Non-Infective
D059905.definition: Formation of a non-infectious THROMBUS, referred to as vegetation, on previously undamaged ENDOCARDIUM. It usually occurs as a complication of connective-tissue diseases and cancers because of the associated hypercoagulable state (see THROMBOPHILIA).

D059906.name: Neuroimaging
D059906.definition: Non-invasive methods of visualizing the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM, especially the brain, by various imaging modalities.

D059907.name: Functional Neuroimaging
D059907.definition: Methods for visualizing REGIONAL BLOOD FLOW, metabolic, electrical, or other physiological activities in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM using various imaging modalities.

D059908.name: HLA-B13 Antigen
D059908.definition: A specific HLA-B surface antigen subtype. Members of this subtype contain alpha chains that are encoded by the HLA-B*13 allele family.

D059909.name: HLA-B14 Antigen
D059909.definition: A specific HLA-B surface antigen subtype. Members of this subtype contain alpha chains that are encoded by the HLA-B*14 allele family.

D059910.name: HLA-B15 Antigen
D059910.definition: A specific HLA-B surface antigen subtype. Members of this subtype contain alpha chains that are encoded by the HLA-B*15 allele family.

D059911.name: HLA-B18 Antigen
D059911.definition: A specific HLA-B surface antigen subtype. Members of this subtype contain alpha chains that are encoded by the HLA-B*18 allele family.

D059912.name: HLA-B37 Antigen
D059912.definition: A specific HLA-B surface antigen subtype. Members of this subtype contain alpha chains that are encoded by the HLA-B*37 allele family.

D059925.name: Anatomic Landmarks
D059925.definition: Reference points located by visual inspection, palpation, or computer assistance, that are useful in localizing structures on or within the human body.

D059945.name: HLA-B38 Antigen
D059945.definition: A specific HLA-B surface antigen subtype. Members of this subtype contain alpha chains that are encoded by the HLA-B*38 allele family.

D059946.name: HLA-B39 Antigen
D059946.definition: A specific HLA-B surface antigen subtype. Members of this subtype contain alpha chains that are encoded by the HLA-B*39 allele family.

D059947.name: HLA-B40 Antigen
D059947.definition: A specific HLA-B surface antigen subtype. Members of this subtype contain alpha chains that are encoded by the HLA-B*40 allele family.

D059948.name: HLA-B44 Antigen
D059948.definition: A specific HLA-B surface antigen subtype. Members of this subtype contain alpha chains that are encoded by the HLA-B*44 allele family.

D059949.name: HLA-B51 Antigen
D059949.definition: A specific HLA-B surface antigen subtype. Members of this subtype contain alpha chains that are encoded by the HLA-B*51 allele family.

D059950.name: HLA-B52 Antigen
D059950.definition: A specific HLA-B surface antigen subtype. Members of this subtype contain alpha chains that are encoded by the HLA-B*52 allele family.

D059951.name: HLA-G Antigens
D059951.definition: Class I human histocompatibility (HLA) surface antigens encoded by alleles on locus B of the HLA complex. The HLA-G antigens are considered non-classical class I antigens due to their distinct tissue distribution which differs from HLA-A; HLA-B; and HLA-C antigens. Note that several isoforms of HLA-G antigens result from alternative splicing of messenger RNAs produced from the HLA-G*01 allele.

D059952.name: Pelvic Floor Disorders
D059952.definition: Injury, weakening, or PROLAPSE of the pelvic muscles, surrounding connective tissues or ligaments (PELVIC FLOOR).

D059965.name: Merkel cell polyomavirus
D059965.definition: A species of POLYOMAVIRUS suspected to be the cause of most cases of MERKEL CELL CARCINOMA, a rare but highly lethal form of skin cancer.

D059985.name: Cryogels
D059985.definition: Macroporous hydrogels that are produced at subzero temperatures. Cryogels have pores that are produced by growing ice crystals and have been developed with a tissue-like elasticity that is suitable for cell immunization experiments.

D060005.name: Genotyping Techniques
D060005.definition: Methods used to determine individuals' specific ALLELES or SNPS (single nucleotide polymorphisms).

D060026.name: Endophytes
D060026.definition: An endosymbiont that is either a bacterium or fungus living part of its life in a plant. Endophytes can benefit host plants by preventing pathogenic organisms from colonizing them.

D060045.name: Genes, Modifier
D060045.definition: GENES with ALLELES that affect the PHENOTYPE associated with a nonallelic gene.

D060046.name: Maintenance Chemotherapy
D060046.definition: Treatment designed to help prevent a relapse of a disease following the successful primary treatments (INDUCTION CHEMOTHERAPY and CONSOLIDATION CHEMOTHERAPY) with a long-term low-dose drug therapy.

D060047.name: Reproductive Isolation
D060047.definition: Mechanisms that prevent different populations from exchanging genes (GENE FLOW), resulting in or maintaining GENETIC SPECIATION. It can either prevent mating to take place or ensure that any offspring produced is either inviable or sterile, thereby preventing further REPRODUCTION.

D060048.name: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphyses
D060048.definition: A developmental deformity in which the metaphysis of the FEMUR moves proximally and anteriorly away from FEMUR HEAD (epiphysis) at the upper GROWTH PLATE. It is most common in male adolescents and is associated with a greater risk of early OSTEOARTHRITIS of the hip.

D060049.name: Asymmetric Cell Division
D060049.definition: Unequal cell division that results in daughter cells of different sizes.

D060050.name: Angina, Stable
D060050.definition: Persistent and reproducible chest discomfort usually precipitated by a physical exertion that dissipates upon cessation of such an activity. The symptoms are manifestations of MYOCARDIAL ISCHEMIA.

D060051.name: Occupational Injuries
D060051.definition: Injuries sustained from incidents in the course of work-related activities.

D060052.name: Nasolabial Fold
D060052.definition: A skin crease on each side of the face that runs from the outer corners of the nose to the corner of the mouth. It is a common site of PLASTIC SURGERY.

D060053.name: Transplant Donor Site
D060053.definition: The body location or part from which tissue is taken for TRANSPLANTATION.

D060054.name: Agrobacterium
D060054.definition: A genus of gram negative, aerobic, rod-shaped bacteria found in soil, plants, and marine mud.

D060066.name: Protein Interaction Maps
D060066.definition: Graphs representing sets of measurable, non-covalent physical contacts with specific PROTEINS in living organisms or in cells.

D060085.name: Coinfection
D060085.definition: Simultaneous infection of a host organism by two or more pathogens. In virology, coinfection commonly refers to simultaneous infection of a single cell by two or more different viruses.

D060086.name: Hydrothermal Vents
D060086.definition: Hot springs on the ocean floor. They are commonly found near volcanically active places such as mid-oceanic ridges.

D060105.name: Animal Shells
D060105.definition: The hard rigid covering of animals including MOLLUSCS; TURTLES; INSECTS; and crustaceans.

D060106.name: Lakes
D060106.definition: Inland bodies of still or slowly moving FRESH WATER or salt water, larger than a pond, and supplied by RIVERS and streams.

D060125.name: Characiformes
D060125.definition: An order of fresh water fish with 18 families and over 1600 species. The order includes CHARACINS, hatchetfish, piranhas, and TETRAS.

D060126.name: Characidae
D060126.definition: A family of fresh water fish in the order CHARACIFORMES, which includes the Tetras.

D060127.name: Kangaroo-Mother Care Method
D060127.definition: A method of continuously holding a partially wrapped baby to the chest, involving skin-to-skin contact. Originally it was a method of caring for LOW-BIRTH-WEIGHT INFANT in developing countries and is now more widespread in developed nations. Aside from encouraging breast feeding, the extra sleep that the infant gets assists in regulating body temperature, helps the baby conserve energy, and redirects calorie expenditures toward growth and weight gain.

D060145.name: Text Messaging
D060145.definition: Communication between CELL PHONE users via the Short Message Service protocol which allows the interchange of short written messages.

D060146.name: Ecotype
D060146.definition: Geographic variety, population, or race, within a species, that is genetically adapted to a particular habitat. An ecotype typically exhibits phenotypic differences but is capable of interbreeding with other ecotypes.

D060148.name: HapMap Project
D060148.definition: A coordinated international effort to identify and catalog patterns of linked variations (HAPLOTYPES) found in the human genome across the entire human population.

D060149.name: Antigens, CD63
D060149.definition: Ubiquitously-expressed tetraspanin proteins that are found in late ENDOSOMES and LYSOSOMES and have been implicated in intracellular transport of proteins.

D060151.name: B-Lymphocytes, Regulatory
D060151.definition: B-cells that have a role in regulating the immune response including the production of CYTOKINES. This function is in addition to their traditional role in making antibodies.

D060152.name: V(D)J Recombination
D060152.definition: The process by which the V (variable), D (diversity), and J (joining) segments of IMMUNOGLOBULIN GENES or T-CELL RECEPTOR GENES are assembled during the development of LYMPHOID CELLS using NONHOMOLOGOUS DNA END-JOINING.

D060165.name: Uroplakins
D060165.definition: Specialized membrane glycoproteins that are found on UROTHELIUM cells. They associate into a hexagonal array of 16-nm cell surface particles which form the asymmetric unit membrane of urothelial plaques.

D060166.name: Capillary Tubing
D060166.definition: Hollow cylindrical objects with an internal diameter that is small enough to fill by and hold liquids inside by CAPILLARY ACTION.

D060167.name: Uroplakin Ia
D060167.definition: A tetraspanin domain-containing uroplakin subtype. It heterodimerizes with UROPLAKIN II to form a component of the asymmetric unit membrane found in urothelial cells.

D060168.name: Thymocytes
D060168.definition: HEMATOPOIETIC PROGENITOR CELLS that have migrated to the THYMUS where they differentiate into T-LYMPHOCYTES. Thymocytes are classified into maturational stages based on the expression of CELL SURFACE ANTIGENS.

D060169.name: Uroplakin Ib
D060169.definition: A tetraspanin domain-containing uroplakin subtype. It heterodimerizes with UROPLAKIN III to form a component of the asymmetric unit membrane found in urothelial cells.

D060170.name: Uroplakin II
D060170.definition: A uroplakin subtype that heterodimerizes with UROPLAKIN IA to form a component of the asymmetric unit membrane found in urothelial cells.

D060171.name: Uroplakin III
D060171.definition: A uroplakin subtype that heterodimerizes with UROPLAKIN IB to form a component of the asymmetric unit membrane found in urothelial cells.

D060172.name: Morpholinos
D060172.definition: Synthetic analogs of NUCLEIC ACIDS composed of morpholine ring derivatives (MORPHOLINES) linked by phosphorodimidates. One standard DNA nucleic acid base (ADENINE; GUANINE; CYTOSINE; OR THYMINE) is bound to each morpholine ring.

D060185.name: Antigens, CD151
D060185.definition: Tetraspanin proteins found associated with LAMININ-binding INTEGRINS. The CD151 antigens may play a role in the regulation of CELL MOTILITY.

D060186.name: Infusions, Spinal
D060186.definition: The administration of medication by insertion of a tiny needle or catheter into the spinal sac or epidural cavity.

D060205.name: Therapeutic Occlusion
D060205.definition: Methods used to temporarily or permanently block the flow of BODY FLUIDS through various ducts and tubules throughout the body, including BLOOD VESSELS and LYMPHATIC VESSELS such as by THERAPEUTIC EMBOLIZATION or LIGATION.

D060225.name: Antigens, CD81
D060225.definition: Tetraspanin proteins that are involved in a variety of cellular functions including BASEMENT MEMBRANE assembly, and in the formation of a molecular complexes on the surface of LYMPHOCYTES.

D060226.name: Head Kidney
D060226.definition: A primitive form of vertebrate kidney that is found in adults of some primitive FISHES and in the embryos of more advanced fishes. In some species of fishes it contains phagocytic cells and is also a major site of HEMATOPOIESIS, analogous to the mammalian BONE MARROW.

D060227.name: Imaginal Discs
D060227.definition: Hollow sacs of cells in LARVA that form adult structures in insects during BIOLOGICAL METAMORPHOSIS.

D060245.name: Antigens, CD9
D060245.definition: A subtype of tetraspanin proteins that play a role in cell adhesion, cell motility, and tumor metastasis. CD9 antigens take part in the process of platelet activation and aggregation, the formation of paranodal junctions in neuronal tissue, and the fusion of sperm with egg.

D060265.name: Antigens, CD53
D060265.definition: Tetraspanin proteins found at high levels in cells of the lymphoid-myeloid lineage. CD53 antigens may be involved regulating the differentiation of T-LYMPHOCYTES and the activation of B-LYMPHOCYTES.

D060285.name: Receptors, Autocrine Motility Factor
D060285.definition: Cell surface receptors for AUTOCRINE MOTILITY FACTOR, which is the secreted form of GLUCOSE-6-PHOSPHATE ISOMERASE. The receptor has an unusual composition in that it shares some structural similarities with G-PROTEIN-COUPLED RECEPTORS and functions as an ubiquitin protein ligase when internalized.

D060305.name: Transition to Adult Care
D060305.definition: Transfer from pediatric to adult care.

D060306.name: Magnetometry
D060306.definition: The measurement of various aspects of MAGNETIC FIELDS.

D060326.name: Chemistry Techniques, Synthetic
D060326.definition: Methods used for the chemical synthesis of compounds. Included under this heading are laboratory methods used to synthesize a variety of chemicals and drugs.

D060327.name: Solid-Phase Synthesis Techniques
D060327.definition: Techniques used to synthesize chemicals using molecular substrates that are bound to a solid surface. Typically a series of reactions are conducted on the bound substrate that results in either the covalent attachment of specific moieties or the modification of existing function groups. These techniques offer an advantage to those involving solution reactions in that the substrate compound does not have to be isolated and purified between the reaction steps.

D060328.name: Magnetic Phenomena
D060328.definition: Characteristics, properties, and effects of magnetic substances and magnetic fields.

D060329.name: Education of Visually Disabled
D060329.definition: The teaching or training of those individuals with visual disability.

D060345.name: Education of Hearing Disabled
D060345.definition: The teaching or training of those individuals with hearing disability or impairment.

D060347.name: Sodium-Coupled Vitamin C Transporters
D060347.definition: Membrane transport proteins that actively co-transport ASCORBIC ACID and sodium ions across the CELL MEMBRANE. Dietary absorption of VITAMIN C is highly dependent upon this class of transporters and a subset of SODIUM GLUCOSE TRANSPORTERS which transport the oxidized form of vitamin C, DEHYDROASCORBIC ACID.

D060348.name: Dirofilaria repens
D060348.definition: A filarial parasite primarily affecting dogs and cats, but causing an emerging zoonosis in humans involving subcutaneous lesions. It is transmitted by MOSQUITOES.

D060365.name: Chloroplast Proteins
D060365.definition: Proteins encoded by the CHLOROPLAST GENOME or proteins encoded by the nuclear genome that are imported to and resident in the CHOROPLASTS.

D060366.name: Entomoplasmatales
D060366.definition: An order of nonhelical (ENTOMOPLASMATACEAE) and helical (SPIROPLASMATACEAE) gram-negative bacteria in the class MOLLICUTES, that are regularly associated with arthropod or plant hosts.

D060367.name: Lacazia
D060367.definition: A mitosporic ONYGENALES fungal genus. The species Lacazia loboi is the etiological agent of LOBOMYCOSIS in humans, dolphins, and other wild animals.

D060368.name: Lobomycosis
D060368.definition: A chronic, fungal, subcutaneous infection endemic in rural regions in South America and Central America. The causal organism is Lacazia labol.

D060386.name: Sex Workers
D060386.definition: People who engage in occupational sexual behavior in exchange for economic rewards or other extrinsic considerations.

D060387.name: Ascorbate Peroxidases
D060387.definition: Peroxidases that utilize ASCORBIC ACID as an electron donor to reduce HYDROGEN PEROXIDE to WATER. The reaction results in the production of monodehydroascorbic acid and DEHYDROASCORBIC ACID.

D060388.name: Support Vector Machine
D060388.definition: SUPERVISED MACHINE LEARNING algorithm which learns to assign labels to objects from a set of training examples. Examples are learning to recognize fraudulent credit card activity by examining hundreds or thousands of fraudulent and non-fraudulent credit card activity, or learning to make disease diagnosis or prognosis based on automatic classification of microarray gene expression profiles drawn from hundreds or thousands of samples.

D060389.name: Construction Industry
D060389.definition: The aggregate business enterprise of building.

D060405.name: Florigen
D060405.definition: Molecule produced in plant leaves that acts like a hormone by inducing flowering in the shoot apical meristem of buds and growing tips.

D060406.name: Brassinosteroids
D060406.definition: Plant steroids ubiquitously distributed throughout the plant kingdom. They play essential roles in modulating growth and differentiation of cells at nanomolar to micromolar concentrations.

D060425.name: Cerebral Phaeohyphomycosis
D060425.definition: CNS infections caused by neurotropic dematiaceous fungi that contain melanin in their cell walls. The infections often result in BRAIN ABSCESS; ENCEPHALITIS; and MENINGITIS in patients who are often immunocompetent. The common causative fungi include members Cladophialophora bantiana, Exophiala dermatitidis, Rhinocladiella mackenziei, and Ochroconis gallopavum. R. mackenziei infection is seen almost exclusively in patients from the MIDDLE EAST.

D060426.name: Anti-N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptor Encephalitis
D060426.definition: Disorder characterized by symptoms of CATATONIA; HYPOVENTILATION; DYSKINESIAS; ENCEPHALITIS; and SEIZURES followed by a reduced CONSCIOUSNESS. It is often followed by a viral-like prodrome. Many cases are self-limiting and respond well to IMMUNOMODULATORY THERAPIES against the NMDA RECEPTORS antibodies.

D060431.name: Thylakoid Membrane Proteins
D060431.definition: Proteins found within the THYLAKOID MEMBRANES of photosynthetic organisms such as PLANTS and PHYTOPLANKTON. Many of the proteins in this class are involved in the process of PHOTOSYNTHESIS and the generation of ADENOSINE TRIPHOSPHATE.

D060432.name: Anthropology, Medical
D060432.definition: Field of social science that is concerned with differences between human groups as related to health status and beliefs.

D060433.name: Administration, Ophthalmic
D060433.definition: Application of pharmaceutically active agents on the tissues of the EYE.

D060434.name: Herbivory
D060434.definition: The act of feeding on plants by animals.

D060436.name: Self-Incompatibility in Flowering Plants
D060436.definition: One of many different processes which occur in ANGIOSPERMS by which genetic diversity is maintained while INBREEDING is prevented.

D060437.name: Artificial Lens Implant Migration
D060437.definition: The shifting and or tilting of implanted artificial lens resulting in impaired vision.

D060446.name: Phaeohyphomycosis
D060446.definition: OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTIONS caused by the dematiaceous (darkly pigmented) MITOSPORIC FUNGI of ALTERNARIA, Bipolaris, CLADOSPORIUM, Curvularia, and EXOPHIALA. These fungi have pigmented HYPHAE due to MELANIN in the cell wall. The initial subcutaneous cyst from the infection can become systemic and spread rapidly to renal, pulmonary and cerebral systems (see CEREBRAL PHAEOHYPHOMYCOSIS) in an IMMUNOCOMPROMISED HOST.

D060447.name: Emergency Shelter
D060447.definition: Temporary shelter provided in response to a major disaster or emergency.

D060449.name: Wnt Signaling Pathway
D060449.definition: A complex signaling pathway whose name is derived from the DROSOPHILA Wg gene, which when mutated results in the wingless phenotype, and the vertebrate INT gene, which is located near integration sites of MOUSE MAMMARY TUMOR VIRUS. The signaling pathway is initiated by the binding of WNT PROTEINS to cells surface WNT RECEPTORS which interact with the AXIN SIGNALING COMPLEX and an array of second messengers that influence the actions of BETA CATENIN.

D060465.name: Axin Signaling Complex
D060465.definition: A specific complex of WNT SIGNALING PATHWAY proteins that mediates the phosphorylation-dependent destruction of cytosolic BETA-CATENIN. The complex is disrupted by cell surface binding of WNT PROTEINS, which allows beta-catenin levels to rise to the point where they migrate to the CELL NUCLEUS and activate transcription.

D060466.name: Axin Protein
D060466.definition: A scaffolding protein that is a critical component of the axin signaling complex which binds to ADENOMATOUS POLYPOSIS COLI PROTEIN; GLYCOGEN SYNTHASE KINASE 3; and CASEIN KINASE I.

D060467.name: Disease Resistance
D060467.definition: The capacity of an organism to defend itself against pathological processes or the agents of those processes. This most often involves innate immunity whereby the organism responds to pathogens in a generic way. The term disease resistance is used most frequently when referring to plants.

D060485.name: Pedobacter
D060485.definition: A genus of gram-negative, aerobic, rod-shaped bacteria in the family Sphingobacteriaceae. They exhibit gliding motility.

D060486.name: Ophthalmoplegic Migraine
D060486.definition: Childhood-onset of recurrent headaches with an oculomotor cranial nerve palsy. Typically, ABDUCENS NERVE; OCULOMOTOR NERVE; and TROCHLEAR NERVE are involved with DIPLOPIA and BLEPHAROPTOSIS.

D060487.name: Alternariosis
D060487.definition: Opportunistic fungal infection by a member of ALTERNARIA genus.

D060488.name: Low Density Lipoprotein Receptor-Related Protein-6
D060488.definition: An LDL-receptor related protein that combines with cell surface FRIZZLED RECEPTORS to form WNT PROTEIN-binding receptors. The protein plays an important role in the WNT SIGNALING PATHWAY during EMBRYONIC DEVELOPMENT and in regulation of vascular cell proliferation.

D060490.name: Receptors, Wnt
D060490.definition: Cell-surface receptors that specifically bind to WNT PROTEINS and activate the WNT SIGNALING PATHWAY.

D060492.name: Low Density Lipoprotein Receptor-Related Protein-5
D060492.definition: LDL-receptor related protein that combines with FRIZZLED RECEPTORS at the cell surface to form receptors that bind WNT PROTEINS. The protein plays an important role in the WNT SIGNALING PATHWAY in OSTEOBLASTS and during EMBRYONIC DEVELOPMENT.

D060493.name: Tenacibaculum
D060493.definition: A genus of gram-negative, rod-shaped bacteria in the family FLAVOBACTERIACEAE. Tenacibaculum adheres to surfaces of marine organisms and is pathogenic to fish.

D060494.name: Riemerella
D060494.definition: A genus of gram-negative, rod-shaped bacteria in the family FLAVOBACTERIACEAE that causes exudative SEPTICEMIA in ducks, pigeons, and other domestic and wild birds.

D060508.name: Wnt3 Protein
D060508.definition: A Wnt protein subtype that plays a role in cell-cell signaling during EMBRYONIC DEVELOPMENT and the morphogenesis of the developing NEURAL TUBE. Defects in Wnt3 protein are associated with autosomal recessive tetra-AMELIA in humans.

D060509.name: Wnt3A Protein
D060509.definition: A Wnt protein subtype that plays a role in cell-cell signaling during EMBRYONIC DEVELOPMENT and the morphogenesis of the developing NEURAL TUBE.

D060525.name: Pudendal Nerve
D060525.definition: A nerve which originates in the sacral spinal cord (S2 to S4) and innervates the PERINEUM, the external GENITALIA, the external ANAL SPHINCTER and the external urethral sphincter. It has three major branches: the perineal nerve, inferior anal nerves, and the dorsal nerve of penis or clitoris.

D060526.name: Magnetic Fields
D060526.definition: Areas of attractive or repulsive force surrounding MAGNETS.

D060527.name: Corneal Keratocytes
D060527.definition: Fibroblasts which occur in the CORNEAL STROMA.

D060528.name: Wnt4 Protein
D060528.definition: A Wnt protein that is involved in regulating multiple developmental processes such as the formation of the KIDNEY; ADRENAL GLANDS; MAMMARY GLANDS; the PITUITARY GLAND; and the female reproductive system. Defects in WNT4 are a cause of ROKITANSKY KUSTER HAUSER SYNDROME.

D060545.name: Pudendal Neuralgia
D060545.definition: Pain associated with a damaged PUDENDAL NERVE. Clinical features may include positional pain with sitting in the perineal and genital areas, sexual dysfunction and FECAL INCONTINENCE and URINARY INCONTINENCE.

D060565.name: Argonaute Proteins
D060565.definition: A family of RNA-binding proteins that has specificity for MICRORNAS and SMALL INTERFERING RNA molecules. The proteins take part in RNA processing events as core components of RNA-induced silencing complex.

D060585.name: Fusariosis
D060585.definition: OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTIONS with the soil fungus FUSARIUM. Typically the infection is limited to the nail plate (ONYCHOMYCOSIS). The infection can however become systemic especially in an IMMUNOCOMPROMISED HOST (e.g., NEUTROPENIA) and results in cutaneous and subcutaneous lesions, fever, KERATITIS, and pulmonary infections.

D060586.name: Trichosporonosis
D060586.definition: Fungal infections caused by TRICHOSPORON that may become systemic especially in an IMMUNOCOMPROMISED HOST. Clinical manifestations range from superficial cutaneous infections to systemic lesions in multiple organs.

D060587.name: Groundwater
D060587.definition: Liquid water present beneath the surface of the earth.

D060588.name: LIM Domain Proteins
D060588.definition: A large class of structurally-related proteins that contain one or more LIM zinc finger domains. Many of the proteins in this class are involved in intracellular signaling processes and mediate their effects via LIM domain protein-protein interactions. The name LIM is derived from the first three proteins in which the motif was found: LIN-11, Isl1 and Mec-3.

D060589.name: Zyxin
D060589.definition: A zinc-binding phosphoprotein that concentrates at focal adhesions and along the actin cytoskeleton. Zyxin has an N-terminal proline-rich domain and three LIM domains in its C-terminal half.

D060605.name: Hyalohyphomycosis
D060605.definition: OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTIONS caused by a heterogeneous group of MITOSPORIC FUNGI with clear (hyalo-) HYPHAE in the host. Common causative agents include ACREMONIUM; ASPERGILLUS; CHRYSOSPORIUM; FUSARIUM; PAECILOMYCES; PENICILLIUM; PSEUDALLESCHERIA; SCEDOSPORIUM; and SCOPULARIOPSIS. Normally a dermatomycoses, it can become invasive in the IMMUNOCOMPROMISED HOST.

D060645.name: Scopulariopsis
D060645.definition: A mitosporic fungal genus commonly found in soil. It includes both saprophytes and animal pathogens. Scopulariopsis brevicaulis and related species may convert ARSENIC to volatile and toxic arsine. ONYCHOMYCOSIS and rarely BRAIN ABSCESS; MYCETOMA, and disseminated infections mainly in the IMMUNOCOMPROMISED HOSTS are associated with Scopulariopsis.

D060666.name: Airway Extubation
D060666.definition: Removal of an endotracheal tube from the patient.

D060685.name: Sense of Coherence
D060685.definition: A view of the world and the individual's environment as comprehensible, manageable, and meaningful, claiming that the way people view their life has a positive influence on their health.

D060705.name: Dyscalculia
D060705.definition: Impaired ability in numerical concepts. These inabilities arise as a result of primary neurological lesion, are syndromic (e.g., GERSTMANN SYNDROME ) or acquired due to brain damage.

D060725.name: Uterine Retroversion
D060725.definition: A condition in which the UTERUS is found tilted backward toward the spine. The uterus is more commonly found in a straight vertical or anteverted (tipped forward) position. Although retroverted uterus is a normal variant position without symptoms, it is sometimes associated with pain, discomfort and other pregnancy complications.

D060726.name: Torso
D060726.definition: The central part of the body to which the neck and limbs are attached.

D060728.name: Reproductive Health
D060728.definition: The physical condition of human reproductive systems.

D060729.name: Coal Ash
D060729.definition: Residue generated from combustion of coal or petroleum.

D060730.name: Glomerular Filtration Barrier
D060730.definition: A specialized barrier in the kidney, consisting of the fenestrated CAPILLARY ENDOTHELIUM; GLOMERULAR BASEMENT MEMBRANE; and glomerular epithelium (PODOCYTES). The barrier prevents the filtration of PLASMA PROTEINS.

D060731.name: Emergency Responders
D060731.definition: Personnel trained to provide the initial services, care, and support in EMERGENCIES or DISASTERS.

D060733.name: Electromagnetic Radiation
D060733.definition: Waves of oscillating electric and MAGNETIC FIELDS which move at right angles to each other and outward from the source.

D060734.name: Nacre
D060734.definition: A biomineral consisting of layers of crystalized ARAGONITE, separated by interlamellar layers of organic matrix containing beta-CHITIN, and surrounded by an intercrystalline organic membrane of silk fibroin. Nacre is the iridescent substance better known as mother-of-pearl that is secreted by MOLLUSCS.

D060735.name: Pharmacovigilance
D060735.definition: The detection of long and short term side effects of conventional and traditional medicines through research, data mining, monitoring, and evaluation of healthcare information obtained from healthcare providers and patients.

D060737.name: Reproductive Tract Infections
D060737.definition: Infections of the genital tract in females or males. They can be caused by endogenous, iatrogenic, or sexually transmitted organisms.

D060739.name: Phonons
D060739.definition: Quanta of acoustic energy which move at the speed of sound.

D060740.name: Disease Eradication
D060740.definition: Termination of all transmission of infection by global extermination of the infectious agent through surveillance and containment (From Porta, A Dictionary of Epidemiology, 5th ed).

D060745.name: Gingival Retraction Techniques
D060745.definition: Techniques used to expose dental surface below the gingival margin in order to obtain better dental impression during periodental and peri-implant applications. The retraction of the gingival tissue can be achieved surgically (e.g., laser gingivectomy and rotary curettage) or chemically with a retraction cord.

D060746.name: Endoplasmic Reticulum-Associated Degradation
D060746.definition: A degradation process whereby incorrectly folded proteins are selectively transported out of the ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM and into the CYTOSOL. The misfolded proteins are subsequently ubiquitinated and degraded by the PROTEASOME.

D060747.name: Fetal Globulins
D060747.definition: Specialized proteins that are preferentially expressed during FETAL DEVELOPMENT.

D060748.name: Fetuins
D060748.definition: A family of calcium-binding alpha-globulins that are synthesized in the LIVER and play an essential role in maintaining the solubility of CALCIUM in the BLOOD. In addition the fetuins contain aminoterminal cystatin domains and are classified as type 3 cystatins.

D060749.name: alpha-2-HS-Glycoprotein
D060749.definition: A fetuin subtype that is synthesized by HEPATOCYTES and secreted into the circulation. It plays a major role in preventing CALCIUM precipitation in the BLOOD.

D060750.name: Bone Anteversion
D060750.definition: Malalignment of a bone in which its head and neck is rotated excessively forward or inward.

D060751.name: Bone Retroversion
D060751.definition: Attachment of a bone in which its head and neck is rotated excessively backward.

D060752.name: Fetuin-B
D060752.definition: A fetuin subtype that is closely-related to ALPHA-2-HS-GLYCOPROTEIN. Although fetuin-B binds calcium, it is a minor component of SERUM and therefore it may not play a primary role in preventing serum calcium phosphate precipitation.

D060753.name: Water Quality
D060753.definition: A rating of a body of water based on measurable physical, chemical, and biological characteristics.

D060754.name: Equol
D060754.definition: A non-steroidal ESTROGEN generated when soybean products are metabolized by certain bacteria in the intestines.

D060755.name: Germ Theory of Disease
D060755.definition: The fundamental tenet of modern medicine that certain diseases are caused by microorganisms. It was confirmed by the work of Pasteur, Lister, and Koch.

D060756.name: Social Networking
D060756.definition: Individuals connecting by family, work or other interests. It also includes connectivity facilitated by computer-based communications.

D060765.name: Secretoglobins
D060765.definition: A structurally-related family of small, multimeric proteins that are secreted in the mucosa of mammalian epithelial tissues. A variety of proteins are classed under this heading including some secretoglobin subtypes that appear unique to a particular mammalian species, and others whose functions differ between species.

D060766.name: Drinking Water
D060766.definition: Water that is intended to be ingested.

D060785.name: Mammaglobin A
D060785.definition: A secretoglobin that is produced by the MAMMARY GLAND of HUMANS and may be involved in the binding of ANDROGENS and other STEROIDS. The expression of this protein in normal breast epithelium and in human breast cancer has made it an important histological marker.

D060786.name: Holy Roman Empire
D060786.definition: Realm in central Europe consisting of a confederation of German and Italian territories under the suzerainty of an emperor and existing from the 9th or 10th century to 1806.

D060787.name: Neoplasm Grading
D060787.definition: Methods which attempt to express in replicable terms the level of CELL DIFFERENTIATION in neoplasms as increasing ANAPLASIA correlates with the aggressiveness of the neoplasm.

D060788.name: Mammaglobin B
D060788.definition: A MAMMAGLOBIN A-related secretoglobin that is expressed in several HUMAN tissues including the UTERUS; BREAST; SALIVARY GLAND; and LACRIMAL GLAND.

D060789.name: Prostatein
D060789.definition: A secreted prostate-specific protein which can bind non-polar steroids, cholesterol and a group of small, proline-rich peptides. The protein is specifically found in RATS and comprises three distinct secretoglobin-related subunits referred to as prostatic steroid-binding protein C1, C2 and C3.

D060805.name: Performance Anxiety
D060805.definition: Anxiety related to the execution of a task. (Campbell's Psychiatric Dictionary, 9th ed.)

D060807.name: Bioluminescence Resonance Energy Transfer Techniques
D060807.definition: Techniques for determining the proximity of molecules based on ENERGY TRANSFER between bioluminescent chromophores and acceptor fluorophores that have overlapping emission and absorption spectra.

D060825.name: Mild Cognitive Impairment
D060825.definition: A prodromal phase of cognitive decline that may precede the emergence of ALZHEIMER DISEASE and other dementias. It may include impairment of cognition, such as impairments in language, visuospatial awareness, ATTENTION and MEMORY.

D060826.name: Cementoplasty
D060826.definition: Injection of BONE CEMENTS into bone to treat bone lesions.

D060828.name: Induction Chemotherapy
D060828.definition: Initial drug treatment designed to bring about REMISSION INDUCTION. It is typically a short-term and high-dose drug treatment that is followed by CONSOLIDATION CHEMOTHERAPY and then MAINTENANCE CHEMOTHERAPY.

D060829.name: Arthropod Proteins
D060829.definition: Proteins synthesized by organisms belonging to the phylum ARTHROPODA. Included in this heading are proteins from the subdivisions ARACHNIDA; CRUSTACEA; and HORSESHOE CRABS. Note that a separate heading for INSECT PROTEINS is listed under this heading.

D060830.name: Consolidation Chemotherapy
D060830.definition: Drug treatment designed to further diminish the disease toward complete remission following INDUCTION CHEMOTHERAPY. It helps to consolidate the gains during induction chemotherapy and may be followed by MAINTENANCE CHEMOTHERAPY.

D060831.name: Hand-Foot Syndrome
D060831.definition: Chemotherapy-induced dermal side effects that are associated with the use of various CYTOSTATIC AGENTS. Symptoms range from mild ERYTHEMA and/or PARESTHESIA to severe ulcerative dermatitis with debilitating pain involving typically palmoplantar and intertriginous areas. These cutaneous manifestations are sometimes accompanied by nail anomalies.

D060832.name: Apomixis
D060832.definition: Asexual reproduction resulting in the formation of viable seeds from FLOWERS without fertlization (i.e. use of POLLEN). Progeny plants produced from apomictic seeds are perfect clones of the parent.

D060833.name: Cellular Microenvironment
D060833.definition: Local surroundings with which cells interact by processing various chemical and physical signals, and by contributing their own effects to this environment.

D060845.name: Obsessive Hoarding
D060845.definition: Persistent difficulty discarding or parting with possessions, regardless of the value of these possessions. Epidemiological studies suggest that hoarding occurs in 2-5% of the population and can lead to substantial distress and disability, as well as serious public health consequences.

D060846.name: Cell Engineering
D060846.definition: Methods and techniques used to modify or select cells and develop conditions for growing cells for biosynthetic production of molecules (METABOLIC ENGINEERING), for generation of tissue structures and organs in vitro (TISSUE ENGINEERING), or for other BIOENGINEERING research objectives.

D060847.name: Metabolic Engineering
D060847.definition: Methods and techniques used to genetically modify cells' biosynthetic product output and develop conditions for growing the cells as BIOREACTORS.

D060848.name: Agatoxins
D060848.definition: A class of polyamine and peptide toxins which are isolated from the venom of spiders such as Agelenopsis aperta.

D060850.name: LIM-Homeodomain Proteins
D060850.definition: A subclass of LIM domain proteins that include an additional centrally-located homeodomain region that binds AT-rich sites on DNA. Many LIM-homeodomain proteins play a role as transcriptional regulators that direct cell fate.

D060851.name: Gulf of Mexico
D060851.definition: A body of water located at the southeastern corner of North America. It is bordered by the states to the north of Florida, Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana, Texas; by five Mexican states to the west: Tamaulipas, Veracruz, Tabasco, Campeche, Yucatan; and by Cuba to the southeast.

D060865.name: Repetition Priming
D060865.definition: A type of procedural memory manifested as a change in the ability to identify an item as a result of a previous encounter with the item or stimuli.

D060866.name: Accountable Care Organizations
D060866.definition: Organizations of health care providers that agree to be accountable for the quality, cost, and overall care of Medicare beneficiaries who are enrolled in the traditional fee-for-service program who are assigned to it. Assigned means those beneficiaries for whom the professionals in the organization provide the bulk of primary care services. (www.cms.gov/OfficeofLegislation/Downloads/Accountable CareOrganization.pdf accessed 03/16/2011)

D060867.name: Facilitated Tucking
D060867.definition: A method of soothing PREMATURE INFANTS during POSTNATAL CARE. It involves holding the infant's arms and legs in flexed positions close to the midline of the TORSO.

D060885.name: Multiplex Polymerase Chain Reaction
D060885.definition: Methods for using more than one primer set in a polymerase chain reaction to amplify more than one segment of the target DNA sequence in a single reaction.

D060887.name: B7 Antigens
D060887.definition: A family of cell-surface proteins found on ANTIGEN-PRESENTING CELLS. B7 antigens are ligands for specific cell surface receptor subtypes found on T-CELLS. They play an immunomodulatory role by stimulating or inhibiting the T-CELL activation process.

D060888.name: Real-Time Polymerase Chain Reaction
D060888.definition: Methods used for detecting the amplified DNA products from the polymerase chain reaction as they accumulate instead of at the end of the reaction.

D060889.name: Inducible T-Cell Co-Stimulator Protein
D060889.definition: A costimulatory receptor that is specific for INDUCIBLE T-CELL CO-STIMULATOR LIGAND. The receptor is associated with a diverse array of immunologically-related effects including the increased synthesis of INTERLEUKIN 10 in REGULATORY T-LYMPHOCYTES and the induction of PERIPHERAL TOLERANCE.

D060890.name: Antigens, CD274
D060890.definition: An inhibitory B7 antigen that has specificity for the T-CELL receptor PROGRAMMED CELL DEATH 1 PROTEIN. CD274 antigen provides negative signals that control and inhibit T-cell responses and is found at higher than normal levels on tumor cells, suggesting its potential role in TUMOR IMMUNE EVASION.

D060891.name: Root Cause Analysis
D060891.definition: Multi-step systematic review process used for improving safety by investigation of incidents to find what happened, why it happened, and to determine what can be done to prevent it from happening again.

D060905.name: Coxa Vara
D060905.definition: Hip deformity in which the femoral neck leans forward resulting in a decrease in the angle between femoral neck and its shaft. It may be congenital often syndromic, acquired, or developmental.

D060906.name: Coxa Valga
D060906.definition: Hip deformity in which the angle between the femoral neck and its shaft is increased. It may be congenital, acquired, or developmental.

D060907.name: V-Set Domain-Containing T-Cell Activation Inhibitor 1
D060907.definition: A B7 antigen subtype that inhibits the costimulation of T-cell activation, proliferation, cytokine production and development of cytotoxicity. The over expression of this protein in a variety of tumor cell types suggests its role in TUMOR IMMUNE EVASION.

D060908.name: CTLA-4 Antigen
D060908.definition: An inhibitory T CELL receptor that is closely related to CD28 ANTIGEN. It has specificity for CD80 ANTIGEN and CD86 ANTIGEN and acts as a negative regulator of peripheral T cell function. CTLA-4 antigen is believed to play role in inducing PERIPHERAL TOLERANCE.

D060909.name: Economics, Behavioral
D060909.definition: The combined discipline of psychology and economics that investigates what happens in markets in which some of the agents display human limitations and complications.

D060910.name: Pronephros
D060910.definition: The primordial kidney that develops from the INTERMEDIATE MESODERM in the embryos of vertebrates, and is succeeded by the MESONEPHROS. In higher vertebrates and humans, the pronephros is a vestigial and transient structure.

D060926.name: Remuneration
D060926.definition: Payment for a service or for a commodity such as a body part.

D060945.name: Inducible T-Cell Co-Stimulator Ligand
D060945.definition: A B7 antigen that binds specifically to INDUCIBLE T-CELL CO-STIMULATOR PROTEIN on T-CELLS. It provides a costimulatory signal for T-cell proliferation and cytokine secretion.

D060946.name: Pharmaceutical Services, Online
D060946.definition: Pharmacy services accessed via electronic means.

D060965.name: Clonal Evolution
D060965.definition: The process of accumulation of genetic and epigenetic changes over time in individual cells and the effect of the changes on CELL PROLIFERATION.

D060966.name: Clonal Selection, Antigen-Mediated
D060966.definition: LYMPHOCYTE ACTIVATION by a specific ANTIGEN thus triggering clonal expansion of LYMPHOCYTES already capable of mounting an immune response to the antigen.

D060985.name: Natural Springs
D060985.definition: Water that emerges to the surface of the earth from underground.

D060986.name: Water Wells
D060986.definition: Constructions built to access underground water.

D061005.name: Ponds
D061005.definition: Inland bodies of standing FRESHWATER usually smaller than LAKES. They can be man-made or natural but there is no universal agreement as to their exact size. Some consider a pond to be a small body of water that is shallow enough for sunlight to reach the bottom.

D061006.name: Bays
D061006.definition: An area of water mostly surrounded by land, usually smaller than a gulf, and affording access to the sea.

D061025.name: Costimulatory and Inhibitory T-Cell Receptors
D061025.definition: A family of receptors that modulate the activation of T-LYMPHOCYTES by the T-CELL ANTIGEN RECEPTOR. The receptors are responsive to one or more B7 ANTIGENS found on ANTIGEN-PRESENTING CELLS and, depending upon the specific ligand-receptor combination, modulate a variety of T-cell functions such as the rate of clonal expansion, CELL SURVIVAL and cytokine production. Although commonly referred to as costimulatory receptors, some of the receptors have inhibitory effects such as inducing PERIPHERAL TOLERANCE.

D061026.name: Programmed Cell Death 1 Receptor
D061026.definition: An inhibitory T-lymphocyte receptor that has specificity for CD274 ANTIGEN and PROGRAMMED CELL DEATH 1 LIGAND 2 PROTEIN. Signaling by the receptor limits T cell proliferation and INTERFERON GAMMA synthesis. The receptor also may play an essential role in the regulatory pathway that induces PERIPHERAL TOLERANCE.

D061027.name: Programmed Cell Death 1 Ligand 2 Protein
D061027.definition: A costimulatory B7 antigen that has specificity for the T-CELL receptor PROGRAMMED CELL DEATH 1 RECEPTOR. It is closely-related to CD274 antigen; however, its expression is restricted to DENDRITIC CELLS and activated MACROPHAGES.

D061028.name: Trigger Points
D061028.definition: Discrete spots in taut bands of muscle that produce local and referred pain when muscle bands are compressed.

D061046.name: Biological Control Agents
D061046.definition: Organisms, biological agents, or biologically-derived agents used strategically for their positive or adverse effect on the physiology and/or reproductive health of other organisms.

D061065.name: Polyketides
D061065.definition: Natural compounds containing alternating carbonyl and methylene groups (beta-polyketones), bioenergenetically derived from repeated condensation of acetyl coenzyme A via malonyl coenzyme A, in a process similar to fatty acid synthesis.

D061066.name: Plant Pathology
D061066.definition: The study of infectious diseases associated with plants.

D061067.name: Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized
D061067.definition: Antibodies from non-human species whose protein sequences have been modified to make them nearly identical with human antibodies. If the constant region and part of the variable region are replaced, they are called humanized. If only the constant region is modified they are called chimeric. INN names for humanized antibodies end in -zumab.

D061085.name: Agenesis of Corpus Callosum
D061085.definition: Birth defect that results in a partial or complete absence of the CORPUS CALLOSUM. It may be isolated or a part of a syndrome (e.g., AICARDI'S SYNDROME; ACROCALLOSAL SYNDROME; ANDERMANN SYNDROME; and HOLOPROSENCEPHALY). Clinical manifestations include neuromotor skill impairment and INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY of variable severity.

D061086.name: NADP Transhydrogenase, B-Specific
D061086.definition: A NADP transhydrogenase subtype found in certain types of BACTERIA. This transhydrogenase uses a mechanism that transfers hydrogen to the B side of the NAD(+) or NADP(+) ring structure.

D061087.name: NADP Transhydrogenase, AB-Specific
D061087.definition: A NADP transhydrogenase subtype found in certain types of BACTERIA and mammalian MITOCHONDRIA. This transhydrogenase uses a mechanism that can transfer hydrogen to either side, A or B, of the NAD(+) or NADP(+) ring structure.
