In heart mitochondria, the enzyme is A-specific with respect to NAD(+) and B-specific with respect to NADP(+).

D061088.name: Photoacoustic Techniques
D061088.definition: Investigative and diagnostic methods and procedures based on the photoacoustic effect, which is the generation of SOUND WAVES from the absorption of ELECTROMAGNETIC RADIATION.

D061089.name: Radiotherapy, Image-Guided
D061089.definition: The use of pre-treatment imaging modalities to position the patient, delineate the target, and align the beam of radiation to achieve optimal accuracy and reduce radiation damage to surrounding non-target tissues.

D061105.name: Peroxiredoxin III
D061105.definition: A THIOREDOXIN-dependent hydroperoxidase that is localized in the mitochondrial matrix. The enzyme plays a crucial role in protecting mitochondrial components from elevated levels of HYDROGEN PEROXIDE.

D061106.name: Radiotherapy Setup Errors
D061106.definition: Mistakes committed in the preparations for radiotherapy, including errors in positioning of patients, alignment radiation beams, or calculation of radiation doses.

D061107.name: Nucleoside Diphosphate Kinase D
D061107.definition: A nucleoside diphosphate kinase subtype that is localized to the intermembrane space of MITOCHONDRIA. It is believed to play a role in the synthesis of triphosphonucleotides using ATP formed through OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION.

D061108.name: Social Media
D061108.definition: Platforms that provide the ability and tools to create and publish information accessed via the INTERNET. Generally these platforms have three characteristics with content user generated, high degree of interaction between creator and viewer, and easily integrated with other sites.

D061125.name: Genes, Chloroplast
D061125.definition: Those nucleic acid sequences that function as units of heredity which are located within the CHLOROPLAST DNA.

D061145.name: Microvascular Decompression Surgery
D061145.definition: Surgery performed to relieve pressure from MICROVESSELS that are located around nerves and are causing NERVE COMPRESSION SYNDROMES.

D061146.name: Chlorophyll Binding Proteins
D061146.definition: A large family of proteins that have been traditionally classified as the light-harvesting proteins of the photosynthetic reaction complex. Chlorophyll binding proteins are also found in non-photosynthetic settings where they may play a photoprotective role in response to light stress.

D061147.name: Therapy with Helminths
D061147.definition: The treatment of immune system diseases by deliberate infestation with helminths. This therapy is partly based on the HYGIENE HYPOTHESIS which states that the absence of parasites increases immune dysregulation because of the lack of stimulation of REGULATORY T-CELLS.

D061148.name: Hygiene Hypothesis
D061148.definition: The theory that infectious agents, symbiotic microorganisms, and parasites are normal stimulants for the maturation of the immune system toward a balanced immune response. The theory predicts that lack of such stimulation leads to allergies and AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES.

D061149.name: Thysanoptera
D061149.definition: An order of very small, fringed-wing INSECTS including many agricultural pests.

D061165.name: Glenoid Cavity
D061165.definition: A depression in the lateral angle of the scapula that articulates with the head of the HUMERUS.

D061166.name: Peripheral Tolerance
D061166.definition: The mechanism, in peripheral lymphoid organs (LYMPH NODES; SPLEEN; TONSILS; and mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue), that prevents mature lymphocytes from reacting to SELF-ANTIGENS. This is accomplished through a variety of means including CLONAL ANERGY and CLONAL DELETION.

D061167.name: Central Tolerance
D061167.definition: The mechanism, in central lymphoid organs (THYMUS; BONE MARROW), that prevents immature lymphocytes from reacting to SELF-ANTIGENS. This is accomplished by CLONAL ANERGY and CLONAL DELETION.

D061185.name: Mechanical Thrombolysis
D061185.definition: Procedures to cause the disintegration of THROMBI by physical interventions.

D061186.name: Breast Milk Expression
D061186.definition: The act of evacuating BREAST MILK by hand or with a pump.

D061205.name: Vascular Calcification
D061205.definition: Deposition of calcium into the blood vessel structures. Excessive calcification of the vessels are associated with ATHEROSCLEROTIC PLAQUES formation particularly after MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION (see MONCKEBERG MEDIAL CALCIFIC SCLEROSIS) and chronic kidney diseases which in turn increase VASCULAR STIFFNESS.

D061206.name: Neoplasm Micrometastasis
D061206.definition: Newly arising secondary tumors so small they are difficult to detect by physical examination or routine imaging techniques.

D061207.name: Calcium Ionophores
D061207.definition: Chemical agents that increase the permeability of CELL MEMBRANES to CALCIUM ions.

D061208.name: Pulsed Radiofrequency Treatment
D061208.definition: The application, via IMPLANTED ELECTRODES, of short bursts of electrical energy in the radiofrequency range, interspersed with pauses in delivery of the current long enough to dissipate the generated heat and avoid heat-induced tissue necrosis.

D061209.name: Proton Ionophores
D061209.definition: Chemical agents that increase the permeability of CELL MEMBRANES to PROTONS.

D061210.name: Sodium Ionophores
D061210.definition: Chemical agents that increase the permeability of CELL MEMBRANES to SODIUM ions.

D061212.name: Memory, Episodic
D061212.definition: Type of declarative memory, consisting of personal memory in contrast to general knowledge.

D061213.name: Mortality, Premature
D061213.definition: Deaths that occur before LIFE EXPECTANCY is reached within a given population.

D061214.name: Patient Safety
D061214.definition: Efforts to reduce risk, to address and reduce incidents and accidents that may negatively impact healthcare consumers.

D061215.name: Energy Drinks
D061215.definition: Beverages consumed as stimulants and tonics. They usually contain a combination of CAFFEINE with other substances such as herbal supplements; VITAMINS; AMINO ACIDS; and sugar or sugar derivatives.

D061216.name: Potassium Ionophores
D061216.definition: Chemical agents that increase the permeability of CELL MEMBRANES to POTASSIUM ions.

D061217.name: Weight Reduction Programs
D061217.definition: Services providing counseling and activities that help overweight individuals to attain a more healthy body weight.

D061218.name: Depressive Disorder, Treatment-Resistant
D061218.definition: Failure to respond to two or more trials of antidepressant monotherapy or failure to respond to four or more trials of different antidepressant therapies. (Campbell's Psychiatric Dictionary, 9th ed.)

D061219.name: Olfactory Nerve Injuries
D061219.definition: Traumatic injuries to the OLFACTORY NERVE. It may result in various olfactory dysfunction including a complete loss of smell.

D061220.name: Oculomotor Nerve Injuries
D061220.definition: Traumatic injuries to the OCULOMOTOR NERVE. This may result in various eye movement dysfunction.

D061221.name: Trigeminal Nerve Injuries
D061221.definition: Traumatic injuries to the TRIGEMINAL NERVE. It may result in extreme pain, abnormal sensation in the areas the nerve innervates on face, jaw, gums and tongue and can cause difficulties with speech and chewing. It is sometimes associated with various dental treatments.

D061222.name: Lingual Nerve Injuries
D061222.definition: Traumatic injuries to the LINGUAL NERVE. It may be a complication following dental treatments.

D061223.name: Vagus Nerve Injuries
D061223.definition: Traumatic injuries to the VAGUS NERVE. Because the vagus nerve innervates multiple organs, injuries in the nerve fibers may result in any gastrointestinal organ dysfunction downstream of the injury site.

D061224.name: Laryngeal Nerve Injuries
D061224.definition: Traumatic injuries to the LARYNGEAL NERVE.

D061226.name: Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Injuries
D061226.definition: Traumatic injuries to the RECURRENT LARYNGEAL NERVE that may result in vocal cord dysfunction.

D061227.name: Accessory Nerve Injuries
D061227.definition: Traumatic injuries to the ACCESSORY NERVE. Damage to the nerve may produce weakness in head rotation and shoulder elevation.

D061228.name: Hypoglossal Nerve Injuries
D061228.definition: Traumatic injuries to the HYPOGLOSSAL NERVE.

D061245.name: Axenic Culture
D061245.definition: Culture of an isolated organism free from any other associating or contaminating organisms.

D061247.name: Trochlear Nerve Injuries
D061247.definition: Traumatic injuries to the TROCHLEAR NERVE.

D061249.name: Batch Cell Culture Techniques
D061249.definition: Methods for cultivation of cells, usually on a large-scale, in a closed system for the purpose of producing cells or cellular products to harvest.

D061250.name: Transferrins
D061250.definition: A group of iron-binding proteins that tightly bind two ferrate ions along with two carbonate ions. They are found in the bodily fluids of vertebrates where they act as transport and storage molecules for iron.

D061251.name: Primary Cell Culture
D061251.definition: The initial culturing of cells derived directly from fresh TISSUES.

D061252.name: Feeder Cells
D061252.definition: Cells used in COCULTURE TECHNIQUES which support the growth of the other cells in the culture. Feeder cells provide auxillary substances including attachment substrates, nutrients, or other factors that are needed for growth in culture.

D061265.name: Biphasic Insulins
D061265.definition: An insulin preparation that is designed to provide immediate and long term glycemic control in a single dosage. Biphasic insulin typically contains a mixture of REGULAR INSULIN or SHORT-ACTING INSULIN combined with a LONG-ACTING INSULIN.

D061266.name: Insulin, Short-Acting
D061266.definition: Insulin derivatives and preparations that are designed to induce a rapid HYPOGLYCEMIC EFFECT.

D061267.name: Insulin Aspart
D061267.definition: Insulin that has been modified to contain an ASPARTIC ACID instead of a PROLINE at position 38 of the B-chain.

D061268.name: Insulin Lispro
D061268.definition: Insulin that has been modified so that the B-chain contains a LYSINE at position 28 instead of a PROLINE and a PROLINE at position 29 instead of a LYSINE. It is used to manage BLOOD GLUCOSE levels in patients with TYPE 2 DIABETES.

D061269.name: DNA Transformation Competence
D061269.definition: The ability of bacterial cells to take up exogenous DNA and be genetically transformed by it.

D061270.name: Nasal Septal Perforation
D061270.definition: An opening or hole in the NASAL SEPTUM that is caused by TRAUMA, injury, drug use, or pathological process.

D061271.name: Acidobacteria
D061271.definition: A physiologically diverse phylum of acidophilic, gram-negative bacteria found in a wide variety of habitats, but particularly abundant in soils and sediments.

D061285.name: Vestibulocochlear Nerve Injuries
D061285.definition: Traumatic injuries to the VESTIBULOCOCHLEAR NERVE.

D061286.name: Osmometry
D061286.definition: Measurement of the OSMOLARITY of solutions or BODY FLUIDS.

D061287.name: Glossopharyngeal Nerve Injuries
D061287.definition: Traumatic injuries to the GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL NERVE.

D061305.name: Lymphoscintigraphy
D061305.definition: Radionuclide imaging of the LYMPHATIC SYSTEM.

D061306.name: Fibrobacteres
D061306.definition: A phylum of gram-negative bacteria closely related to the BACTEROIDETES. Species have been found in the gastrointestinal tracts of animals, especially termites, though indications are that species are more broadly distributed in other environments.

D061307.name: Human Umbilical Vein Endothelial Cells
D061307.definition: Endothelial cells that line venous vessels of the UMBILICAL CORD.

D061325.name: Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer Syndrome
D061325.definition: Autosomal dominant HEREDITARY CANCER SYNDROME in which a mutation most often in either BRCA1 or BRCA2 is associated with a significantly increased risk for breast and ovarian cancers.

D061326.name: Index of Orthodontic Treatment Need
D061326.definition: A dental health survey developed to evaluate a patient's orthodontic treatment need and priority for orthodontic care. The index is based on an assessment of degree of MALOCCLUSION and the potential aesthetic and dental health benefit of the treatment under consideration.

D061327.name: Verrucomicrobia
D061327.definition: A phylum of gram-negative bacteria containing seven class-level groups from a wide variety of environments. Most members are chemoheterotrophs.

D061328.name: Planctomycetales
D061328.definition: A order of gram-negative bacteria whose members are found in a variety of aquatic habitats as well as animal hosts.

D061329.name: Oil and Gas Fields
D061329.definition: Areas of the earth where hydrocarbon deposits of PETROLEUM and/or NATURAL GAS are located.

D061330.name: Multidetector Computed Tomography
D061330.definition: Types of spiral computed tomography technology in which multiple slices of data are acquired simultaneously improving the resolution over single slice acquisition technology.

D061345.name: Early Medical Intervention
D061345.definition: Action taken to reduce susceptibility or exposure to health problems and to detect and treat disease in early stages.

D061346.name: Laser Capture Microdissection
D061346.definition: Techniques using a laser to cut away and harvest a specific cell or cluster of cells from a tissue section while viewing it under the microscope.

D061347.name: Forgiveness
D061347.definition: Excusing or pardoning for an offense or release of anger or resentment.

D061348.name: Medical Chaperones
D061348.definition: Individuals who are present as a third party during medical encounters such as physical examination by a healthcare professional of an individual of the opposite sex.

D061349.name: Unrelated Donors
D061349.definition: Providers of tissues for transplant to non-related individuals.

D061350.name: Sympatry
D061350.definition: In evolutionary theory, overlapping geographic distribution of diverging species. In sympatric GENETIC SPECIATION, genetic diversion occurs without geographic separation.

D061351.name: Telescopes
D061351.definition: Instruments used to observe distant objects.

D061352.name: Pasteurization
D061352.definition: Treatment of food with physical methods such as heat, high pressure, radiation, or electric current to destroy organisms that cause disease or food spoilage.

D061354.name: Acinar Cells
D061354.definition: Cells lining the saclike dilatations known as acini of various glands or the lungs.

D061365.name: Amish
D061365.definition: An ethnic group with shared religious beliefs. Originating in Switzerland in the late 1600s, and first migrating to the mid-Atlantic, they now live throughout Eastern and Mid-Western United States and elsewhere. Communities are usually close-knit and marriage is within the community.

D061366.name: Numbers Needed To Treat
D061366.definition: Number of patients who need to be treated in order to prevent one additional bad outcome. It is the inverse of Absolute Risk Reduction.

D061385.name: Insulins
D061385.definition: Peptide hormones that cause an increase in the absorption of GLUCOSE by cells within organs such as LIVER, MUSCLE and ADIPOSE TISSUE. During normal metabolism insulins are produced by the PANCREATIC BETA CELLS in response to increased GLUCOSE. Natural and chemically-modified forms of insulin are also used in the treatment of GLUCOSE METABOLISM DISORDERS such as DIABETES MELLITUS.

D061386.name: Insulin, Regular, Human
D061386.definition: Regular insulin preparations that contain the HUMAN insulin peptide sequence.

D061387.name: Chlamydial Pneumonia
D061387.definition: Pneumonia caused by infections with the genus CHLAMYDIA; and CHLAMYDOPHILA, usually with CHLAMYDOPHILA PNEUMONIAE.

D061388.name: Firefighters
D061388.definition: Professional or volunteer members of a fire department who are trained to suppress fire and respond to related emergency.

D061389.name: Insulin, Regular, Pork
D061389.definition: Regular insulin preparations that contain the SUS SCROFA insulin peptide sequence.

D061405.name: Insulin, Lente
D061405.definition: An insulin, zinc chloride preparation in the form of a suspension of crystals and amorphous material in a ratio of approximately 7:3. Typically, lente insulin has a duration of activity that lasts between 13-20 hours after dosage.

D061406.name: Insulin, Ultralente
D061406.definition: A preparation of insulin and zinc chloride in the form of a crystalline suspension. Typically the duration of ultralente insulin activity lasts between 18-30 hours after dosage.

D061466.name: Lopinavir
D061466.definition: An HIV protease inhibitor used in a fixed-dose combination with RITONAVIR. It is also an inhibitor of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP3A.

D061485.name: Tobacco Use Cessation Products
D061485.definition: Items used to aid in ending a TOBACCO habit.

D061505.name: Cell Surface Display Techniques
D061505.definition: Techniques utilizing cells that express RECOMBINANT FUSION PROTEINS engineered to translocate through the CELL MEMBRANE and remain attached to the outside of the cell.

D061525.name: Perforator Flap
D061525.definition: A mass of tissue for transplantation that includes the skin and/or the SUBCUTANEOUS FAT, and the perforating blood vessel that traverses the underlying tissue to supply blood to the skin. Perforator flaps are named after the anatomical region or muscle from where they are transplanted and/or the perforating blood vessel.

D061545.name: Carbonated Water
D061545.definition: Water naturally or artificially infused with CARBON DIOXIDE.

D061565.name: Cycloaddition Reaction
D061565.definition: Synthetic organic reactions that use reactions between unsaturated molecules to form cyclical products.

D061566.name: Voltage-Gated Sodium Channels
D061566.definition: A family of membrane proteins that selectively conduct SODIUM ions due to changes in the TRANSMEMBRANE POTENTIAL DIFFERENCE. They typically have a multimeric structure with a core alpha subunit that defines the sodium channel subtype and several beta subunits that modulate sodium channel activity.

D061567.name: Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel Blockers
D061567.definition: A class of drugs that inhibit the activation of VOLTAGE-GATED SODIUM CHANNELS.

D061585.name: Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel Agonists
D061585.definition: Compounds that either stimulate the opening or prevent closure of VOLTAGE-GATED SODIUM CHANNELS.

D061605.name: Administration, Intravenous
D061605.definition: Delivery of substances through VENIPUNCTURE into the VEINS.

D061625.name: Immunoreceptor Tyrosine-Based Activation Motif
D061625.definition: A conserved AMINO ACID SEQUENCE located in the intracellular domains of a family of transmembrane proteins involved in various IMMUNE RESPONSES. The CONSENSUS SEQUENCE of this motif is YXXL(or I)X(6-8)YXXL(or I) (where X denotes any amino acid). When phosphorylated ITAM motifs provide docking sites for PROTEIN TYROSINE KINASES of the Syk family thus forming signaling complexes which lead to activation of immune responses.

D061626.name: Immunoreceptor Tyrosine-Based Inhibition Motif
D061626.definition: A conserved AMINO ACID SEQUENCE located in the intracellular domains of a family of transmembrane proteins that negatively regulate the signal transduction processes emanating from transmembrane proteins containing IMMUNORECEPTOR TYROSINE-BASED ACTIVATION MOTIFS. The CONSENSUS SEQUENCE of this motif is I(or V)LXYXXL(or V) (where X denotes any amino acid). Also known as ITIM motifs.

D061645.name: Abdominoplasty
D061645.definition: Surgical removal of excess abdominal skin and fat and tightening of the ABDOMINAL WALL. Abdominoplasty may include LIPECTOMY of INTRA-ABDOMINAL FAT, tightening of the ABDOMINAL MUSCLES, and re-creation of the UMBILICUS.

D061646.name: Operative Time
D061646.definition: The duration of a surgical procedure in hours and minutes.

D061665.name: Time-to-Treatment
D061665.definition: The interval of time between onset of symptoms and receiving therapy.

D061685.name: Time-to-Pregnancy
D061685.definition: Time interval, or number of non-contraceptive menstrual cycles that it takes for a couple to conceive.

D061686.name: Premature Ejaculation
D061686.definition: The emission of SEMEN and seminal fluid during the act of preparation for sexual intercourse, i.e. before there is penetration, or shortly after penetration.

D061705.name: Image-Guided Biopsy
D061705.definition: Conducting a biopsy procedure with the aid of a MEDICAL IMAGING modality.

D061725.name: Accelerometry
D061725.definition: Qualitative and quantitative measurement of MOVEMENT patterns.

D061745.name: Antioxidant Response Elements
D061745.definition: Nucleotide sequences that are found in the PROMOTER REGIONS of the genes of stress-responsive and cytoprotective proteins, such as those encoding antioxidant and PHASE II DETOXIFICATION enzymes. NF-E2-RELATED FACTOR 2 containing transcription factors bind to these elements during induction of these genes.

D061765.name: Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Fine Needle Aspiration
D061765.definition: Conducting a fine needle biopsy with the aid of ENDOSCOPIC ULTRASONOGRAPHY.

D061766.name: Proton Therapy
D061766.definition: The use of an external beam of PROTONS as radiotherapy.

D061785.name: Transcription Initiation, Genetic
D061785.definition: The process that starts the transcription of an RNA molecule. It includes the assembly of the initiation complex and establishment of the start site.

D061805.name: Transcription Elongation, Genetic
D061805.definition: The lengthening of a nascent RNA molecule by RNA POLYMERASE during transcription.

D061806.name: Transcription Termination, Genetic
D061806.definition: The discontinuation of transcription at the end of a transcription unit, including the recognition of termination sites and release of the newly synthesized RNA molecule.

D061807.name: Catheter Obstruction
D061807.definition: A hindrance to the passage of fluids through a CATHETER.

D061808.name: Air Filters
D061808.definition: Barriers used to separate and remove PARTICULATE MATTER from air.

D061809.name: Human Papillomavirus DNA Tests
D061809.definition: Methods for detecting or typing the DNA of an ALPHAPAPILLOMAVIRUS in biological tissues and fluids.

D061810.name: One-Lung Ventilation
D061810.definition: Techniques for supplying artificial respiration to a single lung.

D061825.name: Metal-on-Metal Joint Prostheses
D061825.definition: Types of prosthetic joints in which both wear surfaces of the joint coupling are metallic.

D061826.name: Foot Orthoses
D061826.definition: Devices used to support or align the foot structure, or to prevent or correct foot deformities.

D061827.name: Dimensional Measurement Accuracy
D061827.definition: The closeness of a determined value of a physical dimension to the actual value.

D061845.name: Smoke-Free Policy
D061845.definition: Prohibition against tobacco smoking in specific areas to control TOBACCO SMOKE POLLUTION.

D061846.name: Hospitals, Low-Volume
D061846.definition: Hospitals with a much lower than average utilization by physicians and smaller number of procedures.

D061847.name: Hospitals, High-Volume
D061847.definition: Hospitals with a much higher than average utilization by physicians and a large number of procedures.

D061848.name: Optical Imaging
D061848.definition: The use of light interaction (scattering, absorption, and fluorescence) with biological tissue to obtain morphologically based information. It includes measuring inherent tissue optical properties such as scattering, absorption, and autofluorescence; or optical properties of exogenous targeted fluorescent molecular probes such as those used in optical MOLECULAR IMAGING, or nontargeted optical CONTRAST AGENTS.

D061885.name: Chromophore-Assisted Light Inactivation
D061885.definition: A technique for causing a targeted loss of molecular function from REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES that are formed by the illumination of dyes placed in the immediate vicinity of the target molecule.

D061886.name: Neuromuscular Monitoring
D061886.definition: The use of peripheral nerve stimulation to assess transmission at the NEUROMUSCULAR JUNCTION, especially in the response to anesthetics, such as the intensity of NEUROMUSCULAR BLOCKADE by NEUROMUSCULAR BLOCKING AGENTS.

D061887.name: Conversion to Open Surgery
D061887.definition: Changing an operative procedure from an endoscopic surgical procedure to an open approach during the INTRAOPERATIVE PERIOD.

D061888.name: Craniospinal Irradiation
D061888.definition: A comprehensive radiation treatment of the entire CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM.

D061889.name: Healthcare Financing
D061889.definition: Methods of generating, allocating, and using financial resources in healthcare systems.

D061891.name: Controlled Substances
D061891.definition: Drugs or chemical agents whose manufacture, possession, or use are regulated by government. This may include narcotics and prescription medications.

D061895.name: External Debt
D061895.definition: Money owed to creditors outside of a country.

D061905.name: Single-Domain Antibodies
D061905.definition: An immunoglobulin fragment composed of one variable domain from an IMMUNOGLOBULIN HEAVY CHAIN or IMMUNOGLOBULIN LIGHT CHAIN.

D061906.name: Advanced Trauma Life Support Care
D061906.definition: The initial life support care of the severely injured patient.

D061925.name: Immobilized Nucleic Acids
D061925.definition: DNA or RNA bound to a substrate thereby having fixed positions.

D061945.name: Caspase Inhibitors
D061945.definition: Endogenous and exogenous compounds and that either inhibit CASPASES or prevent their activation.

D061965.name: Matrix Metalloproteinase Inhibitors
D061965.definition: Compounds that inhibit the enzyme activity or activation of MATRIX METALLOPROTEINASES.

D061985.name: Madin Darby Canine Kidney Cells
D061985.definition: An epithelial cell line derived from a kidney of a normal adult female dog.

D061986.name: MCF-7 Cells
D061986.definition: An estrogen responsive cell line derived from a patient with metastatic human breast ADENOCARCINOMA (at the Michigan Cancer Foundation.)

D061987.name: Sf9 Cells
D061987.definition: Cell line derived from SF21 CELLS which are a cell line isolated from primary explants of SPODOPTERA FRUGIPERDA pupal tissue.

D061988.name: Proteasome Inhibitors
D061988.definition: Compounds that inhibit the function or proteolytic action of the PROTEASOME.

D062005.name: Biopsy, Large-Core Needle
D062005.definition: The use of needles usually larger than 14-gauge to remove tissue samples large enough to retain cellular architecture for pathology examination.

D062025.name: Organophosphate Poisoning
D062025.definition: Poisoning due to exposure to ORGANOPHOSPHORUS COMPOUNDS, such as ORGANOPHOSPHATES; ORGANOTHIOPHOSPHATES; and ORGANOTHIOPHOSPHONATES.

D062026.name: Alice in Wonderland Syndrome
D062026.definition: Neurological condition characterized by disturbances in VISUAL PERCEPTION, most often of BODY SCHEMA, TIME PERCEPTION and HALLUCINATIONS. It is associated with MIGRAINE, infections (e.g., INFECTIOUS MONONUCLEOSIS), FEVER, EPILEPSY, and other neurological and psychiatric disorders.

D062027.name: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis
D062027.definition: Autoimmune disease characterized by subepidermal blisters and linear deposition of autoantibodies at the dermoepidermal junction. The accumulated autoantibodies are of IMMUNOGLOBULIN A and occasionally IMMUNOGLOBULIN G classes against epidermal BASEMENT MEMBRANE proteins. The dermatosis is sometimes associated with malignancies and use of certain drugs (e.g., VANCOMYCIN).

D062028.name: Bioprinting
D062028.definition: A material transfer technique used for assembling biological material or cells into a prescribed organization to create functional structures such as MICROCHIP ANALYTICAL DEVICES, cell microarrays, or three dimensional anatomical structures.

D062047.name: Silorane Resins
D062047.definition: Polymeric resins containing a combination of SILOXANES and OXIRANES.

D062048.name: Narrow Band Imaging
D062048.definition: Imaging techniques that use illumination created with several optical interference filters by which the frequency ranges are spectrally narrowed and light scatter is greatly reduced. Thus the reflected photons reconstituting the images are from distinct depths (the surface and deeper layers) of the object being imaged.

D062065.name: Waste Water
D062065.definition: Contaminated water generated as a waste product of human activity.

D062066.name: Water Resources
D062066.definition: Environmental reservoirs of water related to natural WATER CYCLE by which water is obtained for various purposes. This includes but is not limited to watersheds, aquifers and springs.

D062067.name: Chemical Safety
D062067.definition: Risk or hazard associated with the handling and use of chemicals.

D062068.name: Inventors
D062068.definition: Persons or entities that introduce a novel composition, device, or process, as well as improvements thereof.

D062069.name: Inventions
D062069.definition: A novel composition, device, or process, independently conceived de novo or derived from a pre-existing model.

D062070.name: Hydrology
D062070.definition: Science dealing with the properties, distribution, and circulation of water on and below the earth's surface, and atmosphere.

D062071.name: Infant, Extremely Premature
D062071.definition: A human infant born before 28 weeks of GESTATION.

D062072.name: Patient Acuity
D062072.definition: An assessment of a patient's illness, its chronicity, severity, and other qualitative aspects.

D062085.name: RNA, Long Noncoding
D062085.definition: A class of untranslated RNA molecules that are typically greater than 200 nucleotides in length and do not code for proteins. Members of this class have been found to play roles in transcriptional regulation, post-transcriptional processing, CHROMATIN REMODELING, and in the epigenetic control of chromatin.

D062086.name: Transtympanic Micropressure Treatment
D062086.definition: The intermittent delivery of pulses of air pressure (5 -20 cmH2O) to the middle ear space through a TYMPANOSTOMY tube.

D062087.name: Plant Mucilage
D062087.definition: A type of viscous polysaccharide that is secreted from PLANTS. It has natural properties that are useful in the formulation of ADHESIVES.

D062088.name: Acellular Dermis
D062088.definition: Remaining tissue from normal DERMIS tissue after the cells are removed.

D062105.name: Molecular Docking Simulation
D062105.definition: A computer simulation technique that is used to model the interaction between two molecules. Typically the docking simulation measures the interactions of a small molecule or ligand with a part of a larger molecule such as a protein.

D062106.name: Protein Degradation End Products
D062106.definition: Degraded protein components that are found within TISSUES, bodily fluids, and cells under certain pathological conditions. They are largely formed through chemical reactions which occur during non-physiological conditions such as ISCHEMIA; HYPERGLYCEMIA; and PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS.

D062107.name: Advanced Oxidation Protein Products
D062107.definition: A class of dityrosine-containing protein-derived molecules formed by OXIDATIVE STRESS. Their accumulation in plasma is associated with certain pathological conditions.

D062108.name: May-Thurner Syndrome
D062108.definition: A compression of ILIAC VEIN that results in a decreased flow in the vein and in the left LOWER EXTREMITY due to a vascular malformation. It may result in left leg EDEMA, pain, iliofemoral DEEP VENOUS THROMBOSIS and POSTTHROMBOTIC SYNDROME. Compression of the left common ILIAC VEIN by the right common ILIAC ARTERY against the underlying fifth LUMBAR VERTEBRA is the typical underlying malformation.

D062109.name: Dermatologic Surgical Procedures
D062109.definition: Operative procedures performed on the SKIN.

D062125.name: Thermometry
D062125.definition: Measurement of the temperature of a material, or of the body or an organ by various temperature sensing devices which measure changes in properties of the material that vary with temperature, such as ELASTICITY; MAGNETIC FIELDS; or LUMINESCENCE.

D062126.name: Databases, Chemical
D062126.definition: Databases devoted to knowledge about specific chemicals.

D062145.name: Maternal Serum Screening Tests
D062145.definition: Analysis of the level of specific BIOMARKERS in a pregnant woman's sera to identify those at risk for PREGNANCY COMPLICATIONS or BIRTH DEFECTS.

D062165.name: Receptors, Artificial
D062165.definition: Receptors that are created by SYNTHETIC CHEMISTRY TECHNIQUES. They are usually designed to mimic endogenous CELL SURFACE RECEPTORS.

D062185.name: Atrial Pressure
D062185.definition: The pressure within the CARDIAC ATRIUM. It can be measured directly by using a pressure catheter (see HEART CATHETERIZATION). It can be also estimated using various imaging techniques or other pressure readings such as PULMONARY CAPILLARY WEDGE PRESSURE (an estimate of left atrial pressure) and CENTRAL VENOUS PRESSURE (an estimate of right atrial pressure).

D062186.name: Arterial Pressure
D062186.definition: The blood pressure in the ARTERIES. It is commonly measured with a SPHYGMOMANOMETER on the upper arm which represents the arterial pressure in the BRACHIAL ARTERY.

D062187.name: Spinal Cord Stimulation
D062187.definition: Application of electric current to the spine for treatment of a variety of conditions involving innervation from the spinal cord.

D062205.name: Strategic Stockpile
D062205.definition: Planned and coordinated pre-event accumulation of ESSENTIAL DRUGS and medical supplies.

D062206.name: Spatial Analysis
D062206.definition: Techniques which study entities using their topological, geometric, or geographic properties.

D062207.name: Brain-Computer Interfaces
D062207.definition: Instrumentation consisting of hardware and software that communicates with the BRAIN. The hardware component of the interface records brain signals, while the software component analyzes the signals and converts them into a command that controls a device or sends a feedback signal to the brain.

D062209.name: Patient Handoff
D062209.definition: The transferring of patient care responsibility from one health-care professional to another.

D062210.name: Personal Narratives
D062210.definition: Works consisting of accounts of individual experience in relation to a particular field or of participation in related activities.

D062211.name: Spatio-Temporal Analysis
D062211.definition: Techniques which study entities using their topological, geometric, or geographic properties and include the dimension of time in the analysis.

D062245.name: RxNorm
D062245.definition: A standardized nomenclature for clinical drugs and drug delivery devices. It links its names to many of the drug vocabularies commonly used in pharmacy management.

D062265.name: Health Insurance Exchanges
D062265.definition: State-provided health insurance marketplaces established under the PATIENT PROTECTION AND AFFORDABLE CARE ACT.

D062305.name: Geographic Mapping
D062305.definition: Creating a representation of areas of the earth or other celestial bodies, for the purpose of visualizing spatial distributions of various information.

D062306.name: Geography, Medical
D062306.definition: The area of medicine concerned with the effects on health and disease due to geographic factors such as CLIMATE, environmental conditions, and geographic location.

D062307.name: Medical Device Legislation
D062307.definition: Laws and regulations pertaining to devices used in medicine, proposed for enactment, or enacted by a legislative body.

D062308.name: Optogenetics
D062308.definition: The combination of genetic and optical methods in controlling specific events with temporal precision in targeted cells of a functioning intact biological system.

D062309.name: Community Integration
D062309.definition: Policies and programs which ensure that DISPLACED PERSONS and chronic illnesses receive the support and SOCIAL SERVICES needed to live in their communities.

D062312.name: Islands
D062312.definition: Tracts of land completely surrounded by water.

D062313.name: Databases, Pharmaceutical
D062313.definition: Databases devoted to knowledge about PHARMACEUTICAL PRODUCTS.

D062325.name: Intense Pulsed Light Therapy
D062325.definition: Treatment of the skin with flashlamps of prescribed wavelengths, fluence, and pulse durations which target specific chromophores to induce photothermolysis at specific locations in the skin such as at the HAIR FOLLICLE or SPIDER VEINS.

D062326.name: Re-Epithelialization
D062326.definition: Reconstitution of eroded or injured EPITHELIUM by proliferation and migration of EPITHELIAL CELLS from below or adjacent to the damaged site.

D062327.name: Skin Lightening Preparations
D062327.definition: Substances used to obtain a lighter skin complexion or to treat HYPERPIGMENTATION disorders.

D062345.name: Nuclear Microscopy
D062345.definition: A method of simultaneously imaging and measuring elements at the submicron level. Nuclear microscopy uses a focused high-energy ion beam of PROTONS and ALPHA PARTICLES (a nuclear microprobe) to interact with the sample. The resulting emitted radiations are analyzed by a group of techniques simultaneously: PARTICLE INDUCED X RAY EMISSION SPECTROMETRY for minor and trace element identification; Rutherford Backscattering Spectroscopy to assess sample thickness and bulk elements such as carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen; and Scanning Transmission Ion Microscopy to assess sample structure and density.

D062346.name: Molecular Medicine
D062346.definition: The field of medicine concerned with understanding the biochemical basis of health and disease and involved in developing diagnostic and therapeutic methods that utilize MOLECULAR BIOLOGY techniques.

D062365.name: Aminobenzoates
D062365.definition: Derivatives of BENZOIC ACID that contain one or more amino groups attached to the benzene ring structure. Included under this heading are a broad variety of acid forms, salts, esters, and amides that include the aminobenzoate structure.

D062366.name: para-Aminobenzoates
D062366.definition: Benzoic acids, salts, or esters that contain an amino group attached to carbon number 4 of the benzene ring structure.

D062367.name: ortho-Aminobenzoates
D062367.definition: Benzoic acids, salts, or esters that contain an amino group attached to carbon number 2 or 6 of the benzene ring structure.

D062368.name: meta-Aminobenzoates
D062368.definition: Aminobenzoate derivatives that contain an amino group attached to carbon number 3 or 5 of the benzene ring structure.

D062385.name: Hydroxybenzoates
D062385.definition: Benzoate derivatives substituted by one or more hydroxy groups in any position on the benzene ring.

D062405.name: Motivational Interviewing
D062405.definition: It is a client-centered, directive method for eliciting intrinsic motivation to change using open-ended questions, reflective listening, and decisional balancing. This nonjudgmental, nonconfrontational interviewing style is designed to minimize a patient's resistance to change by creating an interaction that supports open discussion of risky or problem behavior.

D062406.name: Fukushima Nuclear Accident
D062406.definition: Nuclear power accident that occurred following the Tohoku-Kanto earthquake of March 11, 2011 in the northern region of Japan.

D062407.name: Meals
D062407.definition: A portion of the food eaten for the day, usually at regular occasions during the day.

D062408.name: Breakfast
D062408.definition: The first meal of the day.

D062425.name: Hydroxybenzoate Ethers
D062425.definition: Benzoate derivatives that contain one or more alkyl or aryl groups linked to the benzene ring structure by OXYGEN.

D062445.name: Claudin-1
D062445.definition: An integral membrane protein that is localized to TIGHT JUNCTIONS, where it plays a role in controlling the paracellular permeability of polarized cells. Mutations in the gene for claudin-1 are associated with Neonatal Ichthyosis-Sclerosing Cholangitis (NISCH) Syndrome.

D062446.name: Claudin-2
D062446.definition: A claudin subtype that is associated with the formation of cation-selective channels and increased epithelial permeability. It is localized to the TIGHT JUNCTIONS of the PROXIMAL KIDNEY TUBULE and INTESTINAL EPITHELIUM.

D062465.name: Claudin-3
D062465.definition: A ubiquitously-expressed claudin subtype that acts as a general barrier-forming protein in TIGHT JUNCTIONS. Elevated expression of claudin-3 is found in a variety of tumor cell types, suggesting its role as a therapeutic target for specific ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS.

D062485.name: Breath Holding
D062485.definition: An involuntary or voluntary pause in breathing, sometimes accompanied by loss of consciousness.

D062486.name: Public Health Surveillance
D062486.definition: The ongoing, systematic collection, analysis, and interpretation of health-related data with the purpose of preventing or controlling disease or injury, or of identifying unusual events of public health importance, followed by the dissemination and use of information for public health action. (From Am J Prev Med 2011;41(6):636)

D062487.name: Social Marginalization
D062487.definition: Individuals or groups, excluded from participation in the economic, social, and political activities of membership in a community.

D062489.name: Health Impact Assessment
D062489.definition: Combination of procedures, methods, and tools by which a policy, program, or project may be judged as to its potential effects on the health of a population, and the distribution of those effects within the population.

D062505.name: Value-Based Purchasing
D062505.definition: Purchasers are provided information on the quality of health care, including patient outcomes and health status, with data on the dollar outlays going towards health. The focus is on managing the use of the health care system to reduce inappropriate care and to identify and reward the best-performing providers. (from http://www.ahrq.gov/qual/meyerrpt.htm accessed 11/25/2011)

D062506.name: Claudin-4
D062506.definition: A claudin subtype that takes part in maintaining the barrier-forming property of TIGHT JUNCTIONS. Claudin-4 is found associated with CLAUDIN-8 in the KIDNEY COLLECTING DUCT where it may play a role in paracellular chloride ion reabsorption.

D062507.name: Claudin-5
D062507.definition: A claudin subtype that is found localized to TIGHT JUNCTIONS in VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL CELLS. The protein was initially identified as one of several proteins which are deleted in VELOCARDIOFACIAL SYNDROME and may play an important role in maintaining the integrity of the BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER.

D062525.name: Narrative Therapy
D062525.definition: A form of PSYCHOTHERAPY that centers on the individuals as the experts in their own lives and views problems as separate from people. It is assumed that people have many skills, competencies, beliefs, values, commitments, and abilities that will assist them to reduce the influence of problems in their lives.

D062526.name: Patient Navigation
D062526.definition: The process of helping patients to effectively and efficiently use the health care system when faced with one or more of these challenges: (1) choosing, understanding, and using health coverage or applying for assistance when uninsured; (2) choosing, using, and understanding different types of health providers and services; (3) making treatment decisions; and (4) managing care received by multiple providers.

D062527.name: Meaningful Use
D062527.definition: Using certified ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS technology to improve quality, safety, efficiency, and reduce HEALTHCARE DISPARITIES; engage patients and families in their health care; improve care coordination; improve population and public health; while maintaining privacy and security.

D062528.name: Medicalization
D062528.definition: A process by which nonmedical problems become defined and treated as medical problems, usually in terms of illnesses, or disorders. (Annu Rev Sociol 1992 18:209)

D062546.name: Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel beta Subunits
D062546.definition: Voltage-gated sodium channel subunits that play a role in the assembly, expression, and functional modulation of the sodium channel. They form a heterotrimeric complex with the pore-forming sodium channel alpha subunits.

D062547.name: Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel beta-1 Subunit
D062547.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel beta subunit abundantly expressed in SKELETAL MUSCLE; HEART; and BRAIN. It non-covalently associates with voltage-gated alpha subunits. Defects in the SCN1B gene, which codes for this beta subunit, are associated with generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus, type 1, and Brugada syndrome 5.

D062548.name: Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel beta-2 Subunit
D062548.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel beta subunit that binds covalently to voltage-gated alpha subunits.

D062549.name: Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel beta-3 Subunit
D062549.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel beta subunit subtype that non-covalently associates with voltage-gated alpha subunits. Defects in the SCN3B gene which codes for this beta subunit are associated with Brugada syndrome 7.

D062550.name: NAV1.1 Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel
D062550.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel subtype that is predominantly expressed in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. Defects in the SCN1A gene which codes for the alpha subunit of this sodium channel are associated with DRAVET SYNDROME, generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus, type 2 (GEFS+2), and familial hemiplegic migraine type 3.

D062551.name: NAV1.2 Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel
D062551.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel subtype that mediates the sodium ion permeability of excitable membranes. Defects in the SCN2A gene which codes for the alpha subunit of this sodium channel are associated with benign familial infantile seizures type 3, and early infantile epileptic encephalopathy type 11.

D062552.name: NAV1.3 Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel
D062552.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel subtype found in neuronal tissue that mediates the sodium ion PERMEABILITY of excitable membranes.

D062553.name: NAV1.4 Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel
D062553.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel subtype that mediates the sodium ion PERMEABILITY of SKELETAL MYOCYTES. Defects in the SCN4A gene, which codes for the alpha subunit of this sodium channel, are associated with several MYOTONIC DISORDERS.

D062554.name: NAV1.5 Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel
D062554.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel subtype that mediates the sodium ion PERMEABILITY of CARDIOMYOCYTES. Defects in the SCN5A gene, which codes for the alpha subunit of this sodium channel, are associated with a variety of CARDIAC DISEASES that result from loss of sodium channel function.

D062556.name: NAV1.7 Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel
D062556.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel subtype found widely expressed in nociceptive primary sensory neurons. Defects in the SCN9A gene, which codes for the alpha subunit of this sodium channel, are associated with several pain sensation-related disorders.

D062557.name: NAV1.6 Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel
D062557.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel subtype found widely expressed in neurons of the central and peripheral nervous systems. Defects in the SCN8A gene which codes for the alpha subunit of this sodium channel are associated with ATAXIA and cognitive deficits.

D062558.name: NAV1.9 Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel
D062558.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel subtype found in the neurons of the NERVOUS SYSTEM and DORSAL ROOT GANGLIA. It may play a role in the generation of heat and mechanical pain hypersensitivity.

D062559.name: NAV1.8 Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel
D062559.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel subtype that is expressed in nociceptors, including spinal and trigeminal sensory neurons. It plays a role in the transmission of pain signals induced by cold, heat, and mechanical stimuli.

D062565.name: Acid Sensing Ion Channels
D062565.definition: A family of proton-gated sodium channels that are primarily expressed in neuronal tissue. They are AMILORIDE-sensitive and are implicated in the signaling of a variety of neurological stimuli, most notably that of pain in response to acidic conditions.

D062585.name: Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel beta-4 Subunit
D062585.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel beta subunit subtype that covalently associates with voltage-gated alpha subunits. Defects in the SCN4B gene, which codes for this beta subunit, are associated with long QT syndrome-10.

D062605.name: Quillaja Saponins
D062605.definition: Natural detergents made up of a heterogeneous mixture of molecules having a triterpenoid core structure. They vary in aglycone (sapogenin) and sugar moieties, including glucose.

D062606.name: Tertiary Care Centers
D062606.definition: A medical facility which provides a high degree of subspecialty expertise for patients from centers where they received SECONDARY CARE.

D062607.name: Fungal Capsules
D062607.definition: An extracellular layer outside the cell wall of a fungus composed of polysaccharides. It may serve a protective role amongst others.

D062609.name: Electronic Nose
D062609.definition: A device used to detect airborne odors, gases, flavors, volatile substances or vapors.

D062610.name: Fungal Polysaccharides
D062610.definition: Cell wall components constituting a polysaccharide core found in fungi. They may act as antigens or structural substrates.

D062611.name: Solid Waste
D062611.definition: Garbage, refuse, or sludge, or other discarded materials from a wastewater treatment plant, water supply treatment plant, and air pollution control facility that include solid, semi-solid, or contained material. It does not include materials dissolved in domestic sewage, irrigation return flows, or industrial discharges.

D062625.name: Cystadenofibroma
D062625.definition: Benign or borderline malignant neoplasm of the ovary and surrounding tissues. It is characterized by tumor(s) with cystic glands which are lined by cuboidal EPITHELIAL CELLS with clear cytoplasm, resembling ENDOMETRIUM cells. The glands are separated by fibroblastic STROMAL CELLS.

D062626.name: Degenerin Sodium Channels
D062626.definition: A family of mechanosensitive sodium channels found primarily in NEMATODES where they play a role in CELLULAR MECHANOTRANSDUCTION. Degenerin sodium channels are structurally-related to EPITHELIAL SODIUM CHANNELS and are named after the fact that loss of their activity results in cellular degeneration.

D062645.name: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
D062645.definition: A family of percutaneous techniques that are used to manage CORONARY OCCLUSION, including standard balloon angioplasty (PERCUTANEOUS TRANSLUMINAL CORONARY ANGIOPLASTY), the placement of intracoronary STENTS, and atheroablative technologies (e.g., ATHERECTOMY; ENDARTERECTOMY; THROMBECTOMY; PERCUTANEOUS TRANSLUMINAL LASER ANGIOPLASTY). PTCA was the dominant form of PCI, before the widespread use of stenting.

D062646.name: Acid Sensing Ion Channel Blockers
D062646.definition: A subclass of sodium channel blockers that are specific for ACID-SENSING SODIUM CHANNELS.

D062665.name: Epidemiological Monitoring
D062665.definition: Collection, analysis, and interpretation of data about the frequency, distribution, and consequences of disease or health conditions, for use in the planning, implementing, and evaluating public health programs.

D062666.name: Vascular Access Devices
D062666.definition: Devices to be inserted into veins or arteries for the purpose of carrying fluids into or from a peripheral or central vascular location. They may include component parts such as catheters, ports, reservoirs, and valves. They may be left in place temporarily for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes.

D062685.name: Steatocystoma Multiplex
D062685.definition: A disorder characterized by multiple, wide spread cutaneous cysts that often become inflamed and rupture. It is caused by the same mutations in the gene coding for KRT-17 that are causative mutations for Pachyonychia congenita, Type 2. Natal teeth involvement is sometimes associated with steatocystoma multiplex.

D062686.name: Epithelial Sodium Channel Blockers
D062686.definition: A subclass of sodium channel blockers that are specific for EPITHELIAL SODIUM CHANNELS.

D062687.name: Sodium Channel Agonists
D062687.definition: A class of drugs that stimulate sodium influx through cell membrane channels.

D062688.name: Buschke-Lowenstein Tumor
D062688.definition: Exophytic tumor of the anogenital region associated with HPV infections. It becomes a large cauliflower-like, hyperkeratotic, verrucous mass that is locally destructive with little atypical cells. Histologically, tumor cells are broad rete peg structures that tend to invade deeper than CONDYLOMATA ACUMINATA.

D062689.name: Lipoblastoma
D062689.definition: Benign tumors of fatty tissues found in infancy and childhood. It is associated chromosomal aberrations that result in activation of an oncogene on chromosome band 8q12.

D062690.name: Vaccines, Live, Unattenuated
D062690.definition: Live vaccines prepared from microorganisms without their virulence altered. Examples include smallpox (vaccinia) and adenovirus vaccines.

D062705.name: Adenovirus Vaccines
D062705.definition: Vaccines used to prevent infection by any virus from the family ADENOVIRIDAE.

D062706.name: Prodromal Symptoms
D062706.definition: Clinical or physiological indicators that precede the onset of disease.

D062707.name: Return to Work
D062707.definition: Resumption of normal work routine following a hiatus or period of absence due to injury, disability, or other reasons.

D062708.name: Epithelial Sodium Channel Agonists
D062708.definition: Compounds that either stimulate the opening or prevent closure of EPITHELIAL SODIUM ION CHANNELS.

D062725.name: Tight Junction Proteins
D062725.definition: Proteins that take part in the formation or structure of TIGHT JUNCTIONS.

D062726.name: Junctional Adhesion Molecules
D062726.definition: A family of membrane glycoproteins localized to TIGHT JUNCTIONS that contain two extracellular Ig-like domains, a single transmembrane segment, and a cytoplasmic tail of variable length.

D062727.name: Coxsackie and Adenovirus Receptor-Like Membrane Protein
D062727.definition: An Ig superfamily transmembrane protein that localizes to junctional complexes that occur between ENDOTHELIAL CELLS and EPTHELIAL CELLS. The protein may play a role in cell-cell adhesion and is the primary site for the attachment of ADENOVIRUSES during infection.

D062745.name: Junctional Adhesion Molecule A
D062745.definition: A cell adhesion protein that is found within TIGHT JUNCTIONS of ENDOTHELIAL CELLS and on the CELL MEMBRANE surface of circulating PLATELETS.

D062765.name: Junctional Adhesion Molecule B
D062765.definition: A junctional adhesion molecule subtype that is localized to high endothelial VENULES, heart ENDOTHELIUM, TROPHOBLASTS of the PLANCENTA, and in the ENDOTHELIUM of ARTERIOLES.

D062785.name: Hemiarthroplasty
D062785.definition: A partial joint replacement in which only one surface of the joint is replaced with a PROSTHESIS.

D062786.name: Junctional Adhesion Molecule C
D062786.definition: A junctional adhesion molecule subtype that is expressed at high levels in PLACENTA; BRAIN; KIDNEY; and PLATELETS. It serves a variety of functions such as mediating leukocyte-platelet interactions, regulating trans-epithelial migration of POLYMORPHONUCLEAR LEUKOCYTES, and acting as a counter receptor for ALPHAM INTEGRIN.

D062787.name: Drug Overdose
D062787.definition: Accidental or deliberate use of a medication or street drug in excess of normal dosage.

D062788.name: Adenomyosis
D062788.definition: The extension of endometrial tissue (ENDOMETRIUM) into the MYOMETRIUM. It usually occurs in women in their reproductive years and may result in a diffusely enlarged uterus with ectopic and benign endometrial glands and stroma.

D062789.name: Tobacco Products
D062789.definition: Substances and products derived from NICOTIANA TABACUM.

D062791.name: Optically Stimulated Luminescence Dosimetry
D062791.definition: The use of a radiation monitoring device composed of material which emits light after being illuminated. The amount of light emitted is proportional to the amount of IONIZING RADIATION to which the material has been previously exposed.

D062792.name: MARVEL Domain-Containing Proteins
D062792.definition: A family of proteins that share a domain with a four transmembrane-helix architecture referred to as the MARVEL domain. The MARVEL domain proteins play important role in vesicular trafficking and in the formation of TIGHT JUNCTIONS.

D062793.name: Occludin
D062793.definition: A MARVEL domain protein that plays an important role in the formation and regulation of the TIGHT JUNCTION paracellular permeability barrier.

D062794.name: MARVEL Domain Containing 2 Protein
D062794.definition: A tight junction-associated MARVEL protein that may play a role in separating the endolymphatic and perilymphatic spaces of the ORGAN OF CORTI. Defects in the gene that codes for MARVELD2 protein are a cause of deafness autosomal recessive type 49.

D062805.name: Synaptogyrins
D062805.definition: A subfamily of MARVEL domain-containing proteins that are found in SYNAPTIC VESICLES, where they may play a role in modulating neuronal signaling.

D062806.name: Myelin and Lymphocyte-Associated Proteolipid Proteins
D062806.definition: A family of MARVEL domain-containing proteolipid proteins involved in vesicular trafficking cycling between the GOLGI COMPLEX and the apical PLASMA MEMBRANE.

D062825.name: Zonula Occludens Proteins
D062825.definition: A family of proteins that play a role in TIGHT JUNCTION formation by binding to and anchoring proteins to the ACTIN CYTOSKELETON.

D062826.name: Zonula Occludens-1 Protein
D062826.definition: A 195-kDa zonula occludens protein that is distinguished by the presence of a ZU5 domain at the C-terminal of the molecule.

D062827.name: Zonula Occludens-2 Protein
D062827.definition: A zonula occludens protein subtype found in epithelial cell junctions. Several isoforms of zonula occludens-2 protein exist due to use of alternative promoter regions and alternative mRNA splicings.

D062845.name: Chloroacetates
D062845.definition: ACETIC ACID or acetic acid esters substituted with one or more CHLORINE atoms.

D062846.name: Non-Filarial Lymphedema
D062846.definition: A form of elephantiasis caused by soil particles which penetrate the skin of the foot. It is limited to tropical regions with soils of high volcanic content.

D062865.name: Diuretics, Potassium Sparing
D062865.definition: A subclass of diuretics that limits the secretion of POTASSIUM into the URINE.

D062885.name: Urinary Catheters
D062885.definition: Catheters inserted into the URINARY BLADDER or kidney for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes.

D062905.name: Central Venous Catheters
D062905.definition: Catheters that are inserted into a large central vein such as a SUBCLAVIAN VEIN or FEMORAL VEIN.

D062906.name: Cardiac Catheters
D062906.definition: Catheters inserted into various locations within the heart for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes.

D062907.name: Oxaloacetic Acid
D062907.definition: A dicarboxylic acid ketone that is an important metabolic intermediate of the CITRIC ACID CYCLE. It can be converted to ASPARTIC ACID by ASPARTATE TRANSAMINASE.

D062947.name: rho-Specific Guanine Nucleotide Dissociation Inhibitors
D062947.definition: A subcategory of guanine nucleotide dissociation inhibitors that are specific for RHO GTP-BINDING PROTEINS.

D062948.name: rho Guanine Nucleotide Dissociation Inhibitor alpha
D062948.definition: An abundantly-expressed rho GDP-dissociation inhibitor subtype that regulates a broad variety of RHO GTPASES.

D062949.name: rho Guanine Nucleotide Dissociation Inhibitor beta
D062949.definition: A rho GDP-dissociation inhibitor subtype that is highly expressed in hematopoietic cells and in LYMPHOCYTES. The expression of this subtype is associated with the regulation of CELL PROLIFERATION; TUMORIGENESIS; and APOPTOSIS.

D062950.name: rho Guanine Nucleotide Dissociation Inhibitor gamma
D062950.definition: A rho GDP-dissociation inhibitor subtype that has a unique C-terminal alpha helical membrane-binding domain. It is found bound to CYTOPLASMIC VESICLES such as those associated with the GOLGI APPARATUS.

D062951.name: Endoreduplication
D062951.definition: A type of nuclear polyploidization in which multiple cycles of DNA REPLICATION occur in the absence of CELL DIVISION and result in a POLYPLOID CELL.

D062952.name: Stratospheric Ozone
D062952.definition: Ozone in the Earth's stratosphere. It is produced continuously by the action of solar ULTRAVIOLET RAYS on oxygen in the stratosphere. The stratospheric ozone (especially at the ozone layer) blocks much of the solar UV radiation of wavelengths of 320 nanometers or less from being transmitted to lower ATMOSPHERE of the Earth.

D062965.name: Cyclic GMP-Dependent Protein Kinase Type I
D062965.definition: A cyclic GMP-dependent protein kinase subtype that is expressed in SMOOTH MUSCLE tissues and plays a role in regulation of smooth muscle contraction. Two isoforms, PKGIalpha and PKGIbeta, of the type I protein kinase exist due to alternative splicing of its mRNA.

D062966.name: Ozone Depletion
D062966.definition: A shift in the balance between production and destruction of STRATOSPHERIC OZONE that results in a decline of the amount of OZONE in the lower stratosphere.

D062967.name: Cyclic GMP-Dependent Protein Kinase Type II
D062967.definition: A cyclic GMP-dependent protein kinase subtype that is expressed predominantly in INTESTINES, BRAIN, and KIDNEY. The protein is myristoylated on its N-terminus which may play a role its membrane localization.

D062985.name: Health Services for Transgender Persons
D062985.definition: Access to specialized care for transgender populations. Health systems organized to take account of the special healthcare needs of marginalized groups who may face barriers in accessing health services. (http://www.who.int/reproductivehealth/topics/linkages/guidance_package.pdf)

D063005.name: Health Information Systems
D063005.definition: A system for the collection and/or processing of data from various sources, and using the information for policy making and management of health services. It could be paper-based or electronic. (From http://web.worldbank.org/WBSITE/EXTERNAL/TOPICS/EXTHEALTHNUTRITIONANDPOPULATION/EXTHSD/0,,contentMDK:22239824~menuPK:376799~pagePK:148956~piPK:216618~theSitePK:376793,00.html. http://www.who.int/healthinfo/systems/en/)

D063025.name: Health Information Management
D063025.definition: Management of the acquisition, organization, retrieval, and dissemination of health information.

D063026.name: Dual MEDICAID MEDICARE Eligibility
D063026.definition: Coordination of coverage eligibility of those individuals who are entitled to MEDICAID and MEDICARE.

D063045.name: Crowdsourcing
D063045.definition: Social media model for enabling public involvement and recruitment in participation. Use of social media to collect feedback and recruit volunteer subjects.

D063046.name: Patient Medication Knowledge
D063046.definition: Patient health knowledge related to medications including what is being used and why as well as instructions and precautions.

D063065.name: Organophosphonates
D063065.definition: Carbon-containing phosphonic acid compounds. Included under this heading are compounds that have carbon bound to either OXYGEN atom or the PHOSPHOROUS atom of the (P=O)O2 structure.

D063066.name: Organofluorophosphonates
D063066.definition: A subclass of organophosphates that have a FLUORINE atom substituted for one of the OXYGEN atoms.

D063085.name: Organothiophosphonates
D063085.definition: Carbon-containing thiophosphonic acid compounds. Included under this heading are compounds that have carbon bound to either SULFUR atom, PHOSPHOROUS atom, or the OXYGEN atom of the SPO2 core structure.

D063086.name: Organothiophosphates
D063086.definition: Carbon-containing thiophosphoric acid derivatives. Included under this heading are compounds that have carbon bound to either SULFUR atom, or the OXYGEN atom of the SPO3 core structure.

D063087.name: Noninvasive Ventilation
D063087.definition: Techniques for administering artificial respiration without the need for INTRATRACHEAL INTUBATION.

D063088.name: Phosphoramides
D063088.definition: Amide derivatives of phosphoric acid such as compounds that include the phosphoric triamide (P(=O)(N)(N)(N)) structure.

D063105.name: Food Assistance
D063105.definition: Food or financial assistance for food given to those in need.

D063106.name: Transgender Persons
D063106.definition: Persons having a sense of persistent identification with, and expression of, gender-coded behaviors not typically associated with one's anatomical sex at birth, and with or without a desire to undergo SEX REASSIGNMENT PROCEDURES.

D063125.name: Balloon Embolectomy
D063125.definition: The use of balloon CATHETERS to remove emboli by retraction of the balloon that is inflated behind the EMBOLUS.

D063126.name: Balloon Valvuloplasty
D063126.definition: Widening of a stenosed HEART VALVE by the insertion of a balloon CATHETER into the valve and inflation of the balloon.

D063127.name: Secondary Care
D063127.definition: Specialized healthcare delivered as a follow-up or referral from a PRIMARY CARE provider.

D063128.name: Tertiary Healthcare
D063128.definition: Care of a highly technical and specialized nature, provided in a medical center, usually one affiliated with a university, for patients with unusually severe, complex, or uncommon health problems.

D063129.name: Parental Death
D063129.definition: The death of the father or mother or another person in this role.

D063130.name: Maternal Death
D063130.definition: The death of the female parent.

D063132.name: Connectome
D063132.definition: A comprehensive map of the physical interconnections of an organism's neural networks. This modular organization of neuronal architecture is believed to underlie disease mechanisms and the biological development of the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM.

D063146.name: Polycomb-Group Proteins
D063146.definition: A family of proteins that play a role in CHROMATIN REMODELING. They are best known for silencing HOX GENES and the regulation of EPIGENETIC PROCESSES.

D063147.name: Animal Distribution
D063147.definition: A process by which animals in various forms and stages of development are physically distributed through time and space.

D063148.name: Plant Dispersal
D063148.definition: The physical distribution of plants in various forms and stages of development through time and space.

D063150.name: Polycomb Repressive Complex 1
D063150.definition: A multisubunit polycomb protein complex with affinity for CHROMATIN that contains methylated HISTONE H3. It contains an E3 ubiquitin ligase activity that is specific for HISTONE H2A and works in conjunction with POLYCOMB REPRESSIVE COMPLEX 2 to effect EPIGENETIC REPRESSION.

D063151.name: Polycomb Repressive Complex 2
D063151.definition: A multisubunit polycomb protein complex that catalyzes the METHYLATION of chromosomal HISTONE H3. It works in conjunction with POLYCOMB REPRESSIVE COMPLEX 1 to effect EPIGENETIC REPRESSION.

D063154.name: Mitochondrial Dynamics
D063154.definition: The continuous remodeling of MITOCHONDRIA shape by fission and fusion in response to physiological conditions.

D063165.name: Neurotology
D063165.definition: A subspecialty of otolaryngology dealing with the parts of the nervous system related to the ear.

D063166.name: Maxillary Osteotomy
D063166.definition: Surgery of the upper jaw bone usually performed to correct upper and lower jaw misalignment.

D063168.name: Mandibular Osteotomy
D063168.definition: Intraoral OSTEOTOMY of the lower jaw usually performed in order to correct MALOCCLUSION.

D063169.name: Dentofacial Deformities
D063169.definition: An abnormality of the jaws or teeth affecting the contour of the face. Such abnormality could be acquired or congenital.

D063171.name: Corneal Pachymetry
D063171.definition: Measurement of the thickness of the CORNEA.

D063172.name: Genioplasty
D063172.definition: A surgical procedure done largely for cosmetic reasons to correct receding chins, chin misalignment, or chin excess.

D063173.name: Retrognathia
D063173.definition: A physical misalignment of the upper (maxilla) and lower (mandibular) jaw bones in which either or both recede relative to the frontal plane of the forehead.

D063175.name: Mandibular Reconstruction
D063175.definition: The physical restoration of oromandibular defects.

D063177.name: Pulse Wave Analysis
D063177.definition: Evaluation of the contour of the PULSE waves which vary in different parts of the circulation and depend on physiological as well as pathophysiological conditions of the individual.

D063185.name: Epigenetic Repression
D063185.definition: The turning off of GENETIC TRANSCRIPTION in certain regions of CHROMATIN without changes in the DNA sequence. Typically epigenetic repression is a way that developmental changes are programmed at the cellular level.

D063186.name: Uterine Myomectomy
D063186.definition: Surgical removal of a LEIOMYOMA of the UTERUS.

D063187.name: Nursing Stations
D063187.definition: An area in a clinic, unit, or ward in a health care facility that serves as the administrative center for nursing care. (from Mosby's Medical Dictionary, 8th ed)

D063188.name: Rana clamitans
D063188.definition: A species of the family Ranidae which occurs primarily in the eastern half of the United States and Canada. Two subspecies exist, commonly referred to as green frog (R. c. melanota) and bronze frog (R. c. clamitans).

D063191.name: Odonata
D063191.definition: An order of insects comprising three suborders: Anisoptera, Zygoptera, and Anisozygoptera. They consist of dragonflies and damselflies.

D063192.name: Pregnancy, Heterotopic
D063192.definition: MULTIPLE PREGNANCY with EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occuring at different locations, involving both an intrauterine site and an extrauterine (ECTOPIC PREGNANCY) site.

D063193.name: Heavy Ion Radiotherapy
D063193.definition: The use of a heavy ion particle beam for radiotherapy, such as the HEAVY IONS of CARBON.

D063194.name: Adventitia
D063194.definition: The outermost covering of organs, blood vessels, and other such structures in the body.

D063205.name: Pneumorrhachis
D063205.definition: Presence of air or gas within the spinal canal cavity (EPIDURAL SPACE; or SUBARACHNOID SPACE). It may result from traumatic injuries, emphysema, infection and other conditions. It can also develop as a complication of various SURGICAL PROCEDURES (e.g., MYELOGRAPHY).

D063206.name: N-Terminal Acetyltransferases
D063206.definition: Enzymes that catalyze the transfer of an acetyl group, usually from ACETYL COENZYME A, to the N-terminus of a peptide chain.

D063208.name: Methionyl Aminopeptidases
D063208.definition: Aminopeptidases that remove METHIONINE from the amino-terminus of a peptide chain, such as the initiator METHIONINE found on nascent peptide chains.

D063209.name: N-Terminal Acetyltransferase A
D063209.definition: An N-terminal acetyltransferase subtype that consists of the Naa10p catalytic subunit and the Naa15p auxiliary subunit. The structure of this enzyme is conserved between lower and higher eukaryotes. It has specificity for N-terminal SERINE; ALANINE; THREONINE; GLYCINE; VALINE; and CYSTINE residues and acts on nascent peptide chains after the removal of the initiator METHIONINE by METHIONYL AMINOPEPTIDASES.

D063210.name: N-Terminal Acetyltransferase B
D063210.definition: An N-terminal acetyltransferase subtype that consists of the Naa20p catalytic subunit and the Naa25p auxiliary subunit. The structure of this enzyme is conserved between YEASTS and HUMAN. It has specificity for the N-terminal METHIONINE of peptides where the next amino acid in the chain is either ASPARTATE; GLUTAMATE; ASPARAGINE; OR GLUTAMINE.

D063211.name: N-Terminal Acetyltransferase C
D063211.definition: An N-terminal acetyltransferase subtype that consists of the Naa30p catalytic subunit, and the Naa35p and Naa38p auxiliary subunits. It has specificity for the N-terminal METHIONINE of peptides where the next amino acid in the chain is either LEUCINE; PHENYALANINE; ISOLEUCINE; or TRYPTOPHANE.

D063212.name: N-Terminal Acetyltransferase D
D063212.definition: An N-terminal acetyltransferase subtype that consists of the Naa40p catalytic subunit. It has specificity for N-termini of HISTONE H2A and HISTONE H4.

D063213.name: N-Terminal Acetyltransferase E
D063213.definition: An N-terminal acetyltransferase subtype that consists of the Naa50p catalytic subunit, and the Naa10p and Naa15p auxiliary subunits. It has specificity for the N-terminal METHIONINE of peptides where the next amino acid in the chain is hydrophobic.

D063214.name: N-Terminal Acetyltransferase F
D063214.definition: An N-terminal acetyltransferase subtype that consists of the Naa60p catalytic subunit. It is found in higher eukayotes and displays a substrate specificity for the N-terminal METHIONINE of peptides where the next amino acid in the chain is either LEUCINE; LYSINE; PHENYALANINE; ISOLEUCINE; or TRYPTOPHANE.

D063225.name: Organically Modified Ceramics
D063225.definition: Organic-inorganic hybrid polymers developed primarily for DENTAL RESTORATION. They typically contain a defined mixture of ORGANOSILICON COMPOUNDS; CERAMICS; and organic POLYMERS.

D063226.name: Central Pattern Generators
D063226.definition: Networks of nerve cells that control the firing patterns of MOTOR NEURONS to produce rhythmic movements such as MASTICATION; WALKING; SWIMMING; RESPIRATION; and PERISTALSIS.

D063245.name: Plant Development
D063245.definition: Processes orchestrated or driven by a plethora of genes, plant hormones, and inherent biological timing mechanisms facilitated by secondary molecules, which result in the systematic transformation of plants and plant parts, from one stage of maturity to another.

D063246.name: Organogenesis, Plant
D063246.definition: Transformative processes which occur in cells and tissues to produce differentiated plant organs.

D063265.name: Sialic Acid Binding Immunoglobulin-like Lectins
D063265.definition: A family of SIALIC ACID binding proteins found in vertebrate species. They are transmembrane proteins which act as cell surface receptors for a variety of sialylated GLYCOCONJUGATES. While a subset of siglec protein subtypes are evolutionarily conserved between mammalian species, there are many others that are species specific.

D063267.name: Sialic Acid Binding Ig-like Lectin 1
D063267.definition: A sialic acid binding lectin that was originally identified as an adhesion molecule for inflammatory MACROPHAGES and activated MONOCYTES. This protein is the largest known siglec subtype and contains 16 immunoglobulin C2-set domains. It plays a role in cell to cell interactions and interactions with BACTERIA.

D063268.name: Sialic Acid Binding Ig-like Lectin 3
D063268.definition: A 67-kDa sialic acid binding lectin that is specific for MYELOID CELLS and MONOCYTE-MACROPHAGE PRECURSOR CELLS. This protein is the smallest siglec subtype and contains a single immunoglobulin C2-set domain. It may play a role in intracellular signaling via its interaction with SHP-1 PROTEIN-TYROSINE PHOSPHATASE and SHP-2 PROTEIN-TYROSINE PHOSPHATASE.

D063269.name: Mitochondrial Turnover
D063269.definition: The cellular processes involved in adjustments to the MITOCHONDRIAL VOLUME, content, and activity, that depend on the energy demands of the cell.

D063285.name: Fibrin Clot Lysis Time
D063285.definition: A measurement of the time needed for FIBRINOLYSIS to occur.

D063287.name: Brown Recluse Spider
D063287.definition: A spider of the genus Loxosceles, found in the midwestern and other parts of the United States, which carries a hemolytic venom that produces local necrosis or ulceration.

D063305.name: Organ Dysfunction Scores
D063305.definition: Ratings that express, in numerical values, the degree of impairment or abnormality in the function of specific organs.

D063307.name: AU Rich Elements
D063307.definition: RNA sequences composed of ADENINE NUCLEOTIDES and URACIL NUCLEOTIDES, that are located in the 3'UNTRANSLATED REGIONS of MESSENGER RNA molecules that are rapidly degraded. They are also known as AREs.

D063308.name: Myelin-Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein
D063308.definition: A transmembrane protein present in the MYELIN SHEATH of the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. It is one of the main autoantigens implicated in the pathogenesis of MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS.

D063309.name: 2',3'-Cyclic Nucleotide 3'-Phosphodiesterase
D063309.definition: A phosphodiesterase that specifically cleaves the 3'-phosphate linkage of 2',3'-cyclic nucleotides. It is found at high level in the cytoplasm of cells that form the MYELIN SHEATH.

D063325.name: Tiapride Hydrochloride
D063325.definition: A benzamide derivative that is used as a dopamine antagonist.

D063326.name: Exosome Multienzyme Ribonuclease Complex
D063326.definition: An intracellular ribonucleolytic protein complex that participates in POSTRANSCRIPTIONAL RNA PROCESSING and RNA DEGRADATION.

D063345.name: Oligodendrocyte-Myelin Glycoprotein
D063345.definition: A glycosylated extracellular myelin protein found on the MYELIN SHEATH of the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. It is linked to the cell surface via a GLYCOSYLPHOSPHATIDYLINOSITOL LINKAGE.

D063346.name: Singing
D063346.definition: Modulation of human voice to produce sounds augmented by musical tonality and rhythm.

D063347.name: Native Polyacrylamide Gel Electrophoresis
D063347.definition: Polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis under conditions in which the components, such as PROTEINS, being separated can remain in their naturally folded state.

D063365.name: Genocide
D063365.definition: The deliberate annihilation of a national, ethnic, or religious group, in part or in whole.

D063366.name: Estuaries
D063366.definition: A partially enclosed body of water, and its surrounding coastal habitats, where saltwater from the ocean mixes with fresh water from rivers or streams. The resulting mixture of seawater and fresh water is called brackish water and its salinity can range from 0.5 to 35 ppt. (accessed http://oceanservice.noaa.gov/education/kits/estuaries/estuaries01_whatis.html)

D063367.name: Virtual Reality Exposure Therapy
D063367.definition: Treatment technique in a virtual environment which allows the participant to experience a sense of presence in an immersive, computer-generated, three-dimensional, interactive environment that minimizes avoidance behavior and facilitates emotional involvement. (from Curr Psychiatry Rep (2010) 12:298)

D063368.name: Balkan Peninsula
D063368.definition: A peninsula in Southeast EUROPE between the Adriatic and Ionian seas on the West and Aegean and Black Seas on the East. (from www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/balkan%20peninsula)

D063369.name: Literature Based Discovery
D063369.definition: A process that searches for hidden and important connections among information embedded in published literature.

D063371.name: Myringosclerosis
