D063371.definition: The formation of dense connective tissue in the TYMPANIC MEMBRANE that does not necessarily cause or lead to loss of hearing.

D063372.name: Physical Therapist Assistants
D063372.definition: Persons who, under the supervision of licensed PHYSICAL THERAPISTS, provide patient treatment using various PHYSICAL THERAPY THECHNIQUES.

D063373.name: Hand Hygiene
D063373.definition: Practices involved in preventing the transmission of diseases by hand.

D063385.name: Cannabinoid Receptor Modulators
D063385.definition: Compounds that interact with and modulate the activity of CANNABINOID RECEPTORS.

D063386.name: Cannabinoid Receptor Agonists
D063386.definition: Compounds that interact with and stimulate the activity of CANNABINOID RECEPTORS.

D063387.name: Cannabinoid Receptor Antagonists
D063387.definition: Compounds that inhibit or block the activity of CANNABINOID RECEPTORS.

D063388.name: Endocannabinoids
D063388.definition: Fatty acid derivatives that have specificity for CANNABINOID RECEPTORS. They are structurally distinct from CANNABINOIDS and were originally discovered as a group of endogenous CANNABINOID RECEPTOR AGONISTS.

D063405.name: Anatomic Variation
D063405.definition: Peculiarities associated with the internal structure, form, topology, or architecture of organisms that distinguishes them from others of the same species or group.

D063425.name: Binge Drinking
D063425.definition: Drinking an excessive amount of ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES in a short period of time.

D063426.name: Human Migration
D063426.definition: Periodic movement of human settlement from one geographical location to another.

D063427.name: Food Quality
D063427.definition: Ratings of the characteristics of food including flavor, appearance, nutritional content, and the amount of microbial and chemical contamination.

D063465.name: Skin Cream
D063465.definition: A water-soluble medicinal preparation applied to the skin.

D063466.name: Respiratory Aspiration of Gastric Contents
D063466.definition: Inhaling refluxed gastric or duodenal contents.

D063485.name: Acanthocheilonemiasis
D063485.definition: A tropical infectious disease found mainly in Africa that is caused by the filarial parasite ACANTHOCHEILONEMA. Symptoms include skin rashes, abdominal, chest, muscle, and joint pains, neurologic disorders, skin lumps, and elevated levels of white blood cells. The parasite is transmitted through the bite of small flies.

D063486.name: Acanthocheilonema
D063486.definition: A common genus of tropical filarial worms parasitic in humans and monkeys.

D063487.name: Prescription Drug Misuse
D063487.definition: Improper use of drugs or medications outside the intended purpose, scope, or guidelines for use. This is in contrast to MEDICATION ADHERENCE, and distinguished from DRUG ABUSE, which is a deliberate or willful action.

D063505.name: Racism
D063505.definition: Differential treatment or unequal access to opportunities, based on group membership such as origin or ethnicity.

D063506.name: Ageism
D063506.definition: Biased behaviors or attitudes, differential treatment, unequal access to social participation or opportunities based on age.

D063507.name: Sexism
D063507.definition: Prejudice or discrimination based on gender or behavior or attitudes that foster stereotyped social roles based on gender.

D063508.name: Social Discrimination
D063508.definition: Group behavior toward others by virtue of their group membership.

D063509.name: Homophobia
D063509.definition: Differential treatment or unequal access to opportunities or services based on perceived homosexual preference or orientation.

D063545.name: Personal Narratives as Topic
D063545.definition: Works about accounts of individual experience in relation to a particular field or of participation in related activities.

D063546.name: Apicoplasts
D063546.definition: Non-photosynthetic plastids derived from RED ALGAE endosymbionts. They are found in species of the phylum APICOMPLEXA including PLASMODIUM MALARAIAE.

D063566.name: Biodegradable Plastics
D063566.definition: Organic polymeric materials which can be broken down by naturally occurring processes. This includes plastics created from bio-based or petrochemical-based materials.

D063586.name: Social Validity, Research
D063586.definition: Evaluation of the degree of acceptance for the immediate variables associated with a procedure or program designed to change behavior. This includes the social significance of the goals of treatment, the social appropriateness of the treatment procedures, and the social importance of the effects of treatments.

D063588.name: National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent Health
D063588.definition: Longitudinal study of a nationally representative sample of adolescents in grades 7-12 in the United States during the 1994-95 school year. The Add Health cohort has been followed into young adulthood. (from http://www.cpc.unc.edu/projects/addhealth accessed 08/2012)

D063607.name: Dander
D063607.definition: Microscopic particles comprising dead skin, dried salivary proteins, hair, SEBUM and microorganisms, shed by animals which causes allergic reactions in atopic persons.

D063646.name: Carcinogenesis
D063646.definition: The origin, production or development of cancer through genotypic and phenotypic changes which upset the normal balance between cell proliferation and cell death. Carcinogenesis generally requires a constellation of steps, which may occur quickly or over a period of many years.

D063647.name: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders
D063647.definition: An umbrella term used to describe a pattern of disabilities and abnormalities that result from fetal exposure to ETHANOL during pregnancy. It encompasses a phenotypic range that can vary greatly between individuals, but reliably includes one or more of the following: characteristic facial dysmorphism, FETAL GROWTH RETARDATION, central nervous system abnormalities, cognitive and/or behavioral dysfunction, BIRTH DEFECTS. The level of maternal alcohol consumption does not necessarily correlate directly with disease severity.

D063726.name: Delusional Parasitosis
D063726.definition: A delusional disorder of belief in infestation by insects or other parasites. This FORMICATION is typically accompanied by dermatological manifestation such as PRURITUS that may lead to self-mutilation in order to remove the perceived parasites. It can be either primary or secondary to a somatic or psychiatric condition.

D063728.name: Secondary Care Centers
D063728.definition: A healthcare facility equipped to provide all but the most specialized forms of care, surgery, and diagnostic techniques.

D063729.name: Sublingual Immunotherapy
D063729.definition: A method of treating an ALLERGY by administering ALLERGENS, in liquid formulation or tablets, to the ORAL MUCOSA under the tongue.

D063730.name: Rickets, Hypophosphatemic
D063730.definition: A disorder characterized by HYPOPHOSPHATEMIA; RICKETS; OSTEOMALACIA; resulting from lack of phosphate reabsorption by the kidneys and possible defects in vitamin D metabolism.

D063731.name: Mobile Applications
D063731.definition: Computer programs or software installed on mobile electronic devices which support a wide range of functions and uses which include television, telephone, video, music, word processing, and Internet service.

D063746.name: Methanocaldococcaceae
D063746.definition: A family of anaerobic METHANOCOCCALES whose organisms are thermophilic methanogens that produce methane from hydrogen and simple carbon sources such as carbon dioxide.

D063747.name: Methanocaldococcus
D063747.definition: A genus of obligate anaerobic METHANOCALDOCOCCACEAE whose organisms are non-motile despite possessing long thin flagella. These methanogens are found in deep-sea vent and other hydrothermal environments.

D063748.name: Bland White Garland Syndrome
D063748.definition: A congenital coronary vessel anomaly in which the left main CORONARY ARTERY originates from the PULMONARY ARTERY instead of from AORTA. The congenital heart defect typically results in coronary artery FISTULA; LEFT-SIDED HEART FAILURE and MITRAL VALVE INSUFFICIENCY during the first months of life.

D063766.name: Pediatric Obesity
D063766.definition: BODY MASS INDEX in children (ages 2-12) and in adolescents (ages 13-18) that is grossly above the recommended cut-off for a specific age and sex. For infants less than 2 years of age, obesity is determined based on standard weight-for-length percentile measures.

D063807.name: Dandruff
D063807.definition: Excessive shedding of dry scaly material from the scalp in humans.

D063809.name: Satellite Imagery
D063809.definition: Composition of images of EARTH or other planets from data collected during SPACE FLIGHT by remote sensing instruments onboard SPACECRAFT. The satellite sensor systems measure and record absorbed, emitted, or reflected energy across the spectra, as well as global position and time.

D063826.name: Kosovo
D063826.definition: Independence from SERBIA was declared on February 17, 2008.

D063847.name: Mean Platelet Volume
D063847.definition: A measure of the size of PLATELETS.

D063866.name: Medical Identity Theft
D063866.definition: Unauthorized access to personal information to obtain medical care or drugs, or to submit fraudulent billing for services. (from https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/medical-id-theft/index.asp)

D063867.name: Identity Theft
D063867.definition: All types of crime in which personal data is obtained wrongfully, typically for economic gain.(from www.justice.gov/criminal/fraud/websites/idtheft.html)

D063886.name: Patient Discharge Summaries
D063886.definition: Summaries that serve as the primary documents communicating a patient's care plan to the post-hospital care team.

D063906.name: Prisoners of War
D063906.definition: Members held prisoner of the armed forces, members of militias of such armed forces, members of other militias, members of other volunteer corps, and organized resistance movements. (Geneva Convention of 1929 and 1949)

D063926.name: Drug Hypersensitivity Syndrome
D063926.definition: Severe drug eruption characterized by high fever, erythematous rash and inflammation of internal organ(s).

D063927.name: Lujo virus
D063927.definition: A species of ARENAVIRUS, OLD WORLD that is the etiologic agent of acute febrile illness with hemorrhagic manifestations in Africa.

D063928.name: Ependymoglial Cells
D063928.definition: The macroglial cells of EPENDYMA. They are characterized by bipolar cell body shape and processes that contact BASAL LAMINA around blood vessels and/or the PIA MATER and the CEREBRAL VENTRICLES.

D063947.name: Slavery
D063947.definition: The status or condition of a person over whom any or all of the powers attaching to the right of ownership are exercised. The slave trade is all acts involved in the capture, acquisition or disposal of persons with intent to reduce them to enslavement; all acts involved in the acquisition of enslaved persons with a view to selling or exchanging them; all acts of disposal by sale or exchange of persons acquired with a view to being sold or exchanged, and, in general, every act of trade or transport of slaves. ( from http://www.ohchr.org/Documents/Publications/slaveryen.pdf accessed 10/18/2012)

D063948.name: Slaves
D063948.definition: A person involuntarily owned or controlled by another and exploited for forced or compulsory work or service.

D063967.name: Material Safety Data Sheets
D063967.definition: Information or data used to ensure the safe handling and disposal of substances in the workplace. Such information includes physical properties (i.e. melting, boiling, flashing points), as well as data on toxicity, health effects, reactivity, storage, disposal, first-aid, protective equipment, and spill-handling procedures.

D063986.name: Vascularized Composite Allotransplantation
D063986.definition: Transference of multiple tissues, such as muscle, bone, nerve, and skin, as a functional unit for reconstructive purposes. Blood supply to the transplanted tissues is maintained throughout the transplantation procedure with minimal ischemia. Maintenance of vascularity in the graft promotes its viability, function, and survival in the recipient.

D063987.name: Hand Transplantation
D063987.definition: The transference of a complete HAND, as a composite of many tissue types, from one individual to another.

D063988.name: 3-Hydroxyacyl-CoA Dehydrogenase
D063988.definition: An NAD-dependent 3-hydroxyacyl CoA dehydrogenase that has broad specificity with regards to the acyl chain length of the substrate.

D063989.name: Long-Chain-3-Hydroxyacyl-CoA Dehydrogenase
D063989.definition: An NAD-dependent 3-hydroxyacyl CoA dehydrogenase that has specificity for acyl chains containing 8 and 10 carbons.

D063990.name: Gene Ontology
D063990.definition: Sets of structured vocabularies used for describing and categorizing genes, and gene products by their molecular function, involvement in biological processes, and cellular location. These vocabularies and their associations to genes and gene products (Gene Ontology annotations) are generated and curated by the Gene Ontology Consortium.

D063991.name: Mitochondrial Trifunctional Protein
D063991.definition: A mitochondrial protein consisting of four alpha-subunits and four beta-subunits. It contains enoyl-CoA hydratase, long-chain-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase, and acetyl-CoA C-acyltransferase activities and plays an important role in the metabolism of long chain FATTY ACIDS.

D063992.name: Mitochondrial Trifunctional Protein, alpha Subunit
D063992.definition: The alpha subunit of mitochondrial trifunctional protein. It contains both enoyl-CoA hydratase activity (EC 4.2.1.17) and long-chain-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity (EC 1.1.1.211). There are four of these alpha subunits in each mitochondrial trifunctional protein molecule.

D063993.name: Mitochondrial Trifunctional Protein, beta Subunit
D063993.definition: The beta subunit of mitochondrial trifunctional protein that contains acetyl-CoA C-acyltransferase activity. There are four of these beta subunits in each trifunctional protein complex.

D063994.name: Peroxisomal Bifunctional Enzyme
D063994.definition: A monomeric protein found in liver peroxisomes that contains two enzymatically active domains; an enoyl-CoA hydratase/3,2-trans-enoyl-CoA isomerase domain, and an (S)-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase domain. The enzyme is stereospecific with regards to how cis and trans double bonds are metabolized. It is complemented by PEROXISOMAL MULTIFUNCTIONAL PROTEIN-2, which has the opposite stereospecificity.

D063996.name: Warm-Up Exercise
D063996.definition: Physical activities done to prepare the body for more intense physical activities.

D064006.name: Dodecenoyl-CoA Isomerase
D064006.definition: A carbon-carbon double bond isomerase that catalyzes the movement double bond from C3 to C2 of an unsaturated acyl-CoA. The enzyme plays a key role in allowing acyl-CoA substrates to re-enter the beta-oxidation pathway.

D064007.name: Ataxia Telangiectasia Mutated Proteins
D064007.definition: A group of PROTEIN-SERINE-THREONINE KINASES which activate critical signaling cascades in double strand breaks, APOPTOSIS, and GENOTOXIC STRESS such as ionizing ultraviolet A light, thereby acting as a DNA damage sensor. These proteins play a role in a wide range of signaling mechanisms in cell cycle control.

D064008.name: Enoyl-CoA Hydratase 2
D064008.definition: A PEROXISOME-specific enzyme that catalyzes the hydration step of the beta-oxidation pathway.

D064026.name: Calbindins
D064026.definition: Calcium-binding proteins that are found in DISTAL KIDNEY TUBULES, INTESTINES, BRAIN, and other tissues where they bind, buffer and transport cytoplasmic calcium. Calbindins possess a variable number of EF-HAND MOTIFS which contain calcium-binding sites. Some isoforms are regulated by VITAMIN D.

D064027.name: Pteridophyta
D064027.definition: An extremely diverse group of approximately 12,000 species of FERNS and so-called fern allies.

D064028.name: Tracheobionta
D064028.definition: A subset of various vascular plants (also known as the Tracheophyta) which include seed-bearing and non seed-bearing species.

D064029.name: Peroxisomal Multifunctional Protein-2
D064029.definition: A dimeric protein found in liver peroxisomes that plays an important role in FATTY ACID metabolism and steroid metabolism. The dimer is formed by cleavage of a single protein precursor and contains an enoyl-CoA hydratase-2 domain and a second domain that displays (S)-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and 17-beta-estradiol dehydrogenase activities. The enzyme is stereospecific with regards to arrangement of the substrate double bonds and position of the 3-hydroxy group of the reaction intermediate. It is complemented by PEROXISOMAL BIFUNCTIONAL ENZYME, which has the opposite reaction stereospecificity.

D064030.name: S100 Calcium Binding Protein G
D064030.definition: A calbindin protein found in many mammalian tissues, including the UTERUS, PLACENTA, BONE, PITUITARY GLAND, and KIDNEYS. In intestinal ENTEROCYTES it mediates intracellular calcium transport from apical to basolateral membranes via calcium binding at two EF-HAND MOTIFS. Expression is regulated in some tissues by VITAMIN D.

D064032.name: Calbindin 2
D064032.definition: A calbindin protein that is differentially expressed in distinct populations of NEURONS throughout the vertebrate and invertebrate NERVOUS SYSTEM, and modulates intrinsic neuronal excitability and influences LONG-TERM POTENTIATION. It is also found in LUNG, TESTIS, OVARY, KIDNEY, and BREAST, and is expressed in many tumor types found in these tissues. It is often used as an immunohistochemical marker for MESOTHELIOMA.

D064046.name: Secretagogins
D064046.definition: Secretagogins are EF HAND MOTIF-containing calcium-binding proteins that are involved in early neuronal migration and neurogenesis. They are also present in many adult organs and in brain and endocrine neoplasms.

D064047.name: Spindle Poles
D064047.definition: The sites in a dividing cell where the minus ends of the spindle MICROTUBULES assemble and where the separated sister CHROMATIDS converge.

D064048.name: Spindle Pole Bodies
D064048.definition: Microtubule organizing centers of FUNGI and DIATOMS. They are embedded in the NUCLEAR ENVELOPE and evolve into the spindle apparatus during CELL DIVISION.

D064067.name: Rho Guanine Nucleotide Exchange Factors
D064067.definition: Signaling proteins which function as master molecular switches by activating Rho GTPases through conversion of guanine nucleotides. Rho GTPases in turn control many aspects of cell behavior through the regulation of multiple downstream signal transduction pathways.

D064068.name: Collagenous Sprue
D064068.definition: A malabsorption syndrome characterized by collagenous mucosal lesions of the SMALL INTESTINE, atrophy of MICROVILLI, severe malabsorption, diarrhea, and MALNUTRITION often refractory to a gluten-free diet.

D064086.name: Medical Marijuana
D064086.definition: Product of the CANNABIS plant, CANNABINOIDS, or synthetic derivatives thereof, used in the treatment of a wide range of clinical symptoms.

D064087.name: Head Impulse Test
D064087.definition: Identification of SACCADES during a rapid head rotation to assess VESTIBULOOCULAR REFLEX.

D064088.name: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points
D064088.definition: A system of safety management (abbreviated HACCP) applied mainly to the food industry. It involves the analysis and control of biological, chemical, and physical hazards, from raw material production, procurement and handling, to manufacturing, distribution and consumption of finished products.

D064089.name: Allelopathy
D064089.definition: The process by which organisms release chemical compounds known as ALLELOCHEMICALS which influence the physiology, growth, survival, colonization, and reproductive activities of other species usually located nearby.

D064090.name: Intraocular Lymphoma
D064090.definition: A form of malignant cancer which occurs within the eyeball.

D064091.name: Waste Disposal Facilities
D064091.definition: Sites that receive and store WASTE PRODUCTS. Some facilities also sort, process, and recycle specific waste products.

D064092.name: Calbindin 1
D064092.definition: A calcium-binding protein that mediates calcium HOMEOSTASIS in KIDNEYS, BRAIN, and other tissues. It is found in well-defined populations of NEURONS and is involved in CALCIUM SIGNALING and NEURONAL PLASTICITY. It is regulated in some tissues by VITAMIN D.

D064094.name: Interleukin-27
D064094.definition: A heterodimeric cytokine composed of the IL-27p28 and EBI3 subunits. It is produced primarily by antigen-presenting cells after stimulation by microbial products or inflammatory mediators.

D064096.name: Aurora Kinase A
D064096.definition: An aurora kinase that localizes to the CENTROSOME during MITOSIS and is involved in centrosome regulation and formation of the MITOTIC SPINDLE. Aurora A overexpression in many malignant tumor types suggests that it may be directly involved in NEOPLASTIC CELL TRANSFORMATION.

D064106.name: Human Coprophagia
D064106.definition: A rare aberrant human behavior involving consumption of excrement.

D064107.name: Aurora Kinase B
D064107.definition: An aurora kinase that is a component of the chromosomal passenger protein complex and is involved in the regulation of MITOSIS. It mediates proper CHROMOSOME SEGREGATION and contractile ring function during CYTOKINESIS.

D064108.name: Aurora Kinase C
D064108.definition: Aurora kinase C is a chromosomal passenger protein that interacts with aurora kinase B in the regulation of MITOSIS. It is found primarily in GERM CELLS in the TESTIS, and may mediate CHROMOSOME SEGREGATION during SPERMATOGENESIS.

D064110.name: Minichromosome Maintenance Proteins
D064110.definition: A family of proteins that were originally identified in SACCHAROMYCES CEREVISIAE as being essential for maintaining the structure of minichromosomes00. They form into a protein complex that has helicase activity and is involved in a variety of DNA-related functions including replication elongation, RNA transcription, chromatin remodeling, and genome stability.

D064111.name: Minichromosome Maintenance Complex Component 2
D064111.definition: A minichromosome maintenance protein that is a key component of the six member MCM protein complex. It contains a NUCLEAR LOCALIZATION SIGNAL which may provide targeting of the protein complex and an extended N-terminus which is rich in SERINE residues.

D064112.name: Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats
D064112.definition: Repetitive nucleic acid sequences that are principal components of the archaeal and bacterial CRISPR-CAS SYSTEMS, which function as adaptive antiviral defense systems.

D064113.name: CRISPR-Cas Systems
D064113.definition: Adaptive antiviral defense mechanisms, in archaea and bacteria, based on DNA repeat arrays called CLUSTERED REGULARLY INTERSPACED SHORT PALINDROMIC REPEATS (CRISPR elements) that function in conjunction with CRISPR-ASSOCIATED PROTEINS (Cas proteins). Several types have been distinguished, including Type I, Type II, and Type III, based on signature motifs of CRISPR-ASSOCIATED PROTEINS.

D064126.name: Minichromosome Maintenance Complex Component 3
D064126.definition: A minichromosome maintenance protein that is a key component of the six member MCM protein complex. It contains a NUCLEAR LOCALIZATION SIGNAL, which provide targeting of the protein complex. In addition, acetylation of this protein may play a role in regulating of DNA replication and cell cycle progression.

D064127.name: Aurora Kinases
D064127.definition: A family of highly conserved serine-threonine kinases that are involved in the regulation of MITOSIS. They are involved in many aspects of cell division, including centrosome duplication, SPINDLE APPARATUS formation, chromosome alignment, attachment to the spindle, checkpoint activation, and CYTOKINESIS.

D064128.name: Nodding Syndrome
D064128.definition: Unexplained neurologic condition characterized by episodes of atonic seizures, convulsions or staring spells with further cognitive decline.

D064129.name: Prostatic Neoplasms, Castration-Resistant
D064129.definition: Tumors or cancer of the PROSTATE which can grow in the presence of low or residual amount of androgen hormones such as TESTOSTERONE.

D064130.name: CRISPR-Associated Proteins
D064130.definition: Protein components of the CRISPR-CAS SYSTEMS for anti-viral defense in ARCHAEA and BACTERIA. These are proteins that carry out a variety of functions during the creation and expansion of the CRISPR ARRAYS, the capture of new CRISPR SPACERS, biogenesis of SMALL INTERFERING RNA (CRISPR or crRNAs), and the targeting and silencing of invading viruses and plasmids. They include DNA HELICASES; RNA-BINDING PROTEINS; ENDONUCLEASES; and RNA and DNA POLYMERASES.

D064132.name: Sports Nutritional Sciences
D064132.definition: The study of NUTRITION PROCESSES during EXERCISE and ATHLETIC PERFORMANCE as well as specific NUTRITIONAL REQUIREMENTS of ATHLETES and the relationship between NUTRITIONAL STATUS and NUTRITION DISORDERS in athletes.

D064133.name: Sports Nutritional Physiological Phenomena
D064133.definition: Nutritional physiology related to EXERCISE or ATHLETIC PERFORMANCE.

D064146.name: Chemotherapy-Induced Febrile Neutropenia
D064146.definition: FEVER accompanied by a significant reduction in NEUTROPHIL count associated with CHEMOTHERAPY.

D064147.name: Febrile Neutropenia
D064147.definition: Fever accompanied by a significant reduction in the number of NEUTROPHILS.

D064148.name: Minichromosome Maintenance Complex Component 4
D064148.definition: A minichromosome maintenance protein that is a key component of the six member MCM protein complex. It is also found in tightly-bound trimeric complex with MINICHROMOSOME MAINTENANCE COMPLEX COMPONENT 6 and MINICHROMOSOME MAINTENANCE COMPLEX COMPONENT 7.

D064149.name: Influenza Pandemic, 1918-1919
D064149.definition: The influenza outbreaks of 1918 to 1919 also known as Spanish flu pandemic. First reported in Haskell County in Kansas in March of 1918 the disease spread throughout the world and may have killed as many as 25 million people.

D064150.name: Minichromosome Maintenance Complex Component 5
D064150.definition: A minichromosome maintenance protein that is a key component of the six member MCM protein complex. In addition, interaction of this protein with cyclin A results in its recruitment to CENTROSOMES where it may play a role in controlling centrosome reduplication.

D064151.name: Minichromosome Maintenance Complex Component 6
D064151.definition: A minichromosome maintenance protein that is a key component of the six member MCM protein complex. It is also found in tightly-bound trimeric complex with MINICHROMOSOME MAINTENANCE COMPLEX COMPONENT 4 and MINICHROMOSOME MAINTENANCE COMPLEX COMPONENT 7.

D064166.name: Vaccine Potency
D064166.definition: The relationship between an elicited ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSE and the dose of the vaccine administered.

D064167.name: Recommended Dietary Allowances
D064167.definition: The amounts of various substances in the diet recommended by governmental guidelines as needed to sustain healthy life.

D064168.name: Minichromosome Maintenance Complex Component 7
D064168.definition: A minichromosome maintenance protein that is a key component of the six member MCM protein complex. It is also found in tightly-bound trimeric complex with MINICHROMOSOME MAINTENANCE COMPLEX COMPONENT 4 and MINICHROMOSOME MAINTENANCE COMPLEX COMPONENT 6.

D064169.name: Intermediate Back Muscles
D064169.definition: Two muscles, the serratus posterior superior and serratus posterior inferior, located in between the deep and the superficial back muscle layers. Their function is to control THORAX movement.

D064170.name: Paraspinal Muscles
D064170.definition: Deep muscles in the BACK whose function is to extend and rotate the SPINE and maintain POSTURE. It consists splenius, semispinalis, multifidus, rotatores, interspinales, intertransversarii and sacrospinalis.

D064171.name: Superficial Back Muscles
D064171.definition: The top layer of the back muscles whose function is to move the SCAPULA. This group of muscles consists of the trapezius, latissimus dorsi, rhomboid major, rhomboid minor and levator scapulae.

D064172.name: Pharmacy Residencies
D064172.definition: Advanced programs of training to meet certain professional requirements in the practice of compounding and dispensing medicinal preparations.

D064173.name: Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
D064173.definition: An E3 ubiquitin ligase primarily involved in regulation of the metaphase-to-anaphase transition during MITOSIS through ubiquitination of specific CELL CYCLE PROTEINS. Enzyme activity is tightly regulated through subunits and cofactors, which modulate activation, inhibition, and substrate specificity. The anaphase-promoting complex, or APC-C, is also involved in tissue differentiation in the PLACENTA, CRYSTALLINE LENS, and SKELETAL MUSCLE, and in regulation of postmitotic NEURONAL PLASTICITY and excitability.

D064174.name: Cephalochordata
D064174.definition: A subphylum of chordates intermediate between the invertebrates and the true vertebrates. It includes the LANCELETS. Its members are characterized by a NOTOCHORD which extends into the adult stage head.

D064175.name: Lancelets
D064175.definition: Small fish-like marine creatures often used in phylogenetic comparative studies of CHORDATES.

D064186.name: Prenatal Education
D064186.definition: Training for pregnant women and parents-to-be to prepare for CHILDBIRTH; CHILD CARE; and parenthood.

D064187.name: Minichromosome Maintenance Complex Component 8
D064187.definition: A minichromosome maintenance protein that forms a hexameric complex with MINICHROMSOME MAINTENANCE COMPLEX COMPONENT 9. The MCM8-MCM9 helicase complex is involved in HOMOLOGOUS RECOMBINATION REPAIR following the formation of DNA interstrand cross-links.

D064188.name: Minichromosome Maintenance Complex Component 9
D064188.definition: A minichromosome maintenance protein that forms a hexameric complex with MINICHROMSOME MAINTENANCE COMPLEX COMPONENT 8. The MCM8-MCM9 helicase complex is involved in HOMOLOGOUS RECOMBINATION REPAIR following the formation of DNA interstrand cross-links.

D064189.name: Apc1 Subunit, Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
D064189.definition: The largest subunit of the anaphase-promoting complex. It acts primarily as a scaffold for the proper organization and arrangement of subunits. The C-terminal region of Apc1 contains a series of tandem amino acid repeats that are also seen in the 26S proteasome regulatory particle, and may assist with forming and stabilizing protein-protein interactions.

D064190.name: Apc2 Subunit, Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
D064190.definition: Together with the Apc11 subunit, forms the catalytic core of the E3 ubiquitin ligase anaphase-promoting complex (APC-C). Its N-terminus has cullin domains which associate with the RING FINGER DOMAINS of Apc11. Apc2 also interacts with the E2 ubiquitin ligases involved in APC-C ubiquitination reactions.

D064191.name: Apc3 Subunit, Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
D064191.definition: A highly evolutionarily conserved subunit of the anaphase-promoting complex (APC-C) containing multiple 34-amino-acid tetratricopeptide repeats. These domains, also found in Apc subunits 6, 7, and 8, have been shown to mediate protein-protein interactions, suggesting that Apc3 may assist in coordinating the juxtaposition of the catalytic and substrate recognition module subunits relative to co-activators and APC-C inhibitors.

D064192.name: Apc4 Subunit, Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
D064192.definition: A subunit of the anaphase-promoting complex whose primary function is to provide structural support for the catalytic and substrate-recognition modules of the complex. Apc4, along with Apc5, tethers the tetratricopeptide-coactivator binding subcomplex to the main structural subunit, Apc1.

D064193.name: Apc5 Subunit, Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
D064193.definition: A subunit of the anaphase-promoting complex whose primary function is to provide structural support for the catalytic and substrate-recognition modules of the complex. Apc5, along with Apc4, tethers the tetratricopeptide-coactivator binding subcomplex to the main structural subunit, Apc1.

D064194.name: Apc6 Subunit, Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
D064194.definition: A highly conserved subunit of the anaphase-promoting complex (APC-C) containing multiple 34 amino acid tetratricopeptide repeats. These domains, also found in Apc3, Apc7, and Apc8, have been shown to mediate protein-protein interactions, suggesting that Apc6 may assist in coordinating the juxtaposition of the catalytic and substrate recognition module subunits relative to coactivators and APC-C inhibitors.

D064195.name: Apc7 Subunit, Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
D064195.definition: A highly conserved subunit of the anaphase-promoting complex (APC-C) containing multiple 34 amino acid tetratricopeptide repeats. These domains, also found in Apc3, Apc6, and Apc8, have been shown to mediate protein-protein interactions, suggesting that Apc7 may assist in coordinating the juxtaposition of the catalytic and substrate recognition module subunits relative to coactivators and APC-C inhibitors.

D064196.name: Apc8 Subunit, Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
D064196.definition: A highly conserved subunit of the anaphase-promoting complex (APC-C) containing multiple 34-amino-acid tetratricopeptide repeats. These domains, also found in Apc3, Apc6, and Apc7, have been shown to mediate protein-protein interactions, suggesting that Apc8 may assist in coordinating the juxtaposition of the catalytic and substrate recognition module subunits relative to coactivators and APC-C inhibitors.

D064197.name: Apc10 Subunit, Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
D064197.definition: Apc10 is necessary for coactivator-dependent substrate recognition by the anaphase-promoting complex-cyclosome. It binds the Apc2 subunit, which is a part of the catalytic core, and interacts with coactivators Cdh1 or Cdc20 to recruit substrates to the complex.

D064198.name: Apc11 Subunit, Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
D064198.definition: Together with the Apc2 subunit, forms the catalytic core of the E3 ubiquitin ligase, anaphase-promoting complex-cyclosome. It has a RING H2 domain which interacts with the cullin domain of Apc2. Apc11 also interacts with the E2 ubiquitin ligases involved in APC-C ubiquitination reactions.

D064199.name: Cdc20 Proteins
D064199.definition: Highly conserved proteins that specifically bind to and activate the anaphase-promoting complex-cyclosome, promoting ubiquitination and proteolysis of cell-cycle-regulatory proteins. Cdc20 is essential for anaphase-promoting complex activity, initiation of anaphase, and cyclin proteolysis during mitosis.

D064200.name: Cdh1 Proteins
D064200.definition: Cdh1 is an activator of the anaphase-promoting complex-cyclosome, and is involved in substrate recognition. It associates with the complex in late MITOSIS from anaphase through G1 to regulate activity of CYCLIN-DEPENDENT KINASES and to prevent premature DNA replication.

D064201.name: Trichomes
D064201.definition: Hair-like extensions on specialized epidermal surfaces of plants which protect against damage from insects, animals, light degradation and fungal infection. Trichomes may also occur on certain unicellular EUKARYOTES.

D064202.name: O'nyong-nyong Virus
D064202.definition: A species of ALPHAVIRUS causing a measles-like acute febrile rash illness. It is closely related to the Chikungunya virus and Igbo Ora viruses.

D064206.name: Aggregatibacter
D064206.definition: A genus of PASTEURELLACEAE. Members are nonmotile, Gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic rods or coccobacilli. Its members are X factor (HEMIN) independent and variably dependent on V factor (NAD).

D064207.name: Aggregatibacter aphrophilus
D064207.definition: A species of Gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic spherical or rod-shaped bacteria indigenous to oral cavity and pharynx. It is associated with BACTERIAL ENDOCARDITIS; and MENINGITIS.

D064208.name: Aggregatibacter segnis
D064208.definition: A species of Gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic pleomorphic rod-shaped often filamentous bacteria in the genus of AGGREGATIBACTER found in the oral cavity. It is associated with DENTAL PLAQUE; and BACTERIAL ENDOCARDITIS.

D064209.name: Phytochemicals
D064209.definition: A broad range of biologically active compounds which occur naturally in plants having important medicinal and nutritional properties.

D064210.name: Secondary Metabolism
D064210.definition: A physiochemical process which occurs in a wide range of organisms which unlike BASAL METABOLISM is not required for or essential to short-term survivability but to long-term general well-being of the organism.

D064211.name: Connectin
D064211.definition: A giant elastic protein of molecular mass ranging from 2,993 kDa (cardiac), 3,300 kDa (psoas), to 3,700 kDa (soleus) having a kinase domain. The amino- terminal is involved in a Z line binding, and the carboxy-terminal region is bound to the myosin filament with an overlap between the counter-connectin filaments at the M line.

D064226.name: Prescription Drug Diversion
D064226.definition: The transfer of prescription drugs from legal to illegal distribution and marketing networks.

D064227.name: Chlorofluorocarbons, Ethane
D064227.definition: A group of ethane-based halogenated hydrocarbons containing one or more fluorine and chlorine atoms.

D064228.name: Bromochlorofluorocarbons
D064228.definition: A series of hydrocarbons containing BROMINE; CHLORINE and FLOURINE.

D064229.name: Biological Ontologies
D064229.definition: Structured vocabularies describing concepts from the fields of biology and relationships between concepts.

D064231.name: Nestin
D064231.definition: A type VI intermediate filament protein expressed mostly in nerve cells where it is associated with the survival, renewal and mitogen-stimulated proliferation of neural progenitor cells.

D064232.name: Visual Analog Scale
D064232.definition: A subjective psychometric response scale used to measure distinct behavioral or physiological phenomena based on linear numerical gradient or yes/no alternatives.

D064233.name: Sulfonylurea Receptors
D064233.definition: ATP-BINDING CASSETTE PROTEINS that are highly conserved and widely expressed in nature. They form an integral part of the ATP-sensitive potassium channel complex which has two intracellular nucleotide folds that bind to sulfonylureas and their analogs.

D064235.name: Matrilin Proteins
D064235.definition: PROTEOGLYCANS-associated proteins that are major components of EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX of various tissues including CARTILAGE; and INTERVERTEBRAL DISC structures. They bind COLLAGEN fibers and contain protein domains that enable oligomer formation and interaction with other extracellular matrix proteins such as CARTILAGE OLIGOMERIC MATRIX PROTEIN.

D064236.name: Cartilage Oligomeric Matrix Protein
D064236.definition: Major component of chondrocyte EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX of various tissues including bone, tendon, ligament, SYNOVIUM and blood vessels. It binds MATRILIN PROTEINS and is associated with development of cartilage and bone.

D064237.name: Lipid Accumulation Product
D064237.definition: An index for monitoring the accumulation of lipids based on the WAIST CIRCUMFERENCE measurement and the level of TRIGLYCERIDES circulating in the blood.

D064246.name: Mad2 Proteins
D064246.definition: Mad2 is a component of the spindle-assembly checkpoint apparatus. It binds to and inhibits the Cdc20 activator subunit of the anaphase-promoting complex, preventing the onset of anaphase until all chromosomes are properly aligned at the metaphase plate. Mad2 is required for proper microtubule capture at KINETOCHORES.

D064247.name: Separase
D064247.definition: Separase is a caspase-like cysteine protease, which plays a central role in triggering ANAPHASE by cleaving the SCC1/RAD21 subunit of the cohesin complex. Cohesin holds the sister CHROMATIDS together during METAPHASE and its cleavage results in chromosome segregation.

D064248.name: Geminin
D064248.definition: Geminin inhibits DNA replication by preventing the incorporation of MCM complex into pre-replication complex. It is absent during G1 phase of the CELL CYCLE and accumulates through S, G2,and M phases. It is degraded at the metaphase-anaphase transition by the ANAPHASE-PROMOTING COMPLEX-CYCLOSOME.

D064249.name: Securin
D064249.definition: Securin is involved in the control of the metaphase-anaphase transition during MITOSIS. It promotes the onset of anaphase by blocking SEPARASE function and preventing proteolysis of cohesin and separation of sister CHROMATIDS. Overexpression of securin is associated with NEOPLASTIC CELL TRANSFORMATION and tumor formation.

D064250.name: Hypertriglyceridemic Waist
D064250.definition: A screening phenotype consisting of both elevated WAIST CIRCUMFERENCE and elevated fasting TRIGLYCERIDES level.

D064251.name: Multifunctional Enzymes
D064251.definition: Molecules that contain multiple active sites which are used to catalyze more than one enzymatic reaction. Proteins in this class generally contain multiple active sites within a single peptide chain and may also contain more than one enzymatically active subunit. They are distinguished from MULTIENZYME COMPLEXES in that their subunits are not found as distinct enzymes.

D064266.name: Preexisting Condition Coverage
D064266.definition: Insurance coverage of a physical or mental health condition, disability, or illness existing before health insurance is applied for or enrolled in.

D064267.name: Intrinsically Disordered Proteins
D064267.definition: Functional proteins that do not have unique, stable, folded, three-dimensional native structures or that possess non-ordered regions under physiological conditions. They are characterized by extraordinary structural flexibility and plasticity, which enable them to adopt different conformations in response to different stimuli or different interactions.

D064286.name: ATP Binding Cassette Transporter 1
D064286.definition: A superfamily of large integral ATP-binding cassette membrane proteins whose expression pattern is consistent with a role in lipid (cholesterol) efflux. It is implicated in TANGIER DISEASE characterized by accumulation of cholesteryl ester in various tissues.

D064306.name: Non-Nutritive Sweeteners
D064306.definition: Chemical additives, such as aspartame, saccharin, and sucralose, that give a sweet taste to foods without contributing significant calories or promoting tooth decay. They are generally much sweeter than sucrose.

D064307.name: Microbiota
D064307.definition: The full collection of microbes (bacteria, fungi, virus, etc.) that naturally exist within a particular biological niche such as an organism, soil, a body of water, etc.

D064308.name: Ecological Parameter Monitoring
D064308.definition: Ongoing collection, analysis, and interpretation of ecological data that is used to assess changes in the components, processes, and overall condition and functioning of an ECOSYSTEM.

D064326.name: MEF2 Transcription Factors
D064326.definition: Activating transcription factors of the MADS family which bind a specific sequence element (MEF2 element) in many muscle-specific genes and are involved in skeletal and cardiac myogenesis, neuronal differentiation and survival/apoptosis.

D064346.name: Sagittal Abdominal Diameter
D064346.definition: The height of the ABDOMEN as measured in the SUPINE POSITION.

D064347.name: Microscopy, Electrochemical, Scanning
D064347.definition: A scanning probe microscopy technique that uses an ultramicroelectrode as the scanning probe that simultaneously records changes in electrochemical potential as it scans thereby creating topographical images with localized electrochemical information.

D064348.name: Torpor
D064348.definition: A state of decreased activity in animals characterized by depressed metabolism, reduced body temperature, and low sensitivity to external stimuli.

D064349.name: Genome, Microbial
D064349.definition: The genetic complement of a microorganism as represented in its DNA or in some microorganisms its RNA.

D064351.name: Genes, Microbial
D064351.definition: The functional hereditary units of a microorganism.

D064367.name: Olfactometry
D064367.definition: Procedures for measuring a response to odorants.

D064368.name: Healthy Volunteers
D064368.definition: Persons with no known significant health problems who are recruited to participate in research to test a new drug, device, or intervention as controls for a patient group. (from http://clinicalcenter.nih.gov/recruit/volunteers.html, accessed 2/14/2013)

D064370.name: Spike Glycoprotein, Coronavirus
D064370.definition: A class I viral fusion protein that forms the characteristic spikes, or peplomers, found on the viral surface that mediate virus attachment, fusion, and entry into the host cell. During virus maturation, it is cleaved into two subunits: S1, which binds to receptors in the host cell, and S2, which mediates membrane fusion.

D064371.name: Hazardous Waste Sites
D064371.definition: Sites where HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES are deposited. Some have facilities for safely storing, processing, and recycling these waste products.

D064406.name: Patient Harm
D064406.definition: A measure of PATIENT SAFETY considering errors or mistakes which result in harm to the patient. They include errors in the administration of drugs and other medications (MEDICATION ERRORS), errors in the performance of procedures or the use of other types of therapy, in the use of equipment, and in the interpretation of laboratory findings and preventable accidents involving patients.

D064407.name: Senior Centers
D064407.definition: Community centers for older adults and providers of resources for the community. In addition to providing services and activities for older adults that reflect the community's diversity, they link participants with resources offered by other agencies.

D064410.name: Human Trafficking
D064410.definition: Recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring or receipt of persons, by means of the threat or use of force or other forms of coercion, of abduction, of fraud, of deception, of the abuse of power or of a position of vulnerability or of the giving or receiving of payments or benefits to achieve the consent of a person having control over another person, for the purpose of exploitation. (UN. Protocol to prevent, suppress and punish trafficking in persons, especially women and children, supplementing the United Nations convention against transnational organized crime. General Assembly resolution 55/25. United Nations General Assembly, 2000)

D064411.name: Streptomyces rimosus
D064411.definition: An actinomycete best known as the producer of the commercially important antibiotic OXYTETRACYCLINE.

D064413.name: 3-Phosphoinositide-Dependent Protein Kinases
D064413.definition: Highly conserved protein-serine threonine kinases that phosphorylate and activate a group of AGC protein kinases, especially in response to the production of the SECOND MESSENGERS, phosphatidylinositol 3,4,-biphosphate (PtdIns(3,4)P2) and phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-triphosphate (PtdIns(3,4,5)P3).

D064414.name: Type B Personality
D064414.definition: Behavior pattern characterized by a generally calm and even-tempered demeanor. Emotionally, such personality types show less frequent irritation, anger, hostility, and aggression than Type A individuals. (from International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences, 2008, p. 223)

D064415.name: Type D Personality
D064415.definition: Behavior pattern characterized by negative emotionality, an inability to express emotions, and social isolation, which has been linked to greater cardiovascular disease and increased mortality. (from International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences, 2008, p. 217)

D064416.name: Hospital Medicine
D064416.definition: The branch of medicine concerned with the delivery of comprehensive medical care to hospitalized patients. Practitioners include physicians and non-physician providers who engage in clinical care, teaching, research, or leadership in the field of general hospital medicine.(from http://www.hospitalmedicine.org/AM/Template.cfm?Section=Hospitalist_Definition)

D064417.name: Vitamin K Epoxide Reductases
D064417.definition: OXIDOREDUCTASES which mediate vitamin K metabolism by converting inactive vitamin K 2,3-epoxide to active vitamin K.

D064419.name: Chemically-Induced Disorders
D064419.definition: Disorders caused by the intentional or unintentional ingestion or exposure to chemical substances such as PHARMACEUTICAL PREPARATIONS; NOXAE; and PESTICIDES.

D064420.name: Drug-Related Side Effects and Adverse Reactions
D064420.definition: Disorders that result from the intended use of PHARMACEUTICAL PREPARATIONS. Included in this heading are a broad variety of chemically-induced adverse conditions due to toxicity, DRUG INTERACTIONS, and metabolic effects of pharmaceuticals.

D064422.name: Ambulance Diversion
D064422.definition: The practice of redirecting ambulances and patients seeking urgent care from one emergency department to others for various reasons such as overcrowding and shortage of skilled staff.

D064423.name: Drug Trafficking
D064423.definition: The illegal acquisition, sale, production, transport, movement, and distribution of controlled substances such as narcotics.

D064424.name: Tobacco Use
D064424.definition: Use of TOBACCO (Nicotiana tabacum L) and TOBACCO PRODUCTS.

D064425.name: Herbals as Topic
D064425.definition: Works about books, articles or other publications on herbs or plants describing their medicinal value.

D064426.name: Gasotransmitters
D064426.definition: Endogenously produced lipid-soluble gaseous molecules which function as neurotransmitters and signal mediators targeting ION CHANNELS and transporters.

D064427.name: Nutritive Sweeteners
D064427.definition: Any agent that adds not only sweet taste but some energy value to food. They include natural sugars such as SUCROSE; FRUCTOSE; and GALACTOSE; and certain SUGAR ALCOHOLS.

D064428.name: Hyperpolarization-Activated Cyclic Nucleotide-Gated Channels
D064428.definition: A subgroup of cyclic nucleotide-regulated ION CHANNELS of the superfamily of pore-loop cation channels that are opened by hyperpolarization rather than depolarization. The ion conducting pore passes SODIUM, CALCIUM, and POTASSIUM cations with a preference for potassium.

D064429.name: Fatty Acid Synthases
D064429.definition: Enzymes that catalyze the synthesis of FATTY ACIDS from acetyl-CoA and malonyl-CoA derivatives.

D064430.name: NAD (+) and NADP (+) Dependent Alcohol Oxidoreductases
D064430.definition: Oxidoreductases that act on the CH-OH group of donors with NAD (+) or NADPH (+) as acceptors.

D064431.name: 3-Oxoacyl-(Acyl-Carrier-Protein) Reductase
D064431.definition: A 3-oxoacyl reductase that has specificity for ACYL CARRIER PROTEIN-derived FATTY ACIDS.

D064446.name: Orexin Receptors
D064446.definition: G-protein-coupled NEUROPEPTIDE RECEPTORS that have specificity for OREXINS and play a role in appetite control, and sleep-wake cycles. Two principle receptor types exist, each having a specificity for OREXIN A and OREXIN B peptide subtypes.

D064447.name: Checkpoint Kinase 2
D064447.definition: Enzyme activated in response to DNA DAMAGE involved in cell cycle arrest. The gene is located on the long (q) arm of chromosome 22 at position 12.1. In humans it is encoded by the CHEK2 gene.

D064448.name: Filamins
D064448.definition: A family of crosslinking filament proteins encoded by distinct FLN genes. Filamins are involved in cell adhesion, spreading, and migration, acting as scaffolds for over 90 binding partners including channels, receptors, intracellular signaling molecules and transcription factors. Due to the range of molecular interactions, mutations in FLN genes result in anomalies with moderate to lethal consequences.

D064449.name: Sequestering Agents
D064449.definition: Compounds that bind to and reduce the biological availability of a chemical or pharmaceutical agent.

D064450.name: Workplace Violence
D064450.definition: Threatened or actual attempt to harm others at place of employment.

D064451.name: Hepcidins
D064451.definition: Forms of hepcidin, a cationic amphipathic peptide synthesized in the liver as a prepropeptide which is first processed into prohepcidin and then into the biologically active hepcidin forms, including in human the 20-, 22-, and 25-amino acid residue peptide forms. Hepcidin acts as a homeostatic regulators of iron metabolism and also possesses antimicrobial activity.

D064466.name: Solute Carrier Family 12, Member 1
D064466.definition: Na-K-Cl transporter in the ASCENDING LIMB OF LOOP OF HENLE. It mediates active reabsorption of sodium chloride and is inhibited by LOOP DIURETICS such as FUROSEMIDE; and BUMETANIDE. Mutations in the gene encoding SLC12A1 are associated with a BARTTER SYNDROME.

D064486.name: Solute Carrier Family 12, Member 3
D064486.definition: Na-Cl cotransporter in the convoluted segments of the DISTAL KIDNEY TUBULE. It mediates active reabsorption of sodium and chloride and is inhibited by THIAZIDE DIURETICS.

D064506.name: Solute Carrier Family 12, Member 2
D064506.definition: Na-K-Cl transporter ubiquitously expressed. It plays a key role in salt secretion in epithelial cells and cell volume regulation in nonepithelial cells.

D064507.name: Solute Carrier Family 12, Member 4
D064507.definition: K-Cl cotransporter ubiquitously expressed with higher expression levels in ERYTHROCYTES of ANEMIA, SICKLE CELL. It mediates active potassium and chloride cotransport across the plasma membrane and contributes to cell volume homeostasis

D064527.name: Etiolation
D064527.definition: Physical changes in the growth patterns of a plant brought on by sustained absence of light. These changes are characterized by lengthened internodes which produce long weak stems, fewer leaves, and pale yellow color (chlorosis). The physiological basis for etiolation is induction of the phytohormone, AUXIN.

D064529.name: Receptor, Metabotropic Glutamate 5
D064529.definition: A type I G protein-coupled receptor mostly expressed post-synaptic pyramidal cells of the cortex and CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM.

D064531.name: Peripherins
D064531.definition: Type III intermediate filament proteins expressed mainly in neurons of the peripheral and CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEMS. Peripherins are implicated in neurite elongation during development and axonal regeneration after injury.

D064532.name: Histocompatibility Antigen H-2D
D064532.definition: A component of the murine major histocompatibility complex class I family. It contains one Ig-like C1-type domain and functions in processing and presentation of exogenous peptide antigens to the immune system.

D064546.name: Protein Kinase C beta
D064546.definition: PKC beta encodes two proteins (PKCB1 and PKCBII) generated by alternative splicing of C-terminal exons. It is widely distributed with wide-ranging roles in processes such as B-cell receptor regulation, oxidative stress-induced apoptosis, androgen receptor-dependent transcriptional regulation, insulin signaling, and endothelial cell proliferation.

D064547.name: Myxovirus Resistance Proteins
D064547.definition: Interferon-induced DYNAMIN-like GTP-binding proteins localized in the cytoplasm, nuclear pore complex and nucleus. They play a role in antiviral defense and immunity.

D064548.name: Hand Sanitizers
D064548.definition: Preparations used as alternatives or supplements to hand washing with soap and water to destroy microorganisms and prevent transmission of pathogens. The active ingredient may be ETHANOL; 1-PROPANOL; or POVIDONE-IODINE in a gel, foam, or liquid solution.

D064549.name: Myeloid Cell Leukemia Sequence 1 Protein
D064549.definition: A member of the myeloid leukemia factor (MLF) protein family with multiple alternatively spliced transcript variants encoding different protein isoforms. In hematopoietic cells, it is located mainly in the nucleus, and in non-hematopoietic cells, primarily in the cytoplasm with a punctate nuclear localization. MLF1 plays a role in cell cycle differentiation.

D064550.name: Death-Associated Protein Kinases
D064550.definition: A family of calcium/calmodulin-dependent PROETIN-SERINE-THREONINE KINASES. They are ubiquitously expressed in adult and embryonic mammalian tissues, and their functions are tightly related to the early stages of eukaryotic programmed cell death.

D064568.name: S100 Calcium Binding Protein beta Subunit
D064568.definition: A calcium-binding protein that is 92 AA long, contains 2 EF-hand domains, and is concentrated mainly in GLIAL CELLS. Elevation of S100B levels in brain tissue correlates with a role in neurological disorders.

D064569.name: alpha7 Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor
D064569.definition: A member of the NICOTINIC ACETYLCHOLINE RECEPTOR subfamily of the LIGAND-GATED ION CHANNEL family. It consists entirely of pentameric α7 subunits expressed in the CNS, autonomic nervous system, vascular system, lymphocytes and spleen.

D064570.name: Ubiquitin-Specific Proteases
D064570.definition: Members of the peptidase C19 family which regulate signal transduction by removing UBIQUITIN from specific protein substrates via a process known as deubiquitination or deubiquitylation.

D064586.name: Selenic Acid
D064586.definition: A strong dibasic acid with the molecular formula H2SeO4. Included under this heading is the acid form, and inorganic salts of dihydrogen selenium tetraoxide.

D064587.name: Osmoregulation
D064587.definition: The response of cells in sensing a difference in OSMOTIC PRESSURE between the inside and outside of the cell. This response includes signaling from osmotic sensors to activate transcription factors, which in turn regulate the expression of osmocompensatory genes, all functioning to maintain CELL VOLUME and the water concentration inside the cells.

D064588.name: Selenium Oxides
D064588.definition: Inorganic compounds formed through the oxidation of selenium.

D064590.name: Cool-Down Exercise
D064590.definition: Tapering-off physical activity from vigorous to light, to gradually return the body to pre-exercise condition and metabolic state.

D064591.name: Allografts
D064591.definition: Tissues, cells, or organs transplanted between genetically different individuals of the same species.

D064592.name: Autografts
D064592.definition: Transplant comprised of an individual's own tissue, transferred from one part of the body to another.

D064593.name: Heterografts
D064593.definition: Tissues, cells or organs transplanted between animals of different species.

D064594.name: Bone-Patellar Tendon-Bone Grafts
D064594.definition: A bone-patellar tendon graft used for fixation of the ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT during surgical reconstruction of the knee.

D064595.name: Composite Tissue Allografts
D064595.definition: A graft consisting of multiple tissues, such as muscle, bone, nerve, vasculature, and skin, comprising a functional unit for reconstructive purposes.

D064596.name: Isografts
D064596.definition: Tissues, cells or organs transplanted between genetically identical individuals, i.e. members of the same species with identical histocompatibility antigens, such as monozygotic twins, members of the same inbred strain, or members of a hybrid population produced by crossing certain inbred strains.

D064606.name: SLC4A Proteins
D064606.definition: Bicarbonate transporters that move BICARBONATE IONS in exchange of CHLORIDE IONS or SODIUM IONS across membranes. They regulate acid-base HOMEOSTASIS, cell volume and intracellular pH. Members include CHLORIDE-BICARBONATE ANTIPORTERS (SLC4A1, 2, 3, and 9); SODIUM-COUPLED BICARBONATE TRANSPORTERS (SLC4A4 and 5, 7, 8 and 10); and a sodium borate cotransporter (SLC4A11 protein).

D064646.name: Cardiovascular Nursing
D064646.definition: A specialty concerned with the nursing care of patients suffering from disorders of the CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM as well as those identified as at risk for adverse cardiac or vascular events.

D064647.name: Nephrology Nursing
D064647.definition: A nursing specialty involving the care of patients with or at risk for KIDNEY DISEASES.

D064648.name: Critical Care Nursing
D064648.definition: A nursing specialty that deals specifically with the care of patients who are critically ill.

D064650.name: Home Health Nursing
D064650.definition: A nursing specialty in which skilled nursing care is provided to patients in their homes by registered or licensed practical NURSES. Home health nursing differs from HOME NURSING in that home health nurses are licensed professionals, while home nursing involves non-professional caregivers.

D064652.name: Basal Bodies
D064652.definition: Structures which form the base of FLAGELLA and CILIA. They contain nine triplets of MICROTUBULES that are arranged around the periphery and that serve as the nucleation center for AXONEME assembly.

D064666.name: Diapause, Insect
D064666.definition: Seasonal suspension of insect growth development. It can be either induced by environmental cues (e.g., PHOTOPERIOD) or as a facultative part of the life cycle in order to time development with seasonal changes.

D064686.name: Nutritionists
D064686.definition: Persons specially trained in NUTRITION SCIENCES.

D064687.name: Diarylquinolines
D064687.definition: A class of quinoline compounds defined by the presence of two aromatic ring structures which are attached via a side chain to carbon 3 of the qunolinyl structure. The two aromatic moieties are typically NAPTHALENE and BENZENE. Several compounds in this class are used as ANTITUBERCULAR AGENTS.

D064688.name: Metabolic Flux Analysis
D064688.definition: Measurement of cells' substrate utilization and biosynthetic output for modeling of METABOLIC NETWORKS.

D064689.name: Nurses, Public Health
D064689.definition: Nurses whose goal is to improve health and quality of life in a population or community through the prevention and treatment of disease and other physical and mental health conditions, the surveillance of cases and health indicators, and the promotion of healthy behaviors through public education and awareness.

D064690.name: Wakefulness-Promoting Agents
D064690.definition: A specific category of drugs that prevent sleepiness by specifically targeting sleep-mechanisms in the brain. They are used to treat DISORDERS OF EXCESSIVE SOMNOLENCE such as NARCOLEPSY. Note that this drug category does not include broadly-acting central nervous system stimulants such as AMPHETAMINES.

D064691.name: Nurses, Community Health
D064691.definition: Nurses whose work combines elements of both primary care nursing and public health practice and takes place primarily outside the therapeutic institution. Primary nursing care is directed to individuals, families, or groups in their natural settings within communities.

D064694.name: Rural Nursing
D064694.definition: A branch of nursing requiring generalist training with specialty knowledge in crisis assessment and management in all subdisciplines of nursing. Rural nursing practices often include geographical and social distance concepts in delivery of health care.

D064697.name: Racemethionine
D064697.definition: A preparation of METHIONINE that includes a mixture of D-methionine and L-methionine isomers.

D064698.name: Parish Nursing
D064698.definition: A nursing specialty involving programs designed to bring wholeness and healing to a particular faith community through addressing the health needs of body, mind, and spirit. They are coordinated by registered NURSES and may involve HEALTH EDUCATION and counseling, facilitation, referral, PATIENT ADVOCACY, and health care plan interpretation, as influenced and defined by the unique needs of the congregation.

D064699.name: Dexmethylphenidate Hydrochloride
D064699.definition: A methylphenidate derivative, DOPAMINE UPTAKE INHIBITOR and CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM STIMULANT that is used in the treatment of ATTENTION DEFICIT HYPERACTIVITY DISORDER.

D064700.name: Nurses, International
D064700.definition: Nurses who provide nursing care in countries other than the ones in which they received their training.

D064701.name: Pediatric Nurse Practitioners
D064701.definition: Registered nurses with graduate degrees in nursing who provide care to pediatric patients who are acutely or critically ill.

D064702.name: International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health
D064702.definition: The World Health Organization's classification categories of health and health-related domains. The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) consists of two lists: a list of body functions and structure, and a list of domains of activity and participation. The ICF also includes a list of environmental factors.

D064703.name: Family Nurse Practitioners
D064703.definition: Registered nurses with graduate degrees in nursing who provide care to patients of all age levels, and who focus their efforts on the health care needs of the entire family.

D064705.name: Racepinephrine
D064705.definition: A racemic mixture of d-epinephrine and l-epinephrine.

D064706.name: Vocal Cord Dysfunction
D064706.definition: A disorder characterized by an intermittent abnormal VOCAL CORDS movement toward the midline during inspiration or expiration resulting in upper AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION.

D064726.name: Triple Negative Breast Neoplasms
D064726.definition: Breast neoplasms that do not express ESTROGEN RECEPTORS; PROGESTERONE RECEPTORS; and do not overexpress the NEU RECEPTOR/HER-2 PROTO-ONCOGENE PROTEIN.

D064727.name: Posterior Capsulotomy
D064727.definition: Procedures performed to remove CAPSULE OPACIFICATION that develops on the POSTERIOR CAPSULE OF THE LENS following removal of a primary CATARACT.

D064728.name: Alveolar Bone Grafting
D064728.definition: Surgical procedure to add bone to the ALVEOLAR RIDGE in children born with a CLEFT LIP and a CLEFT PALATE.

D064729.name: Neurokinin-1 Receptor Antagonists
D064729.definition: Compounds that inhibit or block the activity of NEUROKININ-1 RECEPTORS.

D064746.name: Therapy, Soft Tissue
D064746.definition: The assessment, treatment, and management of soft tissue injury or dysfunction. Therapy is designed to reduce tension and irritation in affected tissues and may include MASSAGE; muscle stretching, or direct pressure on muscles, connective tissue, and TRIGGER POINTS.

D064747.name: Lansoprazole
D064747.definition: A 2,2,2-trifluoroethoxypyridyl derivative of timoprazole that is used in the therapy of STOMACH ULCERS and ZOLLINGER-ELLISON SYNDROME. The drug inhibits H(+)-K(+)-EXCHANGING ATPASE which is found in GASTRIC PARIETAL CELLS. Lansoprazole is a racemic mixture of (R)- and (S)-isomers.

D064748.name: Dexlansoprazole
D064748.definition: The R-isomer of lansoprazole that is used to treat severe GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE.

D064749.name: Retrocaval Ureter
D064749.definition: A rare congenital abnormality resulting in the URETER passing dorsal to and being obstructed by the INFERIOR VENA CAVA.

D064750.name: Rabeprazole
D064750.definition: A 4-(3-methoxypropoxy)-3-methylpyridinyl derivative of timoprazole that is used in the therapy of STOMACH ULCERS and ZOLLINGER-ELLISON SYNDROME. The drug inhibits H(+)-K(+)-EXCHANGING ATPASE which is found in GASTRIC PARIETAL CELLS.

D064751.name: Ammonium Compounds
D064751.definition: Inorganic compounds that include a positively charged tetrahedral nitrogen (ammonium ion) as part of their structure. This class of compounds includes a broad variety of simple ammonium salts and derivatives.

D064752.name: Atrial Remodeling
D064752.definition: Long-term changes in the electrophysiological parameters and/or anatomical structures of the HEART ATRIA that result from prolonged changes in atrial rate, often associated with ATRIAL FIBRILLATION or long periods of intense EXERCISE.

D064753.name: Ammonium Hydroxide
D064753.definition: The hydroxy salt of ammonium ion. It is formed when AMMONIA reacts with water molecules in solution.

D064766.name: Influenza A Virus, H7N9 Subtype
D064766.definition: A subtype of INFLUENZA A VIRUS with the surface proteins hemagglutinin 7 and neuraminidase 9. This avian origin virus was first identified in humans in 2013.

D064786.name: Nocebo Effect
D064786.definition: An adverse effect occurring with a medical treatment that is not attributable to the actions of the treatment.

D064787.name: Portion Size
D064787.definition: The amount of a particular food one chooses to eat at a single meal. It is different from SERVING SIZE, which is a reference amount of food as defined by an authoritative source, such as the Food Guide Pyramid devised by the UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE.

D064788.name: Serving Size
D064788.definition: A reference measure of food used to identify the calorie and nutrient content in a particular amount of that food. It is defined by an authoritative source, such as the Food Guide Pyramid devised by the UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE. It is different from PORTION SIZE, which is the amount of food one chooses to eat at a single meal.

D064789.name: Immunity, Heterologous
D064789.definition: The immunological phenomenon by which exposure to some organisms or vaccines can profoundly alter the host's response to subsequent exposure to unrelated (heterologous) organisms or vaccines.

D064790.name: Clinical Laboratory Services
D064790.definition: Organized services provided by MEDICAL LABORATORY PERSONNEL for the purpose of carrying out CLINICAL LABORATORY TECHNIQUES used for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease.

D064792.name: Pragmatic Clinical Trials as Topic
D064792.definition: Works about randomized clinical trials that compare interventions in clinical settings and which look at a range of effectiveness outcomes and impacts.

D064794.name: Lorajmine
D064794.definition: A monochloroacetyl derivative of ajmaline. It is a class Ia antiarrhythmic agent that is rapidly hydrolyzed to ajmaline by plasma and tissue esterases.

D064795.name: Intraoperative Neurophysiological Monitoring
D064795.definition: The systematic checking of the condition and function of a patient's CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM during the course of a surgical operation.

D064796.name: Veterinary Sports Medicine
D064796.definition: The field of veterinary medicine concerned with PHYSICAL FITNESS of animals in sports (horse racing, dog racing, etc.) and the diagnosis and treatment of sports injuries in animals.

D064797.name: Physical Conditioning, Human
D064797.definition: Diet modification and physical exercise to improve the ability to carry out daily tasks and perform physical activities.

D064798.name: Polypharmacology
D064798.definition: The design or use of pharmaceutical agents that act on multiple targets or disease pathways.

D064799.name: Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-Proline Dioxygenases
D064799.definition: Dioxygenase enzymes that specifically hydroxylate a PROLINE residue on the HYPOXIA-INDUCIBLE FACTOR 1, ALPHA SUBUNIT. They are OXYGEN-dependent enzymes that play an important role in mediating cellular adaptive responses to HYPOXIA.

D064800.name: Prolyl-Hydroxylase Inhibitors
D064800.definition: Compounds that inhibit the action of HYDROXYLASES that act on PROLINE to form HYDROXYPROLINE.

D064801.name: Phospholipase A2 Inhibitors
D064801.definition: Compounds that inhibit or block the activity of a PHOSPHOLIPASE A2 enzyme.

D064804.name: Urological Agents
D064804.definition: Drugs used in the treatment of urogenital conditions and diseases such as URINARY INCONTINENCE; PROSTATIC HYPERPLASIA; and ERECTILE DYSFUNCTION.

D064805.name: Bunolol
D064805.definition: A nonselective beta-adrenoceptor antagonist used in the treatment of glaucoma.

D064806.name: Dysbiosis
D064806.definition: Changes in quantitative and qualitative composition of MICROBIOTA. The changes may lead to altered host microbial interaction or homeostatic imbalance that can contribute to a disease state often with inflammation.

D064807.name: Anticholinergic Syndrome
D064807.definition: Adverse drug effects associated with CHOLINERGIC ANTAGONISTS. Clinical features include TACHYCARDIA; HYPERTHERMIA; MYDRIASIS, dry skin and dry mucous membranes, decreased bowel sounds and urinary retention in peripheral anticholinergic syndrome; and HALLUCINATIONS; PSYCHOSES; SEIZURES; and COMA in central anticholinergic syndrome.

D064826.name: Transfusion Medicine
D064826.definition: The area of hematology that is concerned with the transfusion of blood and blood components, and in prevention and treatment of adverse effects from BLOOD TRANSFUSION errors.

D064827.name: Myocutaneous Flap
D064827.definition: A mass of tissue, including skin and muscle, that has been cut away from surrounding areas for transplantation.

D064828.name: Prolyl Hydroxylases
D064828.definition: Enzymes that specifically hydroxylate PROLINE residues on proteins.

D064830.name: Temperance Movement
D064830.definition: Social effort most active in the 19th and early 20th centuries dedicated to promoting moderation or complete abstinence in the use of ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES.

D064846.name: Sports for Persons with Disabilities
D064846.definition: Activities or games played by PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES, usually requiring physical effort or skill. The activities or games may be specifically created or based on existing sports, with or without modifications, to meet the needs of persons with physical or intellectual disabilities.

D064847.name: Multimodal Imaging
D064847.definition: The use of combination of imaging techniques or platforms (e.g., MRI SCAN and PET SCAN) encompassing aspects of anatomical, functional, or molecular imaging methods.

D064866.name: Mindfulness
D064866.definition: A psychological state of awareness, the practices that promote this awareness, a mode of processing information and a character trait. As a therapy mindfulness is defined as a moment-to-moment awareness of one's experience without judgment and as a state and not a trait.

D064867.name: Mesopotamia
D064867.definition: Ancient land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, corresponding to modern-day Iraq and partly NE Syria, SE Turkey and smaller parts of SW Iran. It is considered to be the cradle of civilization in the West. Bronze Age Mesopotamia included Sumer and the Akkadian, Babylonian and Assyrian empires (from http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/mesopotamia )

D064868.name: Ethnic Violence
D064868.definition: Violence or other hostile behavior arising when an ethnic group either feels itself under threat, or where it seeks to assert its superiority or dominance over other groups.

D064869.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy
D064869.definition: Contextually focused form of cognitive behavioral psychotherapy that uses MINDFULNESS and behavioral activation to increase patients' psychological flexibility in areas such as ability to engage in values-based, positive behaviors while experiencing difficult thoughts, emotions, or sensations.

D064870.name: Air Travel
D064870.definition: Aspects of health and disease related to air travel. It includes the physiologic and psychologic beneficial or adverse effects.

D064871.name: Teach-Back Communication
D064871.definition: Providing the patient, family or others information, and then allowing them to take an action or restate the information in their own words. The clinician prefaces communications with a statement framed to show the clinician has the burden of effective communication rather than the patient.

D064872.name: Patient Care Bundles
D064872.definition: Small sets of evidence-based interventions for a defined patient population and care setting.

D064873.name: Asia, Northern
D064873.definition: A subregion of Asia, consisting of the Asian portion of Russia.

D064874.name: Tatarstan
D064874.definition: Political subdivision of eastern RUSSIA located within Europe. It lies between the Volga River and the Kama River, and extends east to the Ural mountains.

D064876.name: Safety-net Providers
D064876.definition: Providers that by mandate or mission organize and deliver a significant level of health care and other health-related services to the uninsured, Medicaid recipients, and other vulnerable patients.

D064877.name: Organ Trafficking
D064877.definition: Criminal activity that occurs in three broad categories. Firstly, cases where traffickers force or deceive the victims into giving up an organ. Secondly, there are cases where victims formally or informally agree to sell an organ and are cheated because they are not paid for the organ or are paid less than the promised price. Thirdly, vulnerable persons are treated for an ailment, which may or may not exist and thereupon organs are removed without the victim's knowledge.

D064878.name: Web Browser
D064878.definition: Software application for retrieving, presenting and traversing information resources on the World Wide Web.

D064886.name: Dataset
D064886.definition: Works consisting of organized collections of data, which have been stored permanently in a formalized manner suitable for communication, interpretation, or processing.

D064887.name: Observational Studies as Topic
D064887.definition: Works about clinical studies in which participants may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions, but the investigator does not assign participants to specific interventions (as in an interventional study).

D064888.name: Observational Study
D064888.definition: A work that reports on the results of a clinical study in which participants may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions, but the investigator does not assign participants to specific interventions (as in an interventional study).

D064889.name: Psychotherapy, Psychodynamic
D064889.definition: Forms of PSYCHOTHERAPY falling within or deriving from the psychoanalytic tradition, that view individuals as reacting to unconscious forces (e.g., motivation, drive), that focus on processes of change and development, and that place a premium on self understanding and making meaning of what is unconscious.

D064890.name: Social Determinants of Health
D064890.definition: The circumstances in which people are born, grow up, live, work, and age, as well as the systems put in place to deal with illness. These circumstances are in turn shaped by a wider set of forces: economics, social policies, and politics (http://www.cdc.gov/socialdeterminants/).

D064891.name: Disaster Victims
D064891.definition: Persons adversely effected by DISASTERS, occurrences that result in property damage, deaths, and/or injuries to a community.

D064906.name: Qigong
D064906.definition: An ancient Chinese system of postures, exercises, breathing techniques, and meditations designed to improve and enhance the body's QI.

D064907.name: Diagnostic Uses of Chemicals
D064907.definition: Chemicals administered to patients in order to diagnose or study the pathology of medical conditions, diseases, or syndromes.

D064926.name: Neurophysiological Monitoring
D064926.definition: The systematic checking of the condition and function of a patient's CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM during disease periods or following injuries, using various NEUROLOGICAL DIAGNOSTIC TECHNIQUES.

D064927.name: Tick Bites
