D064927.definition: The effects, both local and systemic, caused by the bites of TICKS.

D064946.name: Hospice and Palliative Care Nursing
D064946.definition: A nursing specialty concerned with care of patients facing serious or life-threatening illnesses. The goal of palliative nursing is to prevent and relieve suffering, and to support the best possible quality of life for patients and their families. Hospice nursing is palliative care for people in their final stages of life.

D064966.name: British Virgin Islands
D064966.definition: A British overseas territory, part of the British West Indies, lying about 60 miles east of Puerto Rico. Tortola is the main island, other islands include Virgin Gorda, Jost Van Dyke and Anegada.

D064987.name: Cell- and Tissue-Based Therapy
D064987.definition: Therapies that involve the TRANSPLANTATION of CELLS or TISSUES developed for the purpose of restoring the function of diseased or dysfunctional cells or tissues.

D065006.name: Papanicolaou Test
D065006.definition: Cytological preparation of cells collected from a mucosal surface and stained with Papanicolaou stain.

D065007.name: Pragmatic Clinical Trial
D065007.definition: Works about randomized clinical trials that compare interventions in clinical settings and which look at a range of effectiveness outcomes and impacts.

D065008.name: Scorpion Stings
D065008.definition: The effects, both local and systemic, caused by the bite of SCORPIONS.

D065067.name: Antihyperkalemic Agents
D065067.definition: Compounds used to lower excessive POTASSIUM levels in the body.

D065086.name: Acetaldehyde Dehydrogenase Inhibitors
D065086.definition: Compounds that bind to and inhibit the enzymatic activity of acetaldehyde dehydrogenases.

D065087.name: Acetylcholine Release Inhibitors
D065087.definition: Compounds that block release of the neurotransmitter ACETYLCHOLINE.

D065088.name: Steroid Synthesis Inhibitors
D065088.definition: Compounds that bind to and inhibit enzymes involved in the synthesis of STEROIDS.

D065089.name: Glycoside Hydrolase Inhibitors
D065089.definition: Compounds that inhibit or block the activity of GLYCOSIDE HYDROLASES such as ALPHA-AMYLASES and APHA-GLUCOSIDASES.

D065091.name: Amylin Receptor Agonists
D065091.definition: Compounds that stimulate the activity of AMYMIN RECEPTORS. Included under this heading is the endogenous form of ISLET AMYLOID POLYPEPTIDE and synthetic compounds that mimic its effect.

D065092.name: Antidiuretic Hormone Receptor Antagonists
D065092.definition: Endogenous compounds and drugs that inhibit or block the activity of ANTIDUIRETIC HORMONE RECEPTORS.

D065093.name: beta-Lactamase Inhibitors
D065093.definition: Endogenous substances and drugs that inhibit or block the activity of BETA-LACTAMASES.

D065094.name: Bradykinin B2 Receptor Antagonists
D065094.definition: Compounds and drugs that inhibit ligand binding or cellular signaling by BRADYKININ B2 RECEPTORS.

D065095.name: Calcineurin Inhibitors
D065095.definition: Compounds that inhibit or block the PHOSPHATASE activity of CALCINEURIN.

D065096.name: Calcium Chelating Agents
D065096.definition: Substances that bind to and sequester CALCIUM ions.

D065097.name: Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I Activators
D065097.definition: Substances and drugs that stimulate the synthesis or increase the activity of CARBAMOYL PHOSPHATE SYNTHETASE I. Drugs in this class of compounds have been used to treat the genetic disorder, CARBAMOYL-PHOSPHATE SYNTHASE I DEFICIENCY DISEASE.

D065098.name: Catechol O-Methyltransferase Inhibitors
D065098.definition: Compounds and drugs that inhibit or block the activity of CATECHOL O-METHYLTRANSFERASE enzymes. Drugs in this class are used in management of central nervous system disorders such as PARKINSON DISEASE.

D065099.name: Travel Nursing
D065099.definition: A type of nursing practice involving licensed professional nurses who travel to work in temporary nursing positions.

D065100.name: CCR5 Receptor Antagonists
D065100.definition: Compounds and drugs that inhibit or block the activity of CCR5 RECEPTORS.

D065101.name: Chloride Channel Agonists
D065101.definition: A class of drugs that stimulate chloride ion influx through cell membrane channels.

D065102.name: Licensed Practical Nurses
D065102.definition: Health personnel who do not hold professional degrees or credentials, but have completed training and are licensed to provide routine patient care under the direction of registered nurses and physicians.

D065104.name: Cystine Depleting Agents
D065104.definition: Compounds and drugs that react with CYSTINE and convert it into a compound that can be more easily metabolized or intracellularly transported. Drugs in this class have been used to treat CYSTINOSIS.

D065105.name: Aromatic Amino Acid Decarboxylase Inhibitors
D065105.definition: Compounds and drugs that block or inhibit the enzymatic action of AROMATIC AMINO ACID DECARBOXYLASES. Pharmaceutical agents in this category are used in conjunction with LEVODOPA in order to slow its metabolism.

D065106.name: Demulcents
D065106.definition: Compounds that form soothing films on the surface of MUCOUS MEMBRANES. They are generally used as agents to protect the integrity of internal EPITHELIUM.

D065108.name: Ornithine Decarboxylase Inhibitors
D065108.definition: Substances and drugs that inhibit or block the activity of ORNITHINE DECARBOXYLASE.

D065126.name: Palliative Medicine
D065126.definition: A branch of medicine concerned with preventing and relieving the suffering of patients in any stage of disease. Its focus is on comprehensive care and improving the quality of all areas of the patient's life.

D065127.name: Dopamine D2 Receptor Antagonists
D065127.definition: Compounds and drugs that bind to and inhibit or block the activation of DOPAMINE D2 RECEPTORS.

D065128.name: Endothelin Receptor Antagonists
D065128.definition: Compounds and drugs that bind to and inhibit or block the activation of ENDOTHELIN RECECPTORS.

D065129.name: Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis
D065129.definition: A method of disease prevention (abbreviated PrEP) which involves the administration of drugs to at-risk persons who have not been exposed to the disease-causing agent.

D065130.name: Endothelin A Receptor Antagonists
D065130.definition: Compounds and drugs that bind to and inhibit or block the activation of ENDOTHELIN A RECECPTORS.

D065131.name: Endothelin B Receptor Antagonists
D065131.definition: Compounds and drugs that bind to and inhibit or block the activation of ENDOTHELIN B RECEPTORS.

D065132.name: Bioprospecting
D065132.definition: The systematic search and discovery of natural substances which may have potential commercial applications.

D065133.name: Ephemeroptera
D065133.definition: An Order of aquatic INSECTS comprising about 2,500 species worldwide. It is the only insect group with two flying stages, each with relatively large forewings. The immature stage called "naiad" or "nymph" lasts one year in fresh water, and the adult stage is shortlived, lasting from a few minutes to a few days, depending on the species. The Ephemeroptera includes mayflies (also called shadflies)

D065134.name: Lipedema
D065134.definition: Disorder of adipose tissue characterized by symmetric and bilateral enlargement of the lower extremities due to abnormal deposition of SUBCUTANEOUS FAT often in obese women. It is associated with HEMATOMA, pain and may progress to secondary LYMPHEDEMA which is known as lipolymphedema.

D065136.name: Animal Culling
D065136.definition: Selection and removal of individuals from a population or group. Culling is a common strategy with livestock and wildlife, used to control and eradicate diseases or pests, control population size, select for desired genetic characteristics, and maximize economic profit.

D065146.name: Zeaxanthins
D065146.definition: Carotenoids found in fruits and vegetables. Zeaxanthin accumulates in the MACULA LUTEA.

D065147.name: Viral Fusion Protein Inhibitors
D065147.definition: Drugs that are designed to block the action of VIRAL FUSION PROTEINS and prevent VIRUSES from entering the cell.

D065148.name: Nicolau Syndrome
D065148.definition: An uncommon complication of INTRAMUSCULAR INJECTION leading to variable degrees of necrosis of skin and underlying tissue.

D065150.name: Cellular Reprogramming
D065150.definition: A process where fully differentiated or specialized cells revert to pluripotency or a less differentiated cell type.

D065166.name: Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy
D065166.definition: Acute neurological dysfunction during severe SEPSIS in the absence of direct brain infection characterized by systemic inflammation and BLOOD BRAIN BARRIER perturbation.

D065167.name: Pregnancy, Interstitial
D065167.definition: A type of ectopic pregnancy in which the extrauterine EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occurs in the portion of the FALLOPIAN TUBE that traverses the muscular wall of the uterus.

D065168.name: Bradykinin Receptor Antagonists
D065168.definition: Compounds and drugs that inhibit ligand binding or cellular signaling by BRADYKININ RECEPTORS.

D065169.name: Bradykinin B1 Receptor Antagonists
D065169.definition: Compounds and drugs that inhibit ligand binding or cellular signaling by BRADYKININ B1 RECEPTORS.

D065170.name: Pregnancy, Angular
D065170.definition: A rare type of abnormal pregnancy in which EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occurs at a lateral angle of the UTERUS, medial to the uterotubal junction and the ROUND LIGAMENT OF UTERUS.

D065171.name: Estrogen Receptor Antagonists
D065171.definition: Compounds and drugs that bind to and block or inhibit the activation of ESTROGEN RECEPTORS.

D065172.name: Pregnancy, Ovarian
D065172.definition: A type of pregnancy in which EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occurs in an OVARY instead of in the uterine cavity.

D065173.name: Pregnancy, Cornual
D065173.definition: A type of pregnancy in which the EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occurs in the horn of the UTERUS instead of in the uterine cavity, i.e. at the junction of the uterus and one of the FALLOPIAN TUBES.

D065186.name: Interrupted Time Series Analysis
D065186.definition: A study that uses observations at multiple time points before and after an intervention (the "interruption"), in an attempt to detect whether the intervention has had an effect significantly greater than any underlying trend over time.

D065187.name: Controlled Before-After Studies
D065187.definition: A study in which observations are made before and after an intervention, both in a group that receives the intervention and in a control group that does not.

D065206.name: Extracellular Traps
D065206.definition: Extracellular structure primarily composed of CHROMATIN and associated PROTEASES.

D065207.name: Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus
D065207.definition: A coronavirus first reported in the summer of 2012 in a pneumonia patient in SAUDI ARABIA. It is related to SARS VIRUS. MERS-CoV has an estimated incubation period of 12 days and symptoms include renal failure and severe acute pneumonia with often fatal outcome.

D065228.name: Non-Randomized Controlled Trials as Topic
D065228.definition: A study where participants are assigned to a treatment, procedure, or intervention my methods that are not random. Non-randomized clinical trials are sometimes referred to as quasi-experimental clinical trials or non-equivalent control group designs.

D065246.name: Culturally Competent Care
D065246.definition: Health care services that are respectful of and responsive to the health beliefs, practices and cultural and linguistic needs of diverse patients. The provider and the patient each bring their individual learned patterns of language and culture to the health care experience which must be transcended to achieve equal access and quality health care.

D065260.name: Frankincense
D065260.definition: Resin exudate from certain trees of the genus BOSWELLIA in the BURSERACEAE family.

D065286.name: Prophylactic Surgical Procedures
D065286.definition: Surgical procedures done to prevent or reduce the risk of developing cancer or other disease conditions in persons who may be predisposed to such conditions.

D065287.name: Robotic Surgical Procedures
D065287.definition: Surgical procedures performed using a computer that remotely controls surgical instruments attached to mechanical arms designed to perform the tasks of the surgeon.

D065288.name: Serogroup
D065288.definition: A set of variants within a species of microorganisms that are antigenically, closely related. With bacteria, a serogroup refers to a group that shares a common antigen.

D065289.name: Pedicle Screws
D065289.definition: BONE SCREWS to be used in the pedicle of the vertebral arch.

D065290.name: Acute-On-Chronic Liver Failure
D065290.definition: Sudden liver failure in the presence of underlying compensated chronic LIVER DISEASE (e.g., LIVER CIRRHOSIS; HEPATITIS; and liver injury and failure) due to a precipitating acute hepatic insult.

D065306.name: Corneal Injuries
D065306.definition: Damage or trauma inflicted to the CORNEA by external means.

D065308.name: Morphological and Microscopic Findings
D065308.definition: Morphological findings useful in differentiation and classification of results in CYTODIAGNOSIS and related techniques.

D065309.name: Atypical Squamous Cells of the Cervix
D065309.definition: Morphological abnormalities of the cervical EPITHELIUM, usually revealed in PAP SMEAR, which do not meet the criteria for squamous CERVICAL INTRAEPITHELIAL NEOPLASIA or SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMAS of the CERVIX . It may be a sign of infection with certain types of human papillomavirus (HPV).or sign of a benign (not cancer) growth, such as a cyst or polyp or, in menopausal women, of low hormone levels. More testing, such as HPV test, may be needed.

D065310.name: Squamous Intraepithelial Lesions of the Cervix
D065310.definition: A cytological test finding often from PAP SMEARS that shows abnormal lesions of SQUAMOUS EPITHELIAL CELLS of the CERVIX. It is a diagnostic criterion used in the Bethesda System for UTERINE CERVICAL NEOPLASMS and represents the PAP TEST result that is abnormal. Although squamous intraepithelial lesions test result does not mean UTERINE CERVICAL NEOPLASMS it requires follow-ups (e.g., HPV DNA TESTS; and COLPOSCOPY).

D065311.name: Adenocarcinoma in Situ
D065311.definition: A lesion with cytological characteristics associated with invasive adenocarcinoma but the tumor cells are confined to the GLANDULAR EPITHELIAL CELLS of origin. Adenocarcinoma in situ of the CERVIX and the LUNG are the most common.

D065326.name: Children's Health Insurance Program
D065326.definition: Federal program, enacted in 1997, for the funding of children's health insurance coverage at the state level for low-income families, affording them effective protection against erosions in employer sponsored coverage.

D065327.name: Circuit-Based Exercise
D065327.definition: Alternating sets of exercise that work out different muscle groups and that also alternate between aerobic and anaerobic exercises, which, when combined together, offer an overall program to improve strength, stamina, balance, or functioning.

D065346.name: Lubricant Eye Drops
D065346.definition: Ophthalmic solutions that include LUBRICANTS and WETTING AGENTS such as POLYETHYLENE GLYCOL; HYPROMELLOSE; GLYCEROL; PROPYLENE GLYCOL. They are used to treat conditions caused by deficient tear production such as DRY EYE SYNDROME.

D065347.name: Hypromellose Derivatives
D065347.definition: Polymeric compounds that contain repeating units of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose. The properties of hypromellose polymers can vary greatly and are defined by their molecular weight, the percentage of hydroxyl groups, the percentage of hydroxypropyl groups, and viscosity measurements. They are found a broad variety of commercial products such as FOOD ADDITIVES; EXCIPIENTS; and LUBRICANTS.

D065348.name: Macular Pigment
D065348.definition: A yellow pigment that accumulates in the MACULA LUTEA. It is composed of LUTEIN, meso-zeaxanthin, and ZEAXANTHIN.

D065366.name: Cryptoxanthins
D065366.definition: Mono-hydroxylated xanthophylls formed from the hydroxylation of BETA-CAROTENE. Isomers include: beta-cryptoxanthin, alpha-cryptoxanthin, and zeinoxanthin. The alpha- and beta-cryptoxanthin are provitamin A precursors.

D065386.name: Historically Controlled Study
D065386.definition: A study that compares a group of participants receiving an intervention with a similar group from the past who did not.

D065406.name: Laminoplasty
D065406.definition: A surgical procedure performed on selected pairs of vertebral lamina to relieve pressure on the SPINAL CORD and which also allows for osteoplastic enlargement of the SPINAL CANAL.

D065426.name: Cytoreduction Surgical Procedures
D065426.definition: Operative procedures carried out to reduce a mass of tissue, for example, to reduce the total amount of tissue composing a tumor.

D065427.name: Factor Xa Inhibitors
D065427.definition: Endogenous factors and drugs that inhibit or block the activity of FACTOR XA.

D065446.name: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder
D065446.definition: A condition in which a woman suffers from severe depression, irritability, and tension before MENSTRUATION. Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) may involve a wide range of physical or emotional symptoms, which are more severe and debilitating than those seen with premenstrual syndrome (PMS), and which include at least one mood-related symptom. Symptoms usually stop when, or shortly after, menstruation begins.

D065447.name: Practice Management, Veterinary
D065447.definition: The organization and operation of the business aspects of a veterinary practice.

D065466.name: Lysholm Knee Score
D065466.definition: An instrument used to assess the results of rehabilitation from knee injuries, especially those requiring ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT RECONSTRUCTION. It measures recovery of knee joint function based on ACTIVITIES OF DAILY LIVING.

D065467.name: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement
D065467.definition: Surgical treatment for severe AORTIC VALVE STENOSIS. Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is used as an alternative option in patients who are deemed at high risk or inoperable for traditional open-heart surgery.

D065468.name: Dasyproctidae
D065468.definition: A family of Central and South American plant-eating rodents comprising the agoutis (Dasyprocta) and acouchis (Myoprocta). They look similar to guinea pigs (CAVIA) but are larger and have longer legs. Their fur is reddish or dark brown.

D065469.name: Cuniculidae
D065469.definition: A family of large (20 to 30 inches long) plant eating rodents found in Central and South America. They are nearly tailless and have chunky bodies, dark brown fur with spotted lines along their sides and back, with stout legs and hind limbs that are longer than the forelimbs, and a large, square head with short ears.

D065506.name: Vascular Closure Devices
D065506.definition: Products used to seal the openings in BLOOD VESSELS from incisions or punctures made during ENDOVASCULAR PROCEDURES.

D065507.name: Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococci
D065507.definition: Strains of the genus Enterococcus that are resistant to the antibiotic VANCOMYCIN. The enterococci become resistant by acquiring plasmids carrying genes for VANCOMYCIN RESISTANCE.

D065508.name: Diving Reflex
D065508.definition: BREATH HOLDING; VASOCONSTRICTION; and a drop in HEART RATE in response to submersion of the face in cold water.

D065527.name: Brachial Plexus Block
D065527.definition: A blocking of NEURAL CONDUCTION in the network of nerve fibers innervating the UPPER EXTREMITY.

D065546.name: Drug Liberation
D065546.definition: Release of drugs from DOSAGE FORMS into solution.

D065566.name: Subcutaneous Absorption
D065566.definition: The uptake of substances via the SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE.

D065567.name: Absorption, Physiological
D065567.definition: Uptake of substances by the body, tissues, or cells. The uptake may occur by various forms of BIOLOGICAL TRANSPORT or by simple DIFFUSION.

D065568.name: Oral Mucosal Absorption
D065568.definition: Uptake of substances into the body via the mucosal surfaces (MUCOUS MEMBRANE) of the oral cavity.

D065569.name: Gastrointestinal Absorption
D065569.definition: Uptake of substances via the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT.

D065570.name: Gastric Absorption
D065570.definition: Uptake of substances via the stomach.

D065586.name: Intramuscular Absorption
D065586.definition: Uptake of substances via muscle tissue.

D065587.name: Ocular Absorption
D065587.definition: Uptake of substances by tissues of the eye.

D065588.name: Nasal Absorption
D065588.definition: Uptake of substances through the nasal mucosa.

D065589.name: Respiratory Tract Absorption
D065589.definition: Uptake of substances via the RESPIRATORY SYSTEM.

D065590.name: Rectal Absorption
D065590.definition: Uptake of substances from the RECTUM.

D065606.name: Metabolic Side Effects of Drugs and Substances
D065606.definition: Specific effects of drugs and substances on metabolic pathways such as those occurring through the CYTOCHROME P-450 ENZYME SYSTEM. These include effects that often result in DRUG INTERACTIONS; FOOD-DRUG INTERACTIONS; and HERB-DRUG INTERACTIONS.

D065607.name: Cytochrome P-450 Enzyme Inhibitors
D065607.definition: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 ENZYMES.

D065608.name: Renal Reabsorption
D065608.definition: The reuptake of water, ELECTROLYTES, and other substances by the KIDNEY to the blood supply.

D065609.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP1A2 Inhibitors
D065609.definition: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP1A2.

D065626.name: Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease
D065626.definition: Fatty liver finding without excessive ALCOHOL CONSUMPTION.

D065627.name: Familial Primary Pulmonary Hypertension
D065627.definition: Familial or idiopathic hypertension in the PULMONARY CIRCULATION which is not secondary to other disease.

D065628.name: Intestinal Reabsorption
D065628.definition: The re-uptake of substances in the intestines after their prior absorption from the intestines into the PORTAL SYSTEM and reintroduction into the intestines as substances accumulated in the BILE.

D065629.name: Peritoneal Absorption
D065629.definition: Uptake of substances from the PERITONEAL CAVITY.

D065630.name: Hernias, Diaphragmatic, Congenital
D065630.definition: Protrusion of abdominal structures into the THORAX as a result of embryologic defects in the DIAPHRAGM often present in the neonatal period. It can be isolated, syndromic, nonsyndromic or be a part of chromosome abnormality. Associated pulmonary hypoplasia and PULMONARY HYPERTENSION can further complicate stabilization and surgical intervention.

D065631.name: Rhinitis, Allergic
D065631.definition: An inflammation of the NASAL MUCOSA triggered by ALLERGENS.

D065632.name: Chikungunya Fever
D065632.definition: An acute infection caused by a mosquito-borne alphavirus CHIKUNGUNYA VIRUS characterized by RASH; FEVER; JOINT PAINS; CONJUNCTIVITIS; MENINGOENCEPHALITIS; LYMPHOPENIA; and THROMBOCYTOPENIA.

D065633.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP1B1
D065633.definition: A cytochrome P450 aryl hydrocarbon hydroxylase that has specificity for ESTROGENS which it converts into 4-hydroxy estrogens. CYP1B1 has been shown to be physiologically important for FETAL DEVELOPMENT with mutations in the CYP1B1 gene resulting in congenital forms of GLAUCOMA and Peter's anomaly.

D065634.name: Cerebrospinal Fluid Leak
D065634.definition: Discharge of cerebrospinal fluid through a hole through the skull bone most commonly draining from the nose (CEREBROSPINAL FLUID RHINORRHEA) or the ear (CEREBROSPINAL FLUID OTORRHEA).

D065635.name: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo
D065635.definition: Idiopathic recurrent VERTIGO associated with POSITIONAL NYSTAGMUS. It is associated with a vestibular loss without other neurological or auditory signs. Unlike in LABYRINTHITIS and VESTIBULAR NEURONITIS inflammation in the ear is not observed.

D065636.name: Myotonin-Protein Kinase
D065636.definition: Serine/threonine protein kinase responsible for various SKELETAL MUSCLE functions; HEART CONDUCTION SYSTEM activity; calcium HOMEOSTASIS; calcium uptake by SARCOPLASMIC RETICULUM and SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY. It is encoded by the DMPK gene and its abnormal EXPANDED TRINUCLEOTIDE REPEAT of CTG in the 3'-UTR is associated with MYOTONIC DYSTROPHY 1.

D065637.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2A6
D065637.definition: A cytochrome P450 enzyme that has specificity for the 7-hydroxylation of coumarin.

D065638.name: Absorption, Radiation
D065638.definition: The uptake or transfer of energy from RADIATION.

D065646.name: Thyroid Carcinoma, Anaplastic
D065646.definition: An aggressive THYROID GLAND malignancy which generally occurs in IODINE-deficient areas in people with previous thyroid pathology such as GOITER. It is associated with CELL DEDIFFERENTIATION of THYROID CARCINOMA (e.g., FOLLICULAR THYROID CARCINOMA; PAPILLARY THYROID CANCER). Typical initial presentation is a rapidly growing neck mass which upon metastasis is associated with DYSPHAGIA; NECK PAIN; bone pain; DYSPNEA; and NEUROLOGIC DEFICITS.

D065666.name: Mesenteric Ischemia
D065666.definition: Ischemic tissue injury produced by insufficient perfusion of intestinal tissue by the MESENTERIC CIRCULATION (i.e., CELIAC ARTERY; SUPERIOR MESENTERIC ARTERY; INFERERIOR MESENTERIC ARTERY; and MESENTERIC VEINS). It can progress from ISCHEMIA; EDEMA; and GANGRENE of the bowel wall to PERITONITIS and cardiovascular collapse.

D065667.name: Renal Elimination
D065667.definition: The discharge of substances from the blood supply via the URINARY TRACT.

D065668.name: Vitamin D3 24-Hydroxylase
D065668.definition: A cytochrome P-450 enzyme that has specificity for CHOLECALCIFEROL (Vitamin D3). It hydroxylates the molecule at carbon position 24.

D065669.name: Hepatobiliary Elimination
D065669.definition: The removal of substances from the blood supply via the LIVER and BILIARY TRACT.

D065686.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2B6 Inhibitors
D065686.definition: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2B6.

D065687.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C8 Inhibitors
D065687.definition: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2C8.

D065688.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C9 Inhibitors
D065688.definition: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2C9.

D065689.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C19 Inhibitors
D065689.definition: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2C19.

D065690.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2D6 Inhibitors
D065690.definition: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2D6.

D065691.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2E1 Inhibitors
D065691.definition: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2E1.

D065692.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP3A Inhibitors
D065692.definition: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP3A.

D065693.name: Cytochrome P-450 Enzyme Inducers
D065693.definition: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 ENZYMES.

D065694.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP1A2 Inducers
D065694.definition: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP1A2.

D065695.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2B6 Inducers
D065695.definition: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2B6.

D065696.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C8 Inducers
D065696.definition: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2C8.

D065697.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C19 Inducers
D065697.definition: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2C19.

D065698.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C9 Inducers
D065698.definition: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2C9.

D065699.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2D6 Inducers
D065699.definition: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2D6.

D065700.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2E1 Inducers
D065700.definition: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2E1.

D065701.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP3A Inducers
D065701.definition: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP3A.

D065702.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2B6
D065702.definition: A cytochrome P450 enzyme subtype that oxidizes a diverse array of XENOBIOTICS. The expression of CYP2B6 varies widely between individuals which is due to the high rate of GENETIC POLYMORPHISMS.  Examples of drugs metabolized by CYP2B6 include BUPROPION; efavirenz; CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE; and MEPERIDINE.

D065703.name: Malformations of Cortical Development, Group I
D065703.definition: Cortical malformations secondary to abnormal neuronal and glial CELL PROLIFERATION or APOPTOSIS in NEUROGENESIS. This group includes congenital MICROCEPHALIES; MICROLISSENCEPHALIES, megalencephalies, HEMIMEGALENCEPHALIES and cortical dysplasias with balloon cells.

D065704.name: Malformations of Cortical Development, Group III
D065704.definition: Cortical malformations secondary to abnormal cortical maturation after CELL MIGRATION in NEUROGENESIS. This group includes injury to the cortex during later stages of cortical development such as POLYMICROGYRIA and focal cortical dysplasias.

D065705.name: Hemimegalencephaly
D065705.definition: Rare MALFORMATIONS OF CORTICAL DEVELOPMENT, GROUP I characterized by the enlargement of one side of the brain. It is associated with seizures, partial paralysis, and mental retardation.

D065706.name: Polymicrogyria
D065706.definition: Heterogeneous disorders of cortical malformation characterized by excessive and small fused gyri and shallow sulci of the CORTEX with abnormal cortical lamination. It is considered a malformation secondary to abnormal post-migrational development of the neurons during cerebral cortical development and is associated with EPILEPSY and learning difficulties.

D065707.name: Schizencephaly
D065707.definition: Cortical malformations characterized by grey matter-lined cleft or cyst that extends from the EPENDYMA often to the PIA MATER outer surface. The grey matter that lines the cleft is often POLYMICROGYRIA. It is associated with developmental delay, motor disturbance and seizures.

D065708.name: Porencephaly
D065708.definition: Cortical malformations characterized by white matter-lined cleft or cyst associated with ISCHEMIA and hemorrhagic insults. Symptoms include delayed growth and development, HYPOTONIA; SEIZURES; SPASTIC HEMIPLEGIA and MACROCEPHALY; MICROCEPHALY; or HYDROCEPHALUS. Mutations in the genes encoding COLLAGEN TYPE IV are associated with familial types.

D065709.name: Common Data Elements
D065709.definition: Data elements that are common to multiple data sets across different studies.

D065710.name: Glossoptosis
D065710.definition: Posterior displacement of the TONGUE toward the PHARYNX. It is often a feature in syndromes such as in PIERRE ROBIN SYNDROME and DOWN SYNDROME and associated with AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION during sleep (OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNEAS).

D065711.name: Broca Area
D065711.definition: Functional neuroanatomical region of the inferior frontal gyrus consisting of pars opercularis and pars triangularis. It is important in SPEECH and LANGUAGE production. Injuries to Broca area are associated with BROCA APHASIA and APRAXIA.

D065726.name: Limbic Lobe
D065726.definition: The medial surface of the cerebral hemisphere around the brain stem.

D065727.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C8
D065727.definition: A liver microsomal cytochrome P450 hydroxylase that oxidizes a broad spectrum of substrates including STEROIDS, FATTY ACIDS, and XENOBIOTICS. Examples of pharmaceutical substrates for CYP2C8 include; PACLITAXOL; torsemide; and; AMODIAQUINE

D065729.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C9
D065729.definition: A cytochrome P-450 subtype that has specificity for acidic XENOBIOTICS. It oxidizes a broad range of important clinical drugs that fall under the categories of NONSTEROIDAL ANTI-INFLAMMATORY AGENTS; HYPOGLYCEMIC AGENTS; ANTCOAGULANTS; and DIURETICS.

D065730.name: Limonene Hydroxylases
D065730.definition: Members of the P-450 enzyme family that take part in the hydroxylation of limonene.

D065731.name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C19
D065731.definition: A cytochrome P-450 enzyme subtype that oxidizes several important groups of drugs including many PROTON PUMP INHIBITORS and ANTICONVULSANTS.

D065748.name: Euterpe
D065748.definition: A genus in the family Arecaceae. They are a source of ACAI BERRIES.

D065749.name: Phoeniceae
D065749.definition: Tribe of palms in the subfamily Coryphoideae, family Arecaceae.

D065767.name: Activation, Metabolic
D065767.definition: The conversion of an exogenous substance by a biological system resulting in the production on an active metabolite.

D065786.name: Delay Discounting
D065786.definition: The tendency to devalue an outcome as a function of its temporal delay or probability of achievement. It can be evaluated in a psychological paradigm that involves the choice between receiving a smaller immediate reward or a larger delayed reward, and may be used to provide a measure of impulsive behavior.

D065787.name: Salivary Elimination
D065787.definition: The discharge of substances from the blood supply via diffusion into the SALIVA from the ORAL MUCOSA or from the SALIVARY GLANDS.

D065806.name: Xenophobia
D065806.definition: Intense or irrational dislike or fear of anything that is strange or foreign, particularly of people who are strangers or foreigners. It is an attitudinal orientation of hostility against non-natives in a given population that includes attitudes, prejudices and behavior that reject, exclude or vilify persons, based on the perception that they are outsiders or foreigners to the community, society or national identity.

D065808.name: Prepulse Inhibition
D065808.definition: A neurophysiological phenomenon in which the response to a startling stimulus (pulse) is decreased when a weaker prestimulus (prepulse) precedes it closely in time. It is used as an operational measure of sensorimotor gating.

D065809.name: Respiratory Sinus Arrhythmia
D065809.definition: A naturally occurring variation in heart rate that occurs during a BREATHING cycle, where the time between heartbeats is shortened during inspiration and prolonged during expiration. It is not the same as SINUS ARRHYTHMIA, the disorder.

D065811.name: Ethnic Cleansing
D065811.definition: Expulsion of a population from a given territory due to religious or ethnic discrimination, political, strategic or ideological considerations, or a combination of these.

D065812.name: Interoception
D065812.definition: The perception of and sensitivity to stimuli originating inside of the body. It is a sense of the physiological condition of the entire body.

D065813.name: Wernicke Area
D065813.definition: Functional region comprising posterior part of the SUPERIOR TEMPORAL GYRUS in the dominant cerebral hemisphere (see CEREBRAL DOMINANCE) and often portions of the PARIETAL LOBE. Along with BROCA AREA it is important in SPEECH and LANGUAGE processes. A lesion in the area is associated with WERNICKE APHASIA and CONDUCTION APHASIA.

D065814.name: Cerebellar Vermis
D065814.definition: A subregion of the CEREBELLAR CORTEX, located along the midsagittal plane of the CEREBELLUM.

D065815.name: Acalypha
D065815.definition: Nettle-like plants in the subfamily Acalyphoideae. Acalypha is the largest genus in the Euphorbiaceae family.

D065816.name: Neuroscience Nursing
D065816.definition: The nursing specialty focusing on the needs of patients with dysfunction of the NERVOUS SYSTEM.

D065817.name: Congenital Microtia
D065817.definition: Malformation of external portion of EAR AURICLE.

D065818.name: Gamma Rhythm
D065818.definition: Brain waves characterized by a relatively high voltage or amplitude and a frequency of approximately 30-100 Hz. They are primarily observed during network engagement and sensory processing activities, during both waking and sleeping states.

D065819.name: Voriconazole
D065819.definition: A triazole antifungal agent that specifically inhibits STEROL 14-ALPHA-DEMETHYLASE and CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP3A.

D065820.name: Zona Incerta
D065820.definition: A region of the subthalamus located ventral to the THALAMUS and dorsal to the SUBTHALAMIC NUCLEUS.

D065821.name: Pontine Tegmentum
D065821.definition: The dorsal region of pons bounded by the middle CEREBELLAR PEDUNCLES and the ventral part of the pons. It is continuous with the TEGMENTUM MESENCEPHALI and contains CEREBELLAR NUCLEI, lemnisci and RETICULAR FORMATION.

D065822.name: College Fraternities and Sororities
D065822.definition: Local or national organizations of college students, primarily for social purposes, usually with secret initiations and rites and a name composed of two or three Greek letters.

D065823.name: Parabrachial Nucleus
D065823.definition: A cell group in the pontine tegmentum surrounding the surfaces of the superior CEREBRAL PEDUNCLE of the PONS.

D065826.name: Averrhoa
D065826.definition: Tropical trees in the family Oxalidaceae

D065827.name: Abducens Nucleus
D065827.definition: A region in the PONTINE TEGMENTUM that is the nucleus of the ABDUCENS NERVE.

D065828.name: Facial Nucleus
D065828.definition: A region in the pontine tegmentum that is the nucleus of the FACIAL NERVE.

D065829.name: Flower Essences
D065829.definition: Aqueous extracts of flowers that are used in healing systems.

D065830.name: Monks
D065830.definition: Members of a religious community of men typically living under vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience.

D065831.name: Nuns
D065831.definition: Members of a religious community of women typically living under vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience.

D065832.name: Superior Olivary Complex
D065832.definition: An auditory brainstem structure in the pontine tegmentum that contains several nuclei associated with auditory localization and is component of ascending and descending auditory pathways.

D065833.name: Trapezoid Body
D065833.definition: A region in the pontine tegmentum containing nuclei and fibers associated with AUDITORY PATHWAYS.

D065834.name: Religious Personnel
D065834.definition: Persons that live and work according to a religious vocation, or calling, to a consecrated or ordained life.

D065835.name: Barrington's Nucleus
D065835.definition: A nucleus in the pons with exon projections to the sacral parasympathetic nucleus associated with bladder control.

D065836.name: Kolliker-Fuse Nucleus
D065836.definition: A nucleus in the pons associated with RESPIRATION RATE control.

D065837.name: Middle Cerebellar Peduncle
D065837.definition: WHITE MATTER consisting of a large bundle of paired fibers originating in the pontine nuclei in the pre pontis and the nucleus reticularis tegmenti pontis projecting to the contralateral cerebral cortex.

D065838.name: Oculomotor Nuclear Complex
D065838.definition: A collection of nuclei in the midbrain tegmentum for the OCULOMOTOR NERVE fibers.

D065839.name: Edinger-Westphal Nucleus
D065839.definition: Nucleus in the oculomotor nuclear complex associated with oculomotor activities and stress adaptation.

D065840.name: Protective Factors
D065840.definition: An aspect of personal behavior or lifestyle, environmental exposure, or inborn or inherited characteristic, which, on the basis of epidemiologic evidence, is known to be associated with prevention or mitigation of a health-related condition considered important to prevent.

D065841.name: Pars Reticulata
D065841.definition: A region in the substantia nigra located ventral and lateral to the PARS COMPACTA.

D065842.name: Pars Compacta
D065842.definition: A region in the substantia nigra located dorsal to the PARS RETICULATA.

D065843.name: Cerebral Crus
D065843.definition: Anterior portion of the cerebral peduncle which contains the motor tracts.

D065844.name: Tectospinal Fibers
D065844.definition: A neural tract which connects the TECTUM MESENCEPHALI and the SPINAL CORD and is involved in head and eye movement coordination.

D065846.name: Nucleus Raphe Magnus
D065846.definition: A nucleus located directly rostral to the NUCLEUS RAPHE OBSCURUS in the pontine part of the Raphe nuclei. Another pontine nucleus located directly rostral to the magnus nucleus is the nucleus raphe pontis.

D065847.name: Dorsal Raphe Nucleus
D065847.definition: The dorsal region of the raphe nucleus which is a source of the SEROTONERGIC NEURONS innervating the TELENCEPHALON; DIENCEPHALON; MESENCEPHALON; and RHOMBENCEPHALON.

D065848.name: Nucleus Raphe Pallidus
D065848.definition: A nucleus in the medullary Raphe nuclei located rostral to the NUCLEUS RAPHE OBSCURUS and caudal to the NUCLEUS RAPHE MAGNUS.

D065849.name: Nucleus Raphe Obscurus
D065849.definition: A nucleus in the medullary Raphe nuclei located caudal to the NUCLEUS RAPHE PALLIDUS.

D065850.name: Cerebral Peduncle
D065850.definition: Ventral portion of the mesencephalon including the MIDBRAIN TEGMENTUM; CRUS CEREBRI; and the PRETECTUM. It does not include tectum mesencephali and TROCHLEAR NERVE.

D065851.name: Ovarian Reserve
D065851.definition: Capacity of the ovary to provide viable eggs.

D065853.name: Spatial Learning
D065853.definition: A process through which individuals encode information about their environmental CUES to facilitate SPATIAL NAVIGATION.

D065854.name: Spatial Navigation
D065854.definition: Process by which organisms use various cues to develop a route to a destination and their ability to travel such a planned route.

D065855.name: Spatial Processing
D065855.definition: Integration of spatial information perceived by visual and/or auditory CUES.

D065856.name: Rubus
D065856.definition: A plant genus of the family Rosaceae whose members include blackberries and raspberries.

D065866.name: Optic Tract
D065866.definition: Nerve fiber originating from the OPTIC CHIASM that connects predominantly to the LATERAL GENICULATE BODIES. It is the continuation of the VISUAL PATHWAY that conveys the visual information originally from the RETINA to the optic chiasm via the OPTIC NERVES.

D065886.name: Neurodevelopmental Disorders
D065886.definition: These are a group of conditions with onset in the developmental period. The disorders typically manifest early in development, often before the child enters grade school, and are characterized by developmental deficits that produce impairments of personal, social, academic, or occupational functioning.  (From DSM-V).

D065906.name: Hyperlactatemia
D065906.definition: Increase in blood LACTATE concentration often associated with SEPTIC SHOCK; LUNG INJURY; SEPSIS; and DRUG TOXICITY. When hyperlactatemia is associated with low body pH (acidosis) it is LACTIC ACIDOSIS.

D065907.name: Karoshi Death
D065907.definition: Sudden death from overwork, most often as a result of acute CARDIOVASCULAR STROKE.

D065908.name: Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation
D065908.definition: A technique of brain electric stimulation therapy which uses constant, low current delivered via ELECTRODES placed on various locations on the scalp.

D065926.name: Influenza A Virus, H10N8 Subtype
D065926.definition: A subtype of INFLUENZA A VIRUS comprised of the surface proteins HEMAGGLUTININ 10 and NEURAMINIDASE 8. The H10N8 subtype usually infects domestic birds (POULTRY) but there have been some human infections reported.

D065927.name: Waist-Height Ratio
D065927.definition: The ratio of WAIST CIRCUMFERENCE to BODY HEIGHT.

D065928.name: Forests
D065928.definition: An ecosystem dominated by trees and other woody vegetation.

D065929.name: Tundra
D065929.definition: An ecosystem dominated by grasses, lichens, mosses, sedges and shrubs in cold landscapes or at high elevations where a layer of the ground remains perennially frozen (PERMAFROST).

D065946.name: Permafrost
D065946.definition: Perennially frozen layer of soil below the surface in tundra.

D065947.name: Rainforest
D065947.definition: Forests with high average annual rainfall.

D065948.name: Grassland
D065948.definition: An ecosystem dominated by grasses (POACEAE) with few trees or shrubs.

D065966.name: Absorption, Physicochemical
D065966.definition: The physical process of passing into, or being taken up or taken in by a substance.

D065986.name: Citrullus colocynthis
D065986.definition: A plant species of the family CUCURBITACEAE distributed tropically and subtropically mainly in North Africa and Asia. It is a medicinal plant of TRADITIONAL MEDICINE and well known in ancient medicine as the wild gourd.

D066007.name: Toxicokinetics
D066007.definition: The quantitation of the body's metabolism of toxic xenobiotic compounds, as measured by the plasma concentration of the toxicant at various time points.

D066008.name: Cervical Plexus Block
D066008.definition: A blocking of NEURAL CONDUCTION in the network of nerve fibers innervating the neck and shoulder.

D066026.name: Endothelial Progenitor Cells
D066026.definition: Cells derived from BONE MARROW that circulate in the adult bloodstream and possess the potential to proliferate and differentiate into mature ENDOTHELIAL CELLS.

D066027.name: Transplant Recipients
D066027.definition: Individuals receiving tissues or organs transferred from another individual of the same or different species, or from within the same individual.

D066046.name: Diet, Paleolithic
D066046.definition: A nutritional plan based on the presumed diet of pre-agricultural human ancestors. It consists mainly of MEAT, EGGS, NUTS, roots and fresh VEGETABLES and FRUITS, and excludes GRAIN, LEGUMES, DAIRY PRODUCTS, and refined DIETARY SUGARS.

D066047.name: Vincetoxicum
D066047.definition: A plant genus of the dogbane family ASCLEPIADACEAE.

D066066.name: Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors
D066066.definition: An internationally recognized set of published rules used for evaluation of cancer treatment that define when tumors found in cancer patients improve, worsen, or remain stable during treatment. These criteria are based specifically on the response of the tumor(s) to treatment, and not on the overall health status of the patient resulting from treatment.

D066067.name: Military Family
D066067.definition: Men and women serving on active duty in the military, or in a reserve military force, and their immediate family including spouses, children, and parents.

D066086.name: Health Services for Persons with Disabilities
D066086.definition: Health services and access for DISABLED PERSONS. Disabilities include impairments, activity limitations, or participation restrictions, and reflect the interaction between the individual with the disability and personal and environmental factors.

D066087.name: Perinatal Death
D066087.definition: The death of a FETUS of GESTATIONAL AGE 28 weeks or more, or the death of a live-born INFANT less than 28 days of age.

D066088.name: Infant Death
D066088.definition: The death of a live-born INFANT within its first year of life.

D066107.name: Social Skills
D066107.definition: The personal set of abilities required to successfully interact and communicate with others, both verbally and non-verbally through gestures, body language and personal appearance.

D066126.name: Cardiotoxicity
D066126.definition: Damage to the heart or its function secondary to exposure to toxic substances such as drugs used in CHEMOTHERAPY; IMMUNOTHERAPY; or RADIATION.

D066127.name: White Matter
D066127.definition: The region of CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM that appears lighter in color than the other type, GRAY MATTER. It mainly consists of MYELINATED NERVE FIBERS and contains few neuronal cell bodies or DENDRITES.

D066128.name: Gray Matter
D066128.definition: Region of CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM that appears darker in color than the other type, WHITE MATTER. It is composed of neuronal CELL BODIES; NEUROPIL; GLIAL CELLS and CAPILLARIES but few MYELINATED NERVE FIBERS.

D066146.name: Cell Body
D066146.definition: The portion of a cell that contains the NUCLEUS and CYTOPLASM but not CELL SURFACE EXTENSIONS such as FLAGELLA and NEURITES.

D066148.name: Spinal Cord Dorsal Horn
D066148.definition: One of three central columns of the spinal cord. It is composed of GRAY MATTER spinal laminae I-VI.

D066149.name: International Planned Parenthood Federation
D066149.definition: A non-profit organization concerned with providing access to sexual and reproductive health information and services.

D066150.name: Organisation for Economic Co-Operation and Development
D066150.definition: An international organization whose mission is to stimulate world trade and economic progress by offering a forum where governments can collectively develop and refine social and economic policies.

D066151.name: Spinal Cord Ventral Horn
D066151.definition: One of three central columns of the spinal cord. It is composed of GRAY MATTER spinal laminae VIII and IX.

D066152.name: Spinal Cord Lateral Horn
D066152.definition: One of three central columns of the spinal cord. It is composed of GRAY MATTER and is located laterally in lamina VII.

D066166.name: Pectus Carinatum
D066166.definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal anterior protrusion of the STERNUM and adjacent COSTAL CARTILAGE.

D066167.name: Slit Lamp
D066167.definition: A microscope with a light source that can be projected into a linear beam. It allows cross-sectional viewing of the AQUEOUS HUMOR; CONJUNCTEIVA; CORNEA; EYELIDS; IRIS; and lens (see LENS, EYE) of the eye.

D066186.name: Costal Cartilage
D066186.definition: Bars of HYALINE CARTILAGE extending from the anterior ends of the upper RIBS. They attach to the STERNUM directly or indirectly by connecting to upper costal cartilage that attaches to the STERNUM. Costal cartilages extend the ribs anteriorly and contribute to the enhanced elasticity of the THORACIC WALL.

D066187.name: Basal Forebrain
D066187.definition: The region of the telencephalon located rostral and ventral to the STRIATUM comprising AMYGDALA; SEPTAL NUCLEI; SUBSTANTIA INNOMINATA and ventral pallidum.

D066188.name: Taiga
D066188.definition: An ecosystem dominated by coniferous forests including the tree line bordered by TUNDRA to the north and STEPPE to the south.

D066189.name: Missionaries
D066189.definition: Persons sent into an area to evangelize or to perform acts of service, such as medical care, EDUCATION, or SOCIAL JUSTICE.

D066190.name: Allesthesia
D066190.definition: A neurological disorder in which a sensory stimulus, usually tactile but more rarely other sensory modalities, is misperceived in a location distant from the original stimulus.

D066191.name: Sensorimotor Cortex
D066191.definition: A composite area of the cerebral cortex concerned with motor control and sensory perception comprising the motor cortex areas, the somatosensory areas, the gustatory cortex, the olfactory areas, the auditory cortex, and the visual cortex.

D066192.name: Manufacturing Industry
D066192.definition: An INDUSTRY which specializes in the fabrication or manufacture of products from raw or intermediate materials.

D066193.name: Cervical Cord
D066193.definition: The segment of the spinal cord within the CERVICAL VERTEBRAE.

D066194.name: Olfactory Cortex
D066194.definition: Basal forebrain and medial part of temporal lobe areas that receive synaptic inputs from the OLFACTORY BULB.

D066195.name: Piriform Cortex
D066195.definition: An area of the olfactory cortex comprising the rostral half of the uncus of the PARAHIPPOCAMPAL GYRUS and the anterior PARAHIPPOCAMPAL GYRUS. It receives major afferents directly from the OLFACTORY BULB.

D066208.name: Olfactory Tubercle
D066208.definition: Region in the ventral TELENCEPHALON located anterior to the OPTIC CHIASM, posterior to the OLFACTORY PEDUNCLE, rostral to the PIRIFORM AREA and ventral to the NUCLEUS ACCUMBENS.

D066209.name: Medical Writing
D066209.definition: The practice of writing usually by a skilled or specialized writer focused on the reporting or dissemination of medical information for a target audience.

D066228.name: Vaginal Absorption
D066228.definition: The uptake of substances from the VAGINA via the vaginal epithelium/mucosa.

D066229.name: Speech Sound Disorder
D066229.definition: Persistent difficulty with speech sound production such that it interferes with  verbal communication.

D066230.name: Patient-Specific Modeling
D066230.definition: The development and application of computational models of human pathophysiology that are individualized to patient-specific data.

D066231.name: Surgeons
D066231.definition: Medical practitioners qualified to practice surgery.

D066232.name: Pulmonary Elimination
D066232.definition: The discharge of substances from the pulmonary capillary blood into the alveolar space to be exhaled or removed by MUCOCILIARY CLEARANCE.

D066233.name: Psychology, Developmental
D066233.definition: Field of study concerned with age-related changes in BEHAVIOR that occur in human beings over the course of life, from birth to death. It includes all aspects of human growth, including emotional, intellectual, social, perceptual and personality development.

D066234.name: Lacrimal Elimination
D066234.definition: The discharge of substances into the TEARS.

D066235.name: Fluorine-19 Magnetic Resonance Imaging
D066235.definition: Magnetic resonance imaging diagnostic technique which uses fluorine-19 perfluorocarbon probes and contrast agents for high resolution image detection and quantitation.

D066236.name: Bioresonance Therapy
D066236.definition: A form of holistic medicine in which ELECTROMAGNETIC WAVES are used to diagnose and treat human and animal illness via manipulation of endogenous electromagnetic oscillations corresponding to the patient's current physiological condition.

D066237.name: Intestinal Elimination
D066237.definition: The discharge of substances from the blood supply into the intestinal lumen for excretion by DEFECATION.

D066238.name: Cutaneous Elimination
D066238.definition: The discharge of substances from the blood supply to the glands of the skin and excretion in the SWEAT and SEBUM.

D066239.name: Lacteal Elimination
D066239.definition: The discharge of substances from the blood supply into the milk formed in and secreted by the MAMMARY GLAND.

D066240.name: Anterior Cerebellar Commissure
D066240.definition: Bundle of MYELINATED NERVE FIBERS that connects the two CEREBRAL HEMISPHERES in the LAMINA TERMINALIS. It is located ventral to the SEPTAL NUCLEI, and caudal to the median PREOPTIC NUCLEUS.

D066241.name: Carbon-13 Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
D066241.definition: Magnetic resonance spectroscopy involving detection of changes in the resonance of carbon-13 nuclei in organic molecules.

D066243.name: Posterior Cerebellar Commissure
D066243.definition: A bundle of nerve fibers that crosses the midline in the tectum mesencephali dorsal to the CEREBRAL AQUEDUCT.

D066244.name: Proton Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
D066244.definition: Spectroscopy technique which measures changes in organic compounds by tracking the spectral energy of absorption of HYDROGEN atoms.

D066245.name: Telencephalic Commissures
D066245.definition: Set of nerve fibers that cross the midline of the TELENCEPHALON. They include the ANTERIOR COMMISSURE; the CORPUS CALLOSUM; and the HIPPOCAMPAL COMMISSURE of the fornix.

D066246.name: ErbB Receptors
D066246.definition: A family of structurally-related cell-surface receptors that signal through an intrinsic PROTEIN-TYROSINE KINASE. The receptors are activated upon binding of specific ligands which include EPIDERMAL GROWTH FACTORS, and NEUREGULINS.

D066247.name: Receptor, ErbB-4
D066247.definition: A cell surface protein-tyrosine kinase receptor that has specificity for EPIREGULIN; BETACELLIN; NEUREGULINS; and HEPARIN-BINDING EGF-LIKE GROWTH-FACTOR.

D066248.name: High Fructose Corn Syrup
D066248.definition: Syrup made from corn used widely in foods and beverages as a cheaper alternative sweetener to SUCROSE (common table sugar). It is generated by enzymatic processing of natural corn syrup to produce a liquid most widely composed of 42 or 55% FRUCTOSE, GLUCOSE, and various POLYSACCHARIDES.

D066249.name: Craving
D066249.definition: An intense, urgent, or abnormal desire or longing (for food, drugs, alcohol, etc.)

D066250.name: Pretectal Region
D066250.definition: Region of midbrain tectum located posterior to the THALAMUS and anterior to the SUPERIOR COLLICULUS.

D066251.name: Subtractive Hybridization Techniques
D066251.definition: Methods of studying differential GENE EXPRESSION of especially low-abundance, tissue-specific gene transcripts.

D066252.name: Sociological Factors
D066252.definition: Attributes and experiences that influence an individual's personality, attitudes, and lifestyle, which are derived from the social values and/or behavior of the groups to which an individual belongs, or aspires to belong.

D066253.name: Vascular Remodeling
D066253.definition: The active alterations of vascular wall structures, often leading to elevated VASCULAR RESISTANCE. It is associated with AGING; ATHEROSCLEROSIS; DIABETES MELLITUS; HYPERTENSION; PREGNANCY; PULMONARY HYPERTENSION; and STROKE, but is also a normal part of EMBRYOGENESIS.

D066254.name: Axillofemoral Bypass Grafting
D066254.definition: An extra-anatomic method of surgical revascularization in which the AXILLARY ARTERY is anastomosed to FEMORAL ARTERY.

D066255.name: EGF Family of Proteins
D066255.definition: A family of proteins that are related to epidermal growth factor. They share in common a consensus sequence consisting of six spatially conserved CYSTEINE residues which form three intramolecular bonds. This consensus sequence is commonly referred to EGF motif and is considered essential for binding of the proteins to ERB RECEPTORS.

D066256.name: Raw Foods
D066256.definition: Food prepared for consumption without exposure to heat.

D066257.name: Heparin-binding EGF-like Growth Factor
D066257.definition: An EGF family member that is expressed in a variety of hematopoietic, endothelial, vascular smooth muscle, and epithelial cells. It is synthesized as a transmembrane protein which is cleaved by proteases to produce the secreted form of the protein which has specificity for the EGF RECEPTOR and the ERBB-4 RECEPTOR. The membrane-bound form of the protein has been identified as the receptor which binds to and allows DIPHTHERIA TOXIN to enter cells.

D066258.name: Amphiregulin
D066258.definition: An autocrine growth factor and mitogen for a broad range of target cells including EPITHELIAL CELLS; FIBROBLASTS and immune cells. It occurs as a membrane-bound protein that can be cleaved to release an active secreted form.

D066259.name: Betacellulin
D066259.definition: An EGF family member that plays an important role in regulating growth and differentiation of PANCREATIC BETA CELLS. Betacellulin has specificity for the EGF RECEPTOR and the ERBB-4 RECEPTOR.

D066260.name: Epiregulin
D066260.definition: A member of the epidermal growth factor (EGF) family of peptide growth factors that is synthesized as a transmembrane protein which can be cleaved to release a soluble active form. Epiregulin has specificity for the EGF RECEPTOR and the ERBB-4 RECEPTOR.

D066261.name: Epigen
D066261.definition: An EGF family member that is synthesized as a membrane-bound protein that can be cleaved to release an active secreted form. It has a mitogenic effect on EPITHELIAL CELLS.

D066262.name: Social Norms
D066262.definition: Customary standards that govern behavior in groups, cultures, or societies. They reflect what a group deems acceptable in a social context in terms of appropriate and inappropriate values, beliefs, attitudes, and behaviors.

D066263.name: Protein Aggregation, Pathological
D066263.definition: A biochemical phenomenon in which misfolded proteins aggregate either intra- or extracellularly. Triggered by factors such as MUTATION, POST-TRANSLATIONAL MODIFICATIONS, and environmental stress, it is generally associated with ALZHEIMER DISEASE; PARKINSON DISEASE; HUNTINGTON DISEASE; and TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS.

D066264.name: Datasets as Topic
D066264.definition: Description or design of an organized collection of data from research projects, stored permanently in a formalized manner suitable for communication, interpretation, or processing.

D066265.name: Midbrain Reticular Formation
D066265.definition: The midbrain portion of the reticular formation located in the MIDBRAIN TEGMENTUM.

D066266.name: Trigeminal Motor Nucleus
D066266.definition: Nucleus located in the pontine tegmentum with motor neurons that innervate the muscles of the JAW through the motor portion of the TRIGEMINAL NERVE.

D066267.name: Midbrain Raphe Nuclei
D066267.definition: Raphe nuclei located in the midbrain including the dorsal and median raphe nuclei. They are the origin of the major serotonergic innervation in the FOREBRAIN.

D066268.name: Interpeduncular Nucleus
D066268.definition: A nucleus located at the midline of the ventral MIDBRAIN TEGMENTUM with primarily GABAergic projections to the median and dorsal raphe nuclei and the MIDBRAIN CENTRAL GRAY.

D066269.name: Social Theory
D066269.definition: Frameworks of empirical evidence used to study and interpret social phenomena.

D066270.name: Social Capital
D066270.definition: The expected benefits derived from the cooperation between individuals and groups.

D066271.name: External Capsule
D066271.definition: Thin layer of WHITE MATTER mostly of GABAERGIC NEURONS located between the PUTAMEN and the CLAUSTRUM.

D066272.name: Basolateral Nuclear Complex
D066272.definition: A set of amygdalar nuclei bordered laterally by the EXTERNAL CAPSULE and medially by the CENTRAL AMYGDALOID NUCLEUS.

D066273.name: Diet, Western
D066273.definition: A pattern of food consumption adopted mainly by the people of North America and Western Europe. It is mainly characterized by high intake of MEAT, processed grains, DIETARY SUGARS, DAIRY PRODUCTS, and DIETARY FATS.

D066274.name: Central Amygdaloid Nucleus
D066274.definition: A nucleus located in the caudal half of the amygdala. It is a primary region involved in controlling responses and receives many intrinsic GABAergic amygdaloid connections.

D066275.name: Health Information Exchange
D066275.definition: Organizational framework for the dissemination of electronic healthcare information or clinical data, across health-related institutions and systems. Its overall purpose is to enhance PATIENT CARE.

D066276.name: Corticomedial Nuclear Complex
D066276.definition: The rostral part of the amygdala with cortical-like layered structure. It receives major inputs from the OLFACTORY BULB and PIRIFORM CORTEX.

D066277.name: Periamygdaloid Cortex
D066277.definition: The surface of the parahippocampal gyrus overlying the cortical amygdaloid nucleus.

D066278.name: Organum Vasculosum
D066278.definition: Circumventricular cellular structure in the anterior hypothalamic region. It is located in the optic recess at the anteroventral end of the THIRD VENTRICLE and forms the ventral part of the midline anterior wall.

D066279.name: Courage
D066279.definition: State of mind or spirit that enables one to act in the face of perceived danger, difficulty, or pain.

D066280.name: Circumventricular Organs
D066280.definition: Highly vascularized and specialized tissues distributed principally along the midline of the VENTRICULAR SYSTEM from the FOREBRAIN to the HINDBRAIN. They are distinguished by their lack of normal BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER and fenestrated capillaries and contain either neurosecretory neurons or chemoreceptors.

D066288.name: Romanticism
D066288.definition: The attitude or intellectual orientation that characterized many works of literature, painting, music, architecture, criticism, and historiography in Western civilization over a period from the late 18th to the mid-19th century.

D066289.name: Data Curation
D066289.definition: Management activities required to maintain research data to ensure that they are fit for contemporary use and available for discovery and reuse.

D066290.name: Libraries, Special
D066290.definition: Collections covering specialized subjects, containing materials in a special format, or serving a specialized clientele.

D066291.name: Psychiatry in Literature
D066291.definition: Written or other literary works whose subject matter is related to mental disorders or psychiatry from the lay or practitioner perspective. .

D066292.name: Lipid Droplets
D066292.definition: Dynamic cytoplasmic organelles found in almost all cells. They consist of a central core of LIPIDS surrounded by a phospholipid monolayer studded with surface proteins, and are involved in LIPID METABOLISM and storage.

D066293.name: Renshaw Cells
D066293.definition: Ipsilateral glycinergic inhibitory interneurons of the SPINAL CORD VENTRAL HORN which modulate recurrent firing of MOTOR NEURONS. They develop from embryonic progenitor domain V1.Ia inhibitory interneurons which also originate from V1 are responsible for reciprocal inhibition of MOTONEURONS.

D066294.name: Commissural Interneurons
D066294.definition: INTERNEURONS with projections to the contralateral side of the SPINAL CORD. Both excitatory and inhibitory interneurons are involved in coordinating alternative left-right activities during LOCOMOTION.

D066295.name: Open Access Publishing
D066295.definition: Agreement in which author(s) and copyright holder(s) grant(s) to all users a free, irrevocable, worldwide, perpetual right of access to, and a license to copy, use, distribute, transmit and display the work publicly and to make and distribute derivative works, in any digital medium for any responsible purpose, subject to proper attribution of authorship, as well as the right to make small numbers of printed copies for their personal use. A complete version of the work and all supplemental materials, including a copy of the permission as stated above, in a suitable standard electronic format is deposited immediately upon initial publication in at least one online repository that is supported by an academic institution, scholarly society, government agency, or other well-established organization that seeks to enable open access, unrestricted distribution, interoperability, and long-term archiving. (from Bethesda Statement on Open Access Publishing)

D066296.name: Grounded Theory
D066296.definition: The generation of theories from analysis of empirical data.

D066297.name: Hermeneutics
D066297.definition: The art, theory, and philosophy of interpreting the meaning of an object (a text, work of art, social action, utterances of another speaker, etc.) (Dictionary of Qualitative Inquiry, 2nd ed..)

D066298.name: In Vitro Techniques
D066298.definition: Methods to study reactions or processes taking place in an artificial environment outside the living organism.

D066300.name: Electronic Cigarettes
D066300.definition: Electronic devices that are designed to provide NICOTINE in the form of an inhaled aerosol. They typically are made in the shape of CIGARETTES in order to simulate the experience of CIGARETTE SMOKING.

D066308.name: Public Service Announcements as Topic
D066308.definition: Announcements for which no charge is made and which promote programs, activities, or services of federal, state, or local governments or those of non-profit organizations and other announcements regarded as serving community interests.

D066309.name: Public Service Announcements
D066309.definition: Works consisting of announcements which promote programs, activities, or services of federal, state, or local governments or those of non-profit organizations and other announcements regarded as serving community interests.

D066310.name: Digital Divide
D066310.definition: Gap between individuals, households, businesses and geographic areas at different socioeconomic levels with regard to both their opportunities to access electronic  information and communication technologies (ICTs). Their use of the Internet for a wide variety of activities, reflects various differences among and within countries.

D066328.name: Ventral Striatum
D066328.definition: A composite structure of the TELENCEPHALON that is defined by connectivity. It includes the NUCLEUS ACCUMBENS; the ISLANDS OF CALLEJA; and parts of the CAUDATE NUCLEUS; the PUTAMEN; and the SUBSTANTIA INNOMINATA.

D066329.name: Protein Aggregates
D066329.definition: Any mixture of secondary, tertiary, or quaternary protein molecules which appear as clumps in or outside the cell.

D066330.name: Printing, Three-Dimensional
D066330.definition: Process for making, building or constructing a physical object from a three-dimensional digital model by laying down many successive thin layers of building material.

D066331.name: Laser-Evoked Potentials
D066331.definition: Somatosensory evoked potentials generated through the application of HEAT to the SKIN with a LASER. They are often used clinically to assess the function of the central nociceptive system and in diagnosing NOCICEPTIVE PAIN.
